notes.title: The multiplayer menu (MJOLNIRLobby)
notes.summary: CHANGE MAP, picking Danger Canyon and Capture the Flag, SELECT, GAME TYPE and Back all worked. START GAME started Danger Canyon under the Megalo engine, with the multiplayer HUD up.
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-10-01; updated 2026-10-24. MULTIPLAYER on the main menu
opens MJOLNIR's own lobby, map select and game type screens ("Our own
screens" below). The lobby and map selection were verified in game on CU4:
- CHANGE MAP, picking Danger Canyon and Capture the Flag, SELECT, GAME TYPE
  and Back all worked.
- START GAME started Danger Canyon under the Megalo engine, with the
  multiplayer HUD up.

Earlier, the campaign-menu screens (now the fallback) started Gephyrophobia
the same way, and the campaign save stayed byte for byte the same. Finding
and joining other players' games was not built then. It shipped later:
PUBLIC GAME, FIND GAMES and joins by connection string in mods-v0.11.0
(PR #127), joins into a public match under way in mods-v0.12.0 (PR #130),
and FIND GAMES as a server browser in mods-v0.13.0 (PR #132)
([multiplayer_servers.md](multiplayer_servers.md)).

Code: `mods/MJOLNIRLobby` (Lua) and `native/lobby` (its native half,
`mjolnir_lobby.dll`).

## How a map has to start

Only the campaign menu's own Start Game starts the simulation. A bare
`BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem:SetAndBeginCampaign` from script returns true
and loads the Unreal world, but the simulation never starts a game:
`(list_count (players))` stays 0 and the pawn waits at the world origin,
under the map. That is true for shipped missions as well
([new_scenario_loading.md](new_scenario_loading.md)).

The difference is the `BlamScenarioGameOptions` struct:

| field | scripted start | Start Game |
|---|---|---|
| `GameVariant` | none | a `BlamGameEngineCampaignVariant` built by `BP_FrontendGameState` |
| `bFriendlyFireEnabled` | false | true |
| `SaveSlot`, `bLoadFromCoreSave` | 0, false | 0, false |

The simulation's load-map event needs a campaign variant.

The skulls screen's Start Game goes through `BPFL_CampaignMenuHelpers`:
`SetClientLobbySkulls`, then `StartCountdown(CampaignSetup)`. The countdown
is the co-op lobby's countdown, which every fireteam member sees. When it
ends, `LaunchCampaign` builds the options and calls `SetAndBeginCampaign`.

The setup is a `BP_CampaignSetupParameters` held by the frontend player
controller:

- `Mode`
- `CampaignDataAsset`
- `ScenarioRow`
- `Difficulty`
- `InsertionPoint`
- `Skulls`
- `GameVariant`
- `FriendlyFireEnabled`

`SetCampaignMode(pc, 0)` gives a fresh setup for the campaign. The `Selected*`
helpers fill it in; `SelectedMission` copies the `DT_Scenarios` row. None of
them pushes a screen.

START GAME does the same:

1. `SetCampaignMode`
2. `GetCampaignSetup`
3. `SelectedMission`, `SelectedDifficulty`, `SelectedInsertionPoint`
4. `SetClientLobbyMission` and `SetClientLobbyDifficulty`
5. `StartCountdown`

The countdown brings the campaign's Mission Select up behind it.

The game type travels to MJOLNIRLevelLoader as `pending_variant.txt` beside
it. The loader reads it once, when the map starts, and stages
`variants/<mode>.mglo` in place of the level's default `variant`.

**The campaign save.** The campaign menu warns that a New Game overwrites the
save. A multiplayer map never writes it, because it makes no campaign
checkpoints. `CoreSave_0/1.sav` and `Progress.sav` were compared against a
backup after a launch, after spawning and play, and after quitting: all
three unchanged. The menu therefore skips that popup.

## Our own screens

`WBP_MJOLNIRLobby`, `WBP_MJOLNIRMapSelect` and
`WBP_MJOLNIRGameTypeSelect` are MJOLNIR's own Widget Blueprints, cooked
into `pakchunk984-MJOLNIRUI`
(`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_mjolnir_ui.py`,
[custom_ui.md](custom_ui.md)). They derive from `CommonActivatableWidget`, so
`ContentStack:BP_AddWidget` pushes them like any shipped screen: the stack
hides the main menu beneath, and Back (Escape, B) pops them
(`bIsBackHandler`).

- **The lobby:** the players (the frontend's player states), START GAME,
  INVITE FRIENDS, CHANGE MAP, GAME TYPE (opens the current map's mode
  picker), GAME SETTINGS (host only, since mods-v0.16.0;
  [host_game_settings.md](host_game_settings.md)), PRIVATE / PUBLIC GAME,
  MAX PLAYERS (2 to 16, host only;
  [fireteam_join_and_cap.md](fireteam_join_and_cap.md)), FIND GAMES and BACK,
  and a card with what the game will be. Since mods-v0.39.0 (with CE
  runtime 1.16.0's UI container) the card is two tiles, the map (its
  screenshot, name, game and players) and the game type (its icon, name and
  format), over the game settings away from the defaults in two columns of
  at most five lines, the last saying how many more. The tiles and the
  settings are buttons for the host, with the events of CHANGE MAP, GAME
  TYPE and GAME SETTINGS; a fireteam client's are HitTestInvisible. An older
  UI container keeps the one-column card with each part's description.
  JOIN THE DISCORD, beside the MJOLNIR CORE emblem at the top right, opens
  MJOLNIR's Discord invite (`KismetSystemLibrary:LaunchURL`: the browser, or
  the Discord app, opens beside the game) and writes the link in the footer.
  Every menu screen has the emblem, and clicking it opens mjolnircore.com
  tagged for the hub's Google Analytics as a visit from the game:
  `?utm_source=game&utm_medium=menu&utm_campaign=logo&utm_content=<screen>`,
  the screen being `lobby`, `map-select`, `game-type`, `game-settings`,
  `find-games`, `post-game` or `map-download` (`Pick.openSite`; UE4SS.log
  records the link). The emblem's button is cooked HitTestInvisible and made
  clickable by `pushScreen`, so with an older MJOLNIRLobby it only shows.
  A fireteam client without the host's map, or with another release of it,
  sees START GAME as DOWNLOAD MAP or UPDATE MAP (since mods-v0.20.0;
  [live_map_install.md](live_map_install.md)).
  - Team modes (CTF and Team Slayer) show separate Red/Blue roster sections.
    These reflect the game's team assignments, with an Awaiting assignment
    section when the frontend has no simulation team yet. No local team
    choices or fabricated alternating assignments are written to the game.
    Free-for-all uses one list. The roster supports up to 16 players and
    scrolls without moving the surrounding controls.
  - INVITE FRIENDS opens the game's own Friends screen (`WBP_Roster_C`:
    Platform and Cross-Platform friends, each with + Invite). It does this by
    calling `BP_OnClicked` on one of the fireteam panel's INVITE + rows
    (`WBP_SquadBlankListViewItem_C`). Those rows belong to the UI layout's
    squad widget, alive under every screen. Back returns to the lobby.
  - That screen also shows START CAMPAIGN, which starts the campaign, not
    the lobby's map. The last game hosted is remembered in
  `MJOLNIRLobby\last_game.txt`.
- **The map select:** up to 80 maps in a scrolling list: every installed
  map, then the hub's maps this PC does not have, marked DOWNLOAD
  (`MapLive.listings`, the cached `GET /maps`). Chips above it narrow the
  list by game (the hub's `game`: Halo CE or Halo 2), by source (official
  or community) and to installed maps; a map the hub does not list passes
  only the ALL choices. Hovering a map previews its details and game types,
  and leaving it shows the chosen map again; clicking picks it. The game types
  are tabs across the panel, the same families as the game type select, on one
  line each (CTF and King for the two long names). The chosen tab runs into a
  tray with its description and its variants as buttons. SELECT returns to the
  lobby with both, or, for a map not installed, opens the download screen and
  picks the map once it is in.
  Since mods-v0.39.0 (CE runtime 1.16.0's UI container):
  - A search box over the list has the focus when the screen opens. Every
    word typed must be in a map's title, code or game's names ("ce", "halo
    2"); the best matches come first (a word starting the title, then one
    starting a word of it) and the best is picked as you type, so ENTER
    selects it (`Pick.score`). Only ENTER leaves the box focused when it
    commits, which tells it from the focus moving away. CLEAR empties it.
  - Rows are sorted by title and show the map's game (CE or H2) and DOWNLOAD
    or CURRENT (the map the lobby has). A second click on the same row within
    half a second selects it.
  - The details panel has a fixed size, with SELECT and BACK at its foot:
    the screenshot, the title, the hub listing's facts (game, size, players,
    vehicles) and summary, the author line, and the game types as a row of
    icon tiles. Hovering a tile describes its mode beside the row.
- **The game type select:** the host's current map and its available game
  types. The list on the left is families (Slayer, Capture the Flag, Oddball,
  Juggernaut, King of the Hill, Race, Forge), each naming its variants. The
  chosen family's variants are buttons on the right, under the description, so
  Team King is two clicks: KING OF THE HILL, then TEAM KING. A family of one
  has no buttons. Families are what a player would call the game, not the
  engine it runs on: Juggernaut, Stalker and Reverse Tag run on Oddball's engine
  and are a family of their own (`family` in `Scripts/modes.lua`).

  The current game type is marked CURRENT on its family and its button, and
  its family has focus when the screen opens. Hover previews a game type;
  clicking chooses a pending one, and the SELECT button names it. SELECT saves
  that choice and updates the lobby; BACK, Escape or controller B leaves the
  hosted game unchanged. Availability uses the same map support, installed
  variant and required runtime checks as map selection. Team Slayer is
  supported wherever Slayer is, and Forge appears when its editor and runtime
  are installed. Before confirming, `Scripts/gametype.lua` rechecks host
  authority, the map and availability.

  The UI container ships apart from the mod, so `gametype.lua` looks for
  `Variant0`. A container without it has six tiles, one per engine, and a click
  on the chosen tile steps through its variants; an older MJOLNIRLobby on a
  newer container gets the same, since the seventh row and the variant buttons
  start collapsed. Map select does the same with its own tiles. An older UI
  container without this screen opens the existing map picker on the current
  map instead.

The game type icons are original geometric glyphs generated by
`tools/ue/draw_gametype_icons.py`, using Pillow. They contain no extracted
Halo or MCC artwork. Screens draw them on round and diamond backings, so the
script centres each glyph on its canvas (`brand_logo.py` does the same for the
emblem, ignoring the source's faint outer pixels). Run `python tools/ue/draw_gametype_icons.py` to rebuild
the eight transparent 256-pixel PNGs in
`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/GameTypeIcons`; add `--sheet out/gametype-icons.png`
for a preview sheet. The UI builder imports them as `T_MJMode_<Name>` under
`/Game/MJOLNIR/UI/ModeIcons` and cooks them with the screen in chunk 984.
The lobby shows the selected mode's same icon beside its game type title,
including when following the host's choice as a fireteam client. Missing
icon textures hide the lobby emblem and do not prevent mode selection. On a
container without the Race and Juggernaut glyphs, those families borrow the
flag and the Slayer reticle.

Each button's own graph calls the widget's `MJ_Event(<event>)`: `start`,
`invite`, `changemap`, `gametype`, `gamesettings`, `listing`, `maxdown`,
`maxup`, `maxplayers`, `findgames`, `discord`, `logo` (every screen),
`back`, `select`, `map:<i>`,
`hover:<i>`, `unhover:<i>`, `mode:<i>`, `modehover:<i>`, `modeunhover:<i>`,
`search`, `searched`, `search_clear`, `filter:game`, `filter:source`,
`filter:installed` (FIND GAMES and GAME SETTINGS send their own, such
as `game:<i>`, `sort:<column>` and `reset`). Lua hooks it and handles the
event off the click, in `ExecuteInGameThread`. No native delegate binding is involved. Only the
injected fallback MULTIPLAYER button still needs it (next section).
Game type events compare the sender's native UObject address with the
active screen, so delayed events from a previous picker cannot change the
new choice. `tools/tests/test_gametype_picker.lua` covers this and the
selection, cancellation, availability and older-container behavior.

Without the UI container, MULTIPLAYER falls back to the campaign-menu
screens described next.

The custom screens use a 2560×1440 design canvas fitted as a whole to the
viewport, keeping columns together at lower resolutions and ultrawide
aspect ratios. Flat translucent navy panels, fine cyan rules, regular
weight type and gold primary actions share the scoreboard's visual style.
The game's animated background and CommonUI menu stack remain in use.

## The main menu's own MULTIPLAYER button

Verified on CU4, 2026-10-02. MULTIPLAYER is a real button of `WBP_MainMenu`,
cooked into the menu's package:
- It sits after the hidden Remix button, between CAMPAIGN and PLAY CO-OP.
- It is there the first time the menu shows.
- It has the menu's own styling, focus, keyboard and gamepad navigation, and
  Back.
- Its click pushes `WBP_MJOLNIRLobby` itself, through the call the menu uses
  for Customization (`HaloUIManagerSubsystem.PushStreamableContentToLayerFullscreen`).
- Remix keeps its slot, its click and its unlock rule.

Lua only fills the lobby once it exists (`NotifyOnNewObject` on the lobby
class) and handles its events, as above.

```bash
mjolnir ue menu-button --out-dir <dir>      # writes pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU_P
```

`tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh` builds it into the CE runtime pack, beside
the lobby's own container (chunk 984). The defaults are the main menu,
`MultiplayerButton`, "MULTIPLAYER", after `RemixButton`, opening
`/Game/MJOLNIR/UI/WBP_MJOLNIRLobby.WBP_MJOLNIRLobby_C`.
`ue_asset::menu_button` does the work, and finds everything by name.

**What a new button takes** (all in the one package):

| | added | copied from |
|---|---|---|
| the button | a new export in the widget tree, its label changed from the string table entry `Menus/main_item_remixmenu` to the text "MULTIPLAYER" | `RemixButton` |
| its slot | a new `HaloUIButtonContainerSlot` export, listed in `MainButtonContainer.Slots` right after Remix's | Remix's slot |
| the click function | a new `BndEvt__…MultiplayerButton…` export, added to the class's Children and FuncMap; it enters the ubergraph at the new block | Remix's click stub |
| the binding | a `ComponentDelegateBindings` row: `MultiplayerButton.OnButtonBaseClicked` → that function | Remix's row |
| the variable | an `ObjectProperty` named `MultiplayerButton`, last among the class's own properties | `RemixButton`'s |
| the push | a block before the ubergraph's `EX_EndOfScript`: player controller, push, pop | the Customization push |

New exports go at the end of the export map, and the block at the end of
the ubergraph, so no package index, jump or entry point moves. Each new
export gets a dependency bundle like its template's. Its create and
serialize commands sit beside the template's in the export bundle.

**The class default object has to move too.** An unversioned property
header numbers a class's own properties first and its supers' after them.
The new variable is own slot 35, so every inherited value of
`Default__WBP_MainMenu_C` moves up one slot: its header's skip before slot 87
goes from 53 to 54. Without that the CDO reads garbage, and the game
crashed as the frontend built the menu.

**Rebuild after every game update.** The container replaces the whole
`WBP_MainMenu` package. A stale copy would hide the updated menu, so the
runtime pack has to be rebuilt from the new build. The command refuses when
something it looks for is gone, rather than guessing.

**Without the container** (an older runtime pack), the main menu has no
`MultiplayerButton`, and MJOLNIRLobby falls back to injecting its own button
into Remix's slot (next section). The log says which one is in use:
`MULTIPLAYER is on the main menu (its own button)`, or `... (injected: ...)`.

`mjolnir ue disasm --package <pkg> --export <name|index>` prints a
Blueprint function's bytecode (`ue_asset::kismet`). That's how the Remix
gate (`UpdateButtonsEnabled`: `IsRemixMenuUnlocked`) and the pushes were
found.

## Screens from the game's widgets (fallback)

A screen is a `WBP_CampaignMenu_C` (header, sub-header, a
`HaloUIButtonContainer`, a description and the fireteam panel) pushed with
`WBP_MeteoriteUILayout_C.ContentStack:BP_AddWidget`. Its own buttons are
swapped for ours. Buttons are `WBP_MeteoriteStandaloneButtonDefault_C`, the
main menu's kind.

- **Use the container's own slots.** Put a button into one with
  `ReplaceButtonContainerChildAt`. That keeps the button group consistent.
  Appending after hidden native buttons left the group's selection on a
  hidden button, and CommonUI routes Enter through the selected button.
- **Labels.** Set a label after the button is in the tree. A label set before
  construction is lost.
- **Repeat clicks.** `bInteractableWhenSelected = true`. Otherwise a clicked
  button is selected and ignores the next press.
- **Re-activation.** The campaign menu's activation resets its own buttons
  and texts, so `BP_OnActivated` re-applies the screen.
- **Main menu entry.** Without pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU, the injected
  MULTIPLAYER takes the slot of the hidden Remix button. A light poll puts
  it back on each new main menu.
- **Loading classes.** UE4SS's `LoadAsset` needs the asset's object path
  (`/Game/.../WBP_CampaignMenu.WBP_CampaignMenu`). Neither the bare package
  nor the `_C` class path works. The frontend loads most screen classes only
  when they are first opened.

### Clicks

A CommonUI button reports a click only through its `OnButtonBaseClicked`
dynamic delegate, and the path to it is native-to-native. Hooks on the
button's `BP_OnClicked`, `HandleButtonClicked` or `BP_OnPressed` never fire
for a Blueprint that does not implement them. UE4SS's Lua cannot bind a
delegate either: the property comes back as an opaque object.

UE4SS.dll exports what binding needs:

- `UObject::GetPropertyByNameInChain`. The plain `GetPropertyByName` sees
  only the Blueprint class's own properties.
- The `FWeakObjectPtr` and `FName` constructors.
- `FMulticastDelegateProperty::AddDelegate`, the engine's own add.

So `mjolnir_lobby_bind` binds each button's delegate to a clicker. The
clicker is a hidden `WBP_MeteoriteHyperlink_C` whose Blueprint function
`SetHyperlinkText` takes no parameters and only sets its own text. The
Lua hook on that function is the click.

The clicker is parked, collapsed, in the button's `LeafNamedSlot`, so it
lives exactly as long as the button. It is armed 300 ms after creation,
because construction calls `SetHyperlinkText` too. Lua has no C API here
(UE4SS does not export it), so requests and replies travel as
`native/lobby_request.txt` and `lobby_reply.txt`.

**Hook only Blueprint-scripted functions.** A hook on
`HaloUIButtonContainer:HandleButtonGroupSelectionChanged` (native, with
parameters) crashed the game inside UE4SS's argument marshalling.

## Maps and modes

The lobby reads the launcher's `MJOLNIRMaps\maps.json`, rebuilt from every
installed map (`crates/blam-pack/src/maps.rs`). For codes that list lacks, it
reads `MJOLNIRLevelLoader/maps.json`, which `mjolnir level bake
--install-test` writes (Lua cannot list a directory). Each entry has:

- `code`
- `title`
- `description`
- `modes`: the level file's `modes`, else its `variant`

`tools/level/gen_ce_level.py` names the stock maps (`STOCK_TITLES`) and lists
`"modes": ["slayer"]`, plus `"ctf"` when the map has a flag for each team.
A mode is offered when the map lists it and `variants/<mode>.mglo` is
installed.

## Next

**Update 2026-10-21:** the lobby service is built on the hub, as a D1-backed
polled API (`hub/src/lib/api/lobby.ts`, PR #106). The hand-off is the PlayFab
lobby's connection string, given to the game's own Steam join handler
(mods-v0.11.0, PR #127; [multiplayer_servers.md](multiplayer_servers.md)),
and on the Xbox app to the GDK session's invite handler (mods-v0.23.0 and
v0.23.1, PR #179 and #181). FIND GAMES lists the hub's games, not Steam
lobbies. The session join was verified on two PCs on 2026-10-01 (03fae037).
Match chat shipped in the match HUD, not the lobby service (mods-v0.27.0,
PR #200). Discord Rich Presence and public-session Join Game are implemented
through local IPC ([discord_presence.md](discord_presence.md)). Still not
built: join codes (JOIN PRIVATE) and Steam lobbies.

- **A lobby service of our own** (Cloudflare, beside the hub), since Game Pass
  and Store players have no Steam. Planned shape: a game list, join codes, the
  member list and chat, as a D1-backed polled API first. Live chat may move to
  a Durable Object. The open question is the hand-off: how a client joins the
  host's PlayFab session.
- **Steam lobbies**, for Steam players only. Steam is live in the process
  (`steam_api64` v1.57), and its flat API can be called from the native half.
  Pieces:
  - FIND GAMES: a lobby list.
  - JOIN PRIVATE: friends-only and invite lobbies.
  - The friends list's Join Game: `GameLobbyJoinRequested`, `+connect_lobby`.
  - Bringing lobby members into the host's fireteam session.
- **Discord** rich presence over its local IPC pipe is implemented; see
  [setup and verification](discord_presence.md).
- Two-player verification of the session join and of Megalo kill scoring.

notes.title: Server list and hosting
notes.summary: Short answer: Every game is hosted by a player: the host's game is a listen server, and PlayFab Party carries the traffic. Public games are built: a host switches its lobby to PUBLIC GAME, the game is listed on the hub, and FIND GAMES joins it through the game's own invite flow…
notes.body:
**Question:** how do players find games and host them, and can a game run on
a dedicated server that players connect to?

**Short answer:**
- Every game is hosted by a player: the host's game is a listen server, and
  PlayFab Party carries the traffic.
- Public games are built: a host switches its lobby to PUBLIC GAME, the game
  is listed on the hub, and FIND GAMES joins it through the game's own
  invite flow (below).
- A true dedicated server is not possible: there is no server binary, and no
  way to run the Blam sim outside the game client. A headless host (the real
  game, windowless) works on a GPU machine, but the idea was dropped on
  2026-10-02. The findings are kept below.

Status as of 2026-10-02 (CU4); updated 2026-10-21.

## What exists

| Piece | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Lobby API: register, heartbeat, remove, list, join | `hub/src/lib/api/lobby.ts`, migration `0012_maps_and_lobbies.sql` | Live in prod |
| Games page on the website | `hub/src/app/games/page.tsx` | Live |
| `lobbies:write` on launcher device keys | `hub/src/lib/api/device.ts` `DEVICE_SCOPES` | Live; keys paired before it lack the scope (403 `insufficient_scope`) |
| The lobby's connection string | `native/lobby` `mjolnir_lobby_connection` | Verified: `cv2:...`, 106 characters, membership unlocked, max 16 |
| Join by connection string | `native/lobby` `mjolnir_join` (OnlineTick hook) | Verified on one PC: the game left its lobby and called `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` with our string, then showed its own FAILED TO JOIN for a fake one |
| Hub calls from the game | `native/lobby` `mjolnir_hub_call` (WinHTTP) | Verified: `GET /lobbies` 200 |
| PRIVATE / PUBLIC GAME, FIND GAMES | `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/games.lua`, `main.lua`, `WBP_MJOLNIRFindGames` | Built; verified on two PCs 2026-10-09 (FIND GAMES download and join, e98d2152; steps in [two_pc_test.md](two_pc_test.md), Phase 5) |

The listing hides the connection string. A client gets it from `/join`, which
requires sign-in. See the header comment in `lobby.ts`.

## How a game is hosted today

- The host's game creates a PlayFab lobby (membership) and a PlayFab Party
  network (traffic), then opens a `PlayFabNetDriver` when the first remote
  player arrives ([fireteam_join_and_cap.md](fireteam_join_and_cap.md)).
- Party traffic goes through Microsoft's relays, so hosts need no port
  forwarding. The game opens only UDP 57716+.
  - The exe carries `DirectPeerConnectivity` strings. The game's setting for
    it is unread.
- The lobby is Private, with no owner migration. **When the host leaves, the
  game ends.** That is the main argument for always-on hosts.
- Joining needs only the lobby's connection string, which reaches
  `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` through `JoinSession` or the Steam
  invite-accepted path. The exe imports `PFLobbyGetConnectionString`.

## Public games

**Hosting.** A host's lobby opens as PUBLIC GAME: MULTIPLAYER lists the
game unless the host already picked PUBLIC or PRIVATE this launch
(`Games.defaultPublic`), so a private choice holds through matches and back to
the lobby. The button switches between PUBLIC GAME and PRIVATE GAME (host
only). FORGE starts private without counting as the host's choice, and the
mod check can keep the game private. While public, `games.lua`:
- reads the PlayFab lobby's connection string from the native half;
- `POST /lobbies` with the map, game type, players, the host's MAX PLAYERS
  (`max_players`), its game settings line (`settings`,
  [host_game_settings.md](host_game_settings.md)) and the string;
- heartbeats every 30 s, and at once after a map, game type or start
  changes, with players, MAX PLAYERS, game settings, state (`open`,
  `in_game`, `full`) and the current string (the game makes a new lobby
  after leaving one);
- `DELETE`s the listing when the host goes private or joins another game. A
  game that quits drops out when its heartbeat goes stale (90 s).

The lobby's footer says why a game isn't listed (no launcher sign-in, an old
key, the hub unreachable, no online lobby).

**Public or private mid-match** (MJOLNIRLobby 0.24.0). The HOST MENU has MAKE
PUBLIC / MAKE PRIVATE, and chat has `/public` and `/private`
([multiplayer_hud.md](multiplayer_hud.md)); FORGE matches stay private. Each
change and the listing's outcome reach the host's chat as a system line
(`MJOLNIRLobby\chat_notice.txt`, read by MJOLNIRHud). The native half
(`post_join_state`) posts the lobby's joining state at once rather than at the
game's next update:
- **Public:** membership unlocked and `_flags` given the join bits (what a
  game started public keeps). The PreLogin pass and the joiner injection
  follow the flag live.
- **Private, in a match:** the lock and `_flags` the game itself last asked
  for (locked, 1344 after a start), so nobody new can join. Going private in
  the menu posts nothing: the game posts no update on the way back from a
  match, so its last ask there is the match's lock, which would keep invited
  friends out.

**A host stays online alone** (MJOLNIRLobby 0.24.0). As shipped, a match
started with one session member leaves the session to play offline
(`UBlamOnlineSessionSubsystem::SetSessionRunning`, exe 0x7abb940), so a game
started private and alone lost its lobby. It couldn't be listed later, and
RETURN TO LOBBY (a `servertravel`) never got one back. Only SAVE AND EXIT or
a restart did (2026-11-07). Each start from our lobby now writes
`native\host_online.txt`, and the branch patch public games used applies to
any host, public or private. FORGE keeps the shipped branch.

Where a host still ends up with no lobby (FORGE, or a game update that moves
the patched branch), RETURN TO LOBBY with nobody else in the match calls
`BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem:EndCampaign`, SAVE AND EXIT's own exit. About
3 s after the menu loads, the game asks for a new session itself (traced
2026-11-08 through the hooked public `CreateSession`: exe 0x7ac2790 to
0x7abee20). That function returns early on state bits a solo start leaves
set, and only that exit clears them: a `servertravel` back, or `EndCampaign`
from the menu, makes no lobby. In the menu with no lobby, the footer says
how to get one back.

**FIND GAMES** (`WBP_MJOLNIRFindGames`, chunk 984) is a server table of up
to 40 public games:
- **Columns:** server (name, then host account and country), map ("NOT
  INSTALLED" when missing), game type (teams or free for all), players (and
  open slots), ping (signal bars and the estimate), status (LOBBY, IN MATCH,
  FULL, and a different MJOLNIR Lobby version). Columns are fixed-width
  boxes in both the header and the rows, so they line up whatever the text.
- **Sorting:** a column heading sorts by it; again reverses it. Ping, lowest
  first, by default. Ties go to fuller games, then nearer ones.
- **Filters:** GAME TYPE and MAP cycle through the values listed; HIDE FULL,
  HIDE IN MATCH and MAPS I HAVE are toggles. The count above the table says
  how many games the filters hide.
- **Details:** hovering a row previews it; clicking chooses it. The panel
  shows the host, map, game type, a pip per player slot, ping, region
  (country and Cloudflare colo) and version, with warnings for a missing map
  or another version.
- **JOIN** follows the game the details show, and says why it can't join
  (GAME FULL, MAP NOT INSTALLED). **QUICK JOIN** joins the best game the
  filters allow: map installed, a free slot, then the same version, better
  signal, more players.
- The list refreshes every 30 s while the screen is up. The sort, game type
  filter and toggles are kept in `MJOLNIRLobby\find_games.txt`.
- `native\lobbies_sample.json` (a `/lobbies` reply) stands in for the hub
  when present, to try the screen with many games.

An older runtime pack's FIND GAMES (one label per row) still works with
this Lobby, unsorted and unfiltered; this runtime pack's widget keeps the
names an older Lobby fills.

**Joining.** JOIN gets the string from `/lobbies/{id}/join` and writes it to
`native\join_request.txt`. `mjolnir_join` queues it, and the next
`FOnlineAsyncTaskManagerSteam::OnlineTick` (online thread) calls the task
manager's own `GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t` handler with it. That handler
is what a Steam "Join Game" runs:
- it builds `FOnlineAsyncEventSteamInviteAccepted`;
- a connect string without `SteamConnectIP=` is stored whole as
  `CONNECTIONSTRING`;
- the game leaves its fireteam and joins the host's.

How the native half finds it, by pattern rather than address:
- `OnlineTick` by its body bytes; exe RVA `0x6a7b580` on CU4, the only
  pointer to it is vtable slot 6 at `0xbc86b00`;
- the handler by scanning the task manager for the `CCallback` whose
  `m_iCallback` is 337 and whose `m_pObj` is the manager (+0x380 on CU4,
  `m_Func` `0x6a7b5d0`).

The handler converts the connect string as a C string, so Steam's 256-byte
limit doesn't apply. Today's strings are 106 characters anyway.

On the Xbox app there is no Steam subsystem. `mjolnir_join` hands the string
to the GDK session's own invite handler, from the GDK subsystem's tick, the
way an Xbox join arrives (mods-v0.23.0 and v0.23.1, PR #179 and #181;
[game_pass.md](game_pass.md)). `join_request.txt` may carry the host's
SteamID64 or XUID after the string.

A website's `mjolnir://join/<lobby>` link reaches the launcher, which leaves
the lobby id in `native\pending_join.txt`; once signed in on the menu, FIND
GAMES opens and joins that game as JOIN would (mods-v0.21.0 and
launcher-v0.13.0, PR #166).

**Auth.** Listing needs `lobbies:write`; `/join` needs any signed-in key. The
native half reads the launcher's key from
`%APPDATA%\com.devnull9090.mjolnir-launcher\hub_auth.json` and sends it to
the hub only. Players without the launcher can still host for, and be
invited by, friends. An account banned from matchmaking can neither list
nor join (403), and a banned host's game drops out of the list (PR #172;
[player_identity.md](player_identity.md)).

**A game on a map you lack:** JOIN reads DOWNLOAD AND JOIN. The map installs
in the running game first, then the join runs as usual
([live_map_install.md](live_map_install.md)).

**Not built:** JOIN PRIVATE by short code (an unlisted registration the hub
maps to the lobby).

## Dedicated servers

### A. An Unreal dedicated server: not possible

- The shipping exe is a game target, not a server target.
  `IsRunningDedicatedServer` is not in it.
- PlayFab's own server product (`JoinLobbyAsServer`,
  `RequestMultiplayerServer`) needs the title's server credentials. Those
  belong to the publisher.

### B. The Blam sim on its own: not practical

`HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll` could in principle be loaded by our own
process. But clients are Unreal clients:
- they expect an Unreal server speaking UE replication (GameState,
  PlayerState, the BlamExperience readiness flags, pawns), with the Blam
  network endpoints carried inside it;
- all of it runs over PlayFab Party, under a PlayFab identity of the title.

That means reimplementing an Unreal server around the sim. Not worth it.

### C. A headless host: works with a GPU (dropped 2026-10-02)

The real game with no window, hosting through the normal menu path, driven
by script. Tested 2026-10-02 on PC 1, as a second process launched directly
(`SteamAppId=2806050`):

| Launch flags | Signs in | Starts a map |
|---|---|---|
| `-nullrhi -nosound -unattended` | Yes. No GPU driver loads; reaches the frontend in about 2 min | **No.** `StartCountdown` never returned. The game thread hung (190 s and counting), with about 9 cores busy. |
| `-RenderOffScreen -nosound -unattended` | Yes | **Yes.** BGL, Slayer under Megalo, HUD hooks armed, one Spartan spawned |

Sign-in without input: call the title screen's own click event,
`WBP_TitleMenu_C:BndEvt__WBP_TitleMenu_WBP_MeteoriteStandaloneButtonDefault_K2Node_ComponentBoundEvent_1_CommonButtonBaseClicked__DelegateSignature(nil)`.
Then wait for `MULTIPLAYER is on the main menu`. The account is whatever
Steam is signed in as.

Cost at BGL with no players: about 6–7 CPU cores, 55–60% of the GPU's 3D
engine, and 8 GB of working set. `t.MaxFPS 30` and the low `sg.*` settings
barely changed it. Whether those console variables applied was not checked.
`-ResX/-ResY` may be ignored offscreen.

What a headless host still needs:
- **One Steam account and one game licence per server.** PlayFab membership
  is per account (two instances on one account rejoin as the same member).
- **A Windows machine with a GPU.** `-nullrhi` can't start a map. WARP
  (software D3D12) is untested.
- **Its own player out of the game.** The host is a real player and takes
  one of the 16 slots. Options: a Megalo variant that parks it (invisible,
  invulnerable, off the map), plus filtering it out of the scoreboard and
  kill feed. The sim may also allow it never to spawn. Untested.
- **A host loop.** Host on start, register with the hub, rotate maps (the
  post-game vote already exists), watchdog and restart on a hang, and
  re-host after a game update.
- Two hosts can share one PC if each has its own account.

## Open questions

- **Can a player join a match in progress?** ~~The host's lobby membership is
  unlocked at the menu; whether the game locks it in a match, and whether a
  late client gets a seat in the sim, is untested. The local-guest research
  found the sim roster fixed at launch,
  but that was a local `CreatePlayer`, not a network join.~~ **Update
  2026-10-21:** answered 2026-10-03. The match's game mode refuses a login
  mid-match ("Cannot join - game is already in progress"). For a public game
  MJOLNIRLobby's native half skips that refusal and the host puts the
  joiner's players in its running Blam game (mods-v0.12.0, PR #130;
  `native\join_in_progress.txt` = 0 turns it off). A private game still
  refuses. Two-PC test: `tools/remote/jip-test.mjs`.
- Does a Private lobby accept a join by connection string from a stranger?
  Expected yes, per PlayFab's model; not tested with a real host.
- Headless host (dropped): keeping its player from spawning; WARP for a
  GPU-less machine; why `-nullrhi` hangs at map start.

notes.title: Game modes: what runs, what breaks, and how to add more (CU4)
notes.summary: The facts come from a static research pass on 2026-10-21. Nobody launched the game for it. Nine first reports (engine, UE host, flags, armour, repository audit, ReachVariantTool and MCC facts, Bungie corpus, grammar, codec) were each checked by an adversarial verifier, and four…
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-10-21. Section 1 describes what ships at 772eca0d. Sections 2
to 5 are designs and test plans. **Update 2026-10-22:** the two colour fixes
of section 2 and the CLI's 60-tick default are built on branch
`work/reach-game-mode-support-2eca91` (each fix's *Built* paragraph says
where) and untested in game. None of it ships before the user has tested it
in game. **Update 2026-11-04:** King and Oddball are built on converted CE
maps and were hosted and scored on PC 1 on Prisoner (section 3.4). Nothing is
released.
**Binaries:** `HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll` ("sim", image base
0x180000000) and `HaloCampaignEvolved.exe` ("exe", image base 0x140000000),
CU4 (build lock in [`build_lock.md`](build_lock.md)). Every address is an RVA
and says sim or exe.
**Related:** [`re/reach_game_engine.md`](re/reach_game_engine.md) (the full
map of the sim's game-engine layer and how the host consumes it; this document
is the plan built on it), [`re/megalo_engine.md`](re/megalo_engine.md) (the
engine switch and the variant loader, as worked out),
[`re/megalo_variant_format.md`](re/megalo_variant_format.md) (the bitstream),
[`custom_game_types.md`](custom_game_types.md) (the hub design built on
section 5), [`multiplayer_ctf_plan.md`](multiplayer_ctf_plan.md),
[`host_game_settings.md`](host_game_settings.md),
[`multiplayer_hud.md`](multiplayer_hud.md),
[`multiplayer_postgame.md`](multiplayer_postgame.md),
[`ce_map_conversion.md`](ce_map_conversion.md),
[`game_state_reader.md`](game_state_reader.md),
[`hub_architecture.md`](hub_architecture.md),
[`map_distribution.md`](map_distribution.md). The full grammar the codec reads
is `crates/blam-megalo/grammar/megalo_cu4.json`.

## Sources and how to read this

The facts come from a static research pass on 2026-10-21. Nobody launched the
game for it. Nine first reports (engine, UE host, flags, armour, repository
audit, ReachVariantTool and MCC facts, Bungie corpus, grammar, codec) were each
checked by an adversarial verifier, and four follow-up passes then read the
code the verifiers had left open: what the sim publishes to Unreal each frame,
how a fireteam carries a match, what an untrusted variant can do, and how teams
are assigned.

- **Verified** means someone read the code, data or file that shows it.
  **Inferred** means it rests on names, Reach knowledge, analogy, or a chain
  with one unread link; the link is named.
- **Precedence.** Where reports disagree, the verifier's verdict beats the
  first report, a follow-up pass that read the deciding code beats both, and
  the codec's round trip over Bungie's variants beats any reading of the
  bitstream. Section 7 lists what stays open.
- **Reach is a hint, not proof.** Names of Megalo actions, conditions, enums
  and Reach object types below are ReachVariantTool's. Their CU4 wire format is
  verified; their CU4 behaviour is verified only where an RVA is given.
- **Bungie's variants are Microsoft content.** They are read from the user's
  MCC install for comparison and never committed, published or shipped
  (section 4.3). MJOLNIR writes its own game types.

Notation, as in the Megalo docs: `G` = engine globals `[TLS+0x38]`; `GG` = game
globals `[TLS+0x60]`, with the game options at `GG+0x10`; `v` = the running
variant at `GG+0x15f0` and `o = v+4` (variant-format offsets are o-relative);
`P` = a player datum (`[TLS+0x30]`, 0x4b0 bytes each); `D(h)` = an object datum;
`MP(h)` = its multiplayer block at `D(h) + u16 D(h)+0x182`.

## Summary

1. **CE's Standard game types are built** (section 3.6):
   Slayer, Team Slayer, CTF, Assault, Oddball, Team Oddball, Juggernaut, King,
   Crazy King, Team King, Race, Team Race, Rally and Team Rally. This summary was
   written when only Slayer and CTF ran; the rest of it stands.
2. **The engine is all there.** It is Reach's game-engine layer, and every
   Reach mode is data for it. Read statically, a MJOLNIR match runs with the
   options' mode byte 3 (multiplayer) and 60 ticks a second, and the fireteam
   runs Reach's distributed simulation over the exe's Party transport: the
   host is DistributedServer (5) and runs every trigger; a client is
   DistributedClient (4), runs only the variant's `local` trigger and receives
   everything else.
3. **The sim knows every team exactly and paints team colours. Unreal never
   sees them.** A flag's owner team (`MP+0x19`) and a player's team (`P+0xad`)
   are exact and replicate to clients. The sim computes change colours from
   them, but the per-frame snapshot it pushes to Unreal carries no owner team
   and no colour. It carries the model variant, the region permutations and
   the unit team bytes. Both colour bugs come from Lua guessing what the
   snapshot does not say.
4. **CTF flags** are coloured by a guess keyed to the actor, not the sim object:
   nearest stand, then the last incident of either flag, then red. Eleven paths
   pick the wrong team. The deterministic fix is a second flag tag whose
   default model variant is `blue`, read in Lua through `GetVariantName()`. It
   needs no native code.
5. **Custom armour** is a Blam model variant. Every armour except Mk V Classic
   is a body plus 11 to 17 static armour plates and a static helmet. MJOLNIR
   tints only skeletal meshes, so the plates and helmet keep the player's own
   colours over a red or blue body. Timing paths add misses. The fix makes the
   sim choose Mk V Classic for every Spartan in team games (a hook on sim
   `0x2f2730`, on every machine), then tints on the game's own
   `OnRegionsChanged` events.
6. **Other modes.** Team Slayer is a script and nothing else. After it come
   the modes that need a player colour channel (Juggernaut, Infection), then
   carried objects and zones (Headhunter, Oddball, KOTH), then modes whose
   placements must be authored per map (Territories, Stockpile, Assault), then
   Race. The common blockers are a 20-entry object type list, a HUD channel
   for Megalo widgets, objective text and waypoint icons (none reaches Unreal),
   boundary drawing, and MJOLNIR ending every match at the first round.
7. **Proof.** The codec round-trips 417 of 417 of Bungie's Megalo variants bit
   for bit. `mjolnir megalo dump` lists any variant. A local remap would let
   Bungie's own modes run as an oracle on this PC. CU4 enforces almost no
   limits on a variant, so a validator must, before any hub upload. Every mode
   is then checked on two PCs, by the user, before release.

---

## 1. What runs today

### 1.1 The path of a game type

| Step | Where | What | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encode | `crates/blam-megalo` (`variant.rs`, `script.rs`, `ctf.rs`, `powerups.rs`); `mjolnir megalo write --mode empty\|slayer\|tick\|ctf` (`crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs:40-50`, `211-250`) | builds the bitstream; Slayer and CTF get a time-limit trigger, and every mode but empty and tick gets CE health packs unless `--no-health-packs` | Verified |
| Release | `.github/workflows/release-mods.yml` | writes `slayer`, `team_slayer`, `ctf`, `koth` and `oddball` `.mglo` files in `variants/` with `--vehicle-label-pool`; zipped into the signed MJOLNIRLevelLoader | Verified |
| A map's modes | `tools/level/gen_ce_level.py` | `["slayer"]`, plus `"ctf"` when the CE scenario has flags, plus `"koth"` and `"oddball"` from its markers (section 3.4) | Verified |
| Menu | `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/main.lua:61-67` (`MODES`), `118-128` (`modesFor`) | five names (slayer, team_slayer, koth, oddball, ctf); a mode is offered only if the map lists it and `variants/<id>.mglo` exists, so only Slayer and CTF appear | Verified |
| Host's choice to its loader | Lobby `main.lua:181-186` writes `pending_variant.txt`; `mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua:6031-6043` reads it once in the `SetAndBeginCampaign` hook | | Verified |
| Host's choice to clients | the travel URL's insertion point index; loader `GAME_TYPE_SLOTS` (`main.lua:5919`: 0 slayer, 1 ctf, 2 team_slayer, 3 koth, 4 oddball, 5 forge); FIND GAMES joins through `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/games.lua:169, 221` | an id missing from the table falls back to the level's own variant (slayer) on clients | Verified |
| Stage | `native/map_registry/mjolnir_map_registry.c`: seven byte patches (table at `1197-1236`); `mjolnir_megalo_variant` (`1324`) copies `native\variant.mglo` to `HotReload\mjolnir.mglo` and writes `"mjolnir"` to the sim's name buffer (`RVA_MGLO_NAME` 0x152a7c0, line 1279) | | Verified |
| Load | sim round reset `0x2ad560` reads `<name>.mglo`, decodes it through variant vtable slot 5 (sim `0x392a40`), validates it (sim `0x40a310`) and clears the name; there is no simulation-type gate, so every machine loads its own file | | Verified |
| Settings | `mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/variant_settings.lua` patches base-option bits in the staged copy; `mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/variant.lua` reads the score to win and time limit | both stop at user options, script traits or a compressed string table, so any Reach-authored variant breaks them | Verified |

The patch table quotes the start of each patched instruction (`0xf6db`,
`0x55af56`, `0x45b1a3`); `re/megalo_engine.md` quotes the changed byte
(`0xf6dd`, `0x55af5a`, `0x45b1a7`). They are the same three patches.

Game type identity is repeated in at least 13 places (Lobby `MODES`,
`games.lua`, `GAME_TYPE_SLOTS`, `TEAM_GAMES`, `START_EVENTS`,
`vehicle_sets.lua`, the HUD scoreboard and settings tables, `level.rs`,
`gen_ce_level.py`, the hub kit and three hub pages). A new type needs edits in
Lua, Rust, Python and the hub. Verified (repository audit, 2026-10-21).

### 1.2 How the sim runs a MJOLNIR match

| Fact | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Engine index 2 (Megalo) at `G+0x846c`; Megalo vtable sim `0x85dae8`, 114 slots | `current_game_engine()` sim `0x180e70`, table sim `0xbd5210` | Verified |
| The options' mode byte `GG+0x10` is **3** (1 campaign, 2 Firefight, 3 multiplayer) | sim `0xf650` sets pending mode 3 for engines 1 and 2; `0x2060f0` turns it into a session mode; the options builder `0x55e1c0` writes 1 for session mode 1, 2 for session mode 6 and 3 for any other; `0x2069e0` installs the options. The incident filter `0x406cf0` maps modes 1/2/3 to the tag flags campaign, firefight, multiplayer | Verified; one link (the session value `0x55e1c0` reads is the one `0x4c1e10` stored) inferred; live read pending |
| Tick rate **60** | options `+6` defaults to 0x3c (sim `0x208a70`, store at `0x208ab9`), is validated 1..300 (`0x208cb0`) and copied to `[TLS+0x98]+6` at map init (`0x20ff70`). The only immediate 30 or 60 store to such a field is that one. Matches the "about 60 a second" score rise in `re/megalo_engine.md` | Verified statically |
| Simulation type `GG+0x11`: host **5** DistributedServer, client **4** DistributedClient | `0x55e1c0` derives it from the session parameter `simulation-protocol` and "local peer is host": protocol 2 gives 5 or 4. Its only launch-time writer `0x4c1f20` asks engine slot 99, which is `0x47d60` (`mov eax, 2`) in all four engines. A session class `session+0x28` of 1 would force protocol 0 | Chain verified; live read pending |
| The sim's own network protocol is live | sim send `0x532d40` and receive `0x4c7350` go through the transport at `+0x28`, which sim `0x4c2d80` takes from host vtable `+0x150` = exe `0x7ba1930` = the exe's Party transport (`launcher+0x190`). `fireteam.log` shows a sim session with two peers, state 6, mode 3 | Verified |
| Who runs which trigger | per tick: engine update `0x2b1170` -> slot 29 `0x3fdad0` -> slot 113 `0x3fe520`. The host runs every trigger whose attribute is 0 (normal) or 6 (local); a type-4 client runs only the `local` entry point (`v+0xe5f8`). Slot 10 `0x3fd740` runs `init` on the host only and `local init` everywhere; slot 8 `0x3fd550` runs `pregame` at a new map; slot 64 `0x3fe6a0` runs `object death` on the host | Verified |
| Round and game end | `0x2b1170` ends the round when a player (reason 6) or team (5) reaches the score to win; `0x2afa70` turns it into game over on the round count (7), early victory (8, 9) or round 0x3ff (10); `0x2aea40` ends it when too few players or teams remain (0, 2); a team-mask mismatch ends the game outright (13). The round timer only raises warning incidents (`0x2b0f60`): a script must end a round on time | Verified |
| Scores | `G+0x32c0`: player i at `+i*8`, team t at `+0x80+t*8`, each {i16, i16, i16 rounds won}. Replicated to clients by the `game-engine-statborg` entity (apply `0x577520`) | Verified; which of `+0`/`+2` is round or game score inferred |
| Teams | `P+0xad` is the team index (0..7), written only by `0x1823c0` from configuration byte `+0x88`. The host's session membership assigns it (`0x4bab20`): a client's desired team if valid, else the smaller team, two teams seeded; in free-for-all the player's slot index. Megalo reasons with the designator `G+0x1c[P+0xad]` (slot 53 `0x3fee90`); MJOLNIR writes designator = index. `P+0xac` is 0xff in mode 3 | Verified |
| Team score | `team_scoring` (`o+0x734`) through `0x2b0180` -> slot 2 `0x3ef690`: 0 sum, 1 minimum, 2 maximum, 3 none (scripts only); MJOLNIR writes 0 | Verified; names from ReachVariantTool |
| The variant reaches clients twice | the session parameter `game-variant` (`session+0x6340`, sent in 0x200-byte chunks) carries the host's variant and every peer's `0x55e1c0` copies it at game start; then each machine's round reset replaces it with its own staged file | Verified; publish-versus-file ordering open |
| Per-tick Megalo state | global, player and team variables and the HUD widgets travel in three replicated entities whose decoders (`0x56fbc0`, `0x573100`, `0x576e70`) walk the **receiving** machine's own declarations and network priorities. There is no identity check: every machine must hold identical declarations, priorities and widget count | Verified |
| Incidents | Megalo's submit (`0x41df50`) refuses string ids in `[0x67ffff, 0xd00070]`, so a script cannot raise engine incidents such as `recharge_health` (hence the borrowed `lap_complete` in `powerups.rs`). Clients receive only incidents addressed to their players (`0x2f6390`); no CU4 incident definition sets "never network" | Verified |

### 1.3 Slayer

`Variant::slayer` (`crates/blam-megalo/src/variant.rs:558-632`): for each
player, if they died a kill death this tick (killer-type bit 2: the death
record observer, slot 62 at sim `0x3fea10`, writes death type 2 for a kill, 1
for a suicide, 3 for a betrayal and 4 for a quit; verified), fetch the killer and, unless it is the player, add 1 to the killer's score; for
each player, end the round at the score to win. A suicide takes a point from the player, as in CE. The CLI adds the time-limit

### 2.2 CTF flags change colour

**How it works today.** The flag is a weapon tag cloned from the assault bomb,
drawn by the oddball's `BP_SkullActor` (`tools/level/build_ctf_flag.sh:50-55`),
object type list entry 18 (`81-87`). The loader hides the skull and attaches
CE's flag mesh in a team's materials. The team of each new actor is guessed
(`mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua:1976-2009`): the nearest stand
within `FLAG_AT_STAND_CM` (400 cm, line 1902) unless that team's flag is
believed home; otherwise wait up to 15 x 100 ms for any newer flag incident
and take its team; otherwise the nearest stand's team at any distance;
otherwise red. The first-person flag takes the local player's last grab, then
the last flag incident, then red (`2023-2034`).

The script side is right. The flag's owner team and `TEAM_INDEX` come from the
stand's owner team (`ctf.rs:368-371`, `311-327`), and Megalo's team write has
no "team present" check (sim `0x41c8b0` -> `0x41fd80` case 5 -> `0x4089b0` ->
`0x66af70`). Bungie's CTF also sets a flag's owner team once, when it creates
or adopts the flag, not every tick. Verified.

**The fix.** Make each flag's team a property of its tag, which the sim
publishes to Unreal as the model variant name. No native code.

Tags (`tools/level/build_ctf_flag.sh`):

1. Keep `objects\weapons\multiplayer\flag\flag` as the red flag, entry 18. Its
   `default model variant` is empty, which the sim resolves to variant index 0,
   `default`, and publishes by name (sim `0x5a7d90`, `0x5b3190`), so
   `GetVariantName()` should already read `default` today. Verified chain; the
   in-game read below confirms it. Setting the field to `default` explicitly is
   cheap insurance.
2. Add `objects\weapons\multiplayer\flag\flag_blue`: the same recipe plus
   `default model variant = blue`, in its own container
   (`pakchunk990-MJOLNIRFLAGB`). The assault bomb model already has variants
   `default` and `blue`. Verified.
3. Add object type list entry 20 = `flag_blue`. Check that `pack --duplicate`
   appends, as the script already assumes.
4. Ship the variant, the type list override and the blue container together.
   The new variant sets bit 20 of its object types; if the installed list has
   no entry 20, validation (`0x409c40` -> `0x40a310`) wipes the whole script and
   there is no CTF at all. Verified.

Why two tags and not one tag plus a variant name at creation: the Megalo
string-id table (57 entries) has no `red` or `blue`, and an object's model
variant travels only in its creation data, so a variant set after creation
never reaches clients (sim `0x503140`, `0x508a10`, `0x504ea0`). A tag's default
reaches every machine with the tag index, and `0x5a7d90` maps an empty or
unknown name back to the tag default. Verified; which variant id a client's
replicated creation passes is unread, and the tag default covers both answers.

Megalo (`crates/blam-megalo/src/ctf.rs`, `crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs`):

1. `Ctf` gains `blue_flag_type` (CLI `--blue-flag-type`, default 20);
   `object_types` becomes the red and blue types.
2. The stand trigger clears `NEW_FLAG`, then calls three subroutines: create
   the red type when the stand's owner team is 0; create the blue type and set
   `TEAM_INDEX` = 1 when it is 1; and, when `NEW_FLAG` is set, link, copy the
   owner team, set pickup, priority and waypoint. Each branch is its own
   subroutine because a trigger stops at its first failed condition (sim

3. While there: give `flag_dropped` the last carrier as its cause, use Reach's
   flag icon value, score the carrier as a player (the team follows by sum),
   and default the tick rate to 60.
4. Update the fingerprint and range tests (`ctf.rs:425-458`).

Lua (`mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua`):

1. A flag's team is `actor.BlamMeshSynchronization:GetVariantName()`: `blue`
   is blue, anything else non-empty is red. While it reads empty, retry every
   100 ms for about 2 s, then log the actor and leave it undressed rather than
   guess.
2. Log and cross-check `BlamObjectSynchronization.BlamTagDefinitionIndex`,
   which differs between the two types.
3. Pin a flag to its stand only when it has no attach parent and lies within
   about 150 cm of the stand of **its own** team.
4. First person: the enemy of the local pawn's team, because pickup is
   enemies-only. The pawn's team comes from `pawn:GetBlamObjectActor()` (exe
   `0x7b0b0a0`) and its `BlamGameTeam` multiplayer half. Retry while it is
   empty; never default.
5. Remove `flagSerial`, the serial capture, the wait, and `lastFlagTeam`,
   `carriedTeam` and every `"red"` default from colour decisions. Incident
   values stay for the announcer and HUD.
6. The sweep re-reads each flag's team and repairs a mismatch. Key actors by

A replacement path for later, generic: read `MP+0x19` of the actor's
`BlamObjectIndex` in the sim. The owner team replicates to clients, so it gives
the same answer on every machine; it needs a cross-thread read through the sim
thread's TLS. Keep it for objects whose team changes during play (a KOTH hill,
an Oddball ball, an Assault bomb, a territory), which the model-variant route
cannot follow after creation.

Side note: `VariantName` does not change meshes, the permutation pairs do
(exe `0x7a20850` rebuilds only on a pair change). The flag's visible mesh is

**What MJOLNIR does** (`main.lua:2549-2711`). In a team game (`TEAM_GAMES`,
`2556`: ctf and team_slayer) it swaps every component of class
`BPC_SkeletalMesh_C` or `BPC_TranslucentSkeletalMesh_C` to Mk V Classic
(`BIPED_ROLES`, `2596`) and gives it a dynamic material with `Armor Color` red
or blue (layer parameter 0; the comment at `2561` calls it global). The team is
the `EBlamMultiplayerTeam` half of `GetGameTeamString()` (`bipedTeam`, `2581`).
Triggers: the class watch plus 300 and 2000 ms; `retintSoon` at 300, 1500 and
4000 ms after `player_spawn` or `respawn_final_tick` (`2382-2384`,
`2699-2709`); the CTF sweep every ~3 s on levels with a `ctf` block. First
person takes the team of the Spartan nearest the camera (`2683-2697`).

**Root causes, ranked by evidence:**

| # | Cause | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The plates and helmet are static meshes MJOLNIR never touches.** `dressMeshes` enumerates `SkeletalMeshComponent` only (`2617-2618`). Every armour but Mk V Classic keeps its plates and helmet, in its own coating, over the tinted Mk V body. This is why custom armour never reads as red or blue while Mk V Classic players look right | cooked `RuntimeRegions`; `main.lua` | Verified (data and code); on-screen look inferred |
| 2 | Roles are keyed by component class: Lone Wolf and Spartan get two Mk V bodies (body and cloth both swapped), MkIV keeps its thighs | same | Verified; look inferred |
| 3 | A late asynchronous apply puts the player's own body mesh back on the swapped component, leaving the Mk V material on a foreign mesh; a remote player's appearance arriving on a client re-triggers it | exe `0x7a21080`, `0x7a26040`; sim `0x1823c0` | Mechanism verified; timing inferred |
| 4 | Trigger timing: the class watch fires when the pool builds an actor, often before it has a team (`tintBiped` gives up without one, `2646-2652`), not when a pooled actor is reused. On a client, other players' spawns raise no re-tint (`player_spawn` is not relayed, `2427`; their `respawn_final_tick` is personal and dropped, `2377`). The client's own spawn does re-tint, and CTF levels re-tint every 3 s, so the gap is remote spawns on levels without a `ctf` block | `main.lua` | Verified code; frequency inferred |
| 5 | First person takes the nearest biped's team: wrong in melee, vehicles and deaths | `2683-2697` | Verified code |
| - | **Not a cause:** the team value. The multiplayer half of the team component is `P+0xad` on every machine, refreshed with each update. Do not switch to `ActorTeamIs*` or the allegiance half (0xff). Past the second seat a client's `P+0xad` could be the seat number until MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.2 (section 2.1) | section 2.1 | Verified |

**The fix.**

A. **The sim chooses Mk V Classic for everyone in team games** (native, in
`mjolnir_map_registry.dll`). Hook sim `0x2f2730` after the call: when team
armour is on and the object is the Spartans biped, return `og_001`'s string id
(read once from the Spartans entry's first selection). Every player, with or
without a choice, then takes `0x182ef0`'s early return with `og_001` and no
legacy overrides, at spawn (`0x189e90`) and on every configuration update
(`0x1823c0`). Weapon skins (entries 1 to 7) pass through. Constraints:

- Install it on **every** machine. Every sim re-evaluates every player's
  variant on each configuration update, and a variant the host changes after
  creation does not replicate through the base object update (section 2.2;
  the biped-specific decoder was not read), so a host-only hook would be
  undone on clients. Verified chain; on-screen result inferred.
- It answers only while sim `DAT_1813762f4 == 2` (a map is loaded, checked by
  `0x2f2870`). Verified.
- Byte-checked like the existing patch table, but installed once and never
  removed: the simulation thread may be inside the call, and restoring code
  under a running Megalo game froze clients before (2026-10-02). "Off" only
  clears the flag the hook reads.

The mesh sync then loads the Mk V body with no plates and no helmet, first
person included, and nothing fights the tint any more.

B. **Tint on the game's own events** (Blueprint hooks, each fired once per
spawn or apply):

- `BP_SpartansBipedActor_C:BP_OnGameplayStart`: an actor now represents a
  biped; record it by full name and tint on the next tick and ~0.5 s later.
- The biped's `OnRegionsChanged` handler
  (`BndEvt__BP_EliteBipedActor_BlamMeshSynchronization_K2Node_ComponentBoundEvent_4_OnRegionsChanged__DelegateSignature`),
  which runs after every mesh apply: tint now.
- `BP_MeteoritePawn`'s arms and legs `OnRegionsChanged` handlers, for first
  person, with the team from `pawn:GetBlamObjectActor()`.
- Tint only components whose first material is `MI_Spartans_MkV_Classic` or an
  MJOLNIR instance. A check every 1-2 s over the recorded actors repairs pool
  reuse with no mesh event. The fixed timers and the nearest-biped rule go.

Within the project's rules: the loader's `main.lua` is at the 200-local limit,
so the block moves to its own module; no `FindAllOf` or `StaticFindObject` in
loops; actors keyed by full name; only Blueprint functions hooked.

C. **Interim, Lua only:** on the same hooks, also hide every
`BPC_StaticMesh_C`, `BPC_FP_StaticMesh_C` and `BPC_PAWN_StaticMesh_C`, swap
only the body (hide the cloth and the thighs), and redo it on each
`OnRegionsChanged`. The game still loads and briefly shows the player's own
armour after each apply.

D. **Fully native, later** (it also gives Infection and Juggernaut a player
colour channel): the Spartans model already has 18 unused `og_<colour>` body
permutations (`og_red`, `og_blue`, and the rest of CE's palette). Add `og_red`
and `og_blue` keys, with Mk V meshes and coloured material overrides, to the
body `RuntimeRegions` of `BP_SpartansBipedActor` and the arms and legs of
`BP_MeteoritePawn`, and have the sim select them by team through placement
override pairs (`0x2f2990` -> `0x5a7e60`). The keys must exist first: a
permutation missing from `RuntimeRegions` empties the region, so the body
would vanish (exe `0x7a20850`, `0x7a21080`, `0x7a26040`). Verified. Cost:
cooked overrides of two large Blueprints.

**Built (2026-10-22, branch `work/reach-game-mode-support-2eca91`, untested
in game).**

- A (native): `native/map_registry/mjolnir_map_registry.c`, exports
  `mjolnir_team_armor_on` and `_off`. The aligned qword at sim `0x182f08`
  (`f8 e8 22 f8 16 00 8b d8`, the call of `0x2f2730` at `0x182f09`) is
  checked and rewritten in one locked 8-byte write, so the call goes to a
  12-byte `mov rax, imm64; jmp rax` stub allocated within 1.75 GB below
  the simulation, and from there to `team_armor_pick` in the DLL. With
  forcing on, that asks the original for a made-up appearance whose only
  pair is (0, 0): `0x2f2730` matches the definition against the
  customization entries before it reads a pair, so only the Spartans biped
  (entry 0, selection 0 `og_001`) gets an answer; anything else is asked
  again with its real appearance. `0x2f2730` reads only RCX (+0x19, +5+2i,
  +6+2i) and EDX, and `0x182ef0` reads only EAX after the call (verified in
  the disassembly, and the built wrapper's code was read back with
  `dumpbin /disasm`). It never logs per call, only once when it first
  forces. A build with other bytes is refused and logged; the Megalo switch
  is unaffected either way.
- B (Lua, `teams.lua`): hooks `BP_SpartansBipedActor_C:BP_OnGameplayStart`
  (the Blueprint implements it with its own bytecode), the Spartan's
  `OnRegionsChanged` handler and `BP_MeteoritePawn`'s arms and legs
  handlers. Each event records the actor and tints on the next pass: a body
  that is not Mk V Classic (the hook missing or refused) is swapped, and its
  plates, helmet, cloth and extra parts are hidden; then `Armor Color` is set
  on an MJOLNIR instance of the Mk V material. A pass every 1.5 s repairs
  recorded actors by full name. The loader switches the hook on for `ctf`
  and `team_slayer` and off for anything else; with an older DLL it logs
  once and the Lua swap does the work.

**Checks in game before release (the user):**

1. Two PCs, team game, one player in a coating (Blue_001) and one in Chief
   default: screenshots in third and first person, before the change (cause 1).
2. Log the full name in a `BP_OnGameplayStart` hook across respawns (pool
   reuse) and the time of each `OnRegionsChanged` against the old timers
   (causes 3 and 4).
3. With the hook on both PCs: the coated player and the default player both
   spawn in Mk V with no plates or helmet, in third and first person, on host
   and client, after respawns and after a player joins mid-match.
4. On a Team Slayer map (no `ctf` block): remote players' colours after their
   respawns, on the client.
5. Optional: whether the `Color` parameter of `MI_Chief_Armor` (layer index 2)

### 3.4 King and Oddball on converted CE maps

Built 2026-11-04. The mode list comes from each map's own markers: a map offers
`koth` when it has a `HillFlag` polygon and `oddball` when it has an
`OddballSpawn` (`tools/level/ce_objectives.py`, called by `gen_ce_level.py`;
run on a level file, it upgrades a map already converted). Of the 48 converted
maps counted, 46 offer both, with 4 to 14 hills. Nightfall has one stray
`HillFlag` and no ball spawn, and TST authors its own (`prepare_runtime.py`).

- **A hill is a polygon.** Its corners are the `HillFlag`s sharing a team index,
  and that index is the hill's number. The simulation's boundaries are simple
  shapes, so each hill is a cylinder of the polygon's area around its centroid,
  from its lowest corner to 1.5 world units over its highest. A player in a
  sharp corner of a long polygon is outside the cylinder. Fitted radii run from
  1.9 m to 78 m, median 6.4 m (Coldsnap's hills are the wide ones).
- **One `koth.mglo` serves every map.** A label per hill would pass the
  simulation's 16 filters, so every hill has the label `koth_hill` and the
  script reads its place in the rotation from `object.spawn_sequence` (Number
  kind 6, new in the typed builder), counting the hills as it walks the label.
  `--hills` is gone.
- **Markers are owned by a team nobody plays.** The spawn search `0x2f84e0`
  takes any scenery with a multiplayer block whose owner team is the player's
  or neutral. It has no type test: MP type 15 only marks a valid first spawn in
  `0x2f77a0`. Neutral markers took 5 of 13 respawns on Prisoner. With owner team
  `eighth party` (7), 0 of 23 landed on one, and the label loop and the boundary
  test do not look at the team. **Health pack spots had the same bug** on every
  released map: 17 of 23 respawns cycled through three of them. They take the
  same team now. On a rebaked Prisoner, 0 of 24 respawns in Slayer and 0 of 24
  in CTF landed on a spot, the five packs appear, and a pack is consumed when
  a hurt player stands on it (`lap_complete`, health 100%) and returns after
  30 s. CTF's flag stands took none of those 24 either, for the red team; a
  blue player was not tried. Stands keep their team, which the script reads.
- **The staging guard has to know the operand.** `mjolnir_map_registry.dll`
  links `blam-megalo`'s reader and refused the first `koth.mglo` ("failed
  variant validation"), and the default variant ran with the HUD still reading
  "to win 120". **So `koth.mglo` needs a registry DLL built from this code, in
  the same mods release.** Check `map_registry.log` before reading any result.
- **Telling where the hill is.** No waypoint or boundary reaches Unreal (B4,
  B5). The variant raises `hill_moved` with the hill's place as its value, the
  level file lists `koth_hills`, and `mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/hill.lua` draws one
  line under the score: "HILL 12 M LEFT ABOVE", "ON THE HILL". The HUD's relay
  carries `hill_moved` to clients, untested on two PCs; a player joining mid-match
  shows hill 1 until the next spawn, when `checkpoint_reached` resends the live hill. MJOLNIRHud draws the boundary in the world.
- **Oddball's ball** is the flag tag (type 18) drawn as the skull, always made at
  the first spawn the label loop reaches: other spawns are unused. There is no
  marker for a loose or carried ball, so a player finds it by eye.
