notes.title: Multiplayer HUD: kill feed, respawn countdown, scoreboard
notes.summary: mods/MJOLNIRHud draws the HUD for the classic CE maps that MJOLNIRLevelLoader runs under the simulation's Megalo engine. It uses MJOLNIR's own cooked widgets (custom_ui.md):
notes.body:
`mods/MJOLNIRHud` draws the HUD for the classic CE maps that
MJOLNIRLevelLoader runs under the simulation's Megalo engine. It uses
MJOLNIR's own cooked widgets ([custom_ui.md](custom_ui.md)):

- **`WBP_MJOLNIRKillFeed`**: the kill feed at the bottom left, the medal
  callout and the respawn countdown in the middle, and the score bars at the
  top (see [The kill feed](#the-kill-feed) below). The score bars sit above
  the native shield bar: Red/Blue for team modes, or YOU/LEADER for
  free-for-all, each filling toward the score to win, with the round clock
  between them. The local team is marked `/ YOU`. Opening the full
  scoreboard hides the bars until Tab/View is released.
- **`WBP_MJOLNIRScoreboard`**: shown while **Tab** (or the gamepad's View
  button) is held. It has the game type and map, the score to win (or the
  team scores in CTF and Team Slayer), and up to 16 players with score, kills
  and deaths. Team games have separate Red and Blue sections, with team
  totals and player counts; players without a reported team appear under
  Awaiting assignment. Each section is sorted by score. A gold YOU marker
  identifies the local player in addition to the row highlight.

- **`WBP_MJOLNIRChat`**: match chat, above the kill feed (see
  [Chat](#chat) below).

The console opens on `~` only. `MJOLNIRConsoleEnabler` takes Tab out of
`InputSettings.ConsoleKeys`, as Halo CE on PC had it.

## Slash commands

`Scripts/commands.lua`. A chat line starting with `/` is a command: it is
never relayed or recorded. Typing `/` lists the commands you may use under
the box; **Tab** completes the highlighted one, then a player's name, and
again for the next match.

| Command | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| `/help` | everyone | the list, here |
| `/players` | everyone | who is in the match |
| `/bench` | everyone | time this map with and without its foliage (about a minute, camera held) and send it to the hub for the MJOLNIR team ([performance.md](performance.md)); needs the launcher signed in; runs on the player's own machine |
| `/sounds` (`/mixer`) | everyone | open the sound mixer over the match: a slider for each of the map's sounds, kept for that map on the player's own PC ([sound_mixer.md](sound_mixer.md)); runs on the player's own machine |
| `/suicide` (`/respawn`) | everyone | kill your player, to respawn when stuck |
| `/kick <player>` | host | MJOLNIRLobby's kick |
| `/ban <player>` | host | kick, and keep them out (`bans.json`) |
| `/unban <name>` | host | |
| `/slay <player>` | host | kill a player |
| `/bots <0-15> [kind] [level]` | host | this match's AI bots: the ones playing stay, more join or the last ones leave; a kind (`spartans`, `elites`, `grunts`, `jackals`, `mixed`) or a level (`normal`, `heroic`, `legendary`) brings new bots of it instead; alone, how many ([bots.md](bots.md)) |
| `/public` | host | list this match in FIND GAMES, so anyone can join it now; not in FORGE |
| `/private` | host | take this match out of FIND GAMES; everyone in it stays, nobody new can join |
| `/tp <player>` | host | teleport to a player (experimental) |
| `/bring <player>` | host | teleport a player to you (experimental) |

- **The host runs every command.** A client sends `MJOLNIR|cmd|<line>` over
  `ServerExecRPC`; the host takes the sender from the RPC's controller and
  answers them alone with a system line. Host commands run only from the
  host's own box: a client's `/kick` is refused whatever it says. A client's
  `/suicide` needs a seat that is really theirs (index not the host's, and
  the controller's `BlamAbsolutePlayerIndex` agreeing): a joiner reads the
  host's index 0 for a few seconds after joining.
- **A player** is named by hub name or in-game name: exact first, then the
  only one it starts, then the only one it is in.
- **Kick, ban, unban** call MJOLNIRLobby's `mjolnir_auto kick|ban|unban`
  through the console. The Lobby takes an exact name before a partial one.
- **Public, private** call MJOLNIRLobby's `mjolnir_auto public on|off`, the
  HOST MENU's MAKE PUBLIC / MAKE PRIVATE. They say nothing themselves: the
  Lobby writes each listing status to `MJOLNIRLobby\chat_notice.txt` while a
  match runs (`<unix time>\t<line>` a line), and the host's chat shows each
  line under 30 s old as a system line.
- **Kill and teleport** are Blam script, sent through MJOLNIRBlamConsole's
  mailbox (`native\request.txt`, ids from 7000000, one line a poll):
  `(unit_kill (player_get <index>))`; a teleport is `objects_attach` then
  `objects_detach` a poll later, so the child is left where its parent
  stands. `/suicide` was verified on a host on 2026-10-17. That
  `player_get <n>` is the player with absolute index `n` is proven only for
  the host's own seat; the two-PC test must check it before `/slay` or a
  teleport is trusted.
- Six suggestions show at a time (the host has ten commands); typing more
  narrows them.

## Chat

`Scripts/chat.lua`. **T** opens all chat, **Y** team chat (all chat in free
for all), **Home** all chat. **Enter** sends, **Esc** cancels. The first
time, the box shows the chat rules instead (chat is recorded, public matches
post their chat, keep it civil): I AGREE or Enter opens chat and is
remembered in `chat_rules.txt` beside the mod; NOT NOW or Esc leaves it
shut. A new version of the rules asks again. Lines show for
nine seconds, then fade; while the box is open the last ten show on a dark
panel. A line is at most 160 bytes. Each line shows the sender's hub avatar,
round, as the feed and the scoreboard do; MJOLNIRLobby may cache the
picture after the line arrives, so a row asks for it again once a second
for its first 15 seconds.

- **Typing does not move the player.** The Blam simulation takes its keys
  from the game viewport, and a key the text box does not use (W, Space, G)
  bubbles up to it from the focused box. While the box is open the chat sets
  UI-only input (`WidgetBlueprintLibrary:SetInputMode_UIOnlyEx`, the box
  focused, held keys flushed), which makes the viewport ignore input as the
  Unreal console does while it is open; closing sets game-only input again.
  Two things that do not stop it (tried 2026-10-17 on a real keyboard):
  `BlamInputProcessorLocalPlayerSubsystem:SetUIActive`, which the pause menu
  sets (the pause menu freezes the player by pausing the game), and emptying
  GameInput's keyboard readings, which the game never asks for.
- **The game's own chat** (`WBP_HUD_Main.ChatWidget`, `IA_OpenChat` on Home)
  is PlayFab party chat, which never connects in games joined by connection
  string. It draws nothing.
- **The wire.** A client sends `MJOLNIR|say|<a|t>|<text>` over
  `ServerExecRPC`. The host names the sender from the controller the RPC came
  in on, never from the text, and sends
  `MJOLNIR|chat|<a|t>|<Red|Blue|->|<index>|<name>|<text>` to every player, or
  only to the sender's team for team chat. The host allows five lines in six
  seconds from one sender, and tells a flooder to slow down.
- **The record.** The host keeps every line it relays, with the sender's
  in-game name, the hub account MJOLNIRLobby resolved for it, team and
  channel. It writes `chat_<match id>.json` beside the mod every few seconds,
  and at the end of the match names it in `match_outbox.txt`. MJOLNIRLobby
  sends it to `POST /matches/chat`. Private matches are recorded too, because
  a player report cites the match id whether the game was listed or not.
  A public match's chat shows on its match page on the hub
  (`GET /matches/{id}`), as the chat rules tell players. Otherwise only
  moderators read it, beside each report on `/moderation`
  (`GET /moderation/match-chat/{host_match_id}`).

## The kill feed

Every line is a row: a coloured bar at its left edge, then the killer, the
weapon, what made the kill special, and the victim. Event lines have a glyph,
a name, and what happened.

```text
| Noble Six  [assault rifle]  Kat
| (o) devnull  [sniper rifle] (+)  Jorge       <- gold rim: names you; (o) avatar
| (>>) devnull  Double Kill
| (+) Emile  joined the game
```

- **Weapons** are the game's own silhouettes, the ones its weapon cradle
  shows (`/Game/UI/Hud/WeaponCradle/Textures/T_UI_*_WeaponIcon`, grenades in
  `GrenadeCradle`). They are channel-packed masks, so they are drawn through
  the game's own icon material: a dynamic instance of
  `MI_HUDCradleIcon_FragGrenade` with the mask as `InputTexture`, `Empty` 0
  and `Equipped` 1, which gives the HUD's cyan. They are mirrored (render
  scale -1) to face the victim. `Scripts/hudicons.lua` maps every
  `Blam.DamageReporting.Type.*` to one; a type with no silhouette shows one
  of our glyphs (melee, fall, splatter ...) or, failing that, its name.
- **Glyphs** are MJOLNIR's own: white silhouettes drawn by
  `tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py` into `unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/HudIcons`,
  imported by `build_mjolnir_ui.py` as `/Game/MJOLNIR/UI/Icons/T_MJHud_*` and
  cooked into chunk 984 with the widget (a hidden `IconPalette` references
  them). Lua tints them per line: Headshot, Melee, Assassination, Splatter,
  Stuck, Explosion, Fall, Guardians, Telefrag, Skull, Joined, Left, Kicked,
  Flag, Medal, Spree, FirstBlood.
- **Modifiers** (`DamageReportingInfo.Modifier`): a headshot or a stuck
  grenade adds a glyph after the weapon; an assassination replaces the
  weapon with the knife; a splatter adds the splat after the vehicle.
- **Avatars:** a player with a hub account has their avatar beside their
  name, round with a faint rim (`FeedLeadAvatar<i>`, `FeedTailAvatar<i>`):
  the same picture the scoreboard shows, which MJOLNIRLobby caches
  ([player_identity.md](player_identity.md)). Without an account, or before
  the picture is cached, the slot closes up.
- **Colours:** in team games names take their team's colour; in free for all
  the local player is gold and everyone else near white. A line that names
  the local player has a gold rim and flashes warmer as it arrives. A team
  kill says BETRAYAL.
- **Medals:** every multiplayer medal the game raises (100 of them, listed
  in [re/medals.md](re/medals.md)). MJOLNIRLobby's DLL decides which
  incidents are medals, what each is called, which one hides another (a
  sniper headshot hides the plain headshot the game sends with it) and the
  order one kill's medals come in (`native/lobby/medals_core.h`);
  `Scripts/medals.lua` hands it each incident and takes the settled awards
  once a drain, after the kill lines that earned them. Multi-kills, sprees,
  weapon sprees, objective medals and `first_blood` are feed lines for
  everyone. Headshots, melee kills, revenge and the other "how" medals come
  up only in the middle of the earner's own screen, so the feed is not one
  line per kill again. The local player's own come up with their glyph, the
  best three of one burst. On a fireteam client they come from the host: the
  host relays each settled medal after its drain's kill lines (see
  [On fireteam clients](#on-fireteam-clients)), and MJOLNIRLevelLoader's
  sound relay carries the ones that have a sound. Without the DLL's medal
  exports (an older MJOLNIRLobby) there are no medals, and the log says why.
- **Text** uses the game's own fonts, set from Lua over the cooked Roboto:
  Normative Pro for names, Oxanium (the menus' face) for numbers and
  captions.

### Animation

The widget has a pool of seven rows at one anchor. `Scripts/feed.lua` gives
each line a row and stacks them with render translations, newest at the
bottom: a line slides in from the left as it fades in (0.28 s), older lines
rise to make room (0.24 s), and each fades out after six seconds. Past six
on screen, the oldest leaves at once. `Scripts/anim.lua` eases the score bars
to a new score (the fill is a SizeBox width), pops a number that changes,
and brings medals in with a small overshoot.

Every pose is a function of the time alone. The animation runs on a hook of
`BP_MeteoritePlayerController_C:ReceiveTick`, the game's per-frame player
controller tick (as MJOLNIRFlyCam does), and on the 100 ms poll as well. A
host's tick runs once per controller each frame; the hook ignores calls
within 4 ms of the last. The hook is never removed, and is registered again
after a level change collects the hooked function.

### Preview

`mjolnir_feed_demo` (console, in a match) plays a scripted sequence through
the HUD's own drawing with made-up names: kills with several weapons, a
headshot, a melee, a splatter, a stuck grenade, joins, a kick, medals with
their callouts, the score bars moving, and a respawn countdown. Nothing it
shows is counted, and the real scores come back after 14 seconds
(`Scripts/demo.lua`).

## Where the data comes from

The simulation's incidents reach the game state's
`BPC_MeteoriteIncidentHandlerComponent.OnIncident_Event` as a `BlamIncident`:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| `Name` | the incident (see below) |
| `CausePlayerAbsoluteIndex`, `EffectPlayerAbsoluteIndex` | killer and victim; -1 for none |
| `CauseObjectActor`, `EffectObjectActor` | the bipeds |
| `DamageReportingInfo.Modifier` | `EBlamDamageReportingModifier`: Headshot, SilentMelee, CollisionDamage, AttachedDamage, FancyAssassination, ArmorAmplified, ArmorMitigated |
| `DamageReportingInfo.Type` | a gameplay tag naming the weapon: `Blam.DamageReporting.Type.AssaultRifle`, `.FragGrenade`, … (`.Invalid` without damage) |
| `CustomValue` | per incident; `flag_scored` carries the captured flag's team |

A player index becomes a name through the game state's `PlayerArray`. Each
`BlamPlayerState` has a `BlamPlayerStateComponent.BlamAbsolutePlayerIndex`
and `GetPlayerName()`. Use `GameplayStatics.GetPlayerController(…, 0)` for
the local controller: `FindAllOf("PlayerController")` lists the frontend's
leftover controllers first.

## What arrives (Blood Gulch Slayer, 2026-10-01)

Measured with a split-screen second player (`CreatePlayer` at the main menu),
killed by the first.

A kill by player 0 of player 1, one tick, in this order:

```text
first_blood  technician_comm  headshot_kill  headshot_comm
Kill  auto_kill  auto_comm  death
lost_lead (1)  gained_lead (0)
```

Notes on that sequence:

- `Kill` is capitalised, unlike every other incident name.
- Every incident in it carries both players, the modifier and the damage
  type. The medal and commendation incidents (`*_kill`, `*_comm`,
  `first_blood`, the lead changes) are there for a medal display later.
- A grenade that killed both players raised `suicide` + `death` for the
  thrower and `Kill` + `grenade_kill` + `grenades_comm` + `death` for the
  other player.

After a death: `respawn_tick` three times, a second apart, then
`respawn_final_tick` and `player_spawn`. The cause is the respawning
player. The HUD counts the ticks down from 3.

Not seen yet:

- `player_joined`, `player_quit` and `player_booted_player`. They are for
  networked players; the host quitting raised nothing. The HUD has feed lines
  ready for them.
- The `*_comm` incidents carry a `CustomString` not read yet.

## On fireteam clients

The host's incident handler gets every player's incidents; a fireteam
client's gets few of them (two-PC notes disagree on which: one run saw only
the joiner's own spawn, another its respawn ticks). So the host relays what
the feed and the tallies need (`Scripts/relay.lua`): after each drain, one
`ClientMessage` of type `MJOLNIR` to every remote player's controller,

```text
MJOLNIR|feed|kill,2,0,0,1,SniperRifle;death,2,0,0,0,SniperRifle
             name,cause,effect,value,modifier,damage type
```

carrying `Kill`, `suicide`, `death`, `first_blood`, `flag_scored`, the
joins, quits and kicks, and then each medal the drain settled (the DLL has
already hidden the ones another stands for). A message carries 16 at most;
a longer drain sends more than one. A client feeds them
through the same handlers. It takes each incident once: one that also came
from its own handler, or from the level loader's sound relay (which carries
the medals), within 2.5 s and with the same name, cause and effect, is
dropped. Two from the same source are never merged, so a quick respawn
killed twice by the same player counts twice. The host ignores its own
relay, which its `ClientMessage` hook also sees.

The host finds its fireteam's controllers once, three seconds into the match
(`FindAllOf`, ~20 ms), then each new one as it is made
(`NotifyOnNewObject`), never with a scan per message. The round clock's
share uses the same list. The first send of a match logs
`relay: the feed to N player(s)`.

A client running an older HUD ignores `MJOLNIR|feed|` messages; a client
whose host runs an older HUD still gets the loader's medals.

## Scores

Scores live only in the simulation, so the HUD keeps its own tallies from
the incidents, by the rules of the variants MJOLNIR writes
(`crates/blam-megalo`):

- **Slayer:** a point per `Kill` of another player; suicides cost nothing.
- **CTF:** a point to the team per `flag_scored`. The captured flag's team
  arrives as the incident's value, so the point goes to the other team.
- **Team Slayer presentation:** shows kills in the score column and totals
  the observed kill incidents by the killer's reported team. Points stay
  with the team that earned them when a player switches or leaves. The
  Team Slayer variant still needs to be installed to offer this mode.

The team reader accepts only Red and Blue from the simulation's
`BlamGameTeam`. It retries a spawn's biped each second because team
assignment can arrive after the spawn incident, and reads a stored biped
only while that player still controls it (actors are pooled, and a dead
player's old one can carry an enemy). Kill/death actors also refresh known
teams. No player index or roster order implies a team.

A fireteam client could not trust that component before MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.2.
It showed the team in the client's own player record (`P+0xad`), which past
the second player was the slot number: a red player in seat 2 read Green on
both joining copies (test copies, 2026-11-07), so client boards put such
players under AWAITING ASSIGNMENT, or a seat-1 player the balancer put on red
under Blue (#347, #349). Since 0.23.2 the lobby DLL writes the host's team
into each player record on a client every tick, so the component agrees with
the host; the game's own motion tracker compares these components too
([game_modes.md](game_modes.md) 2.1, #350).
The pawn's `BlamGameTeam` has no `GetGameTeamString` at all. So in a
team game the host, whose reads are right, sends each human seat's team
once a second when it changes, and to each player as they arrive
(`Relay.TEAMS`):

```text
MJOLNIR|teams|0R;1B;2R
```

A client takes the host's team for every seat it names over its own reads,
until its match ends. Bot sides already come with the bot roster
(`MJOLNIR|bots|`), and a client drops the roster it heard when its match
ends: kept, the last match's bots came back in the next match's seats with
no side.

The HUD still tallies incidents observed during this session; it cannot
recover earlier scores for a late join. This presentation does not add a
replicated authoritative score reader.

## Building and checking

Install the rebuilt UI chunk and the updated Lobby/Hud Lua scripts together;
the scoreboard now has 19 visual rows (16 players and three possible team
headings). `Scripts/scoreboard.lua` must accompany the HUD's `main.lua`.
See [custom_ui.md](custom_ui.md) for the build and cook commands.

The HUD's glyphs are PNGs in `unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/HudIcons`; change
one in `tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py` (`--sheet preview.png` draws them all
over grey and sky blue), re-run it, then build and cook the UI. The Lua
modules `scoreboard.lua`, `variant.lua`, `buildline.lua`, `matchlog.lua`,
`hubnames.lua`, `feed.lua`, `anim.lua`, `hudicons.lua`, `relay.lua`,
`hitches.lua`, `bench.lua`, `chat.lua`, `commands.lua` and `demo.lua` ship with
`main.lua`. The HUD also adds the console commands `mjolnir_hitches` (the
hitch log) and `mjolnir_bench` ([performance.md](performance.md)).

`tools/tests/test_multiplayer_ui.lua` exercises grouping, a full and uneven
roster, sorting, CTF captures, Team Slayer kills, delayed assignment,
switching teams, leaving, the live score strip (including tied/leaving
leaders), holding/releasing the board, and the kill feed: which silhouette
or glyph each kill shows, the rim, medals after their kill and the callout,
the stacking, the oldest line leaving, the bars, the feed's model on its
own, and the relay to fireteam clients (the wire format, taking an incident
once, a client's feed and tallies from the host's message alone). Run from the root
with Lua 5.4 or Python with lupa:

```powershell
python -c "from lupa import LuaRuntime; LuaRuntime().execute(open('tools/tests/test_multiplayer_ui.lua').read())"
```

## Not done yet

- Split screen: the widgets go on the whole viewport, not on each player's
  half.
- The scoreboard's own fonts (only the feed, callouts, score bars and chat
  use the game's).
- Medal art: medals use the feed's existing glyphs (Medal, Spree,
  Headshot, Melee, Splatter, Stuck ...). The game ships no medal icons.
- Objective medals for killing a carrier (`flagcarrier_kill` and the like)
  need MJOLNIR's variants to raise them (re/medals.md, "Gaps").

## The end of a match

The first `round_over` ends the match (MJOLNIR's variants have 31 rounds).
The scoreboard comes up as the final standings, the results go to
`last_match.txt`, and the host takes the fireteam back to the lobby
([multiplayer_postgame.md](multiplayer_postgame.md)).

notes.summary: A custom game ends with everyone still together: the final standings in the map, then a post-game screen on the menu where the fireteam votes on the next game, and the host starts it. Nobody leaves the fireteam. Status as of 2026-10-02; updated 2026-10-31.
notes.body:
A custom game ends with everyone still together: the final standings in the
map, then a post-game screen on the menu where the fireteam votes on the next
game, and the host starts it. Nobody leaves the fireteam. Status as of
2026-10-02; updated 2026-10-31.

## What the game does on its own, and why we don't use it

- A Megalo variant's `EndRound` (action 21) with rounds left raises
  `round_over` and resets the round in place: everyone respawns on the same
  map with no travel. At the last round it raises `game_over`. About 15 s
  later the host goes back to the menu.
- That return sends every client
  `ClientTravelInternal("/Game/Levels/UI/Frontend/Frontend", TRAVEL_Absolute,
  bSeamless=false)` (two PCs, 2026-10-02). Each client loads its own menu and
  disconnects, and so leaves the fireteam. This is Unreal's "host returns
  to the main menu" behaviour, not an error.
- A *seamless* travel to the frontend keeps the clients:
  `servertravel /Game/Levels/UI/Frontend/Frontend` on the host sends
  `b=2 c=true`, and the client arrives in the client lobby, still connected.
  The host swaps its controller for a `BP_FrontendPlayerController` and can
  start the next game from there as usual.
- Switching straight to the next map from inside a map does not start a game
  under Megalo ([re/megalo_engine.md](re/megalo_engine.md), "Rounds, the end
  of a game, and the next map"). That is why the vote happens on the menu.

So MJOLNIR's variants give a game 31 rounds (`mjolnir megalo write
--rounds`, default 31), and a match is the first round. The game never
reaches `game_over`, and the host ends the match itself.

## The flow

1. **In the map** (MJOLNIRHud): the first `round_over` is the end. Every
   machine freezes its tallies, shows the scoreboard as the final standings
   (winner, game type, map, "RETURNING TO THE LOBBY"), and writes them to
   `MJOLNIRHud\last_match.txt` (`Scoreboard.results`). The round the game
   resets behind the standings does not score. With them go each player's
   medals (a `medals` line after the player's, by the medal's incident name:
   `headshot_kill=4`, `multikill_x2=2` ..., most earned first), their score
   and kills at 48 evenly spaced moments of the match (`series`, `killsat`;
   the HUD samples every five seconds) and how long it ran (`clock`).

   The post-game screen's left side has three pages under the winner
   (`mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/postgame.lua`):

   - **Overview**: the top three as cards (avatar, score, kills, deaths,
     K/D and their five best medals), the local player's medals by name,
     and the match's bests (most kills, best K/D, most medals, fewest
     deaths).
   - **Scoreboard**: every player, as before; a row still opens the report
     panel.
   - **Timeline**: the top four players' scores over the match as lines,
     each ending in its final score, and the kills of every minute as bars
     with the busiest minute in gold.

   A medal is drawn as a disc and a notched rim in its colour with one of
   the feed's glyphs on it, or a numeral for a multi-kill (x2) or a spree
   (5). The art is ours (`tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py`); the game ships no
   medal icons. A medal's title, glyph and class come from MJOLNIRLobby's
   DLL. A UI container from before the pages has no tabs: there the screen
   shows the scoreboard, with the local player's medals as a line of text
   under the winner.
2. **The host** waits 7 s (`FINAL_SECONDS`), then runs the seamless
   `servertravel` to the frontend. A `game_over` (an older 1-round variant)
   makes it travel at once, before the game's own return.
3. **On the menu** (MJOLNIRLobby), the host finds fresh standings (under
   180 s old, not shown yet) and pushes `WBP_MJOLNIRPostGame`. It holds the
   standings and the vote on four options: the same game again, then other
   maps in a random order with the same game type where they have it.
4. **The vote** lasts 20 s. Everyone votes on their own copy of the screen.
   - When it ends, or the host presses START NOW, the most votes win; a tie
     goes to the earlier option. With no votes, the rotation moves on to the
     second option.
   - The host starts the winner through the same calls as START GAME, and
     the fireteam follows into the map.
   - LOBBY, or Back on the host, ends the vote and opens the lobby to pick
     by hand.
   - A chosen game that cannot start (its map is not installed, or its
     world is in no container) does the same, with why on the lobby's
     status line. Before MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0 the vote stayed on STARTING THE
     NEXT GAME with LOBBY disabled (two PCs, 2026-11-07).
   - **A host who leaves the match by hand** gets the lobby, never a vote:
     the pause menu's SAVE AND EXIT (its YES calls
     `BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem.EndCampaign`) or `LeaveGame` from
     script. Standings written before the leave (a leave while the final
     standings are up), or within 30 s after it, belong to the match left
     (`Live.quitEnded`). In the two-PC run a host's `LeaveGame` with a
     joiner in the match opened the vote, which started another match 20 s
     later with nobody voting. A host alone who leaves mid-match writes no
     standings and gets no vote either way.
   - **The joiners of a host who leaves by hand** come along. Between two
     PCs (2026-11-07, both SAVE AND EXIT's `EndCampaign` and `LeaveGame`
     mid-match), the joiner follows the host's travel into its frontend,
     has the host's game state within about 2 s, and stays in its fireteam
     and PlayFab lobby: the host's lobby screen, the joiner's client lobby.
   - **Between test copies on one PC it strands them.** With every copy
     on one account (`tools/remote/instances.mjs`), the joiner lands in a
     frontend with no host's game state: a black screen until the PlayFab
     net driver's `ConnectionTimeout` (120 s; 121.8 s measured), then
     CONNECTION LOST, which leaves the host's lobby and makes the joiner a
     fireteam of its own. Likely because the copies' host listens through
     the `?listen` console command, not the game's `MemberAdded` flow. In a
     test copy only (`MJOLNIR_INSTANCE`; `Live.STRANDED_WATCH`), MJOLNIRLobby
     0.23.1 cuts that short (`Live.stranded`, `Live.watchStranded`):
     - A client that had players and then sits in the frontend with no game
       state, or none with players, for 10 s (`Live.STRANDED_AFTER`;
       `MJOLNIR_STRANDED_AFTER` sets it) cuts the connection's
       `ConnectionTimeout` to 1 s. That is the game's own CONNECTION LOST and
       lobby leave, about 20 s after the host left, then "The host left the
       match." under the game's dialog.
     - The engine's `disconnect` is the fallback. It reaches the menu but
       keeps the joiner in the host's lobby.
     - Not the fireteam's leave: `CanLeaveFireteam` read through the missing
       game state and crashed. It also crashes on a stale view model from
       `FindAllOf`.
     - It stays off on a player's PC, where its one trigger would be a false
       one: a client in the frontend ahead of a slow host's game state. On
       every normal travel seen, on two PCs and on copies, the game state
       came before the next 1.5 s poll.
   - **A client's standings are the host's vote's.** Since MJOLNIRLobby
     0.23.1 a client in the frontend marks them seen. Before, a client back
     on its own menu within 180 s of a match it played (seen on copies,
     after the exit above) opened a post-game vote of its own on it, and the
     vote's cancel put the lobby over the reason it was there.
5. **Joiners** get our lobby instead of the game's CLIENT LOBBY whenever the
   host is in it: the host's map and game type, with START GAME, CHANGE MAP
   and GAME TYPE hidden (and, since they were added, PRIVATE / PUBLIC GAME,
   MAX PLAYERS and GAME SETTINGS). Since mods-v0.20.0, a joiner without the
   host's map, or with another release of it, sees START GAME as DOWNLOAD
   MAP or UPDATE MAP ([live_map_install.md](live_map_install.md)).
6. **A joiner the host starts without** (a map it lacks, or another release
   of it; `starting`, or the host's `kick`) leaves the fireteam, and the
   game itself says only CONNECTION LOST. Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0 the
   joiner's own lobby then opens the map's download screen with why: which
   map and game type, that this PC doesn't have it, and that DOWNLOAD gets
   it without a restart (`Live.leaveFor`, `Live.showNotice`). A kick for
   another reason shows the host's reason. Leaving the fireteam loads the
   frontend again, so since MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.1 the screen waits for that
   fresh frontend (or 12 s) before its 3 s delay; before, a kick from the
   post-game vote, where the joiner already is on the frontend, could put
   the screen up in the world being left, and the joiner saw only the main
   menu (one PC, two copies, 2026-11-07).

The vote, the lobby and their lists offer only maps whose world is in a
container here: MJOLNIRLevelLoader's `mjolnir_worlds_known` answers from the
same index a start's travel resolves its world through, so a maps.json entry
whose containers are gone (a leftover of `mjolnir level bake --install-test`)
is left out and logged, and START GAME on one fails with why.

Each machine shows its own standings. They agree because every machine
counted the same incidents ([multiplayer_hud.md](multiplayer_hud.md)).

## The vote panel

Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.19.0 and the chunk-984 UI container cooked with it
(which ships in the CE runtime pack, 2026-10-31), the options are a
two-by-two grid of tiles, each of them the button you vote with:

- the map's hub screenshot, and over its foot a band with the game type's
  icon (the game type picker's, `T_MJMode_*`), the map, the game type and the
  votes so far;
- a gold bar along the bottom edge, the option's share of the votes;
- pills for PLAY AGAIN (the game just played), DOWNLOAD (a map this PC lacks)
  and YOUR VOTE, and a blue ring round your vote.

Above the tiles: how many have voted, the seconds left on a disc, and a bar
that drains. Both turn gold for the last five seconds and grey while a
report holds the vote. When the vote is decided, the winner gets a gold ring
and NEXT GAME, the others fade, and the header names the next game.

Every text in a tile is clipped to it, so a long map name ends in an
ellipsis. The screen before wrote each option on one line ("AGAIN / BLOOD
GULCH / TEAM SLAYER"), which ran out of the panel. The tallies moved from
the footer into the vote's header, and the leading game's screenshot above
the options went, since every tile has its own.

The two halves still mix either way (checked in game, 2026-10-31). An older
MJOLNIRLobby on the new UI writes its one-line labels into the tiles, cut
short with an ellipsis. This MJOLNIRLobby on an older UI container (one with
no `VoteMode0`) draws the old lines.

## Messages between the host and its fireteam

There is no replicated class of our own. Two of the engine's
`PlayerController` RPCs carry the messages (`mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/net.lua`):

| Direction | RPC | Why it is safe |
|---|---|---|
| client to host | `ServerExecRPC(Msg)` | Its body is compiled out of Shipping builds. The host's hook reads `Msg`; `self` is the sender's controller. |
| host to client | `ClientMessage(S, Type, MsgLifeTime)`, `Type = "MJOLNIR"` | The engine prints only the `None` and `Say` types. The client's hook reads `S`. |

A message is `MJOLNIR|<verb>|<field>...`:

| Verb | From | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `vote` | host, every second | id, seconds left, options (`CODE:mode:again;...`), counts, chosen option, the chosen map's campaign-list index, its hub release id and version, held (below) |
| `ballot` | anyone, the host included | id, option |
| `cancel` | host | id |
| `lobby` | host, while its lobby is up | map code, game type, game settings line ([host_game_settings.md](host_game_settings.md)), campaign-list index, hub release id, version |
| `starting` | host, as it starts a game | map code, hub release id, game type |
| `mapstate` | a client getting the host's map | map code, stage, percent ([live_map_install.md](live_map_install.md)) |
| `where` | a client joining a match under way | map code |
| `mapindex` | host, in answer to `where` | map code, campaign-list index |
| `kick` | host | why; the map code when it is a map they lack (MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0), which the client offers with the reason |
| `reporting` | anyone on the post-game screen | 1 when the report panel opens, 0 when it closes: the host holds the vote |
| `iam` | a client | its identity ticket ([player_identity.md](player_identity.md)) |
| `whois` | a client with no roster yet | none |
| `ids` | host | its hub account, the roster of in-game name to hub account |

The vote's ninth field is 1 while the countdown is held for a report.
MJOLNIRHud's `feed`, `clock`, `match`, `matchid`, `say`, `chat` and `cmd`,
and MJOLNIRLevelLoader's `event`, use the same two RPCs
([multiplayer_hud.md](multiplayer_hud.md)).

Hooks on both functions (native, with parameters) ran on CU4 without trouble
(2026-10-02). The host never sends a client RPC to a controller with no
player or player state: a controller left over from the previous world would
run it locally.

## Files

- `mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/main.lua`: `finishMatch`, the final standings, the
  host's travel.
- `mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/scoreboard.lua`: `Board.winner`, `Board.results`.
- `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/main.lua`, "After a match": the post-game screen,
  the vote and the client lobby.
- `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/net.lua`: the messages.
- `unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_mjolnir_ui.py`, `build_post_game`:
  `WBP_MJOLNIRPostGame`, in chunk 984 with the other screens.
- `mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua`: a travel that names no scenario
  (the way back to the menu) leaves the Megalo patches alone. Restoring them
  under a client's running Megalo game froze it mid-travel.

## Open

- ~~Two PCs: the vote end to end (a client's ballot reaching the host, every
  screen following the outcome) and the client lobby. Steps:
  [two_pc_test.md](two_pc_test.md), Phase 4.~~ **Update 2026-10-21:**
  verified on two PCs on 2026-10-09 (e98d2152): the post-game vote chose The
  Longest, and the host's pick of a map the guest lacked (Hang 'em High) went
  the same way; each was downloaded in game and played by both PCs.
- A client that joins during the vote sees it from the next broadcast; one
  that joins mid-match is not handled yet. **Update 2026-10-21:** since
  mods-v0.12.0 (PR #130) a client can join a public match under way; a
  private game still refuses a join mid-match.
- The vote's tiles (2026-10-31) were checked on one PC, as the host only.
  A fireteam client's view (its clock runs on from the host's last message),
  the DOWNLOAD pill for a map the client lacks, and the grey clock while a
  report holds the vote still need [two_pc_test.md](two_pc_test.md), Phase 4.
- The tallies are HUD-side. Reading the Megalo score itself would make a
  client's standings authoritative.

notes.title: Match history and stats
notes.summary: Every public multiplayer match is reported to the hub when it ends: the final standings, and every incident the simulation raised, in order, with where the players involved stood. The hub shows the history at /matches, one match at /matches/<id>, a player's matches at…
notes.body:
Every public multiplayer match is reported to the hub when it ends: the final
standings, and every incident the simulation raised, in order, with where the
players involved stood. The hub shows the history at `/matches`, one match at
`/matches/<id>`, a player's matches at `/players/<name>`, and a linked
account's on its profile (`/users/<id>`). Matchmaking and ranking will build
on the same records later; for now the job is to collect everything.

## The pieces

```text
host's game                                         hub (mjolnircore.com)
  MJOLNIRHud   Scripts/matchlog.lua                   POST /api/v1/matches
    records incidents + positions,                    POST /api/v1/matches/claims
    writes match_<id>.json        ─┐                  GET  /api/v1/matches[/{id}]
  MJOLNIRLobby Scripts/matches.lua │ match_outbox.txt  GET  /api/v1/players/{name}/stats
    sends the outbox to the hub  <─┘                  GET  /api/v1/users/{id}/match-stats
                                                      D1: matches, match_players,
participant's game                                        match_events, match_claims
  MJOLNIRHud   asks the host for the match id,        (migrations/0014_matches.sql)
               writes claim_<id>.json
  MJOLNIRLobby sends it
```

### Recording (the host)

The host's incident handler gets every player's incidents; a fireteam client's
gets almost none (multiplayer_hud.md), so only the host records. MJOLNIRHud
already hooks `OnIncident_Event` for the kill feed. While its match log is
recording, the hook also reads `K2_GetActorLocation()` of the incident's
`CauseObjectActor` and `EffectObjectActor`: for a kill, the killer's and the
victim's bipeds, at the moment the incident arrives. Every incident is kept
except the respawn countdown (`respawn_tick`, `respawn_final_tick`): kills,
deaths, suicides, spawns (with the spawn point), medals and commendations,
flags, joins and quits, the end.

Positions are the map's Unreal world space, in centimetres, Z up. They are
real biped positions (checked 2026-10-03 on Blood Gulch: a bot standing still
died a few centimetres from where it spawned). The cause object can be a
vehicle when the killer drove one.

A match is **public** if MJOLNIRLobby listed it on the hub at any point while
it ran: the Lobby writes the listing's id to `MJOLNIRLobby\listing.txt` while
listed, and the HUD reads it every five seconds. A private match is recorded
and thrown away at its end.

The record is `MJOLNIRHud\match_<id>.json`, already in the shape the hub's
`MatchReport` takes. It is rewritten every 30 seconds as an *abandoned* match,
so a crash leaves what happened up to then. `match_current.txt` names the match
being recorded; found at the next start, it marks a match a crash cut short,
whose checkpoint is then sent. At the end (`round_over`, `game_over`, or the
host leaving the map: abandoned) the file is written a last time and its id is
appended to `match_outbox.txt`. An abandoned match under a minute long with no
kill is not kept.

The id is 32 random hex digits, made by the host. The hub never shows it; it is
what a participant cites to claim its seat.

### Sending

MJOLNIRLobby's `matches.lua` reads `match_outbox.txt` every 15 seconds and
sends one file at a time through the native hub call public games use
(`mjolnir_hub_call`, the launcher's key). A file is deleted once the hub has it
(200/201) or refuses it for good (400, 409, 413, 422). No connection or a 5xx
retry in a minute, a 429 in five; 401/403 (an old launcher sign-in) and 404 (a
hub without these routes) in ten. Lua has no directory listing, hence the outbox.
The HUD only appends to it; the Lobby rewrites it to the entries whose files
remain. Both run on the game thread, so they never interleave.

### Seats and accounts

A seat is a player as the host's game named them. Names are not identities,
so each participant's own game claims its seat with its own hub key:

1. A client's HUD asks the host: `ServerExecRPC("MJOLNIR|matchid")`, every ten
   seconds until answered.
2. The host's HUD hook (`self` is the asker's controller) answers on that
   controller: `ClientMessage("MJOLNIR|match|<id>|<public>|<index>|<name>",
   "MJOLNIR")`, with the seat as the host recorded it. The host ignores its
   own outgoing answers, which its hook also sees.
3. If public, the client writes `claim_<id>.json` and queues it. A private
   answer is asked again every 30 seconds, since a game can go public.

These are the RPCs MJOLNIRLobby's messages already ride
(multiplayer_postgame.md); the Lobby and the level loader ignore the new verbs.
No object scans on either side.

The hub keeps claims apart from seats (`match_claims`) so either can arrive
first; whichever lands second links the seat (`match_players.user_id`). A
claim links only a seat of the same name, one account per seat and one seat
per account per match; a newer claim replaces the account's own older one. The
host's seat is linked by the report itself (`host_index`).

Both writes take the `lobbies:write` scope every launcher key already has
(migration 0013), so nobody signs in again.

## The hub

`hub/src/lib/api/matches.ts`. The report is validated (16 seats, 20,000
events, six hours), stored in one D1 batch, seats and events each inserted by
a single `json_each` statement (D1 counts statements against a request's
budget). The hub works out each seat's place and outcome (win, loss, draw; none
for an abandoned match) and the match's winner: the team with more points, or
the top score alone (a shared top is a draw). The host's clock is trusted only
to the last week and never ahead of the hub's. Reporting the same id twice from
the same account is a no-op; from another, 409. A listing id that still exists
must be the caller's.

Chat: the host's game also sends each match's chat log (`POST /matches/chat`,
migrations/0020); a reported public match shows it on `/matches/<id>`, naming a
hub account only for a line from a seat linked to that account, while a
private game's log is read only by moderators from the report queue.

Pages: `/matches` (filters by game type and map, player search),
`/matches/<id>` (scoreboard by team, the timeline, and the kill and death
positions over the map, per player with `?p=<index>`), `/players/<name>`
(the combat record below), and the same record on `/users/<id>`.

### The combat record

`players/_components/PlayerRecordView.tsx` draws a career from the match
tables (`lib/api/player-record.ts`), read on each view; no rollup table yet.

- The **career signature** (`CareerRing.tsx`): every match the player fought
  in as a spoke around a ring, oldest at the top and clockwise, kills reaching
  out and deaths reaching in, wins gold. Matches with no kill or death are left
  off it, and it keeps the newest 200.
- **Form**: career K/D match by match, and personal bests.
- **Battlegrounds**: where the player stood for each kill and died, over the
  map (`?map=<CODE>`, the newest 600 marks). It defaults to their busiest map.
- **Arsenal**: kills by weapon and class. The class with 40% of 15 or more
  kills names the player's style; otherwise "All-rounder".
- **Rivals**: who they traded the most kills with, one row a person, by
  account when the seat is linked and by name when it is not.
- **Medal case**: only the incidents in `MEDAL_TYPES`. A kill raises a run of
  sibling incidents (`sniper_kill`, `precision_comm`, ...), so a new medal has
  to be added to that list and to `MEDALS` in `players/_components/record.ts`.
  A medal the game sends together with one that stands for it (a headshot
  beside a sniper headshot, `MEDAL_HIDDEN_BY`) is counted once.

A match's page (`/matches/<id>`) shows the same medals for that match: a
Medals column on the scoreboard and, under it, each player's medals by kind
(`matches/_components/medals.ts`, from the match's own events, with the same
list and the same hiding).

Win rate counts finished matches only: an abandoned match has no outcome. A
name page links a hub profile only when every linked seat under that name is
the same account.

### Leaderboards

`/leaderboards` ranks hub accounts by kills, K/D, wins, win rate, headshots and
best match, all time or over 30 or 7 days (`lib/api/leaderboards.ts`). Two
rules decide what counts, both about trust:

- Only a linked seat places. Anyone can play under any name, so a name on a
  board would be a way to wear someone else's record.
- Only a match with two linked seats counts. A report is its host's word, and a
  host alone, or alone with AI bots, could otherwise fill a board.

So a board can read lower than the career total on a profile, and the page says
so. K/D needs 20 kills over 3 matches, and win rate 3 finished matches, to place. Banned
accounts never show. Two colluding accounts can still report what they like:
weighing host trust is what real ranking still has to add.

### The map under the positions

A match on a map the hub has a preview model of draws its kills and deaths
over the level with three.js (`MatchMap.tsx`, `mapViewer.ts`): a top-down
minimap (orthographic, panned and zoomed) or the level in 3D to orbit. A cut
slider takes off everything above a height, so a lower floor shows on
Prisoner or Chill Out; the map's faces point into the play space, so an
indoor map is seen through its roof either way. Hovering a dot shows the
kill. Other maps, and a browser without WebGL, get the plain SVG plot.

Under the map, a replay (`MatchReplay.tsx`): play the match at 10× to 120×
(the default plays it in about a minute) or scrub it, and the map, either
kind, shows only what had happened by then, the last moments larger and the
rest faded. Ticks on the scrub bar mark when each kill (gold) and death
(red) came. The timeline follows the replay, and a row jumps the replay to
it. "Show all" goes back to the whole match.

The models are `hub/public/map-previews/<CODE>.glb`, listed in
`hub/src/app/matches/_components/map-previews.json`, made from a converted
map's output folder ([ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md)):

```bash
python tools/level/export_map_preview.py out/bgl BGL hub/public/map-previews   --manifest hub/src/app/matches/_components/map-previews.json
```

It takes `scene.gltf` (the BSP with its scenery; no sky, no glass or water),
quantized (`KHR_mesh_quantization`) to 100 KB to 1.2 MB a map, with a vertex
colour for the textures: CE's texture pass with the base map shrunk to 16×16
and each detail map as its average colour, times the lightmap. The model is
glTF metres, Y up, at CE coordinates; a recorded Unreal position is
`(x, z, y) / 100` in it. Checked 2026-10-05 against 12 prod matches on 12
maps: every recorded position falls inside its map's model. Re-export a map
whenever it is re-converted.

## Trust

A report is the host's word. The hub records who reported it, and seats link
only to the accounts that claim them, but standings are not verified. Ranking
built on this should weigh hosts (agreement between participants' own views,
per-host history) before it trusts a report.

## Migration

`0014_matches.sql`. Migration 0001 carried unused placeholder `matches` and
`match_players` tables; 0014 renames them to `legacy_*` rather than dropping
them unseen. Like every migration it must be applied to production by hand
before the hub deploy that uses it (`pnpm db:migrate:prod`).

## Testing

- Hub: `hub` dev server with local D1 (`pnpm db:migrate`), a seeded user and
  key, then POST reports and claims. Claim before and after the report,
  a wrong name, a taken seat, a duplicate report, another account's id.
- Game, one PC (2026-10-03): host BGL Slayer with a `CreatePlayer` bot and a
  hand-written `listing.txt`; `blam unit_kill (unit (list_get (players) 1))`
  for deaths; `mjolnir_auto endgame`. The record, posted to the local hub,
  rendered as written.
- Two PCs (2026-10-03, `tools/remote/jip-test.mjs`, PC 2 joining PC 1's
  public BGL match under way): PC 2 claimed seat 1 in the match PC 1
  recorded. The host's record held two real kills (an assault rifle first
  blood; a Warthog splatter, `WarthogDriver` modifier 3, the cause position
  the vehicle's), with positions for both players. Posted to a local hub,
  claim first, both seats linked. The first run had claimed seat 0: a joiner
  reads index 0 on the host for a few seconds after it is seated, so the host
  now answers only with the asker's own recorded seat.
- A host's ban list kicks a banned joiner about a second in; an old ban of
  the test account looked like a failed join until it was cleared.

## Next

- Heatmaps across matches per map, from `match_events` (indexed by type),
  over the same preview models.
- Periodic position samples (where players walk, not just where they die).
- Ranking: per-account ratings from linked seats in completed matches.

notes.title: Hub identities in game, player reports, matchmaking bans
notes.summary: Everyone who plays online signs the MJOLNIR launcher in with Discord, so in game a player is shown by their hub account, its name and avatar, instead of their Steam or Xbox name. From the post-game screen a player can report another. Moderators review reports at /moderation, and…
notes.body:
Everyone who plays online signs the MJOLNIR launcher in with Discord, so in
game a player is shown by their hub account, its name and avatar, instead of
their Steam or Xbox name. From the post-game screen a player can report
another. Moderators review reports at `/moderation`, and can ban a player
from matchmaking. Status as of 2026-10-10: the hub, the HUD and the Lobby
work end to end on one PC against a local hub. The two-PC exchange (a
joiner proving itself to a host) is still untested. **Update 2026-10-21:**
shipped in mods-v0.22.0 (PR #172), and the hub side reached main with that
merge. No two-PC test of the exchange is recorded since.

## Who is who

A name is the host's to trust or not: anyone can call themselves anything,
and the scoreboard, the kill feed and above all a report must not name the
wrong account. So each player proves its account to the host with a ticket
from the hub:

```text
joiner's game                          hub                          host's game
  POST /identity/tickets  ───────────▶  ticket for (joiner,
  {platform_name, audience=host}         audience host, in-game
                                         name), 15 minutes
  iam|<ticket>  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────▶  (ServerExecRPC)
                                        POST /identity/tickets/resolve  ◀─ {tickets}
                                        ──▶ {platform_name, player, reports, matchmaking_ban}
                                                                     checks platform_name ==
                                                                     the sender's in-game name
  ids|<host account>|<roster>  ◀────────────────────────────────────  (ClientMessage)
```

- **The audience.** Only the host the ticket names can trade it. A host that
  took a joiner's ticket and passed it to another host would get nothing for
  it. The joiner learns the host's account from the host's own `ids`
  broadcast.
- **The in-game name.** The hub returns the name the ticket was issued for.
  The host keeps the answer only if it is the name of the controller that
  sent the ticket. Even with a valid audience, a ticket stolen in transit
  names nobody else.
- **The host itself** asks `POST /identity/tickets` with no audience. That
  makes no ticket and just answers who it is and whether it is banned.

The roster is keyed by in-game name, as everything else between the host
and its fireteam already is (ballots, bans, seats). Each entry is the
account id, its name (display name, else the Discord username) and its
public report count. `ids` goes out when the roster changes, every 30 s
while anyone else is connected, and when a client asks (`whois`, sent by a
client that has not heard one).

Every machine writes what it knows to `MJOLNIRLobby\identities.txt`, one
line per player: `<in-game name>\t<account id>\t<hub name>\t<reports>`.
MJOLNIRHud reads that file; it never touches the hub itself.

### Where the hub name shows

- **Tab scoreboard** (MJOLNIRHud): the name, plus the avatar in a new
  `Avatar<i>` image per row.
- **Kill feed and winner line**: the name. A joiner's "joined the game"
  line waits up to 8 s for its account (its ticket lands a few seconds after
  the join), then falls back to the in-game name. Since MJOLNIRHud 0.7.0
  (PR #189, mods-v0.25.0) each feed row also shows both players' avatars.
- **Match chat** (PR #200, mods-v0.27.0): the sender's hub name and avatar.
- **The game's FIRETEAM panel** (top right of the main menu): each row's
  `NameText`. The game's view model rewrites its names every few seconds,
  and each row writes its text again in `OnBackingDataChanged`, so
  `squadpanel.lua` hooks that (and `OnListItemObjectSet`) and sets the hub
  name after it. Renaming the view model's `DisplayName` does not stick.
- **Our lobby's player list** (`WBP_MJOLNIRLobby`): the name.
- **Name tags over teammates**: the hub name is written into the game's
  `PlayerNameValue` when a tag is shown. This one is untested; the game may
  write its own name back.
- **Post-game screen** (MJOLNIRLobby): the name and avatar per row.

`p.name` stays the in-game name everywhere it is a key: match seats and
claims, host bans, ballots. Only what is drawn changes.

### Avatars

The game's hub call reaches nothing but the hub (`mjolnir_lobby.c` refuses
another host, and must not carry the launcher key to one). So the hub
proxies avatars: `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/avatar` returns the Discord
avatar at 64 px, or Discord's default one for an account without one. It
is a PNG, cached at Cloudflare for a day and in browsers for an hour.

The Lobby fetches each account's avatar once a session with the hub call's
`FILE` mode, into `MJOLNIRMaps\_covers\av_<id>.png`. Lobby and HUD read the
file into a texture with `ImportFileAsTexture2D`, the way map covers are
read. No native change was needed.

## Reporting a player

On the post-game screen every row is now a button (`RowButton<i>`). A row
is enabled when its player has a hub account and is not you; clicking it
opens the report panel:

- who: avatar, hub name, the in-game name if different, and the public
  report count;
- **WHY**: one of CHEATING, BETRAYING, HARASSMENT, GRIEFING / AFK, QUITTING,
  NAME OR AVATAR, OTHER;
- **WHAT HAPPENED**: an optional note of up to 1000 characters, in a
  `MultiLineEditableTextBox` (typing works on the menu stack);
- SEND REPORT / CANCEL.

The report is `POST /api/v1/players/reports` with:
- the account the host resolved for that seat;
- the reason and the note;
- the in-game name the reporter saw;
- the match's id: the host's own record, or the id the host told the
  client. MJOLNIRHud now writes it into `last_match.txt` (field 8 of the
  `match` line).

Each `player` line in `last_match.txt` gained three fields: the account id,
the hub name and the report count. One report per reporter, player and
match: a second one gets 409, and the panel says it was already sent.

The vote lasts 20 s, which is not enough to write a report. While anyone
has the panel open, the host holds the countdown:
- opening or closing the panel sends `reporting|1` or `reporting|0`;
- the hold lasts at most 90 s per vote, and a player's hold lapses after
  120 s;
- the vote message gained a ninth field, `held`, so every screen says
  VOTING PAUSED / A PLAYER IS FILING A REPORT.

### What is public

Only the number. A profile's Multiplayer section (`/users/<id>`) shows
**Reports**: the reports against the account that a moderator has not
dismissed. The same figure is `stats.player_reports` on
`GET /api/v1/users/{id}`, and appears in the report panel and in the
roster. Who reported, and why, is for moderators only.

## Moderation

At `/moderation`, moderators and admins get **Player reports**, grouped by
the player reported (most reports first), with tabs for Open, Upheld and
Dismissed. Each player shows:
- every report against them, with its reason and note;
- who filed it and when;
- the name it was filed under;
- a link to the match when the host reported it, or a flag when either
  player is not linked to a seat in it.

**Update 2026-10-21:** since PR #200 (mods-v0.27.0) a report from a match
whose host sent its chat log opens that log
(`GET /moderation/match-chat/{host_match_id}`, `hub/src/lib/api/matches.ts`,
migration 0020), with the reported player's lines marked. Since PR #201
this desk is the Players tab of `/moderation`.

The decisions:

- **Uphold**: the report stands and stays in the public count.
- **Dismiss**: unfounded; it leaves the public count.
- **Ban from matchmaking**: a reason (the player sees it) and 1, 3, 7 or
  30 days, or permanent. It replaces a ban in force, upholds the player's
  open reports, and takes down a game they have listed. Only an admin can
  ban a moderator or an admin.
- **Lift ban**.

**Matchmaking bans** lists the bans in force. Every decision is written to
`audit_log`.

### What a matchmaking ban does

| Where | Effect |
|---|---|
| `POST /lobbies` | 403 `matchmaking_banned`, with the reason and end; the game's status line shows it |
| `GET /lobbies/{id}/join` | the same 403: no connection string |
| `GET /lobbies` | a banned host's games are not listed |
| Ban issued | the banned player's listing is deleted; their heartbeat then 404s and the game stops listing |
| A public game's host | resolves a banned joiner's ticket, sends them back to their menu (`kick`) |

It is not a hub ban (`users.banned_at`): the account still signs in,
downloads and comments.

A banned player can still join a friend's game by invite: that never
touches the hub. Their identity is still resolved there, and they are kicked
only if that game is public.

## The hub

`hub/src/lib/api/players.ts`, `migrations/0018_player_identity_reports.sql`:

- `identity_tickets`: the hash of each ticket, never the ticket. Rows
  expire after 15 minutes and are swept when new ones are issued.
- `player_reports`: its own table, because `reports.reason` is a CHECK enum
  about mods that SQLite cannot widen. A unique index on (reporter,
  subject, match).
- `matchmaking_bans`: kept after they end or are lifted. The ban in force
  is one that is not lifted and has not expired.

| Route | Who |
|---|---|
| `POST /identity/tickets` | `lobbies:write` (every launcher key) |
| `POST /identity/tickets/resolve` | `lobbies:write`, the ticket's audience |
| `GET /users/{id}/avatar` | anyone |
| `POST /players/reports` | `lobbies:write`, 30 an hour |
| `GET /moderation/player-reports`, `POST /moderation/player-reports/{id}` | moderators |
| `GET`/`POST /moderation/matchmaking-bans`, `DELETE /moderation/matchmaking-bans/{user_id}` | moderators |
| `GET /moderation/match-chat/{host_match_id}` (`matches.ts`, since PR #200) | moderators |

Like every migration, 0018 must be applied to production by hand before
the hub deploy that uses it (`pnpm db:migrate:prod`).

## The UI container

`build_mjolnir_ui.py` adds three things, so chunk 984 must be rebuilt and
cooked:
- `Avatar<i>` images to the scoreboard and post-game rows;
- `RowButton<i>` around each post-game row;
- the `Report` panel.

An older container still works: the Lua checks each new widget and draws
text only, with no click.

## Testing

One PC, 2026-10-10:
- **Setup.** The game was pointed at a local hub (`MJOLNIR_HUB_URL`). The
  launcher's account was seeded there with only its key's hash. The rebuilt
  chunk 984 replaced `pakchunk900-MJOLNIRHUB-mjolnir-ce-runtime-0_P` (the UI
  container as the runtime ships it).
- **Identity.** The Lobby resolved the account, wrote `identities.txt` and
  cached the avatar. The Tab scoreboard showed the hub name and avatar in
  place of the in-game name.
- **Post-game.** A hand-written `last_match.txt` showed the post-game rows
  with avatars, and a row without an account had none. Clicking a row
  opened the panel and held the vote. Typing reached the text box. SEND
  REPORT filed the report with its reason, note, in-game name and match id,
  then the panel closed and the vote resumed.
- **Fireteam and lobby.** The FIRETEAM panel and our lobby's player list
  showed the hub name, and it survived the view model's refreshes. The
  delayed "joined" line is covered by the Lua tests only: it needs a second
  player.
- **Hub API.** Tickets, the audience check, reports and their duplicates,
  bans refusing `POST /lobbies` and joins, lifting, and the avatar proxy.
  The moderation page and the profile count were checked in a browser.

## Open

- **Two PCs.** A joiner's ticket reaching the host, the roster reaching
  the joiner, and a banned joiner kicked from a public game.
- **Name tags.** Whether the game keeps our hub name in a tag.
- **Unverified players.** A public game could refuse players with no
  resolved account (an old launcher, or no sign-in) after a grace period.
  Not done, because it would send away anyone on a stale sign-in.
- **Reporting from the website.** A participant could report from
  `/matches/<id>` too, for when the post-game screen is gone.
- **Linking seats from tickets.** The host could cite resolved accounts in
  its match report, so seats link without each client's claim.

notes.title: Bots
notes.summary: AI players that fill a multiplayer match (issue #247): the simulation's own AI, given a seat and a name on MJOLNIR's scoreboard. They run on the host; a fireteam client sees them through the simulation's own replication.
notes.body:
AI players that fill a multiplayer match (issue #247): the simulation's own
AI, given a seat and a name on MJOLNIR's scoreboard. They run on the host; a
fireteam client sees them through the simulation's own replication.

Proven on Blood Gulch on 2026-10-25, host and one joiner on two PCs: the bots
walk the map, fight the players and each other, die and respawn, and both
machines' feeds and boards name them and count the same kills. In team games
they play for red and blue (PC 1, 2026-10-31): the two sides fight each other,
a bot leaves the players of its own side alone, and its kills score for its
team.

## The pieces

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `level bake`, `blam.bots` ([level_format.md](level_format.md)) | bot squads, a zone of firing positions, an objective, AI pathfinding for the map's BSP; `<CODE>.bots.json`, where the squads stand |
| `crates/blam-sbsp/src/pathfinding.rs` | the pathfinding tables, from a structure BSP's collision shell |
| MJOLNIRLobby's DLL, `mjolnir_bots_enable` | lets `ai_place` place squads in a Megalo game, and makes elites short enough for low doorways there |
| MJOLNIRLobby's DLL, `mjolnir_bots_teams` | in a team game, gives AI units the multiplayer team of their side |
| MJOLNIRLobby `settings.lua` | BOTS, BOT TYPE and BOT DIFFICULTY on the PLAYERS page of the host's game settings: `bots=N;bot_type=K;bot_level=L` in the settings line |
| `tools/level/build_bot_characters.sh` | the bots' characters: the Spartan, and every kind at each difficulty |
| MJOLNIRHud `Scripts/bots.lua` | places, names, respawns and directs the bots on the host |
| MJOLNIRHud `main.lua`, `relay.lua` | bot seats on the board and in the feed, on the host and its clients |
| MJOLNIRHud `commands.lua` | `/bots <0-15> [kind] [level]`: the host changes this match's bots |

## Why each is needed

**`ai_place` refuses multiplayer games.** Its core returns unless the game
mode is campaign or Firefight; a Megalo match is neither. MJOLNIRLobby's DLL
patches that one test (found by its bytes, so an update that moves it is left
alone). Nothing else gates AI: once placed they think, path and fight
([re/ai_in_multiplayer.md](re/ai_in_multiplayer.md)).

**Converted maps have no navigation.** Their BSP replaces B40's geometry, but
the scenario still carries B40's pathfinding for it. The bake builds the
pathfinding from the map's own collision: every walkable shell surface (normal
within about 49 degrees of up, not breakable) is a sector, every collision
edge touching one is a link, oriented so its walkable side is on the left (CE's
winged edges are already the rings the sim walks), and the shell gets one 2D
reference per surface naming its sector. Blood Gulch: 2947 sectors, 4930
links, one connected area of 2828 sectors.

Two things cut a converted map's ground that the edges alone miss, and the
bake handles both the way B40's own data does
([re/ai_in_multiplayer.md](re/ai_in_multiplayer.md#steps-and-seams-in-bungies-pathfinding)):

- **Steps.** A riser under 0.1 wu (where the AI globals' hoist step begins)
  between two floors becomes a step sector, walkable, linked to both. Short
  bands of a taller riser, or a slab's side face hanging below its floor, do
  not.
- **Cracks.** Maps built of separate slabs meet floor to floor without
  sharing an edge: edge to edge, overlapping a hair, or across a crack. Two
  floor edges that both drop away, face each other within 0.1 wu and lie
  less than a step apart in height join through an *intersection link*, a
  hint on each floor's edge naming a link that joins the two.

Neither is a jump, a hoist, a ladder or a teleporter: ground those reach
stays apart. On Night Lockout (PC 1, 2026-10-30) bots walked back and forth
across its slab seams (two bots, 14 crossings in two minutes) and one crossed
the lower level to kill the idle player.

**AI stand still without orders.** They hold firing positions in their task's
areas until they see someone, and AI far from every player go idle. Each bot
is forced active when placed (`ai_force_active`), the bake gives the objective
the tasks `area_0` .. `area_15` (a map with fewer areas repeats them, one
with more shares them out, so every task the HUD names is there) and makes
`hunt` follow the players (radius 3 wu, every player slot), and the host's
HUD orders each bot every 8-16 s, waking its body first (see "Bots frozen
in place" below): three times in
four after an enemy, otherwise `(ai_set_task <squad> mjolnir_bots
area_<r>)` to a random area. An enemy human is hunted: the `hunt` task and
`(ai_magically_see_object <squad> (player_get n))`, where `n` counts the
players there are (`player_get` returns the nth player in the players
table, not a seat), so the HUD passes the target's rank among the humans in
seat order. In a team game an enemy is anyone on the other side, a bot too:
a bot is no player, so it gets an area walk and `(ai_magically_see <squad>
<enemy squad>)`. A human whose side the HUD has not read yet is no one's
target in a team game.

**Where bots spawn.** On the map's own player starts. The bake stands each
bot squad on one of the starts on the ground the bots walk (`bots_finish`),
so a bot appears where a player would. Squad `k` of every kind takes the
`k`-th start farthest first: the first start, then each time the one
farthest from those already taken. A level lists its starts a base at a
time, so taken in the level's order (as before 2026-10-31) the first eight
bots on Blood Gulch all stood at one base and fought there. A map with more
starts than squads (15 per kind) never uses the rest.

The bake also writes where each squad stands, `<CODE>.bots.json` (Unreal cm,
by squad index; with each area's extent and the areas each `area_<k>` task
covers), which the map's pack carries beside its level file
(`map/bots.json`, installed to `ue4ss/MJOLNIRMaps/<CODE>/`; a test install's
goes to MJOLNIRLevelLoader's `levels/`). With it, the host's HUD picks a bot's
squad each time it places the bot, so the bot comes in where its side is.
A side has no base of its own: a converted map's player spawns are all
neutral, and on Blood Gulch Team Slayer the red host's first spawn landed at
the south base in one match and the north in another. So the HUD does what
the game's respawns do for players, in order:

1. a free squad of the bot's kind (none another bot out holds);
2. never within 2 wu of anyone;
3. with an enemy about, a start no enemy is within 25 wu of, or failing that
   the starts farthest from the enemies (within 10 wu of the farthest);
4. with its side about and the enemies clear, the starts nearest one of its
   side (within 8 wu of the nearest);
5. with no one about, its own squad `k` (the farthest-first order);
   otherwise one of what is left at random.

In Free for All everyone is an enemy, so a bot comes in away from all of
them. The first bots wait up to 5 s for the humans' first spawn. A bot
starts each life with what a player starts with: the hub's `bots.json` gives
every Spartan squad the assault rifle (the default multiplayer loadout),
elites the plasma rifle and grunts and jackals the plasma pistol. Anything
better it picks up off the ground, as a player would. (Until 2026-11 a
Spartan's squad carried one of a mixed list, so bots came in with snipers and
rockets.) On Blood Gulch Team Slayer (PC 1, 2026-10-31) the red host spawned
at the north base: the three red bots came in beside him and the five blue
bots at the south base. A map without the file (every map published before
it) keeps squad `k` for bot `k`, as before.

**Why bots stand still.** Seen on Night Lockout and Blood Gulch: a bot sent
to `hunt` a player it cannot reach (on ground the pathfinding does not join)
waits at the nearest point; the HUD picked `area_<r>` from 0-15 while most
maps baked fewer areas, so those orders went nowhere (every map bakes all
sixteen tasks since 2026-10-31); and on narrow ground `hunt`'s 3 wu radius
found no firing position to stand on until the bake narrowed the grid there.
An AI with no target holds its task's positions: the simulation's own
`search` follows a target it lost, it does not roam.

**Bots frozen in place.** Three things kept bots still for minutes on Blood
Gulch (PC 1, 2026-10-31,
[re/ai_in_multiplayer.md](re/ai_in_multiplayer.md#bots-frozen-in-place)):

- **A sleeping body.** A bot's body falls asleep in the physics when it
  stands still, as anyone's does, and sometimes its AI does not wake it
  again: the AI goes on thinking and its squad takes every order, but the
  body neither moves nor turns, not even when shot. A Spartan stood so on
  open ground for five and a half minutes. `ai_force_active` does not wake a
  body; `(object_wake_physics (ai_get_unit <squad>))` does, and the Spartan
  walked off within a second of it. So every order the HUD gives a bot
  starts with that line, and a bot whose body stays asleep waits for its
  next order (8-16 s), not for minutes.
- **The flag rooms.** A bot on the lower floor under a base's deck, by the
  flag, stayed there: ordered anywhere, it walked about the room, a little
  way up an exit ramp and back, and stopped; a jackal stayed over half an
  hour, a grunt over 20 minutes. A converted map's collision is there twice,
  as the map's own shell and as a copy of it placed as instanced geometry,
  at one height to within f32 rounding, and the rounding decides which one
  the simulation meets under a bot: on the flag-room floors the copy nearly
  every time, elsewhere a third to two thirds of the time. On the copy a bot
  is on no sector (the bake gives the copy no pathfinding of its own, and
  giving it the shell's crashed the game): it keeps the last place it stood
  on the shell and walks a path it already has, but cannot plan a new one,
  and wanders until it steps back onto the shell, which in a flag room means
  an exit ramp. Bots stood so beside the bases too; path followers had no
  plan in 29 to 48% of samples. Since 2026-10-31 the bake lowers the copy
  0.001 wu under the shell: in two 10-minute matches the followers had no
  plan in 0.35% and 0.38% of samples, and no bot stayed in a flag room
  longer than 53 s. A map published before then keeps the trap until it is
  rebaked.
- **Elites in the side doorways.** The ramp from a base's deck down to each
  side door passes under the door's lintel, 0.82 wu above the ramp at its
  inner edge. An upright elite (0.8 wu tall, radius 0.18) does not fit on
  that slope: one walking down jams its head on the lintel's corner, facing
  the door, twitching, and stays until it turns back (one stood five
  minutes; sent down on purpose, it jammed every time it took the ramp), and
  one climbing stops 0.1 short of the corner and backs down, so no elite
  walks onto a deck. Spartans, grunts, jackals and a crouching elite fit.
  Flagging the ramps `crouchable` in the pathfinding changes nothing: an AI
  crouches for danger, cover or a script, never for its path. Leaving the
  ramps out of the pathfinding is no answer either: they are the only way to
  walk onto a deck. An elite whose standing capsule is 0.70 tall passes both
  ways, and 0.72 still jams (tested live by writing the capsule, which the
  game builds from the tag's heights at load). Since 2026-10-31 the lobby
  DLL makes every elite 0.70 tall in a Megalo game once the host's HUD has
  started bots. It acts in Megalo games only, and a match's tags unload
  when it ends, so campaign elites should keep their height (by
  construction; not measured in a mission). On PC 1, an elite sent down
  from the south deck took the ramp
  three times out of five and walked out of the door each time (the other
  two times it dropped off the deck); HUD elites walked down two of the
  ramps, and one walked up onto the deck.

**Stuck bots are placed again.** A bot that stays within 6 wu for 40 s is
woken and sent to an area that does not hold it (an `area_<k>` order, with
no other order for 15 s); a bot that waited at a firing position or fought
in one place walks off, and one that has neither left nor reached that area
is erased and placed again on a start, as a respawn without a death (the
HUD logs `stayed ... placing it again`). With the lowered copy it catches
bots idle under their orders, jammed or blocked: on Blood Gulch with eight
bots, 12 in 10 minutes, half of them stuck by the simulation's own reading
and the rest bots whose actors had stopped following them. It judges only a
bot whose actor it has seen move since placing it: a placement sometimes
takes an actor that stays where the bot came in while the bot walks off, and
placing that bot again only takes another. A bot that wanders wider than 6
wu is not caught. The areas come from the map's `bots.json`, so a map baked
before 2026-10-31 (no `areas` there) gets no such help.

**Who bots fight** (measured in Team Slayer on Blood Gulch, 2026-10-30;
[re/ai_in_multiplayer.md](re/ai_in_multiplayer.md#teams-in-a-megalo-match)).
Every unit carries a campaign team and a multiplayer team. A player's unit
is on red or blue with no campaign team; the simulation puts a bot's on its
squad's campaign team (covenant) with no multiplayer team, every tick. In a
Megalo game a unit with no multiplayer team is everyone's enemy, and bot
against bot is decided by campaign teams: bots of one team never fight each
other (covenant, flood, sentinel and heretic bots do fight one another).
That is how bots play Free for All: every one covenant, attacking every
player and leaving the other bots alone. No script function gives an AI unit
a multiplayer team (`mp_ai_allegiance` is compiled out, `ai_allegiance` gated
to campaign).

**Red and blue bots.** In a team game each bot plays for a side.
MJOLNIRLobby's DLL (`mjolnir_bots_teams`) turns the unit update's `or dx,
0xff00` (multiplayer team -1) into a call to a few bytes of its own that look
the multiplayer team up by campaign team, in a table the HUD writes
(`native\bot_teams.txt`: covenant 3 plays for red 0, flood 8 for blue 1). A
bot's squad is put on its side's team (`ai_set_team`: covenant for red,
flood for blue) before its `ai_place`, and the new actor takes it. Moved
after placing, a blue bot was red for a tick, and a blue Spartan could keep
the red armour MJOLNIRLevelLoader tinted it as it appeared (seen on PC 1).
Red and blue bots fight on sight and bots of one side leave each other
alone, and the game's damage code knows the sides: a red bot's hit on a red
player is flagged friendly (`bDamagedByFriendly`), and a player's kill of a
bot on their side raises `kill_betrayal`.

**Players get their side's campaign team too.** An AI picks its enemies by
campaign teams alone: when it notices a unit it marks it an enemy if either
campaign team is -1 or the allegiance matrix says so, and never asks the
Megalo team rule
([re/ai_in_multiplayer.md](re/ai_in_multiplayer.md#how-an-ai-picks-its-enemies)).
A player's unit has campaign team -1 in a Megalo game, so before this every
bot took every player for an enemy: in an isolated run a red bot killed the
red host who walked up to it, as covenant, as sentinel and as human. A
player's unit copies its pair from the player every tick, so while the
table is in, the DLL gives each player on red the covenant campaign team and
each player on blue flood. A red bot then sees a red player as one of its
own and a blue player as an enemy. Tested isolated on Blood Gulch
(2026-10-31, PC 1, nobody at the keyboard): a red covenant grunt beside the
red host held fire for 35 s; with the table turned around (flood red,
covenant blue) a grunt moved to flood before its placement held fire beside
the host, now flood, and a covenant elite placed beside them took the host's
shields in seconds.

The DLL changes the code on the simulation thread between ticks, puts
it back when the HUD clears the table (the match ends), and on its own once
the game is not a Megalo one; Free for All leaves it alone. A bot's side is
chosen when it is first placed, for the side with fewer players (humans and
bots); on a tie the side with fewer humans, as a human plays better than a
bot; then blue. It keeps that side for the match, and the board files it
there (its biped reports the side too, so kills of it read right).

**Slayer's score ignores bots.** Its kill trigger counts kills of players, so
the round never ended on bot kills. With bots playing, the host's HUD ends the
match itself when anyone (bot or player) reaches the score to win, the way the
game's own `round_over` does: final standings, then the post-game screen. A
fireteam client gets no `round_over`; it follows the host's travel.

**AI are not players.** Their incidents carry player index -1 and the AI
biped's actor: a player who kills a bot raises `Kill` (no `death`), or
