`kill_betrayal` and no `Kill` when the bot is on their side; a bot that kills
a player raises the player's `death` (no `Kill`). The HUD gives bot `k`
the seat 100 + k (the match log records only seats 0-15, so bots never reach
the hub) and translates -1 to the seat by actor, then counts both ways (a
`kill_betrayal` of a bot as a kill: -1 in Team Slayer).

**A bot killed by a bot raises nothing**: no `Kill`, no `death`, only kill
medals such as `first_blood` with no seats. Its body stays an actor where it
fell, so the HUD would have counted it alive and never placed it again. The
HUD reads each bot's unit on its actor instead (`BlamObjectDamage:IsDead()`,
every 0.25 s), and the actor's blueprint keeps each hit's aftermath
(`Blam Aftermath Result`: the damage owner's actor, the damage type and
modifier the incidents carry, and `bBodyDepleted` on the killing blow). When
the owner is another bot, the HUD queues the `Kill` the game would have
raised: the feed, the board, the team score and the fireteam's clients all
have it. A bot that dies with no player's `Kill` naming it within 2 s (a
fall, its own grenade) waits out the respawn time with no line.

## Kinds of bot

A map offers kinds (`blam.bots.types`), each with `count` squads of its own:
`spartan_<k>`, `elite_<k>`, `grunt_<k>`, `jackal_<k>` on Blood Gulch. The
host's BOT TYPE picks one (SPARTANS, ELITES, GRUNTS, JACKALS) or MIXED, which
takes them in turn; `/bots 6 elites` changes it mid-match. A map baked before
kinds has `bot_<k>` squads only, which every kind falls back to.

Every kind plays a character of MJOLNIR's own at each difficulty level
(`tools/level/build_bot_characters.sh`): `mjolnir_bot_<kind>_<level>` for
spartan, elite, grunt and jackal, and normal, heroic and legendary (and, for
the Covenant kinds, Warfare's wave-only veteran and ace), each with
`mjolnir_bot_generic_<level>` as its parent. A map bakes a squad set per kind
and level (`spartan_legendary_<k>`; 180 squads on Blood Gulch) and the host's
BOT DIFFICULTY (default LEGENDARY) or `/bots 6 elites heroic` picks one. A
map baked before levels has `<kind>_<k>` squads, which a bot falls back to.

- **Accuracy.** AI aim from per-weapon accuracy bounds and times for normal,
  heroic and legendary. A Megalo match always plays at Normal: the
  simulation reads the difficulty (game options `+0x1e4`) in about fifteen
  places, through two helpers and inline copies, all gated to campaign and
  Firefight, and some of them also scale the players. So the bot characters
  carry their level's values in their Normal slots instead:
  `mjolnir_bot_generic_<level>` is `ai\generic` so tuned, and each bot
  character tunes its own weapon entries the same way (normal keeps the
  shipped values). There is no Easy: the characters have no easy accuracy.
- **Spartans.** No Spartan AI character ships, so `mjolnir_bot_spartan` is the
  Marine's (`trooper`: human weapons, grenades, cover) in the players' own
  body, `objects\characters\spartans\spartans`. Their squads are on the
  Covenant team, since a Marine's own team is the players'.
- **Shields and health.** An AI unit's vitality comes from its character's
  vitality block, not its body's model, and the Marine's has no shield (0)
  and a body that heals itself. So `build_bot_characters.sh` reads the
  players' model (`objects\characters\spartans\spartans`, `new damage
  info`) and writes it into the Spartan bot characters: body 45, shield 70,
  the shield back after 6 s over its recharge time (3 s), no body
  regeneration, at every level. A Spartan bot takes the hits a player takes.
  Checked in game 2026-11-21 (Blood Gulch, values poked into the running
  game): bots had read 105 body and no shield; with these they read 45 and
  70, and a bot and the player hit by the same `damage_object` for 40 lost
  the same 57% and refilled frame for frame. The player's shield starts back
  a second before the model's stun time (7 s) says, so the bots' delay is
  the stun time less a second; at 7 a bot recharged a second late. The host's Shields setting is a player trait and does not
  reach bots.

Every machine in the match needs the characters' containers,
`pakchunk995-MJOLNIRBOT-<kind>-<level>_P` (15). They ship in the CE runtime
pack from 1.16.0, which every map with bots requires.

## Places to hold

A game type with zones (King's hills, Pelican Warfare's capture sites) wants
bots that go to a zone and stay in it. `blam.bots.objectives` names Megalo
labels, and every placed object with one of them and a cylinder or sphere
boundary becomes a place to hold:

- **an area** of the bots' zone, after the grid's, named after it;
- **firing positions** inside its boundary, kept 1 wu in from the rim but
  never more than a quarter of the radius (an AI stops short of its position:
  one stopped 0.3 wu outside a hill from a position on the rim). Grids from 3
  wu down to 0.5 wu are tried, coarsest first, until one gives 32; at most 64
  are kept. A place with fewer than 8 on the main ground is not held, and the
  bake says so;
- **a task** `<label>_<spawn order>` over that one area. `(ai_set_task <squad>
  mjolnir_bots koth_hill_4)` sends a squad there, and it stays.

The grid and its sixteen roaming tasks are as before, and `bots.json`'s
`areas` and `tasks` still list only the grid, so MJOLNIRHud's roaming bots
never wander onto a hill by being sent to `area_<k>`. The places follow under
`holds` (name, area, centre and radius in Unreal cm). A zone's tasks name at
most 32 areas, so grid areas and places together must fit; a level without
`objectives` bakes byte-identical to before.

The rule reads the label, not the boundary: across the converted maps, objects
with a boundary are also flag returns, Oddball spawns, race flags and
teleporters (5,620 of them unlabelled).

**Blood Gulch** (offline): Halo 1 hills are small, 2.3 wu across with 0.5 wu
below their marker. With the first rule (a 1.5 wu grid, 1 wu inset) none of
the ten was held, with 0 to 3 positions each. With the grid going down to 0.5
wu and the inset capped at a quarter of the radius, all ten are held with 8 to
39. Without `objectives` its bake is byte-identical to before.

**Pelican Warfare**, 2026-11-22 **[live]**, with `"objectives": ["koth_hill"]`:
all 11 capture spots held (26 to 46 positions each, 456 in all, 1,727 in the
zone). Solo, six Elites sent to hills: five walked there (55 to 355 wu, one
onto the north pad's structure, one across the river) and stayed for the rest
of the five minutes; the sixth stopped 0.3 wu outside its hill, which led to
the 1 wu inset. Then with two players (PC 1 hosting, PC 3 joining), seven
Elites under live Warfare rules: six reached their hills and held them on both
PCs; one stood at (-18, -20) wu touching no BSP surface, its height wobbling,
and never moved (no placed object stands within 8 wu of it).

Those runs used a 1.5 wu grid for every place. Under the final rule, ten of
the eleven come out the same; `koth_hill_5`, on uneven ground, goes from 26
positions to 64 from a 1 wu grid.

### Waves

`blam.bots.waves` gives every labelled place squads that come to hold it:
`squads` single-actor squads named `wave_<place>_<k>` (for example
`wave_koth_hill_4_0`), of the kinds `kinds` names in turn (entries of
`bots.types`), standing on the main ground in a ring `distance` wu outside
its boundary, spread round it and facing it, where nothing else stands within
2.5 wu above the ground (a rock lying on Pelican Warfare's terrain had two
squads standing on it with no sector, or inside it, never moving). Their **first task is the
place's**, baked in, so `ai_place` alone sends them: nothing has to follow
with an order. Their team is the kind's, or `covenant`. A labelled object
that is not held keeps its squads under `wave_unheld_<j>_<k>`, which no
director asks for. Without `waves` nothing changes.

Pelican Warfare's director (`warfare_waves` in
`native/lobby/warfare_runtime.h`) places them; see
[pelican_warfare_waves.md](pelican_warfare_waves.md#4-covenant-waves).

## Identity: which actor is which bot

Bot actors come from a pool (`BP_EliteBipedActor_C` and friends; a pooled one
waits at the origin), and an erased AI leaves its actor where it stood for the
next placement to reuse. So bots are placed one at a time, and the bot just
placed is the actor that came out of the pool, or jumped more than 4 m, since
its `ai_place` (a jump between two scans, 0.25 s apart, which only a teleport
makes). An actor is that bot's until the `Kill` that names it. A Spartan bot's
actor is the players' class, `BP_SpartansBipedActor_C`, so an actor a player
spawned in (their `player_spawn` names it) is never taken for a bot.

The actors come from `Scripts/bipeds.lua`, one `NotifyOnNewObject` on the
bipeds' native ancestor armed when the HUD loads, before any map. It sees every
biped actor as it is made, the pools a map makes as it loads included, so a
match never walks the object array for them. `FindAllOf` costs about 23 ms a
class in a match:

- Scanning six classes every tick held the game thread 135 ms three times a
  second.
- Scanning the seven classes once when bots started (until MJOLNIRHud 0.19.1)
  made a 108–129 ms Hud tick 3 s into hosted matches, and again on up to three
  rescans.
- A watch on a Blueprint class's own path needs the class loaded, and a
  Blueprint class can be unloaded and loaded again between maps at a new
  address. Spartans have no pool waiting, so a match starting before the first
  spawn (Forge on Yoyorast) once saw none of its Spartan bots. Each placement
  looked like a squad the map lacks, so each bot was placed four times and given
  up on: thirty-two AI with no seat on the board. A native class is never
  unloaded.

A scan (every 0.25 s) reads only the actors out of the pool at the last read:
the bots, their bodies left standing, and the players. Every pooled actor of a
class is read only from the moment a bot of that class is due to be placed
until it is seen, plus a full read every 5 s. The step uses only actors out
of the pool, and a placement must see its actor leave the pool. Reading all of
Blood Gulch's 271 pooled bipeds every scan was about 2,200 calls a second:
with 8 bots, the Hud tick went from 11.6 to 5.0 ms/s (MJOLNIRHud 0.19.1,
`tools/tests/test_bots_scan.lua`).

As a backstop, if the watch could not be armed, bots start with one scan of
each class, and a placement that times out scans its own kind's class once
before placing again (three a match at most). A try that gives up erases its
squad.

## Names on the clients

A client hears bot seats in the host's relayed incidents
([multiplayer_hud.md](multiplayer_hud.md)) and needs their names. When it
meets a seat it cannot name it asks (`ServerExecRPC "MJOLNIR|bots?"`), holding
those lines up to 3 s; the host answers that player alone with
`MJOLNIR|bots|100=Nadia (bot);101=...`, and tells every player once when its
bots change. In a team game each seat carries its side's letter
(`R100=Nadia (bot);B101=...`), which a client from before sides skips: a
relayed line has no biped to read the side from. Once it has the roster, a
client drops its own copies of AI kills and deaths (they name the AI -1) and
counts the host's.

## Making a map with bots

The map needs bot squads and pathfinding in its scenario, so it is baked with
`blam.bots`. Blood Gulch, from the hub install's own files and
`examples/levels/bloodgulch_bots.bake.level.json` (the hub level.json with the
loader-only keys left out, plus the `bots` block the PC 1 tests used):

```bash
# the installed BSP, as the bake's --bsp payload
mjolnir extract --out tags --filter "solo/bgl/"
mjolnir level bake examples/levels/bloodgulch_bots.bake.level.json --standalone BGL \
  --bsp 8=tags/Levels/Halo1/Solo/BGL/_Generated_/BSP_01_1_Start.scenario_structure_bsp \
  --world-object /Game/Levels/Halo1/Solo/BGL/BGL.BGL --out-dir out
```

Every machine in the match needs the same scenario. The test install put the
result beside the hub's as `pakchunk997-MJOLNIRBOTS-BGL_9_P`, whose `_9_P`
outranked the hub release's containers at the time. On launcher 0.24.0 and
newer every hub container sorts above a hand-named one, so install a local
build with `mjolnir dev install <container> --name <name>`, which loads above
the hub release ([chunk_numbering.md](chunk_numbering.md)).

### Giving a published map bots

Bots cannot be added at run time: the simulation reads the squads, zone,
objective and pathfinding from the scenario when the map loads. But nothing
except the scenario changes, so a published map pack is all it takes:

```bash
HCE_PAKS=".../Meteorite/Content/Paks"   python tools/level/add_bots.py ce-blood-gulch-2.1.0.mjolnir --runtime ^1.16.0 --sign
```

For each pack, `tools/level/add_bots.py` takes the map container's BSP and
world out of the pack, bakes the shipped level file (less the keys only the
loader reads) with `defs/level/bots.json` as `blam.bots`, and packs the next
minor version with the new map container in place of the old, and the bake's
`<CODE>.bots.json` as `map/bots.json`. The bots stand on the map's own player
starts. It stops unless every other container, and every package of the map
container but the scenario, comes out byte-identical. Rebaking also brings the map's Forge palettes up to the
current bake's (the only other difference from a 2.1.0 scenario).
`--bake-only` rebakes and checks without packing.

A weapon in `bots.json` that a map's palette lacks is left out of that
map's turn. A map whose level file already has `blam.bots` is refused, and
so is a container with more than one BSP or world.

## Not done

- Spartan bots all wear the default armour colour.
- Slayer's own script counts player kills only. The HUD's board counts bot
  kills, and the host's HUD ends the match when a bot or a bot's team reaches
  the score.
- Team games: a bot keeps its side when players join or leave (the teams
  can end uneven). A fireteam client's view of the sides
  (the roster's letters, its own copy of the units' teams) was tested on two
  PCs on 2026-11-07 (Team Slayer, 4 bots): both boards agree.
- Players' campaign teams: in a team game with bots a player's unit is
  covenant (red) or flood (blue) instead of no campaign team. Nothing else
  seen reads it in a Megalo game (player against player follows the
  multiplayer teams), but only Blood Gulch Team Slayer has been played so.
- Not yet seen in a whole match with the fix: what a side's bots do after a
  player of that side shoots one (the AI turns on a betrayer in campaign,
  which until now no one could see, since every bot shot every player
  anyway); whether bots now follow players of their side as allies do in
  campaign; and why, in one isolated run, a flood grunt and a covenant elite
  of the two sides stood 4 wu apart without fighting while the elite killed
  the host.
- Free for All: every bot is covenant, so bots never fight each other.
- A bot that falls or kills itself gets no suicide on the board.
- Maps with more starts than squads (15) leave the rest unused. A map
  published before 2026-10-31 has no `map/bots.json`, so each bot comes back
  on the start it first used, whichever side is there.
- A map published before 2026-10-31 keeps the copy of its collision at the
  shell's height, where bots lose their place (Blood Gulch's flag-room floors
  above all), and has no `areas` for the HUD to send a stuck bot to: a
  rebake brings both. Only Blood Gulch is measured.
- A placement sometimes takes an actor that stays where the bot came in
  while the bot walks off. The HUD reads the bot's deaths from that actor,
  so it would neither see that bot die nor bring it back.
- Elites are 0.70 tall on the host only (the lobby DLL, "Bots frozen in
  place" above). A fireteam client's elites keep 0.8; whether its view of
  one stutters at a low doorway is not tested on two PCs. The model is drawn
  at full height, so an elite's head may show through a lintel it passes
  under (not looked at). Other maps are not checked for low doorways.
- Why a bot's AI sometimes leaves its sleeping body asleep is not known.
- The HUD sends bots to hunt players they cannot reach. A map published
  before 2026-10-31 still has as many area tasks as it baked areas, so some
  of the HUD's roaming orders go nowhere until it is rebaked.
- No jump, hoist or ladder links, so bots do not use teleporters, lifts or
  man cannons, and ground reached only that way stays apart. Night Lockout's
  two levels meet only by drops and jumps: its bots play the lower one (16
  of its 33 starts; the upper level holds 14).
- Some converted shells keep a copy of the vertices along each seam between
  pieces (13 of the 48 hub maps). Those seams are cracks of width 0 now and
  join like any other.

notes.title: Sound mixer
notes.summary: /sounds (or /mixer) in match chat, or mjolnir_sounds in the console, opens a panel over the match with a slider for each sound the map plays. Each player sets their own levels. They are kept for that map on that PC and read again whenever the map loads.
notes.body:
`/sounds` (or `/mixer`) in match chat, or `mjolnir_sounds` in the console,
opens a panel over the match with a slider for each sound the map plays.
Each player sets their own levels. They are kept for that map on that PC
and read again whenever the map loads.

![The mixer on Zanzibar](/docs-images/sound_mixer_zan.png)

## What it lists

One row for each sound tag the Level Loader plays (the level file's
`source`, the Halo 2 or CE tag path):

| Kind shown | What it is | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BACKGROUND | a map-wide loop (Halo 2's follow the BSP zone you are in) | `environment.sounds.background` |
| N PLACES | a sound scenery loop placed N times | `environment.sounds.emitters` |
| NOW AND THEN, a-b S | Halo 2 detail one-shots, a random variant every a to b seconds | `environment.sounds.details` |
| MACHINE | a turning machine's one-shots | `gears[].motion.events` |
| DOOR | a moving machine's open, opened and button sounds | `doors[].sounds` |

**ALL SOUNDS** at the top scales every row together. A dot marks the
sounds heard from where the player stands: a background in the current
zone, or a placed sound within its falloff.

Levels run from -24 dB to +12 dB in 1 dB steps. Sliding to the far left
mutes the sound. **RESET ALL** puts every row back at 0 dB. **DONE**
closes the panel and saves the file.

## How it works

- `mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/mixer.lua` holds the levels.
  `factor(key)` returns the sound's level times ALL SOUNDS as a linear
  gain.
  - `syncVolumes` multiplies each loop's volume by that factor beside the
    game's volume sliders.
  - `details.lua`, `gears.lua` and `doors.lua` multiply each one-shot by
    it when it plays.
- The panel is `WBP_MJOLNIRSoundMixer`, cooked into chunk 984 by
  `build_mjolnir_ui.py`.
  - It is generic: 12 rows that Lua names, fills and collapses, with pages
    for longer lists.
  - Its sliders send no events Lua can take, so the loader reads them 10
    times a second, only while the panel is open.
  - While open, input goes to the UI, so the player stands still. DONE,
    or `/sounds` again, hands input back.
- Levels are saved to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Meteorite\Saved\MJOLNIR_SoundMix_<map>.json`,
  keyed by tag path, so a rebuilt map keeps them:

```json
{ "version": 1, "map": "ZAN", "levels": { "*": -3, "sound\ambience\zanzibar\zanzibar_ocean_loop\zanzibar_ocean_loop": 4 } }
```

- Without the cooked panel (an older `pakchunk984-MJOLNIRUI`), the
  command logs that the panel is not installed. Sounds then play at
  their built levels.

A level file built before door and gear sounds carried their tag
(`gen_ce_level.py` writes `source` now) keys those rows by the wave's
path, and names door rows by the door's tag and event.

notes.title: KOTH field visuals
notes.summary: The hill uses a dedicated energy-field material so its boundary stays readable while players can see through it. Restrained moving plasma, a visible translucent veil and glowing rails define the field; a layered beacon 1.1 metres in diameter and a ground anchor mark the centre.…
notes.body:
The hill uses a dedicated energy-field material so its boundary stays readable
while players can see through it. Restrained moving plasma, a visible translucent
veil and glowing rails define the field; a layered beacon 1.1 metres in diameter
and a ground anchor mark the centre. The hill's state colours remain
gold when empty, cyan for you, orange-red for another player, violet when
contested, and the owning team's colour in team modes.

The runtime is `mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/hill.lua`. These are client-side visual
actors: changing their rendering does not change the simulation's scoring
boundary. The existing player/height approximation and multiplayer limitations
are described in [game_modes.md](game_modes.md#34-king-and-oddball-on-converted-ce-maps).

## Assets and reserved container

**Shader chunk 966 is reserved for KOTH and the CTF flag's cloth.** Its shared
shader library must keep the `Meteorite_Chunk966` identity when packaging and
installing. The cloth master (`/Game/MJOLNIR/Cloth/M_CE_FlagCloth`,
`Scripts/build_flag_cloth.py`) shares the chunk rather than taking a number of
its own: the launcher numbers other hub containers 900 + their load order, so
a new 9NN number would collide with some player's map container. A 966 built
by `build_koth.ps1` alone lacks the cloth master; MJOLNIRLevelLoader then
moves the cloth's strips from Lua.

| Asset | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/Game/MJOLNIR/KOTH/M_KOTH_Field` | Translucent perimeter field and glowing rails |
| `/Game/MJOLNIR/KOTH/M_KOTH_Beacon` | Central vertical beacon |
| `pakchunk966-MJOLNIRKOTH-Windows.{pak,utoc,ucas}` | Dedicated KOTH materials and shader library |

`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_koth_materials.py` creates the materials
and their chunk label. The classic `M_CE_Plasma` masters are unchanged. If the
dedicated KOTH assets are unavailable, the runtime falls back to the existing
CE plasma material; if neither is available, the direction line remains.

The container ships in the CE runtime pack from 1.19.0
(`tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh`). The launcher names it
`pakchunk966-MJOLNIRHUB-mjolnir-ce-runtime-<j>_P`: `hub::shader_chunk` keeps the
966 because the container carries a shader library. The helper below is for
trying a new build of the materials on one PC; take its container out of Paks
again afterwards, or it hides whatever the hub is missing.

## Build locally

Use UE 5.5 and this branch's `Meteorite` cook project. The fork-layout plugins,
shader settings and property retargeting are required; see the
[project setup](../unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/README.md). On a fresh checkout, build
the two target receipts first from the repository root:

```powershell
$build = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.5\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat'
$project = "$PWD\unreal\MJOLNIRMaterials\Meteorite.uproject"
& $build MeteoriteEditor Win64 Development "-Project=$project" -WaitMutex -MaxParallelActions=4
& $build Meteorite Win64 Shipping "-Project=$project" -WaitMutex -MaxParallelActions=4
cargo build -p blam-cli
```

Build a reviewable package:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/ue/build_koth.ps1
```

The helper runs the material builder through `editor_cmd.ps1`, then `cook.ps1`.
It rejects compiler errors, stale logs, failed fork-layout validation, and a
missing successful retarget of the two KOTH materials. Each run creates a new
directory under ignored `.dream-loop/koth-package/` containing `content/`,
editor/cook logs, an input snapshot and a SHA-256 `receipt.json`. Inputs must
remain unchanged through packaging. `-OutputDir` selects another package root.
Nothing is installed by default.

The default CPU mask is `0x0F` (four logical CPUs), following the cook script's
documented all-core power issue. `-Mask` selects a different nonzero affinity;
the helper temporarily overrides `MJ_CPU_MASK` and re-applies affinity to its
own editor and shader-worker descendants when the editor resets it. It restores
the environment afterward. Build and cook share the project's named mutex, so
another conversion cannot replace staging before the package is copied.

## Install and inspect

Close the game, then explicitly request a build and install:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/ue/build_koth.ps1 -Install
# Or select an install explicitly (Xbox: the directory named Content):
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/ue/build_koth.ps1 -Install -GameDir 'C:\Games\Halo Campaign Evolved'
```

Steam libraries are discovered automatically; `MJOLNIR_GAME_DIR` is also
supported. Installation refuses while `HaloCampaignEvolved` is running. It
copies only the three named chunk966 files into `Meteorite/Content/Paks`, saves
previous versions under the run's `previous-install/`, checks installed hashes,
and writes `installed.json`. Copy or hash failures trigger rollback of those
files while the game remains stopped; a failure record preserves recovery
details. It does not deploy HUD Lua or other containers.
Deploy the branch's HUD scripts separately using the normal local mod workflow.
To undo an installed update, close the game and restore those three previous
files. For a first install with no previous files, remove only the three KOTH
files; the HUD will use its fallback. Keep the package and backups until the
visual check is complete. This helper does not publish a release.

For live checks, follow [game automation](game_automation.md): launch, finish
stock sign-in, verify `mjolnir_auto state` reports `signed_in=1`, then host a
private match with `mjolnir_auto host PRS koth private` or use BGL. Confirm the
loaded mode: released maps without KOTH in their mode list can fall back to
Slayer. A bridge-loaded visual preview in that case checks rendering only.
Capture the
3D world with `foreground:true`; the default window capture can show a black
world. Compare the hill from outside, inside, and across a roof edge, and check
empty, owned and contested states. A stand-in player list is useful for colour
inspection but does not prove live multiplayer state replication.

## Validation status

The branch-local Editor Development and Shipping targets built successfully.
`lua tools/tests/test_hill_marker.lua` passes, including mocked material
selection, actor reuse, parameter updates, material recreation, fallback,
retry and visibility checks. The build helper passed six temporary-filesystem
simulations covering installation, rollback and input-change detection.

The final material cook compiled both materials, passed fork-layout validation,
retargeted both packages and installed the three chunk966 files with matching
hashes. The local evidence is under
`.dream-loop/koth-package/20261105-025531-639818/` (ignored build output).

Live bridge previews loaded the workspace's hill module in private PRS and BGL
matches; the final wider beacon and stronger field were inspected on BGL.
Gold and cyan were visually sampled; other state transitions are covered by
the Lua tests. The installed released HUD differs from this branch, so these
previews do not establish deployed HUD integration or end-to-end KOTH scoring.
Two-PC replication and a controlled final-effect GPU performance comparison
have not been performed. Generated concept images remain design references;
the screenshots capture the running game. No release was published.

notes.title: Pelican Warfare prototype
notes.summary: PWR uses the existing Blam simulation and native Megalo interpreter. Unreal renders the authored map, objective fields and cosmetic parachute. Lua stages the mode, handles a Space key event and presents a bounded native snapshot; it does not implement movement, captures,…
notes.body:
PWR uses the existing Blam simulation and native Megalo interpreter. Unreal
renders the authored map, objective fields and cosmetic parachute. Lua stages
the mode, handles a Space key event and presents a bounded native snapshot;
it does not implement movement, captures, respawns, scoring or match timers.

## Current alpine expansion

The v5 world has a **2 × 2 km playable terrain** with three Forerunner sites,
connected vehicle roads, four crossings, a descending river and a lake.
Its surrounding 8 km mountain field is a render-only backdrop. The gameplay
area has not expanded to 8 km. Gaea supplies eroded terrain; Unreal Landscape,
Nanite scenery and baked PCG instances render it. Blam retains authoritative
collision, vehicles and the native Warfare rules.

The current visual build uses `levels/warfare/pwr/upgrade-v5-visual5.json` and
the isolated `world-v5-visual5` conversion. Its forest contains 4,470 trees,
804 rocks and 279,388 grass instances. Water uses native Fluid Flux surfaces
and saved flow/depth/foam states; this is baked playback, not a map-wide
real-time fluid simulation. See [water integration](flux_water.md),
[surface materials](pwr_surface_materials.md),
[mature pine](pwr_mature_pine.md) and
[terrain preservation](pwr_terrain_preservation.md) for their build contracts.

The original basin commands and acceptance history below describe the first
prototype. Do not apply its `prepare_runtime.py` step to the expansion:
the expansion uses `refresh_native_probes.py` with
`vehicle-spawn-policy-v1.json` to preserve verified vehicle spawn heights and
bind probes to the newly compiled collision. Local installation receipts and
fresh native acceptance evidence live under `out/pwr/world-v5`.

## Play the installed preview

Select map **PWR / Pelican Warfare** and mode **PELICAN WARFARE** in the
MJOLNIR lobby, then start a private match. The installed preview starts with
one player after a five-second warmup. Press **Space** to leave the Pelican
and again to deploy the parachute. Exit from the Pelican is automatic at the end
of its flight; the parachute is not. A player who never pulls it, or pulls it
too late, meets the ground faster than 20 m/s and dies (`WARFARE_SPLAT_SINK`).
Stand on A, B or C on foot for fifteen seconds to capture a neutral site.
Owned uncontested sites score once per second. After a death you respawn at
your base and board your team's waiting Pelican, which leaves with everyone
aboard on the next minute of combat; the target is 500 control points.

## Rules and build

`mjolnir megalo write --mode warfare --vehicle-label-pool --out warfare.mglo`
builds the variant. Install it in `MJOLNIRLevelLoader/variants/warfare.mglo`.
The bundled `mode_descriptors.lua` registers the mode only for PWR and shares
its lobby, loader and scoreboard metadata. The installed variant controls
the score threshold; persisted settings from another mode cannot change it.
Warfare opts into a same-mode postgame rotation on its supported maps. With
only PWR installed, no ballots replay PWR Warfare; LOBBY returns to manual
map/mode selection. Other modes retain the existing mixed-map, mixed-mode vote.

Defaults are two connected players, 60 seconds of warmup, 60 seconds of
insertion, first to 500 control points, or 20 minutes of combat. The three
neutral `koth_hill` markers use spawn sequences 0, 1 and 2, matching the
three `koth_hills` entries in `level.json`. Living players on foot capture;
vehicle occupants do not. One side alone takes a neutral site in fifteen
seconds; changing an enemy site takes fifteen seconds to neutralize and
fifteen more to capture (`--capture-seconds`, 8 before 2026-11-22).
Covenant alone take a neutral site in thirty (`--covenant-capture-seconds`). Extra teammates do not accelerate capture. Opposing
presence stops capture and scoring. An owned empty site continues to earn
one point per second. Kills do not score. Each death respawns the player at
their permanent Red or Blue home after five seconds, with unlimited lives
and no suicide/betrayal delay; the native adapter then puts them aboard the
next reinforcement wave (see [waves and reinforcements](pelican_warfare_waves.md)).
A wave leaves every `reinforcement.interval_seconds` (60) of combat and flies
`flight_seconds` (30) of the insertion route, both from `layout.json`.

CLI flags allow explicit development variants: `--minimum-players`,
`--warmup-seconds`, `--insertion-seconds`, `--capture-seconds`,
`--warfare-minutes` and `--score`. The lobby's fixed settings describe the
shipped defaults; development timing variants are not editable lobby rules.

## Original basin build and installation

Run these commands from the repository root in PowerShell 7. They require
the project's existing Rust/MSVC, Python, Blender, HEK and Unreal 5.5 toolchains.
The commands use the Steam install and the PWR conversion/work directories
in `levels/warfare/pwr/upgrade.json`; change those explicit paths for another
installation. See [the PWR source README](../levels/warfare/pwr/README.md) for
the isolated HEK build and initial CE conversion that produce `pwr.level.json`.

Build the CLI, the map/canopy helper executables and both native DLLs:

```powershell
cargo build --release -p blam-cli
cargo build --release -p ue-asset --examples
cargo build --release -p blam-pack --examples
cargo build --release -p ue-iostore --example extract_file
pwsh -NoProfile -File native/lobby/build.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File native/map_registry/build.ps1
$env:MJOLNIR = (Resolve-Path target/release/mjolnir.exe).Path
$env:EXAMPLES = (Resolve-Path target/release/examples).Path
```

The `ue-asset` examples include `mesh_rewrite` and `retarget_package`; the
`blam-pack` examples include `package_add` and `native_material_clone`.
`extract_file` belongs to `ue-iostore`. Keep both environment variables set
in the PowerShell session used below: the bake stage otherwise defaults to
an older server-list worktree CLI and `C:/haloce/target/debug/examples`, which
can silently mix tools from different checkouts. Reapply these assignments
when resuming a stage in a fresh terminal.

The map-registry build also rebuilds and links `mjolnir-mglo-cabi`. It must
match the variant grammar in this checkout. Replacing only the Lobby DLL
leaves the installed map-registry staging validator at its old version.

Build the Pelican and original canopy into staging directories, then patch,
cook and assemble the map's private visual upgrade:

```powershell
$pwrGame = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Halo Campaign Evolved'
$pwrPaks = Join-Path $pwrGame 'Meteorite\Content\Paks'
pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/level/build_warfare_pelican.ps1 -Paks $pwrPaks -OutDir out/pwr/pelican
python levels/warfare/pwr/canopy/build.py --paks $pwrPaks --preview
python levels/warfare/pwr/prepare_runtime.py --level C:/haloce/ce_conversions/warfare/PWR/converted/pwr.level.json
python levels/warfare/pwr/upgrade.py --stages land,foliage,swap,collision
python levels/warfare/pwr/upgrade.py --stages editor,cook,bake,assemble
```

Current private container assignments are canopy 964, landscape 965 and
Pelican 971. The runtime installer takes the generated container names;
it does not hard-code a stale chunk number. Preserve the map's capture
markers, permanent team spawns and named flags when rebaking.

Close the game before installing. The map install is local and creates no
hub listing. The runtime installer copies the complete Loader, Lobby and HUD
`Scripts` trees, both native DLLs, the variant plus its layout and the staged
Pelican/canopy containers. This is a single compatible runtime: copying only
the new Warfare scripts onto an older release can leave missing helper APIs.

```powershell
python levels/warfare/pwr/upgrade.py --stages install --local-install
pwsh -NoProfile -File levels/warfare/pwr/install_runtime.ps1 -Game $pwrGame -SoloPreview
```

`-SoloPreview` builds a one-player, five-second warmup variant for the private
test. Omit that flag to restore the normal two-player, 60-second warmup.
The user's current local installation uses `-SoloPreview` with the default
500-point target, recorded in
[`out/pwr/runtime-20261108-224928/install-receipt.json`](../out/pwr/runtime-20261108-224928/install-receipt.json).
The five-point variants below were acceptance-test artifacts, not the final
installed score limit.
The installer writes `out/pwr/runtime-<timestamp>/install-receipt.json` and
backs up each replaced runtime file before copying it. Standalone variant
generation and validation, without installation, are:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force out/pwr/variants | Out-Null
target/release/mjolnir.exe megalo write --mode warfare --vehicle-label-pool --out out/pwr/variants/warfare.mglo
target/release/mjolnir.exe megalo validate out/pwr/variants/warfare.mglo
target/release/mjolnir.exe megalo read out/pwr/variants/warfare.mglo
```

Launch and sign in at the frontend, then explicitly host a private PWR test:

```powershell
node tools/mcp/game/cli.mjs launch
node native/lobby/smoke-warfare.mjs --host --jump --respawn --capture-a --seconds=90
```

The probe waits for frontend sign-in and requests `host PWR warfare private`.
Its explicit flags request jump/deployment, kill the landed test player once
to verify respawn, and teleport that player to capture A. It writes JSONL
evidence under `out/pwr/`. To observe an already running match without those
actions, use `node native/lobby/smoke-warfare.mjs --seconds=50`.

After insertion, `node native/lobby/smoke-warfare-vehicles.mjs --drive --screenshots`
checks a private active layout-2 match with exactly one local player, then boards
the home fleet's Warthog, Scorpion and Banshee through the installed probe volumes.
It verifies each actual salted vehicle parent before four bounded one-second W
inputs and records body displacement and player/vehicle health. `--team=blue`
selects the other fleet; `--seconds=3..5` adjusts total input time.
`--banshee-ascend` additionally holds Space and requires upward displacement;
that input binding still needs a live check. The harness leaves the final
Banshee occupied, does not end the match, and makes no game calls without
`--drive`. JSONL evidence and optional screenshots go to `out/pwr/`.

## Native bridge and presentation

The loader requires level metadata `warfare: {protocol: 20569, layout_revision: 3}`
and opens `MJOLNIRLobby/native/mjolnir_lobby.dll` with a configuration
containing `warfare-config 2`, `map PWR`, `layout 3` and `protocol 20569`.
That number is the map's layout protocol; the Megalo rules publish their own
revision in slot 2 (20571), so a rules change needs no new map.
Its four exported Lua entrypoints
are `mjolnir_warfare_open`, `close`, `action` and `pump` (all with the
`mjolnir_warfare_` prefix). Space sends only a jump/deploy request. The native
adapter validates the simulation build, scenario, engine, instance,
Megalo protocol and the four baked flight endpoint positions before acting.
The endpoint check rejects an old PWR scenario even if its JSON was updated.
Movement remains on the owning simulation
peer; the host controls the named transports. Late joins and later
respawns board the next reinforcement wave from the home base.

Global number slots are phase 0, phase age in ticks 1, rules magic 20571
at 2, the clock 3, connected count before combat and the defeat clock from
combat on 4, scratch 5–6, Red/Blue
score 7–8 and A/B/C site states 9–11. Phases are warmup 0, insertion 1, combat 2
and complete 3. A site state packs `owner + 4 × (red present + 2 × blue present)
+ 16 × (progress + 17)`: owner neutral 0, Red 1, Blue 2 in the low two bits, and
capture progress in sixteenths toward Red (+16) or Blue (−16), counted against
thresholds fixed when the variant is built (`SiteState` in `warfare.rs`). Steps,
not ticks, keep the replicated value from changing every tick. A value under 16
is an owner alone (older variants, or before combat). Slot 3, the clock,
counts the warmup down in whole seconds in phase 0 (-1 while fewer than the
minimum players are connected), publishes the configured insertion duration
in phase 1, then resets to zero and counts combat seconds in phase 2; the
reinforcement schedule is derived from it, and the HUD shows it as MATCH TIME.
Phase, age, magic, clock,
scores, owners and slot 4 (the connected count, then the defeat clock) have high
replication priority,
and scratch remains local. Native code reads this state; Megalo owns it.
An absent team's native score operand is -1 in the supported build; the
published score mirror clamps that sentinel to zero without creating or
changing the absent team's engine score.

### The Covenant can win

If the Covenant hold all three sites (owner 3) for `covenant_hold_seconds`
(default 60; `mjolnir megalo write --covenant-hold-seconds`, 0 turns it off),
the match ends and both teams lose. Slot 4 carries it from combat on: the full
hold when combat starts, one less each combat second while every chosen site is
the Covenant's, back to the full hold the second any site is not, and -1 when
the rule is off. At 0 the host sets phase 3 and ends the round; the end trigger
checks the three owners again, so a stray 0 cannot end a match. The HUD's line
says THE COVENANT HOLD EVERY ZONE with the time left while it runs, OPERATION
FAILED at the end, and the post-game title is THE COVENANT WIN
(`Match.winnerTitle`, read by `Scoreboard.winner`). Rules revision 20571 began
this: the HUD and DLL reject an older variant, so HUD, DLL and variant ship
together.

`levels/warfare/pwr/layout.json` generates `native/lobby/warfare_layout.h`.
The native build regenerates it; the portable test runner rejects stale output.
Layout 2 uses a 2 km scenario, a ±950 m play area and 240 m flight altitude.
The host projects desired world velocity into the verified full 3D vehicle
axes, corrects bounded route/altitude error and caps speed at 30 m/s.
Default automatic exit occurs at 54 of 60 seconds; explicit development
durations scale the exit time without exceeding that speed cap. Descent
has a 90-second timeout and accepts settled landings at any height inside
the play volume. Slopes keep the canopy state until vertical movement settles.

The parachute opens only when the player pulls it; nothing opens it for them.
The descent stays protected from falling damage, and the host decides the
landing at the first real ground contact:
- if the descent controller's sink is above `WARFARE_SPLAT_SINK` (20 m/s), it
  sends `WF_SPLAT`, a host-authority `(unit_kill (player_get N))`;
- freefall reaches 55-63 m/s;
- a canopy settles at 10.5-18.5 m/s, so an open canopy always lands.

`test_warfare.c` covers the outcomes:
- with no pull, the 550 m exit hits at about 53 m/s after 10.7 s, at every
  tick rate;
- a pull 0.4 s out still dies;
- a pull 4 s out lands.
- a joiner under canopy lands on the host (`test_remote_landing`).
- On two PCs (2026-11-24), a joiner pulled at 3 s and landed under canopy on
  its own screen. The host's copy stayed in freefall throughout and logged
  the landing (stage 3 to 5) with no splat, and the joiner lived. A joiner
  with no pull died on impact, from the engine, with its own HUD saying the
  warning, the yell and the splat line.

The splat is judged from the body's own last airborne sink, not the host's
simulation of the descent. The host is told only of a joiner's cabin jump,
never their parachute pull, so its controller copy stays in freefall; judged
from that, every joiner died on landing (caught in review before release).

Before 2026-11-24 the chute opened itself near 76 m; the user asked for the
fall to be the player's responsibility. Bots are AI bipeds, not players, and
never ride.
These expansion changes require live validation independently of the smaller
prototype's successful insertion tests recorded below.

The loader publishes `MJOLNIRLobby/native/warfare_state.txt` every 500 ms;
the HUD reads at the same interval. The `warfare-state 3` format includes
the reinforcement timing, layout revision and configured insertion duration.
The HUD checks the complete format,
ready/status flags, mirrored globals, exact uint64 instance text and current
PWR world. Two advancing tick/time samples are required before accepting
a file or a new instance. Live samples expire after two seconds without
advancing; a verified final snapshot remains usable during stopped postgame
and the engine's brief same-instance round reset before lobby travel.
Malformed or stale files cannot change score. Team CONTROL totals and the
winner come from accepted native scores, never summed player incidents.
Individual control cells show a dash; kills and deaths remain visible.
Final standings allow 1.5 seconds for the final publication to arrive.

The status line gives the warmup countdown, boarding, Space-to-jump, exiting,
Space-to-deploy, canopy, landing/active and failed-deployment information, and
for a waiting reinforcement rider the time to departure and whom they watch.
During insertion every line ends with ZONES OPEN IN 0:23 (from the published
insertion length and its tick count, `Warfare.insertionLeft`), and once a rider
has landed the line is ZONES OPEN IN 0:23 / PREPARE TO CAPTURE A, B AND C. The
last ten seconds of warmup, and of insertion, also count down large in the
middle of the screen (`warfare_countdown.lua`), then DEPLOY or CAPTURE for two
seconds. During combat it
gives way to three slim zone bars stacked in the top left (`WBP_MJOLNIRWarfareZones`,
chunk 958 beside the tactical map with its two hexagon badge textures from
`tools/ue/draw_zone_badges.py`, filled by `warfare_zones.lua`). Each row is a
hexagon badge with the zone's letter in the owner's colour (purple for the
Covenant), then the state word (NEUTRAL / RED / BLUE / COVENANT / CAPTURING /
NEUTRALIZING / UNDER ATTACK / OVERRUN / CLEARING / CONTESTED) with a pip for each
team standing in the zone, over the capture bar. The badge's outline turns gold on
the zone the local player stands in.
A site changing hands puts "Red team captured zone B" (or "… neutralized zone B")
in the kill feed on every client from its own snapshot. Three fixed holographic
fields and A/B/C waypoints still mark the sites in the world. Contest and progress
come from Megalo's published site state, never from rendered positions.

`warfare_canopy.lua` uses the original
`/Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/PWR/SM_PWR_Parachute.SM_PWR_Parachute` mesh, a 274.4 cm
relative Z offset and uniform scale 4.1166 from the canopy build metadata.
It disables collision and shadows and attaches once to an existing validated
cached biped. Unreal follows the attachment without a Lua movement loop.
Only native stage 4 displays it; landing, death, missing/stale state and map
exit hide it. Native drop stages currently exist for owning local players,
so remote canopy visibility needs a verified replicated stage channel before
it can be claimed. The cosmetic asset is optional for gameplay.

A loaded mesh is held only as a handle. Once no parachute uses it, the garbage
collector frees it, so a dead handle is loaded again. Before that fix, a
respawn's drop fell back to the legacy canopy (2026-11-24).

### Voice (local testing only)

`MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/warfare_voice.lua` gives Warfare two voices: Cortana talks
the player through the match, and the announcer names the game, the zones and
the result. Every line comes from a change between two accepted warfare
snapshots, inside the existing HUD tick, with no loop of its own. Each machine
decides from replicated state, so a joiner hears its own match:

| When | Who | Line |
|---|---|---|
| warmup begins / 20 s left | announcer / Cortana | "Pelican Warfare!" / gear up |
| insertion launches, 3 s in | Cortana | wheels up; the briefing (after the launch line) |
| seated 11 s in an insertion Pelican | Cortana | "that's your stop", after the briefing (riders are put out when the flight ends) |
| freefall below 320 m / 170 m | Cortana | "pretty close to the ground" / "Chief! Pull your chute!" |
| out of the air, still falling faster than 20 m/s, under 30 m (the splat) | Cortana | "Well. I tried to warn you." / "That's going to leave a mark." / "I'll log that as a hard landing." |
| combat begins | announcer | "Capture the zones!" |
| 10 s before a Covenant wave | Cortana | the first always; later ones only while no Covenant stand in a zone (a wave at the cap is skipped) |
| Covenant step into a zone | announcer / Cortana | "Zone X contested!" if it is ours, else "Contact!" after 20 s of quiet |
| a zone changes hands | announcer / Cortana | secured, lost, the enemy took it, the Covenant took it, retaken |
| the Covenant hold two / all three / 10 s left / broken | Cortana | escalating warnings (the all-zones line replaces that update's single-zone line) |
| a reinforcement Pelican boards | Cortana | "Your ride's here" |
| the end | announcer, Cortana | Victory / Defeat; "Not bad, Chief"; "We've lost the island" |

Mechanics:

- **One at a time.** One line plays at a time, through `SpawnSound2D` at the dialogue slider.
- **Turns with the announcer.** The loader's announcer queue (`MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/announcer.lua`) and this voice share `MJOLNIR.voiceUntil`. A calm line waits for the other voice; the player's own fall does not.
- **Urgency.** A more urgent line cuts a calmer one off (priority 3 is the player's own fall).
- **Staleness.** A line that waits past its time-to-live is dropped.
- **Baselines.** A new instance, or the first sample after the state went stale, only sets a baseline.

The loader no longer announces Warfare at the first spawn. Its start event
used to say "King of the Hill"; `startEvent` is now `warfare_game_start`,
which has no `events.json` row.

The waves are generated by local voice models (`tools/voice/README.md`):
- they live under `/Game/MJOLNIR/Sounds/Warfare`;
- they are cooked into `pakchunk950` by `unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_warfare_voice.py`;
- `warfare_voice_lines.lua` lists them with their lengths.

**They are not shipped.** Without the container, the first wave fails to load,
the voice logs that once, and it stays silent for the session.

Solo on PC 1 (2026-11-24), across several runs, the log shows these lines
played on their triggers:
- the title and warmup, the launch, the briefing and the call to jump
  (after the briefing);
- the two altitude warnings, and the splat line after a no-pull death;
- zones open, secured, contested, lost and taken;
- the first wave, a later wave's warning, and a landing on a zone nobody
  holds;
- two zones, all three (one line, not two), ten seconds, and the Covenant
  win;
- reinforcements boarding.

The final build, without the voice container, logged once that the voice
was off and stayed silent. Waiting showed the zones' overview and its line.

The solo splats were the engine's own impact kills. A 53 m/s landing killed
even with falling damage off, so `WF_SPLAT` itself has not fired in game.

Not yet triggered in game:
- a retake;
- breaking the defeat clock;
- an enemy capture;
- victory or defeat by score, and "Not bad, Chief" (team against team
  needs two PCs).

Not yet checked:
- a client's view;
- the lines heard by ear for level and timing (the log shows what played,
  not how it sounded).

## Validation and remaining runtime checks

The private solo acceptance run passed all seven recorded milestones:
native bridge ready, Pelican seated, canopy deployed, landed, respawned,
site scoring and round ended. The local receipt is
[`out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-27-03-197Z.jsonl`](../out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-27-03-197Z.jsonl).
It used a short test variant with a five-point target; the verified terminal
snapshot has phase 3, Red 5–Blue 0 and capture A owned by Red. Screenshot
events include seated, canopy, landed and end; the final screen showed Red
winning 5–0. The tested native DLL SHA-256 is
`4073f89c8d51bbf7229e7571613fdb0b79ef12a87bb533c5e200d2b3e8fa8068`.
The earlier absent-team -1 score sentinel is now covered by the publishing
clamp and a behavioral regression test.

A subsequent private test with two local player slots also passed, recorded
in [`out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-30-30-841Z.jsonl`](../out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-30-30-841Z.jsonl).
Red player 0 and Blue player 1 boarded their respective transports, exited
automatically, deployed canopies and landed. Native landing positions in
metres were Red `(172.518, -62.345, 0.244)` and Blue
`(-176.537, 64.270, 0.588)`. Red then died, respawned, captured A and won
the short five-point test 5–0. Both slots ran in one local game process;
this establishes the local two-team transport flow, not remote networking.

After the spawn-palette correction, the installed 500-point solo variant
passed the keyboard and transport-lifecycle run in
[`out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-46-27-499Z.jsonl`](../out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-46-27-499Z.jsonl).
It observed ready, seated, canopy, landing, respawn and scoring, plus early
exit from an actual Space key input. Named transport counts were zero in
warmup, two during insertion and zero after cleanup. This used the
`4073f89c...` native DLL above. No round end was expected during this short
500-point run; the earlier five-point tests cover that transition.

A live visual comparison found that passenger seat `pelican_p_l04` avoids
the large gray polygons visible from `pelican_p_l01`. The native boarding
order now prefers `l04, l05, r04, r05, l01, l02, l03, r01, r02, r03`, retaining
all ten passenger seats. Only l04's view has been visually verified; the
other nine seats have not been visually certified. The updated native DLL
build and portable tests passed with SHA-256
`498aa411f354124f9a79ab7f48d5c08f97acd960eb88510c5c2194340200624b`.
That DLL is in the latest installation receipt above. Its final private live
run passed in
[`out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-50-20-538Z.jsonl`](../out/pwr/smoke-2026-11-09T05-50-20-538Z.jsonl):
ready, seated, canopy, landing, death/respawn, capture scoring, actual Space
exit before the automatic fallback, and transport counts 0 / 2 / 0. The
in-flight seated screenshot confirms the improved l04 view. This 90-second
run retained the installed 500-point target and did not require a match end;
the earlier five-point runs separately verified victory.

`cargo test -p blam-megalo --lib --test warfare_behavior` validates typed and
independent grammar roundtrips plus deterministic warmup, capture, contested
scoring, on-foot eligibility and victory behavior. Lua tests
`test_warfare_bootstrap.lua`, `test_warfare_hud.lua` and
`test_warfare_canopy.lua` cover bootstrap, freshness, score authority,
persisted settings, presentation and canopy attachment lifecycle.
`test_lobby_postgame.lua` covers the scoped Warfare rotation and the unchanged
ordinary rotation. The latest Warfare-only postgame rotation has been unit
tested but has not yet been verified in a live postgame vote. The HUD
regression preserves a verified terminal result
when the engine starts resetting its round before frontend travel.

Integration is ongoing. Remote host/client replication, remote seating and
drop, remote canopy visibility, join-in-progress, a full 16-player match,
full vehicle combat remain unverified. Opposing teams
contesting a capture site is covered by the deterministic VM tests, not a
live contested-site test. The historical runs above used the original
400 × 300 metre basin; they do not certify the current expansion's terrain,
scenery or performance. The expansion requires its own installed-build
checks. No increased player cap or third team is implemented.

notes.title: Pelican Warfare: waves, reinforcements and moving zones
notes.summary: Design for the second round of Pelican Warfare (PWR) features, agreed 2026-11-22. It extends the prototype; read that first for the slot layout, the native adapter and the HUD bridge.
notes.body:
Design for the second round of Pelican Warfare (PWR) features, agreed
2026-11-22. It extends [the prototype](pelican_warfare.md); read that first
for the slot layout, the native adapter and the HUD bridge.

Four features, in build order (1-3 are built; 4 is a design, see [AI feasibility](pwr_ai_feasibility.md)):

1. **Warmup countdown**: a large centred countdown before insertion.
2. **Reinforcement waves**: the dead wait, spectate their team, and fly back
   in together on a shared clock.
3. **Moving zones**: each match picks where A, B and C are.
4. **Covenant waves**: AI arrive on Spirit dropships, fight both teams and
   contest the zones.

Decisions taken with the owner (2026-11-22): Covenant are hostile to both
teams; Covenant inside a zone block capture and payout the way an enemy player
does; reinforcements use one shared 60-second clock for both teams.

## What the spikes found

- **Global numbers are full.** Megalo holds 12 global numbers and the variant
  uses all 12 (`variant.rs` refuses a 13th). New published values must be packed
  into existing slots or derived from them. Object numbers have room (5 of 8).
- **Randomness exists.** CU4 keeps Megalo action 25 *Random Number* and action 96
  *Get Random Object With Label*, plus *Delete Object* (3).
- **No engine respawn hold is needed.** Instead of holding dead players in the
  engine's respawn queue (the `respawn_sync_with_team` bit is only inferred), the
  dead respawn after the normal short delay straight into a reinforcement Pelican
  parked at their team's flight start, which already exists for insertion.
- **A spectator camera is available.** `SetViewTargetWithBlend` already drives
  the view in MJOLNIRFlyCam and the HUD bench. A camera actor attached to a
  teammate's biped actor follows it with no Lua loop.
- **The Spirit dropship exists as a vehicle.** It is
  `objects/Vehicles/covenant/tuning_fork/tuning_fork` (its sounds are
  `spirit_anim_door_*`; Unreal has `Vehicles/covenant/SpiritDropShip`). It has 31
  AI passenger seats (`fork_p_*`). It can be cloned the way
  `tools/level/build_warfare_pelican.ps1` clones the Pelican.
- **PWR has no AI data yet.** No pathfinding, squads, zones or objectives. The
  `blam.bots` bake lane has never run on a 2 km heightfield shell. That, and the
  16 Havok proxies the AI memory notes, are the open risks for feature 4.

## Protocol

The map's metadata keeps `protocol 20569` and layout 3, so the published map
does not change. The Megalo rules get their own magic in slot 2, **20570** (20571 from the Covenant defeat clock, docs/pelican_warfare.md).
The native DLL, HUD and variant ship together; each refuses the other's old
revision.

Slot 3 (the clock) changes meaning by phase:

| Phase | Slot 3 |
|---|---|
| 0 warmup | `-1` while waiting for the minimum players, else whole seconds left |
| 1 insertion | the insertion duration in seconds (was also published in phase 0) |
| 2 combat | combat seconds elapsed (unchanged) |

Native reads the insertion duration only in phase 1. Slot 6 (scratch, never
replicated) counts ticks inside the second in phases 0 and 2.

## 1. Warmup countdown (built)

Megalo counts the warmup down in whole seconds in slot 3. The status line says
"DEPLOYMENT IN 0:23" (or "WAITING FOR PLAYERS" while slot 3 is `-1`), and the
last ten seconds count down large in the middle of the screen
(`MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/warfare_countdown.lua`), gold for the last three, then
"DEPLOY" for two seconds as insertion begins.

The number is a Lua-made TextBlock in the game's own countdown face
(`Font_Oxanium` Medium, from `WBP_MatchStartCountdown`) at 420 pt. A TextBlock's
font can be set from Lua only before the widget first reaches the screen;
SetFont afterwards changes nothing, and a hand-built font struct passed to
SetFont crashed the game. Render scale works but blurs.

Verified 2026-11-22 in a solo match at 4K, and the clock reached both joiners
on three game copies.

## 2. Reinforcement waves (built)

- **Schedule.** Wave k (k >= 1) leaves at combat second k x 60 and flies 30
  seconds of its team's insertion route (`reinforcement` in `layout.json`,
  generated into `warfare_layout.h` and written to the state file for the HUD).
  It is derived from the replicated combat clock, so every machine agrees with
  no extra slot. The 30-second flight at the 30 m/s cap reaches the middle of
  the map; the forced exit is at 27 s (the insertion's 54/60).
- **Sortie.** The per-player state machine (`warfare_core.h`) takes a
  `warfare_sortie` instead of "phase 1": the insertion is sortie 0, the wave
  that parks before departure k is sortie k. A rider stays aboard only the
  sortie they boarded, so an insertion rider still seated at combat start
  leaves even though a reinforcement Pelican is parked.
- **Boarding.** After death the player respawns at home (Megalo's five
  seconds) and is boarded while their team's Pelican is parked at
  `pwr_<team>_flight_start`. Only a player still waiting where they spawned is
  taken: on foot within 40 m of the home flag. Someone who walked off or took a
  vehicle is never pulled out. Every machine checks "parked" itself (the
  transport near its flight start), so a client never tries to board a Pelican
  that is not there. Late joiners and players not admitted at roster lock take
  the next wave. A seat is allocated at boarding (late joiners have no roster
  seat). A boarding the host never completes fails quietly and retries on the
  next wave; a client that loses the race with its host's boarding adopts the
  seat it finds itself in.
- **Transport.** The host holds the parked Pelican at its flight start with a
  bounded correction (about 2 m of sag in 55 s), flies it on schedule, and once
  it is empty after a flight makes it anew at its flight start. The first one
  replaces the insertion Pelican after the usual cleanup delay. Empty Pelicans
  fly their waves too, which keeps the schedule identical everywhere.
- **Jumping while parked** leaves at once by the normal exit (host detach,
  cabin clearance, canopy). The parked Pelican hovers over the team's base, so
  this is how to stay home. A first version that detached and teleported the
  rider home left a remote rider hanging at 550 m on three copies: the client's
  HS teleport never took. A body detached from a stationary Pelican also
  sleeps, so the fall starts with `object_wake_physics` (`WF_WAKE`).
- **Spectating** (`warfare_spectate.lua`). While seated in a parked wave with
  more than three seconds to go, the view follows a teammate on foot through a
  CameraActor attached behind their biped (`SetViewTargetWithBlend`), and the
  line adds "WATCHING <name>". Restoring the cabin view is the default on any
  other tick. The game hides actors outside its own player's view, so the
  watched body is un-hidden while watched and given back its own state after.
  There is no key to change teammates yet; with nobody to watch the cabin view
  stays.
- **Waiting for the Pelican** (native `WF_WAITING`, stage 8; 2026-11-24).
  - **When.** Between waves the Pelican waits out of sight and can be
    boarded only about 15 s before it leaves, so a death early in a cycle
    left the player standing at base for most of a minute. Now a body
    spawned in combat, on foot and supported within 40 m of home, waits
    while its Pelican cannot be boarded. The host makes it
    damage-proof (`object_cannot_take_damage (player_get N)`, `WF_SHIELD`),
    and its weapon is lowered (the unarmed profile, `WF_LOWER_WEAPON`). A
    body left while its player watches is neither a target nor an
    invulnerable turret.
  - **How it ends.** The Pelican parking boards the player straight from
    waiting: the shield comes off, and the weapon stays lowered for the
    ride. Moving more than 2 m, a vehicle, 75 s, the match ending or a new
    warmup also end it: the shield comes off, the weapon comes back, and
    the life plays from home without waiting again.
  - **One exit path.** Every exit goes through `warfare_end_wait` or the
    boarding paths, which unshield (`test_waiting`).
  - **The HUD.** It follows the stage. While waiting it spectates a
    teammate, or with nobody to watch it shows the three zones from
    above, and the line reads "WAITING FOR YOUR PELICAN / IT LEAVES IN
    m:ss / MOVE TO PLAY FROM BASE". Boarding keeps the view until the
    seat.
  - **Seen solo on PC 1.** Respawns early in a cycle waited, about 35 s
    once, and boarded when the Pelican came in. The overview showed the
    zones with "WAITING FOR YOUR PELICAN / IT LEAVES IN 0:19".
  - **Two PCs, 2026-11-24 (PC 1 host, PC 3 joiner).** The host shielded a

    The joiner's own screen showed the zones' overview with "WAITING FOR

## 3. Moving zones (built)

- **Markers.** Each site may have up to six candidate `koth_hill` markers. A
  marker's spawn order is `site + 3 * candidate`, so the classic 0, 1 and 2 are
  candidate 0 and a map with one marker per site plays exactly as before
  (including today's published PWR).
- **The pick** (`warfare.rs`). Every warmup tick draws a *Random Number*
  (action 25) to stir the host's LCG, whose seed may repeat between launches.
  At launch each candidate draws a number and the highest wins per site. The
  last site then takes the first site's candidate index when it has one: on
  PWR, C's candidates mirror A's across the line between the homes, so every
  draw is equally fair to both teams. From insertion on the unchosen markers
  are deleted; only the chosen ones capture and score.
- **Publishing.** Each site's slot adds `1024 * candidate` to its packed state
  (`SiteState.candidate`), from insertion on, so riders can steer toward where
  the zones went.
- **Positions.** `layout.json` `capture_candidates_m` holds each site's extra
  spots (metres). `prepare_runtime.py` turns them into the extra markers and
  `warfare.capture_candidates` (Unreal cm) in the level file, which the HUD
  reads for the holo fields, waypoints and zone tiles. The native layout
  header carries them for the tactical map.
- **Choosing spots** (`plan_capture_candidates.py`). It searches the accepted
  runtime terrain's masks for 20 m discs that are flat (under 3 m of rise over
  26 m), walkable, dry, off the shore and nearly tree-free, at least 150 m from
  other sites, 100 m from the site's own candidates and 160 m from both homes.
  A is searched on red's half and mirrored for C; B runs along the centre line.
  It writes `capture_candidates_m` with `--write` and a preview map.
- **The map.** The candidates are scenario markers, so the map needs one
  rebake. Only the scenario tag changes: a standalone bake of
  `river-basin/native/native-level.json` (patched by `prepare_runtime.py`) with
  the release's own `pwr.sbsp` and `LPE.umap`, against the rehearsal Paks,
  differed from the sealed chunk 997 in `PWR-scenario.uasset/.ubulk` only. The
  map registry DLL must be rebuilt too: it validates variants with its own copy
  of the Megalo crate, and an old one refuses a variant that uses *Random Number*.

Verified 2026-11-22 in a solo match on the rebaked scenario: A took candidate
3, B candidate 2 and C candidate 3 (following A), announced at launch; the
tactical map and all three holo fields stood at the new spots and nothing

## 4. Covenant waves

**The director is built** (2026-11-22, not released). The parts:

- **The map** gets wave squads from the bake: `blam.bots.objectives:
  ["koth_hill"]` makes each capture spot a place to hold with its own task,
  and `blam.bots.waves` four squads per spot (an Elite, two Grunts and a
  Jackal) whose first task is that spot ([bots.md](bots.md#waves)). Pelican
  Warfare gets 44.
- **The host's lobby DLL** (`warfare_waves`, run from the Warfare tick) does
  the rest, with no map data of its own:
  - once a world, in combat, it reads each site's chosen spot from its slot
    (`SiteState.candidate`), names the place `koth_hill_<site + 3 x
    candidate>` and counts that place's squads with `ai_living_count`. A map
    without wave squads answers "no such squad", and the director stands
    down for the match;
  - on each wave time of the combat clock (the first at 45 s, then every 90
    s; a crossing, so a late tick still fires it once) it counts the live
    Covenant per site and picks the site with the fewest. On a tie an owned
    site comes before a neutral one, and equal sites take turns;
  - it places that site's free squads, `ai_force_active` and wakes each, up
    to 12 live Covenant in all (the Havok proxy budget is unmeasured);
  - it stands down for the rest of the match if the bots' team table is in
    force, since that table puts red on the Covenant's side (not yet run
    with bots on).
- The pure rules (`warfare_wave_due`, `warfare_wave_target`,
  `warfare_wave_size`) are in `warfare_core.h` with `test_warfare.c` cases.

**The contest is built** (2026-11-22, not released). Megalo cannot see AI,
so the host counts them: in combat, ten times a second, the lobby DLL counts
living bipeds that no player owns and nothing carries inside each chosen
site's boundary (20 m, from 1 m below to 4 m above the marker). It writes the
count to that site marker's Megalo object number 6
(`warfare_contest` in `native/lobby/warfare_runtime.h`), every pass, zeros
included, and zeros on any stand-down. It finds the marker as global object 2
+ site and its Megalo object entry by handle (`[TLS+0x3a0]`, 0x94 bytes, the
object at `+0x38`, numbers at `+0x50`), and writes only when that entry's
number 4 equals the site's published slot. The rules (`COVENANT` in
`blam-megalo` `warfare.rs`) read it: while it is above zero neither team's
capture advances and the owner gets no payout. A game type with no writer
reads 0 and plays as before (a `warfare_behavior.rs` case).

**The Covenant take zones** (2026-11-22, not released). The same count now
captures as well as contests. Owner 3 (`OWNER_COVENANT`) is a site the
Covenant hold, and a marker's object number 7 (`COVENANT_PROGRESS`) is their
capture progress, so variants declare 8 object numbers. Per tick, on each
chosen site:

- **Covenant alone** (count above 0, no player): a team's progress drains
  toward 0 at one a tick, the teams' own rate, and the site goes neutral as
  usual. Only on a neutral site does number 7 then fill, one a tick; at the
  Covenant capture time (`covenant_capture_seconds`, default 30 s, CLI
  `--covenant-capture-seconds`) the owner becomes 3. So an undefended team
  site falls in the team capture time (15 s) plus 30 s. (The live runs below
  used the first defaults, 8 s and 20 s.)
- **A Covenant site pays nobody**, and stays theirs when they are all killed.
- **Players alone** on it drain number 7 back to 0 first (owner back to 0 as
  soon as it drops below full), then capture as on any neutral site.
- **Covenant and players together**: nothing moves, nobody is paid.
- Numbers 1 and 7 are never both non-zero (a `warfare_behavior.rs` case),
  and with no writer every published value is the old packing, tick for tick
  (another).

The published slot carries it for every machine. Owner 3 sits in the low two
bits. While number 7 is above 0, the progress field holds
`COVENANT_STEP_BASE` (34) plus its steps, past the teams' 1 to 33. `COVENANT_PRESENT`
(8192) is added while Covenant stand in the zone. That is above the candidate
bits, so the candidate is `(value % 8192) / 1024`: `warfare_site_candidate`
in `warfare_core.h`, `SiteState` in Rust and `Warfare.site` in the HUD decode
the same vectors in their tests. The director's tie-break presses a team's
site, then a neutral one, then a Covenant one. The tactical map draws a
Covenant site as unowned.

On the HUD a Covenant site is purple, and its tile reads COVENANT. Covenant
alone on a team site read UNDER ATTACK, and on a neutral one OVERRUN, with
their progress in purple. Players alone on a Covenant site read CLEARING;
Covenant with players read CONTESTED. The capture feed says "The Covenant
took zone B", "Zone A was neutralized by the Covenant", and "Red team cleared
zone B".

  simulation reaches the warfare tick in bursts (PC 3: 728 gapped ticks in a
  minute and a half; the host 388), and every gap cleared the samples, so the
  two-minute timeout sent it home instead. Now a velocity across up to 0.1 s of
  ticks counts, a missing sample neither counts nor breaks the run, and a second
  of unbroken world contact (`WARFARE_GROUNDED_SECONDS`) lands anyone. Shown: PC 3
  landed 5-6 s after opening its canopy, in both matches.
- **Countdown lag.** The HUD read the warfare state at 2 Hz, each machine at its
  own phase; near a countdown it now reads at 10 Hz and has the state written each
  time (`Warfare.countdownNear`). Screens taken together showed the same number;
  what remains is replication.
- **Troops jumped through the doors.** The Spirit opens over its spot and its
  troops jump `WARFARE_SPIRIT_DOOR_SECONDS` (2) later; it leaves once only its
  pilot rides (counted by parent), or 12 s after. Shown: 16 aboard, out in 5.1 s.
- **A respawn rode a hidden Pelican.** Boarding counted anywhere on the Pelican's
  way in from out of sight. Riders now board only at its flight start, where it
  shows, and it gets there `WARFARE_PELICAN_BOARDING_LEAD` (15) s before the wave
  leaves. Shown: a killed player boarded 16 s after it started in, inside a
  visible cabin with nine seconds to departure.
- **Full Spirits.** `tuning_fork` has 31 seats but 16 troop seats (`fork_p_l1`-`l8`,
  `fork_p_r1`-`r8`, AI seat type passenger; the rest are its pilot's and cargo).
  The bake's `waves.transport` makes one wave squad per troop seat from the tag;
  PWR's waves are legendary kinds, half Elites. The alive cap is 48 (the
  simulation keeps 96 actors). Shown: 31 placed lived, 16 rode, all 16 jumped and
  walked off; wave 1 brought 16.
- **Stronger.** A Megalo match plays at Normal, so AI take their character's
  normal vitality (an Elite 75 body and 75 shield, its legendary 100 and 135).
  The bake's `waves.vitality: "legendary"` writes a script per place,
  `wave_vitality_<place>`, raising each wave squad's maximum vitality to its
  character's legendary values (read from the tag; `--extra-paks` reaches the CE
  runtime's bot characters when `--paks` is a bare game copy), and the host calls
  it after placing a wave. Maximum only: a fresh unit is full, an earlier
  wave's hurt survivor is not healed. Bot matches are untouched. Shown: wave 1's
  8 Elites read 100 and 135, its Grunts 60 and Jackals 80; the same 60 damage
  left a raised Elite's shield at 56% and a normal one's at 20%. The kinds are
  legendary, so they also aim better.

## Waves that get harder (2026-11-24)

Each wave is harder than the last few: the host takes tier `(wave - 1) / 3`
(`warfare_wave_tier`; `WARFARE_WAVES_PER_TIER`), the map's last tier from then
on. The bake's `waves.tiers` makes a pool per tier of three Spirits' worth (one
per site), `wave_t<tier>_<fork>_<seat>`, standing by the first place held; the
host places a free fork of the wave's tier, sends its squads to the chosen
spot's task (`ai_set_task <squad> mjolnir_bots koth_hill_<place>`), loads them
into the Spirit and calls the tier's `wave_vitality_t<tier>`. A fork is the
site's it was sent to until its squads are dead. A site whose Spirit is still
out waits; with no Spirit at all the wave is skipped, as the pools stand away
from every site.

PWR's ladder (`prepare_runtime.py`):

| Waves | From | Kinds | Vitality |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-3 | 0:45 | heroic: Elite, 2 Grunts, Jackal in turn | normal (Elite 75/75) |
| 4-6 | 5:15 | legendary: 2 Elites, Grunt, Jackal | legendary (Elite 100/135) |
| 7-9 | 9:45 | veteran: 3 Elites, Grunt | legendary x1.25 |
| 10- | 14:15 | ace: 3 Elites, Jackal | legendary x1.5 |

**Aim past legendary.** A Megalo match reads each weapon's firing pattern 1,
the Normal one: an Elite whose plasma rifle fired 1, 3, 6 and 12 shots a second
in patterns 0-3 fired 2.74 and 2.82 a second over two 13 s counts, every bolt
seen in two samples (2026-11-24). `build_bot_characters.sh` makes two levels
past legendary for the Covenant kinds and their generic parent, which holds
the Covenant weapons' patterns:

| | Accuracy | Projectile error | Burst separation | Tracking, leading | Damage modifier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| veteran | (0.85, 1) after 0.25 s | x0.5 | x0.6 | 1, 1 | 1 where set |
| ace | (1, 1) at once | 0 | x0.35 | 1, 1 | 1 where set |

The error and separation scale the tightest of normal, heroic and legendary
(Bungie's legendary is not always the tightest). They are wave-only kinds
(`bots.types[].wave_only`: no bot squads of their own; PWR has 402 squads of
512). They ship in the CE runtime as `pakchunk995-MJOLNIRBOT-<kind>-<level>_P`,
so the map needs a runtime release that carries them; until then they are
developer builds on PC 1 and PC 3.

## Testing

Each rule gets a `warfare_behavior.rs` case and each native change a
`test_warfare.c` case. Live proof needs two game copies
(`tools/remote/instances.mjs up 2`), then PC 2. Nothing is released until the
owner has played it.

notes.title: Covenant AI on Pelican Warfare: feasibility
notes.summary: Research for pelican_warfare_waves.md section 4 (Covenant waves), 2026-11-22. Nothing here is shipped code. The measurements were made offline on the released map's sealed inputs (map 0.1.1, saturday.45/map-input) and the shipped campaign scenarios. The game was not run. Tools…
notes.body:
Research for [pelican_warfare_waves.md](pelican_warfare_waves.md) section 4
(Covenant waves), 2026-11-22. Nothing here is shipped code. The measurements
were made offline on the released map's sealed inputs (map 0.1.1,
`saturday.45/map-input`) and the shipped campaign scenarios. The game was not
run. Tools and outputs are in `out/pwr-ai/` (listed at the end).

## Verdict in one paragraph

Feasible, but not with the bots lane as it stands. PWR's walkable ground is
not in the BSP's collision shell. It lives in 151 instanced-geometry
definitions: 1.2 million unwelded triangles. The bots lane only reads the
shell, so on PWR it "succeeds" while producing nothing usable: one sector on
a box floor 42 wu under the map. Bungie's own pathfinding has the shape PWR
needs. Every shipped campaign BSP keeps its sectors on instanced geometry
(`object refs`), merges many collision triangles into each sector, and goes
past 32,767 links. The terrain is also friendly: one connected area joins
both bases, all three sites and both flight-start grounds, and the routes
are close to straight lines. The work is a new pathfinding generator, an
"instances" mode that builds coarse convex sectors over the welded terrain.
That is the first step and the biggest risk, because the one earlier attempt
at object-ref pathfinding crashed the game. After it, the AI side reuses
what Bungie's own missions do: a Spirit loaded with `vehicle_load_magic`,
objectives and tasks over zones of firing positions, and `ai_set_task` when
the target changes.

## 1. Can the bots lane generate pathfinding for PWR?

**It runs, and the result is unusable.** The bake input was the shipped
`pwr.level.json` with the loader-only keys removed and `defs/level/bots.json`
added as `blam.bots`, exactly as `tools/level/add_bots.py` builds it. It was
baked into `out/pwr-ai/bake/` from the shipped map container's BSP and world.

| | |
|---|---|
| Wall time | 51 s (`level bake`, release build, PC 1) |
| Exit | 0, with no warning |
| Pathfinding | 1 sector, 4 links, 4 vertices, 9 surface refs, 151 instance refs (all -1) |
| Spawns | "16 of 16 on the main walkable ground" (false: see below) |
| Firing positions | 1,849, widened to a 15.38 wu grid to fit the 2,048 cap |
| Squads | 180 (12 kinds x 15) |
| Output | `pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-PWR_P` 397.4 MB (shipped 402.7 MB). Package-by-package, only `PWR-scenario.uasset/.ubulk` differ (scenario bulk 237,714 -> 453,373 bytes). The BSP, world and lighting packages are byte-identical; the smaller `.ucas` is compression. |

Why the result is useless:

- **The shell is a 9-surface box.** Its only floor is at z -6.56 wu
  (-20 m, the scenario's lower bound). `pathfinding::shell_collision` reads
  only that, so the lane makes one sector there. Every spawn "stands on" it
