  because `sector_at` takes the highest floor under the point, and that floor
  is 42 wu below the actual ground. The firing positions all lie under the
  terrain.
- **The ground is in instances.** There are 151 instances, each of its own
  definition. Instance 0 / definition 0 is a copy of the box. The other 150
  hold the terrain, the bases and the rocks, in definitions of up to 8,192
  surfaces each, 1,199,995 in all. Edges and vertices are both exactly
  3 x surfaces: every triangle has its own three vertices and edges, so no
  two triangles share an edge. 268,595 triangles are walkable
  (normal z >= 0.65). By count, 20.8% of the triangles face down, 34.6% are
  walls, 22.2% are steep and 22.4% walkable. By area, 38.8% are nearly flat
  floor. Most of the downward and wall area is the box (definition 0, a
  656 x 656 wu floor, ceiling and walls). Every definition's surfaces have an
  edge loop (`first_edge` >= 0 on all of them).
- **Every instance ref is -1**, so an AI standing on the terrain is on no
  sector. That is the Blood Gulch "copy" failure (path follower state 3,
  cannot plan a path; docs/re/ai_in_multiplayer.md), but over the whole map.
- **The current generator could not do it even if pointed at the
  definitions.** One sector per walkable triangle, summed over the
  definitions, gives 268,595 sectors, 1,089,160 links and 810,929 vertices.
  That is 4 to 17 times over the engine's limits, and the triangles are
  unwelded, so the sectors would not connect to each other.

The lane should refuse this case loudly instead of passing. For example:
stop when the chosen spawn sector lies more than about 2 wu below the spawn,
or when the shell has under some minimum of walkable area while instances
hold more.

**Engine limits, checked against shipped data** (census of the 13 shipped
Halo 1 scenarios, `out/pwr-ai/census.txt`):

| Block | Limit | Largest shipped |
|---|---|---|
| sectors | 65,534 (tag max) | A30 BSP 3: 17,301 |
| links | 16-bit indices | A30 BSP 3: **59,826**, forward/reverse up to 59,356 |
| vertices | 65,535 (tag max) | A30 BSP 3: 42,028 |
| object refs | 8,192 | 44 (C45) |
| instanced geometry refs | 16,384 | 11,813 (D40) |
| bsp2d refs per object entry | 262,136 | 9,228 |
| hints | 32,767 | 1,335 |

Bungie's link indices go past 32,767, so the sim reads them as unsigned
16-bit numbers. The generator's cap of 32,767 (`pathfinding.rs`, i16 types)
is half the real budget of about 65,535 links and vertices.

Two more facts from the census decide the generator's design:

- **No shipped BSP uses the structure's own refs** (`bsp2d refs` = 0
  everywhere). Every sector sits on instanced geometry through `object refs`
  (one per definition, each with its own `bsp2d refs`, one per collision
  surface, and a `vertex offset`). Every instance maps to an object through
  `instanced geometry refs`.
- **Sectors merge triangles.** A30 BSP 3's object 9 has 9,228 surface refs:
  4,614 none, 426 into `bsp2d nodes` (a surface split between sectors), and
  the rest naming only 1,706 sectors. B40 BSP 8 has 632 sectors and 2,377
  links in all. Sector flags are mostly 0x11. 0x15 (adds `mobile`) is rare
  on A30 but about a quarter of B40 BSP 8's sectors (149 of 632), and B40
  also has step sectors (0x1045, 0x1085, 0x1105, 0x1205).

**Which definitions own the ground.** Measured on the raster below:

- 18 large terrain tiles (instances 126-143) own 96.5% of the main walkable
  top, each as one big patch or two. So the definitions are spatial tiles.
  Their bounds look wide only because a tile's box reaches across its
  neighbours.
- 131 other instances (rocks, the bases, props) own the rest, in 1,419
  patches under 10 cells: mostly rock tops.
- Tile-to-tile seams total 8,387 wu. Seams that involve a smaller owner
  total 9,908 wu.

So a generator that works per definition and joins seams with intersection
links (Bungie's way) fits PWR's layout, at a cost of a few thousand
intersection links and hints (the hint limit is 32,767). Small rock tops
should get ref -1, which removes most of the second kind of seam. The BSP
itself does not need re-chunking.

## 2. Is a graph usable on a 2 km heightfield?

This was measured on a 1 wu (3.05 m) raster of the topmost upward-facing
instance surface: `out/pwr-ai/probe/probe.txt`, with a walkable map in
`probe/walkable.pgm`. A raster is a stand-in for the real graph: it misses
tree trunks and anything thinner than 3 m, so its obstacle count is a floor.

- **Slopes.** Of the top surface, 55.8% is under 10 degrees, then 15.5%
  (10-20), 13.9% (20-30), 10.9% (30-40), 2.4% (40-50) and 1.2% steeper.
  99% of covered ground passes the 49-degree walkable rule.
- **Connectivity.** 423,967 wu^2 is walkable. One component holds 420,635
  cells (99.2%). There are 291 components in all, 223 of them under 10
  cells. Both homes, all three sites (on their layout positions, with the
  raster height matching the layout height to within 0.01 wu) and the ground
  under both flight starts are on the main component.
- **Routes** (Dijkstra on the raster). Home to near site: 121 to 123 wu,
  1.03-1.04x the straight line. Home to far site: 277 to 298 wu. Site to
  site: 157 to 255 wu, 1.01-1.08x. Base to base: 392 wu.
- **Water.** The simulation has no water: Fluid Flux is Unreal-only, so the
  river and lake beds are ordinary walkable collision. Estimated from the
  flux sources' heights and the lake level (55 m), 35,080 wu^2 lies under
  water and 30,330 wu^2 of it deeper than 0.5 wu (1.5 m). The shortest
  route crosses water on 6 of the 10 pairs tested, up to 1.1-1.3 wu (3.4 to
  4 m) deep: an AI would walk along the river bed under the surface. Each of
  those pairs also has a dry route, 2% to 14% longer. The dry routes pass
  the river at two places only: around (-23, -84) m and (-75, 209) m, on
  terrain tile 143, where the ground is about 20 m above the nearest flux
  source's height. **So the navmesh must leave out water deeper than about
  0.5 wu**, taken from the flux state, which the level already ships.
- **Bridges and roads: unverified.** `layout.py` puts the three main
  bridges at y -350, 0 and 350 m and fords at y ±800 m. The two dry
  crossings above do not obviously match, so they may be a bridge deck
  merged into the tile, a high bank, or a gap in the water estimate: it only
  knows water within 15 wu of a flux source point. No bridge deck shows as a
  separate layer in the core. The 10,186 cells with a walkable floor more
  than 2 wu under the top cluster at the map's edges (around |x| or |y| of
  450 to 840 m). Before the navmesh cuts water out, the bridges must be
  confirmed in collision (`pf_where dump` at the bridge positions), and the
  water mask built from the baked height fields rather than source points.
  Roads are part of the terrain surface.
- **Obstacles.** The play area has 2,215 blobs of non-walkable ground
  (rocks, steep bumps, cut-offs): 1,977 of 1-2 cells (1,931 of those cells
  steep), 176 of 3-20 cells, and 62 larger (largest 2,079 cells).

**Graph size.** A coarse navmesh fits the engine, though not the
generator's present cap. These are estimates on the raster, made with a
right-triangle bisection (RTIN): a triangle splits until it is all main
walkable ground and its heights fit one plane. RTIN is about 2x worse than a
proper polygon or Delaunay decomposition, so the real counts should come in
lower:

| Coverage | Sectors | Links (~1.6x) |
|---|---|---|
| Whole map, every obstacle, plane fit 1 wu | 34,417 | ~55,000 |
| Whole map, every obstacle, plane fit 2 wu | 30,388 | ~48,600 |
| Whole map, 1-2 cell bumps ignored, 2 wu | 20,578 | ~32,900 |
| Central band \|x\| <= 450 m (sites, not bases), bumps ignored, 2 wu | 7,723 | ~12,400 |

A quadtree is worse: 26,600 to 36,900 sectors and 72,000 to 94,000 links,
which is over budget. What drives the count is the obstacle edges, not the
terrain's curvature.

Recommendation: a polygonal navmesh (welded walkable triangles, deep water
and obstacles cut out, then merged into convex regions under a height
tolerance), aiming at 10-25k sectors and under 50k links. The central band
can be the first cut. Two things are open:

- **Height tolerance** of a coarse sector. The AI finds its sector through
  the collision surface it stands on (bsp2d refs), so a sector need not be
  flat. How far its vertices may stray before paths or firing positions look
  wrong is not known; Bungie's sectors follow their surfaces exactly.
- **A sector is a union of whole collision triangles**, or the triangles it
  cuts need `bsp2d nodes` (Bungie uses both). The estimates above ignore
  that constraint.

## 3. The Havok proxy budget

What is known for certain (Ghidra on `HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll`,
project `C:\ghidra_proj\sim`):

- `FUN_180375470` creates the data array `"havok proxies"` with a fixed
  maximum of **16** (0x10) entries of 0x50 bytes, stored at `[TLS+0x268]`.
  This matches the memory note.
- `game_performance_throttle` (`globals\default`, referenced by the
  scenario) has one profile, for 3 or more players: `maximum havok proxy
  count` 0, ragdolls 3, impacts 10. Proxies are a throttled resource like
  ragdolls.
- A physics model material has a `proxy collision group`. The Spirit's
  (`tuning_fork`) material 0 is `machine`, the grunt's `NONE`.

What is not known: which objects take a proxy, and what happens when all 16
are in use. The allocation sites were not found within the time box.

**Leading hypothesis: proxies are switched off in any real match.** The
throttle profile is restrictive (3 ragdolls, 10 impacts) and sets the proxy
maximum to 0 from 3 players up. That would explain both readings:

- the Blood Gulch reading (4 Warthogs plus one per live biped = 13, with
  eight bots and a host) was taken with one human player, below the
  profile's threshold;
- PWR places 18 vehicles (8 Warthogs, 4 Scorpions, 4 Banshees, 2 Pelicans)
  and plays with players on top, which would be over 16 if every vehicle
  and biped held one.

Whether bots count toward "player count" is unknown, and "0" could also
mean "no limit". Nobody has seen a failure caused by proxies either way.

**A safe wave size cannot be derived from "16".** Until it is measured:

- one Spirit carrying **8 AI** (two squads of 4: 2 elites and 6 grunts or
  jackals), and at most **12 live Covenant** on the map;
- the first live test reads the proxy array (the `[TLS+0x268]` data array:
  count, then each datum's object handle at +0x44) across the throttle
  threshold: a PWR match with 2 players, then with 3 or more. In each, read
  it with no AI, then 8 and 16 AI plus the Spirit. Check that the last AI
  placed still stands on the ground and is hit by vehicles;
- raise the cap only on that evidence. Shipped missions run dozens of AI
  (B40 loads 2-3 squads per Spirit), so AI count is not otherwise the limit.

## 4. Making the AI "smart"

Everything below is what CE/Reach AI data already does, in shipped
missions. The bake should generate it per candidate spot, from tag data and
never from the map's name.

### What Bungie's B40 does with a Spirit (decompiled, `out/pwr-ai/scripts/B40.hsc` ~line 1596, 1897)

```
(ai_place sq_..._dropship)                                    ; pilot squad with the Spirit
(set v (ai_vehicle_get_from_starting_location sq_..._dropship/pilot_spawn))
(ai_place gr_..._drop_e)                                      ; the passengers
(vehicle_load_magic v "fork" (ai_actors sq_..._ge))           ; seat name substring: any fork_p_* seat
; command script on the pilot:
(cs_enable_pathfinding_failsafe true) (cs_ignore_obstacles true)
(cs_vehicle_speed 0.66) (cs_fly_to ps_dropship_a_flightpath/p0 0.1)
(unit_open v)
(begin_random (begin (vehicle_unload v "fork_p_r1") (sleep 5)) ... "fork_p_l8")
(unit_close v) (cs_fly_by ps_..._flightpath/p1) ...           ; and away
```

All of these calls are in the shipped script corpus (`defs/hce/scripting.json`):
`ai_place`, `vehicle_load_magic`, `vehicle_unload`, `unit_open`,
`ai_set_objective`, `ai_set_task`, `ai_vehicle_enter`,
`ai_vehicle_reserve_seat`, `cs_fly_to`, `cs_vehicle_speed`,
`cs_run_command_script`, `ai_magically_see`, `ai_set_team`,
`object_wake_physics`, `ai_task_count`, `ai_living_count`. `ai_force_active`
and `ai_get_unit` are not in the corpus, but MJOLNIRHud's bots already use
them.

Two ways to fly the Spirit:

- **AI pilot** (Bungie's way, and the simulation-first choice in
  CLAUDE.md). This needs point sets (`scripting data` is cleared on PWR
  today) and a command script per drop compiled through `blam.script`.
  Flight here uses `cs_ignore_obstacles` and does not need the ground
  navmesh. A command script running in a Megalo game is untested.
- **Native host flight**, like the Pelicans, as the waves doc plans. That is
  proven for Pelicans, but it is more code of ours.

Spike the AI pilot first.

Outcome (2026-11-22): native host flight was built, and the AI pilot spike
was not run. A pilot needs point sets, and PWR's scripting data is cleared;
it needs a command script per drop, and a command script in a Megalo game is
untested; the Pelicans' velocity flight was already proven on every machine.
An awake Spirit with no pilot falls through PWR's terrain, so the host holds
its velocity for the whole flight, hover included. The cost is that it backs
out of the hover tail-first along its route; an AI pilot, which turns as it
flies, is the likely fix if that looks wrong. See pelican_warfare_waves.md,
"Spirits bring them".

### Who the Covenant fight

An AI marks a unit an enemy when either campaign team is -1 or the
allegiance matrix says so. Players have campaign team -1 in a Megalo game
unless the lobby DLL's team table gives them one. So with no team table in
force (no red/blue bots in the same match), Covenant squads already treat
both teams as enemies. No `ai_set_team` and no new table are needed, which
is simpler than the waves doc's "human and player" mapping. If red/blue bots
are wanted alongside the Covenant, the table must map red and blue to two
teams that are both hostile to `covenant` (for example `human` and
`player`), and that case needs its own test.

### Generated data per map

Proposed names. The inputs are the `koth_hill` candidate markers (spawn
sequence `site*10 + candidate`, waves doc section 3), the capture radius and
the flight starts.

| Block | Generated | Count (3 sites x 10 candidates) | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| pathfinding | object refs per terrain definition, coarse sectors, bsp2d refs/nodes, intersection links across definition seams, deep water cut out | 150 objects, 10-25k sectors | see section 1 |
| zones | `cov_site_<s>` (one per site) | 3 | 128 |
| areas (per zone) | `c<k>_core` (inside the capture radius), `c<k>_ring` (20-45 m), `c<k>_approach` (45-90 m, toward the map's centre) | 30 per zone | 128 |
| firing positions | ~60 per area. Flags `partial`/`closed` where an obstacle blob or rise stands between the position and the core, `open` elsewhere. Facing toward the core. | ~1,800 per zone | 2,048 |
| LZ areas | `c<k>_lz`, preset `dropship`, for the Spirit's hover point | 30 | (same zone) |
| objectives | `cov_site_<s>` | 3 | 64 |
| tasks (per objective) | `c<k>_assault` (approach + ring, attitude aggressive, movement run), `c<k>_hold` (core + ring, defensive, capacity bounds), `c<k>_fallback` (ring + approach, inhibit nothing), plus `roam` | 31 | 100 |
| squads | `cov_<kind>_<n>` (elite/grunt/jackal, characters `mjolnir_bot_*_legendary`), `cov_spirit_<n>` (vehicle squad + pilot) | ~24 + 4 | 512 |
| squad groups | `cov_wave_<n>` | 4-8 | 130 |
| point sets | `ps_spirit_<s><k>`: entry at a map edge, approach, hover over `c<k>_lz`, exit | 30 | 200 x 32 points |

### Runtime orders

Native, on the host only, issued once per event. This is not a Lua poll.

1. **Match start**, once the candidates are chosen: nothing to send if task
   activation can read the choice (below). Otherwise remember the three
   chosen candidates.
2. **Wave k** (on the combat clock):
   `(ai_place cov_spirit_0)` `(ai_place cov_wave_0)`
   `(vehicle_load_magic (ai_vehicle_get_from_starting_location cov_spirit_0/pilot) "fork" (ai_actors cov_wave_0))`
   `(ai_set_objective cov_wave_0 cov_site_a)`
   `(ai_set_task cov_wave_0 cov_site_a c3_assault)`
   `(cs_run_command_script cov_spirit_0/pilot cs_spirit_a3)`.
   Target the site the Covenant hold least, or the one being captured.
3. **At the hover**, in the command script: `unit_open` and `vehicle_unload`
   per seat. Then from native `(ai_force_active cov_wave_0 true)` and
   `(object_wake_physics ...)` per unit (bots.md: AI far from players go
   idle, and still bodies fall asleep).
4. **On a zone event** (site captured, held, contested): re-task the squads
   that serve it, for example `c3_hold` once inside, or the next site's
   `c<k>_assault` after the site falls. Use `ai_task_count` and
   `ai_living_count` to decide.

**Re-targeting without orders** (to test): a task's `activation script` is
a script fragment the objective system evaluates itself. If the bake can
compile one per task, such as `(= g_site_a 3)` on `c3_*`, then native sets
three globals once at warmup and the objectives pick the current spot with
no per-squad orders. Whether `level bake` can write task fragments today is
unchecked. The `ai_set_task` route above works without them.

**Smart behaviour knobs** that already exist:

- task `attitude`, `movement`, `inhibit groups` (leave Cover and Vehicles
  on), `capacity` (spreads squads over tasks), `priority` and
  `exhaustion delay`;
- task `filter` (`strength < 0.5` for a fallback task);
- the bot characters' per-level accuracy;
- cover-flagged firing positions (open, partial, closed);
- `ai_magically_see` on landing, so they engage at once.

Contesting a zone is a separate piece. The host counts living Covenant
bipeds within the capture radius (native already reads the zone positions),
as the waves doc plans.

## 5. Risks

1. **Our object-ref writer is unproven.** Object refs as such work in a
   Megalo match: the first bots spike (BOT, on B40's stock BSP 8) ran
   Bungie's own object-ref pathfinding in Slayer. What crashed on Blood
   Gulch was our attempt: an object for the shell copy, reusing the shell's
   refs, with no sectors or vertices of its own, crashed 2-5 s after the
   bots moved. The risk is getting Bungie's layout exactly right (own
   sectors, a `vertex offset`, node trees), and BOT is the control to test
   against. The fallback is decimated terrain in the shell, but the
   collision-source notes say that route needs the kd hierarchy and
   structure physics rebuilt for a 2 km world.
2. **Unsigned 16-bit indices** are inferred from shipped data (A30 has
   59,826 links). The generator's types are i16 and need widening, and the
   sim's treatment of 0xFFFF as "none" must hold.
3. **The proxy budget** is unknown (section 3).
4. **Activation at 2 km.** AI far from every player go idle;
   `ai_force_active` covers that. Perception and engagement ranges are
   campaign-sized, which may suit PWR's open ground poorly.
5. **AI pilot and command scripts in Megalo** are untested. So is
   compiling the point sets and scripts into PWR's generated scenario.
6. **Water** looks wrong if deep water is not cut out of the navmesh (AI
   walking under the Flux surface).
7. **Network.** AI far from a joiner lag a few metres (two-PC test,
   2026-10-25). With 16 players and 12 AI over 2 km this is unmeasured.
8. **A map republish is needed.** All AI data lives in the scenario, and
   every machine needs the same scenario. The bake changes only the
   scenario packages (verified above), so the map container changes in the
   `add_bots.py` style, plus the HUD and native changes. The release also
   needs the bot character containers (CE runtime 1.16.0 or later) and a
   container for the cloned Spirit.
9. **The bots lane's silent pass** on maps like PWR (section 1) could ship
   broken data by accident.

## Step list (in order, each with its test)

1. **Template from B40** (offline). Run `pf_dump` raw and summary on B40
   BSP 8 with its sbsp, to confirm whether object vertices are
   definition-local (`vertex offset`), how sector rings cross definition
   seams (intersection hints), the node trees and flags 0x11/0x15.
   *Test:* write B40's own pathfinding back through the new writer and
   compare byte for byte.
2. **Widen the indices** in `blam_sbsp::pathfinding` to u16 (65,535).
   *Test:* unit tests, plus a round-trip of A30 BSP 3's 59,826-link block.
3. **"Instances" generator.** Weld each definition's triangles; take the
   walkable ones; cut out water deeper than 0.5 wu (from flux state) and
   obstacles; merge into convex sectors per definition; write object refs,
   bsp2d refs/nodes and vertex offsets; join definition seams with
   intersection links; point instanced refs at their objects; give
   definition 0 (the box) none. *Test:* offline. Every sector ring closes
   (`check_rings`). Homes, sites and flight-start grounds are on one
   component. Route lengths are within 15% of the raster's. The counts fit.
4. **Guard the bots lane.** Refuse when spawns stand far above their
   sector, or when instances hold the walkable ground. *Test:* PWR fails
   loudly, and the 48 hub maps bake unchanged (the `add_bots.py
   --bake-only` sweep).
5. **First live run, the crash gate.** A private PWR test install, one
   player, one placed grunt squad ordered between two far areas, with BOT
   (Bungie's own object refs) as the control. Watch for the Blood Gulch
   crash (2-30 s), follower state (actor +0x874 in state 1, not 3) and the
   sector under the unit. *Test:* 10 minutes with no crash and the squad
   walking 300 wu across a river crossing.
6. **Proxy measurement** (section 3). *Test:* read the proxy array with 2
   players and then with 3 or more (across the throttle threshold), each
   with 0, 8 and 16 AI plus a Spirit; check that the last AI placed still
   collides. This sets the wave cap.
7. **Zones, objectives and squads** from the candidate markers (needs the
   moving-zones work). *Test:* `pf_where`-style offline check that each
   area's positions are on the main component, and that every task reaches
   its areas.
8. **The Spirit.** Clone `tuning_fork`, generate point sets, AI pilot with
   command scripts; native fallback if command scripts fail in Megalo.
   *Test:* solo, the Spirit reaches its hover point, unloads 8 AI on the
   ground, and leaves; then on two game copies, the joiner sees the drop.
9. **Native wave director and contest.** Waves on the combat clock,
   targeting, re-tasking on zone events, the AI presence count blocking
   capture. *Test:* `test_warfare.c` cases, then one solo and one
   two-copy match.
10. **Tuning against players**, by the owner. *Test:* the owner plays it.
    No release before that.

## What was not tested

- Nothing ran in the game. The crash risk of object-ref pathfinding, the
  proxy behaviour, AI flight in Megalo and AI replication over 2 km are all
  open.
- The graph counts are raster estimates, not a built navmesh. A real
  generator was not written.
- The water depths are an estimate from flux sources (nearest source within
  15 wu) and the lake level, not the baked water height fields.
- The havok proxy allocation sites were not found.
- Task activation-script compiling in `level bake` was not checked.

## Files (`out/pwr-ai/`, not tracked)

| | |
|---|---|
| `bake/`, `bake.log`, `pwr.bots.level.json` | the bots-lane bake of PWR (51 s) |
| `pfprobe/` (`src/main.rs`, `src/bin/pfcensus.rs`) | the probe and the shipped-pathfinding census (`cargo build --release` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/haloce/target`) |
| `probe/probe.txt`, `probe/walkable.pgm` | instance census, raster, routes, water, graph estimates |
| `census.txt` | every shipped Halo 1 BSP's pathfinding sizes |
| `instances.txt` | PWR's 151 instances |
| `scripts/*.hsc` | decompiled shipped mission scripts (B40's Spirit drops) |
| `ghidra_375470.c` | the `havok proxies` array creation |
| `water.json` | flux source heights and lake bounds used for the water estimate |
| `tags/`, `shipped/`, `gptd/`, `src/`, `PWR.umap` | extracted game and map content (local only) |

## Update, 2026-11-22: the format is settled and a generator exists

The first step and biggest risk above is done offline. The findings moved to
the engine reference, which is now the one place for how pathfinding works:
[AI pathfinding: sectors, links and how the simulation finds them](engine_ai_pathfinding.md).
In short, and correcting sections 1, 4 and 5 above:

- **The lookup is traced.** An instance's sectors are read only when its
  `pathfinding policy` is `static`. All 151 PWR instances say `none`, so the
  terrain tiles must be set `static` in the BSP (a change to the BSP package,
  not only the scenario).
- **Objects are per instance, not per definition.** Each static instance gets
  its own object ref, with one ref per surface of its definition.
- **The writer is proved.** B40 BSP 8's object refs rebuild byte for byte. The
  Blood Gulch crash is most likely the missing child blocks of the earlier
  writer.
- **Indices are 16-bit unsigned** in our generator now (65,535 links and
  vertices).
- **The generator is built** (`blam_sbsp::navmesh`). On B40 BSP 8 it picks the
  same walkable surfaces as Bungie's data on 2,075 of 2,078. On PWR it gives
  one connected ground over all 18 terrain tiles in 8 seconds: 15,197 sectors
  and 51,844 links with sector borders allowed to move by 1 wu, or 19,290 and
  62,109 at 0.6 wu. With exactly convex sectors of whole triangles PWR does
  not fit (about 98,000 links).
- **Three structures are separate pieces**: the two bases (near (-590, -80) m
  and (600, -80) m) and one more of the same size at (0, 690) m. They sit on
  the terrain without sharing its edges, so nothing joins them to it yet.
  Covenant waves that land at the sites do not need them; AI that should walk
  into a base does.
- **Water was not cut out in that run.** River and lake beds counted as
  floor. Section 2 above says deep water must be left out; whether the ground
  stays connected then is not measured.

**Run live on B40 (same day).** `level bake` now takes `blam.pathfinding` and
writes the generated sectors as object refs. On B40's BSP 8 an Elite walked
generated sectors across three instances to the player and killed them; the
control with Bungie's data behaved the same way. One thing the first run
taught: firing positions store the sector they stand on, and must be looked up
again when sectors change. Details in the engine article.

**Run live on PWR (same day).** With `instances: "ground"` the bake picks the
24 instances that carry ground, sets them `static` in the BSP, adds their 24
object refs, and the bots lane puts its spawns and 1,854 firing positions on
the generated sectors. Four AI placed at the capture sites and ordered to
distant areas all arrived, the furthest after 365 wu (1.1 km), with no crash
in about six minutes. One PC, one player, in warm-up.

The remaining steps, in order:

1. **Capture platforms and bases: done (same day).** The bake cuts the
   terrain away under a floor that lies on it (`headroom`), so the two end on
   one line and a seam joins them. All three bases and the four pads are now
   part of the main ground, an AI on a pad has a sector, and an Elite walked
   from open terrain onto the west base's floor. Not yet watched: an AI
   walking onto the centre platform. Details in the engine article,
   "Structures on the terrain".
2. **Water: done (same day).** The bake reads the map's two baked Flux
   states and leaves out floor more than 0.5 wu under the surface (27,788
   wu²). Both banks and both bases stay one piece of ground, and Elites
   ordered across the river in both directions arrived without a position
   sample in water. Details in the engine article, "Water".
3. **Zones and tasks per capture candidate: done (same day).**
   `blam.bots.objectives: ["koth_hill"]` gives each of the 11 capture spots an
   area, firing positions inside its boundary and a task `koth_hill_<order>`
   ([bots.md](bots.md#places-to-hold)). The wave director picks the task for
   the site the variant chose (site = order mod 3).
4. **A second player, and a fight: done (same day).** PC 1 hosted and PC 3
   joined through the hub list, with the same bake on both (hashes checked)
   and the same lobby (0.31.0). Results below.

5. **Wave director: built (same day).** Waves on the combat clock,
   targeting by live Covenant, the cap, and refilling a site after deaths
   live on PC 1; then on two PCs, where waves held all three sites and killed
   a player of each team ([pelican_warfare_waves.md](pelican_warfare_waves.md#4-covenant-waves)).
   Still open: the Spirit, the contest, re-tasking on zone events.

### Two PCs, 2026-11-22

The first run with two players: they end the warm-up, the Pelicans deploy,
and the score bar runs (a screenshot a few minutes in showed it live). Four
Elites were placed about 30 s after the join, whether before or after
deployment was not recorded; three more a few minutes later.

| | |
|---|---|
| AI in the joiner's object table | the first four at every one of 35 samples over 2.5 minutes; all seven in a listing and a 20 s watch after |
| Host and joiner copies apart | median 0.00 to 0.38 wu, never more than 0.44 wu. The two tables are read a moment apart, so this is an upper bound; an Elite still walking showed the 0.38. Most samples were 160 to 305 wu from the joiner, only 7 within 60 wu |
| Holding | six of seven held their hills on both PCs, the west hill's with positions 1 wu in from the rim; one stood on something not in the BSP and never moved |
| A fight | PC 3's player, moved beside the Elite on the west hill, lost its shield and then its body in about 10 s, and died there; the host logged a death with no player as its cause. It respawned at its base. Both PCs showed the same health and shield at every sample |
| Crash | none on either PC in about ten minutes |

Both PCs ran the released mods (HUD 0.23.1, LevelLoader 0.21.0, Lobby
0.31.0), not this branch's countdown and waves. The bot characters, the lobby
DLL and every HUD, LevelLoader and Lobby file hashed the same on both.

Not shown: a fight the joiner's player starts (it has no input driver in this
run), AI in vehicles, the Covenant waves, or AI counted in a zone's contest
(not built).

Two things for later runs:

- **The Elite's maxima read differently on the joiner** (body 50 and shield 79
  against the host's 75 and 75), though both show 100%, with the same
  character containers on both PCs. The joiner's unit seems to take its
  maxima from somewhere other than the character. Harmless so far; worth a
  look before damage is compared between PCs.
- **The AI nearest the centre platform has stuck in three runs**: on a bank
  facet with no sector (fixed), standing beside it 9 wu from the player, and
  here at (-18, -20) wu touching no BSP surface, its height wobbling 0.4 wu.
  No placed object stands within 8 wu of that spot. Not explained.
- **`mjolnir_sim_script` runs 16 lines a call** (`SCRIPT_MAX` in
  `native/lobby/mjolnir_lobby.c`). A 28-line call placed four of seven squads
  and dropped the rest without a word. One placed squad walking 300 wu across tiles, with the
   looser and the tighter border setting, to choose between them.
4. Steps 6 to 10 of the list above (proxy budget, zones and objectives, the
   Spirit, the wave director, tuning).

If the looser borders misbehave, the alternative is to cut triangles with
`bsp2d nodes` as Bungie does. The lookup for those is traced; a node writer is
not built.

notes.title: Pelican Warfare map 0.1.2: how it was built
notes.summary: Map 0.1.2 is 0.1.1 with four changes, built on 2026-11-23 and not yet released:
notes.body:
Map 0.1.2 is 0.1.1 with four changes, built on 2026-11-23 and not yet released:

- **No grass or plants on the approach roads.** `meadow_life.visual_margin` measured
  asphalt against the terrain geometry's road list only. The approach roads are asphalt
  in the road atlas but not in that list, so the baked meadow plants and the grass field
  grew across them (shot 8: the blue base's approach). The editor bakes both into the
  landscape level, so the fix needs the vegetation round re-run. The loose
  `foliage.bin` is not what draws them.
- **No rock through the middle bridge.** `pwr_bank_desert_b_806` stood 5.5 m up through
  the deck (shot 9). Its render row is dropped from the level, and its collision is sunk
  30 m into the bank (`visual_dressing/sink_rock_collision.py`). The new rule in
  `outcrops_v3.py` and `check_structure_clearance.py` keeps the next outcrop pass off
  bridge and culvert decks.
- **Zone bars in the top left**, the rebuilt chunk 958 (`build_pwr_warfare_zones.py`).
- **The branch's level additions** baked into chunk 997: bots, pathfinding, the
  Covenant wave squads, Spirits, Pelican staging and the moved-zone candidates.

## Inputs, pinned by hash

0.1.1 is `saturday.45/map-input` in the pelican-warfare Codex worktree
(`C:/Users/will/.codex/worktrees/pelican-warfare/haloce/out/pwr/river-riparian/`), which
is `saturday.44` with the newer chunk 958. Every `.ucas`, `pwr.level.json` and
`foliage.bin` matched PC 1's installed 0.1.1. Four `.utoc` files differ there only
because the launcher renames shader libraries at install (`ue-iostore` `shader_library`).

`saturday.44` was sealed from round 9031's content with this command, recovered from the
session that ran it (the receipts do not record the round's inputs):

```sh
RELEASE=1 UI=out/pwr/tactical-map-ui-v2/cooked GRASS=out/pwr/meadow-life/grass-r14/grass-mix.json \
  BRIDGES=out/pwr/bridges/fit RIDGES=1 VISTA_APRON=out/pwr/vista/apron-v9b AMBIENCE=out/pwr/ambience/sounds \
  BASES_COOKED=out/pwr/base-polish/gate6-native/Meteorite/Saved/StagedBuilds/Windows/Meteorite/Content/Paks \
  BASES_MANIFEST=out/pwr/base-int/art2/import.manifest.json \
  bash .dream-loop/vegetation/round.sh out/pwr/meadow-life/r12 44
```

A backup of that worktree's Unreal project, every saturday round, its Python environment
and `.dream-loop/vegetation` is on the NAS:
`\\UNAS-Pro\TheBigShareDrive\Unreal Projects\pelican-warfare-20261123` (90 GB).

## Steps

All new folders, nothing earlier overwritten; the Codex checkout ends clean.

1. **Plants** (`out/pwr/meadow-life/r13-roadfix`): `r12`'s eight inputs (candidates, both
   PCG outputs, home and edge shrubs, request, receipt, prepare) copied, then
   `meadow_life.py finalize` with the fixed script and `PWR_LEVEL_JSON` at the released
   level. `finalize` now drops plants on roads by `candidates()`'s own margins, so the
   PCG pass is not re-run: 903 of 388,953 plants go, nothing else changes.
2. **Grass field** (`out/pwr/meadow-life/grass-r15`): `meadow_grass_field.py` with the same
   command as `grass-r14`, plus a copy of its `grass-mix.json`. 915 texels change, 854 go
   to zero (shot 8's road: 81-104 to 0), none gain grass.
3. **Round** `saturday.46`: the command above with `r13-roadfix`, `grass-r15` and
   `UI=out/pwr/tactical-map-ui-v3/cooked`, version 46. The Codex worktree needed its own
   CLI and six example binaries built first (`blam-cli`; `ue-asset` retarget_package,
   mesh_rewrite, world_imports; `ue-iostore` extract_file, replace_members; `blam-pack`
   package_add). Against `saturday.45` only 958, 965 (landscape) and 997 (world bake)
   differ; `BakeFoliage` baked exactly 388,050 plants.
4. **Collision**: `sink_rock_collision.py` on `river-riparian/native/physics`
   (1174 triangles matched the rock hull's 1174 faces), then `mjolnir level collision`
   as `cook_riparian_toe.py` runs it. The untouched scene re-cooks to the released BSP
   byte for byte (`b03b92e6`); the new one differs in instance 21's bounds only. A ray
   at the rock's old top met it at 38.43 wu before and passes to the deck after, and in
   game a player walked through the spot.
5. **Final bake** of 997: the round's `river-basin/native/native-level.json` plus the
   branch's `blam` bots, pathfinding, objects, object names, vehicles and
   `warfare.capture_candidates` (equal to `out/pwr-nav/pwr-ai.level.json` without the rock),
   with `--bsp 8=` the new BSP and `--world` round 46's `river-riparian/packaging/LPE.umap`.
   This branch's CLI re-bakes the round's own level to the round's 997 byte for byte.
6. **Pack**: `saturday.46/map-input` with the new 997 and `pwr.level.json` (0.1.1's, rock
   row out, candidates in), `map pack --version 0.1.2 --sign` with 0.1.1's metadata.
   `release_loss.py` against 0.1.1: nothing lost. Members changed: 958, 965, 997,
   `map/level.json` (and `mjolnir.json`, `signature.json`).

Working files are in this worktree's `out/pwr-rebuild/` (not in git): the signed
`pelican-warfare-0.1.2.mjolnir`, `map-input-final`, `physics`, `bake-final`.

## Proven

On PC 1 with the pack's containers as developer builds (`mjolnir dev install`):
shot 8's road is bare, shot 9's deck is clear and walkable, the zone bars load from the new
958, the seated rider reads ZONES OPEN IN 0:46, and every one of the 11 wave places holds
its four squads. Not yet: the tactical map opened with M (its widget only loads when
opened), and a two-PC match on 0.1.2.

notes.title: Pelican Warfare: shipped-quality detail from the base game's own assets
notes.summary: The goal: PWR should look as if 343 shipped it. The base game already contains most of what a temperate alpine valley needs, and PWR uses only 106 of the 4,955 relevant assets. levels/warfare/pwr/data/base-game-assets.md (and .json) catalogues them all, from a read of every…
notes.body:
The goal: PWR should look as if 343 shipped it. The base game already contains most of what
a temperate alpine valley needs, and PWR uses only 106 of the 4,955 relevant assets.
`levels/warfare/pwr/data/base-game-assets.md` (and `.json`) catalogues them all, from a
read of every base-game container on 2026-11-23: package path, class, size, vertex count,
which shipped levels use it, and whether PWR already does.

## What the survey found

- **A30 ("Halo") is a whole temperate river-valley biome PWR barely touches.** It ships
  landscape layers for meadow, stony soil, scree and riverbed (`MM_A30_Landscape` blends
  Megascans sets with hex texture bombing, `MF_Hex_TextureBombing`), and art-directed
  PCG assemblies for river boulders, log jams, scree, tree skirts, rushes and sedges.
- **C10 ships a riparian bank kit**: eroded bank modules 45-80 m long, each with a wet
  material instance. These are exactly the river and lake cut banks PWR models by hand.
- **PWR's open meadow is shaded from CE detail textures**, not the Megascans surfaces
  next to them, and three Megascans sets PWR does sample are read for diffuse and normal
  only: their roughness, height and AO maps (`_ORHG`) ship unused.
- **The rocks PWR places all use their `_NoSnow` instances.** The same meshes ship with
  snow-capped instances (`MI_Rock_Glacial_*`, `MI_Rock_AllSnow`), and B40 shipped the
  snow-line surfaces (snow-covered grass, windswept snowy stones, melting snow) that PWR
  jumps over between meadow and peak.
- **No road furniture shipped**: no signs, lamp posts, fences, cones, curbs, puddles or
  tire-mark decals. Roads have to be finished with their verges (gravel shoulders, scree,
  boulders) and the landscape deformation system for tracks.
- **Wrecks ship as meshes**: a destroyed Pelican, a destroyed Scorpion, A30's crashed
  lifepod with 21 debris pieces and its crash mound. A crash site is on-theme for a mode
  called Pelican Warfare.
- **About 2,700 ambience sounds** (A30 river, rapids and waterfall loops among them) sit in
  Wwise; whether level data can trigger them is unverified. Fluid Flux's plain
  `SW_RiverAmbient` works with PWR's emitters today.

## Constraints every step keeps

- Reference base-game assets in place; never copy them into PWR's packs.
- Foliage is already about 18% of the GPU frame: new plants replace plant kinds, they do not
  add on top. Measure frame time before and after every step.
- Cooked decal masters crashed the game (a PSO fatal), so caustic and wet decals are out
  until that is solved; that rules out the Fluid Flux river template's decal pieces.
- Anything a player can touch needs Blam collision (the outcrop hull path, or a crate tag
  that collides and syncs by itself). Rocks and banks must clear
  `check_structure_clearance.py` and stay off roads (`meadow_life.visual_margin`).
- Everything is data the map ships: decor, level `effects`, `lights` and sounds, cooked
  landscape layers. No per-frame Lua.
- Before and after shots from the user's FlyCam set (`MJOLNIR_FlyCam_shots_PWR.json`)
  for every step, plus a two-PC check.

## The work, in order of what a player notices first

1. **Ground that reads as real.** Give `M_PWRPilot` A30's meadow, stony-soil, scree and
   beach-sand-with-pebbles layers with their ORHG maps, height blending and hex texture
   bombing, plus B40's snow-line surfaces between meadow and snow. This changes every
   square metre of the map: no more flat green, no visible tiling, wet and dry variation.
   Needs new layer slots and a landscape cook (`landscape-shaders-in-world-chunk`: the
   LAND chunk changes and the world rebakes).
2. **Rivers and lakes with real edges.** C10's riparian banks (wet instances at the water
   line) on the cut banks; river cobbles on gravel bars; A30's boulder and log-jam
   assemblies at bends and fords (their member meshes re-placed as decor with hulls).
   Lake margins get a shore band: beach sand with pebbles and shoreline beach rocks in the
   landscape, Nordic beach rocks and driftwood (the fallen spruce meshes) on top, so the
   lakes read as beaches rather than grass meeting water.
3. **Mountains that belong to the valley.** Snow-capped instances on every rock above the
   snow line; alpine scree fans under cliffs (`SM_Scree_Alpine_A-C`, scree clumps, A30's
   scree assembly) to bed boulders into the ground; C20's snowy mountain vista in front of
   the distant ring for a nearer silhouette; snow gusts on the ridge crests.
4. **Forest floors with depth.** Deadfall (fallen spruce and old fallen trees), mossy roots
   and boulders, lumpy moss, turkey-tail mushrooms and lichen, swapped in for some of the
   current understory kinds; windswept dead snags at the treeline; falling pine needles
   and light cones (`SM_LightCone_Plane_1x` with its animated fading instance) in the
   pine stands.
5. **Life and air.** The waterfall mist and rainbow set on the cascade; ambient ground fog
   over the lakes and river bends; dragonflies over the reeds; river and rapids audio
   along the water.
6. **Bases and roads.** Forerunner tall and panel light fixtures with real lights on base
   walls and pads; the shipped Forerunner metal instances with grime tiers on base and
   bridge surfaces; Forerunner exterior ruins (crash-site abutments, beach terminal
   pillars, tarmac pillars) on ridges; gravel shoulders and boulders along the roads;
   vehicle tracks through the landscape deformation system.
7. **A landmark.** A crashed-Pelican site: the destroyed Pelican hull, lifepod debris and
   crash mound, a wind-bent smoke column, and the E30 wreckage crate tags for collision
   that syncs with no code.

## Progress

### Step 1, first half: A30 ground as level data (2026-11-23)

The landscape textures are not baked into `M_PWRPilot`: the loader binds them at load from
`landscape.pbr.surfaces` (`Land.pbr` in the level loader). So the first half of step 1 is
level data, with no cook. PWR builds carry the last release's `pwr.level.json` forward
(`docs/pwr_map_0.1.2.md`, step 6), so the next pack runs
`levels/warfare/pwr/visual_dressing/ground_surfaces.py` on it; PWR's look in
`tools/level/build_landscape.py` holds the same values for a level generated from scratch:

- **Meadow** (`GrassD/N/O`): A30's wild grass and weeds (`T_Wild_Grass_NSVT_D_A30`, its
  normal and ORHG) in place of a desaturated grass the tint painted green. Up close the flat
  green felt becomes clover, leaf litter and soil; `grass_tint` goes from 0.40/0.62/0.36 to
  1.0/1.05/0.9.
- **Track stone** (`MidD/N/O`): A30's stones on soil in the wheel ruts and shoulders. PWR
  runs the shader's alpine branch (`Alpine.w > 1.5`), where `SandD` is the track's earth
  and `MidD` its stone; `SandB*` is not read there. Putting stony soil in `SandD` (the
  first try) turned the forest tracks grey, so the earth stays.
- The default grass map is OHRG and A30's is ORHG. The shader reads `.r` (occlusion) the
  same and floors grass roughness at 0.92, so only partial-grass edges read height as
  roughness. Nothing visible came of it.

Tested on PC 1 by swapping the loose `level.json` and rehosting, FlyCam shots 1-9 before and
after in one session (`out/pwr-detail/before2`, `afterB`). Frame cost at 4K, GPU ms:

| shot | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (lake meadow) | 13.00 | 13.03 |
| 3 (lake shore) | 14.43 | 14.40 |
| 8 (road) | 11.62 | 11.49 |

Same sampler count and no measurable GPU cost; a little more texture memory (A30's grass
is 2048 px where the old one was 1024). From the air (FlyCam at 480 m over the south
meadow) the valley reads olive and khaki instead of lawn green, with no tiling carpet
and no seam against the distant ring.

Still to do for step 1, and these need the shader and a landscape cook: the beach band
at lake shores (PWR has no sea, so the shader draws no shore band; it needs a shore mask),
and B40's snow-line surfaces between meadow and snow (`Rip*` holds the snow itself, and
there is no slot for a band between them).

### Step 2, first part: a shore band along every lake and river (2026-11-23)

**What did not work.** Scattering the base game's rocky-beach patches and beach stones along
the banks as decor: the patches are scanned half-discs made to blend into a landscape, and
drew as hard-edged discs (`S_Nordic_Beach_Rocky_Ground_ukohbbi` drew black); 20 cm stones
read as specks on banks tens of metres long. The collision scene is also full (1,199,995 of
the pipeline's 1,200,000 surfaces), so anything a player could walk into has to reuse hull
slots. The single stones draw correctly and stay candidates for that later round.

**What was built (release 48, on PC 1 as dev chunks; not packed or released).** The banks' surface itself:

- `tools/level/shore_mask.py` bakes a mask from the map's own baked Fluid Flux water (any map
  with `flux_state/`): signed metres from the water's edge, height above that water, and
  coverage, 2048 px over `landscape.pbr.rect`.
- `unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/apply_pwr_shore_band.py` binds it to `M_PWRPilot`'s valley
  node (`PWRShoreData`, plus `LandRect` for its placement) and replaces the northern lake's
  compiled-in shoreline (48 hand-entered spans) with the same beach drawn wherever the mask
  has water: damp earth, gravel toward the water, darker and glossier at the wet line. A mask
  with no coverage draws nothing.
- GPU cost at 4K, shots 1, 3, 8: 12.88 / 14.27 / 11.65 ms against 13.03 / 14.40 / 11.49.

**How it is built** (release 48 in the pelican-warfare Codex worktree):

1. `python tools/level/shore_mask.py <map folder>/pwr.level.json T_PWRShoreData.png`.
2. `.dream-loop/vegetation/round_shore.sh` (a copy of `round.sh` there, which is gitignored)
   adds one step: with `SHORE=<mask png>` it runs `apply_pwr_shore_band.py` (apply, then
   verify in a fresh editor) right after the round restores `M_PWRPilot`, **before** the grass
   step, and declares `M_PWRPilot` and `T_PWRShoreData` as allowed landscape changes. The
   order matters: the landscape grass maps bake from the material, and an edit after them
   left most of the meadow tufts missing (round 47).
3. Same command as 0.1.2's round with `SHORE=` added and version 48.
4. **The world bake (997) has to be redone from the new round's `LPE.umap`.** The landscape
   draws through a `LandscapeMaterialInstanceConstant` stored in the world, with the shaders
   of the material it was cooked against: a new 965 under the old 997 draws the old ground.
   0.1.2's bake command with `--world` the new round's `packaging/LPE.umap`.

A plain `round.sh` restores the old `M_PWRPilot` and silently drops the band; only
`round_shore.sh` with `SHORE=` keeps it. Checked: the band touches road only under the
bridge decks (the road atlas, offline), no outline from the air, release 48 differs from 46
only in 965 and 997.

**Gravel.** The band first drew its stones from the `SandBD/N` slot, which road shoulders,
tracks and the riverbed share. Of seven base-game surfaces tried there,
`Shoreline_Beach_Rocks_ullmagidy` was the only one where cobbles read on a bank, but from
the air it outlined every road and the dirt track in pale stone. So that slot keeps the
ground gravel, and the band samples the river cobble scan the outlet already uses
(`RiverCobble`/`RiverCobbleN`), which touches no road. Release 49 (2026-11-23): real cobbles
at the water on every river and lake, roads unchanged from the air.

**Driftwood and boulders, in recycled collision slots.**
`levels/warfare/pwr/visual_dressing/riparian_swaps.py` swaps 48 of the 133 shore rocks
(Glacial Med/Lrg rows within 9 m of the water, 35 m apart, clear of roads and decks) for
24 driftwood logs (A30's large fallen tree, the 5.5 m fallen log at 1.4-1.8x; the smaller
log scans read as twigs) and 24 boulders (mossy boulder, Nordic beach rocks, tundra
boulder). Logs lie along the shore, pitched to the ground under both ends. Each new piece's
convex hull is capped to the rock's own triangle count (`budget = (slots + 4) / 2 - 8`) and
written into the rock's triangles; spare triangles sink 30 m. 2,154 triangles written,
1,490 sunk, the scene's size unchanged. Log triangles get the scene's `tough_organic_wood`
material (they sound and spark as wood), boulders `hard_terrain_stone`; a plane index's flip
flag is honoured (none of the swapped surfaces has it). The plan is `levels/warfare/pwr/data/riparian-swaps.json`.

    riparian_swaps.py plan  <level> <shore mask> <terrain> visual-v6/scenery/hulls <new hulls> plan.json
    riparian_swaps.py level <level> plan.json <out level>
    riparian_swaps.py collide <0.1.2 physics> <level> plan.json visual-v6/scenery/hulls <new hulls> <out>
    mjolnir level collision <out>/collision_scene.json ... --out pwr.sbsp   (as cook_riparian_toe.py)
    mjolnir level bake ... --bsp 8=<that pwr.sbsp> --world <round 49 LPE.umap>

Checked on PC 1 by dropping the player on log root ends 4-4.6 m from where the old rocks
stood: it came to rest 0.58 and 0.64 m above the ground, on the logs, against bare ground
3 m away (28.64 wu, heightfield 28.65). No new footprint touches the road atlas or comes
within 4 m of any of the level's 262 gameplay points (15 m for zone candidates). Only the
tops were tested in game; sides and bullets use the same triangles. GPU at 4K, shots 1, 3, 8:
12.94 / 14.42 / 11.49 ms.

**River stones and the band without tiling (release 51, 2026-11-23).** From the air the
band's cobble repeated every 2.6 m along a bank, and up close it was a photo on flat ground.

- The band now samples the cobble scan the way the surveyed reach does
  (`pwr_scanned_riverbank.ush`): a skewed triangle lattice of about 3.7 m picks three
  rotated, offset, rescaled copies and blends them by sharpened barycentric weight.
- `levels/warfare/pwr/visual_dressing/river_stones.py` scatters real stone meshes over the
  same band, from the shore mask and the heightfield: about 64,700 cobbles (River Stone 01
  C/E/G at 1-2.1x, 25-75 cm, densest just under the water and halving every 1.4 m up the
  bank) and 7,200 larger stones with shadows (River Stone 01 I and Nordic Beach Rock
  vbumba2fa at 1.4-2.8x). They sit a third sunk and tilt half way to the ground. None on
  slopes steeper than 0.7, within 2.5 m of a road, or within 2 m of a bridge corridor. The
  Megascans scan `Nordic_Beach_Rock_vgjidiqmw` draws black in game and is left out. They
  bake into LPE as static instances (`apply_pwr_river_stones.py`, actor `PWR_RiverStones`,
  through `bake_foliage` like the meadow life) and have no collision.
- Cull: cobbles 90-110 m, stones 100-120 m. At 40-55 m (release 50) the cobbles were gone
  from FlyCam shot 4, where the bank is 60-100 m off.
- Cost: none measurable. With the stones hidden or shown, frame 15.39 / 16.67 / 14.00 ms and
  GPU 12.92 / 14.37 / 11.55 ms at shots 1, 3, 8. This session's game thread ran about 1.5 ms
  higher than the afternoon's at the same shots, stones hidden or not; GPU matched.

Build: `round_shore.sh` with `STONES=<river_stones.py output>` bakes them right after the
meadow life (round 51), then the world bake (997) from that round's `LPE.umap`, as above.

    river_stones.py <level> <shore mask> <terrain dir> <out>

**Reflections behind the saplings.** At FlyCam shot 1 the headwater lake drew a pale column
behind every sapling in front of it. The screen-trace thickness (0.03, 2026-11-21) never
fixed it: 0.03, 0.1 and 0.5 look the same. With hardware ray tracing, Lumen gives a surface
its lighting cards only within `r.RayTracing.Culling.Radius`, and the game ships it at -1, so
no surface had cards (Lumen's overview shows the terrain yellow, "no mesh cards"). A
reflection ray that left the screen behind a sapling found the terrain unlit and fell through
to the sky. LevelLoader 0.21.2 sets the radius from `environment.reflections.trace_radius`;
PWR's `vista.json` sets 30000 (300 m). The columns are gone for +0.05-0.09 ms. Other maps
with Lumen reflections may have the same dead cards ("far = black" on Containment, for one),
not yet tried.

Next for step 2: the bank shapes themselves (long smooth slopes no texture fixes).

Each step is its own dressing round through the existing pipeline (the vegetation round
for landscape and baked plants, the outcrop and decor passes for meshes with hulls,
level data for effects, lights and sound), sealed as a numbered build and compared with
the last release (`release_loss.py`) like 0.1.2 (`docs/pwr_map_0.1.2.md`).

notes.title: Pelican Warfare tactical overview
notes.summary: Press M during Pelican Warfare to open or close the north-up map. It shows your heading, living teammates, available and friendly occupied Warthogs, Scorpions and Banshees, the friendly Pelican, both bases, and capture sites A–C with their current owners. The side panel shows…
notes.body:
Press **M** during Pelican Warfare to open or close the north-up map. It shows
your heading, living teammates, available and friendly occupied Warthogs,
Scorpions and Banshees, the friendly Pelican, both bases, and capture sites A–C
with their current owners. The side panel shows the control score and legend.
The map remains a read-only overlay; movement and the match continue.
Press **N** while it is open to cycle the full overview, 2× and 4× views.
Zoomed views follow your position; map edges are clamped to the actual terrain.

Chat, chat rules, pause menus and a hidden HUD suppress the map. It closes on
travel and at the end of a match. Enemy players and enemy occupied vehicles
are excluded by native code; known base locations and capture ownership are
public. Unknown vehicle occupants are treated conservatively. Empty vehicles
use neutral icons. Dead bodies do not appear as teammates.

The background is generated from the shipped runtime heightfield, graded road
polygons, water mask, actual tree positions and base geometry. Its extent is
the 2 km × 2 km playable terrain; decorative distant mountains are outside it.
Authoring/native metre coordinates map to `u=(x+1000)/2000`,
`v=(1000-y)/2000`. The image and markers share those exact bounds. The source
and reproducible generator are in `levels/warfare/pwr/tactical-map`.

`native/lobby/warfare_map_core.h` implements the bounded visibility policy;
`warfare_map.h` reads salted native simulation handles at 5 Hz. The native
map pump publishes a versioned snapshot only while the overlay requests it.
The existing 2 Hz warfare HUD protocol remains unchanged. Lua only parses and
places a fixed pool of 64 UMG icons; it performs no world actor scans or gameplay
writes. Two advancing snapshots from the HUD's current match instance are
required, and stale samples clear the icons.

The standalone widget builder is
`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_pwr_tactical_map.py`. Chunk 958 owns
`/Game/MJOLNIR/UI/WBP_MJOLNIRTacticalMap` and the eight overview and marker
textures under `/Game/MJOLNIR/TacticalMap`. The class-lifetime allowlist retains its Blueprint
class across travel, as for the existing HUD. Temporary hiding reuses the same
widget pool.

After the widget import and Unreal cook, run
`python levels/warfare/pwr/tactical-map/package.py` to verify the generated
class, marker pool and textures and stage chunk 958 under
`out/pwr/tactical-map-ui-v2/cooked`.

Validation commands:

```powershell
powershell -File native/lobby/test-warfare-map.ps1
lua tools/tests/test_tactical_map.lua
lua tools/tests/test_ui_class_lifetime.lua
```

Live verification must include M toggle/reopen, movement and heading updates,
chat/pause suppression, vehicle positions, capture ownership, and map travel.
Multiplayer teammate filtering has portable regression coverage; a live remote
teammate requires a second connected player and should be reported separately.

notes.title: Installing a map while the game runs
notes.summary: A player who joins a server on a map they don't have, or whose host or post-game vote picks one, gets a prompt with the map's hub screenshot and details. DOWNLOAD installs the map and loads it into the running game, and the join (or the lobby) carries on. There is no restart.…
notes.body:
A player who joins a server on a map they don't have, or whose host or
post-game vote picks one, gets a prompt with the map's hub screenshot and
details. DOWNLOAD installs the map and loads it into the running game, and the
join (or the lobby) carries on. There is no restart. The same screenshots now
appear on the map select, the lobby card, FIND GAMES and the post-game vote.

Verified on CU4, 2026-10-09:

- Wizard was uninstalled (launcher state, cache, Paks, `MJOLNIRMaps`, and the
  registration container rebuilt without it). From the running game's
  download screen it then downloaded, verified, installed, mounted and
  registered in under six seconds, and hosted and played.
- Reactor, a halomaps.org conversion that was never in the registration
  container or in Paks at boot, was registered and mounted by hand while the
  game ran, then hosted and played. The game exited cleanly afterwards.

Then on two PCs (PC 2 without Wizard: launcher uninstall, so its
registration container lacked it too):

- **FIND GAMES:** PC 2 used DOWNLOAD AND JOIN on PC 1's Wizard game. It
  downloaded, mounted and registered the map, joined the lobby, and both
  played it.
- **The host's pick:** PC 1 changed the lobby to Hang 'em High. PC 2 got the
  prompt, PC 1's lobby showed "WAITING FOR 1 PLAYER TO DOWNLOAD", PC 2
  downloaded it, and both played.
- **The vote:** the post-game vote chose The Longest. PC 2's option read
  `/ DOWNLOAD`, it got the prompt, PC 1 held its countdown until PC 2 was
  ready, and both played.

Two things only a second PC could show, both fixed:

1. **The map's index in the campaign list must match on every machine**
   (next section).
2. **The live row's MapGuid has to match the cooked one.** The C copy of
   `map_guid` upper-cased all of "MJOLNIR map CODE", not just the code. A
   host alone never notices: it only has to agree with itself. A client
   whose row disagrees with the host's loads the world, and the game never
   starts.

## Every machine needs the same index for the map

`SetAndBeginCampaign` (0x7B446E0) finds the map by a linear scan of
`DA_FirstPlayableCampaign.ScenarioList` and keeps its index
(BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem+0x38). A fireteam only starts when every
machine's index agrees:

- PC 1 has two local maps (CSN, YOY) that PC 2 lacks. Danger Canyon is index
  15 on PC 1 and 14 on PC 2, and both loaded the world and stayed "not in a
  game".
- Blood Gulch sits before both local maps, at 12 on each, and started.

Installed map sets differ from player to player, and a live install appends
at the end, so this has to be handled:

- The host sends its index with the map: field 4 of the lobby message,
  field 6 of the vote message.
- A guest joining a match under way asks for it (`where` / `mapindex`).
- Clients call `MapLive.follow`, which uses `mjolnir_scenario_place`
  (native/map_registry) to swap the handle to that index. When the list is
  shorter, it pads with copies of B40's handle; the scan finds the real B40
  first, so a filler never answers for anything.

The map registry logs the move, e.g. `place DCN: index 14 -> 15`.

## What a converted map needs, and when each step happens

| Step | At boot (the launcher's install) | While the game runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Containers in Paks | `hub::materialize` copies them; the engine mounts them at startup | the launcher's live install copies them under the same names; `mjolnir_mount_paks` mounts them |
| Short world name resolves | `mjolnir_map_registry` indexes `Paks/*.utoc` at load | the mount re-reads the indexes |
| `DT_Scenarios` row and campaign `ScenarioList` handle | cooked into `pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P` | `mjolnir_scenario_add` clones the B40 row in memory |
| Frontend levels cache entry | built at boot from every `DT_Scenarios` row | the same insert, called by `mjolnir_scenario_add` |
| Level data and the menu list | `maps::sync` writes `MJOLNIRMaps/<CODE>/` and `maps.json` | `maps::add_live` writes the same; the lobby re-reads it every time |

The frontend levels cache was the missing piece. The 2026-09 notes put the
boot-time gate in the simulation's own levels registry. That registry is the
data arrays `campaign levels` (64) and `multiplayer levels` (50) in
`HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll` at 0xbd5738 and 0xbd5748, and on CU4 they are
**empty**. Nothing reads them, and their caps limit nothing.

The real boot-time step is in the exe:
`UBlamFrontendLevelsEngineGlueSubsystem::BuildRuntimeCachesFromBuiltInMapInfoDataAsset`
(0x7B7D180). It passes every row of the tables `BuiltInMapInfoData` names to
a per-row insert (0x7BAC140). That insert builds the subsystem's per-map
entries: 0x14c bytes each, keyed by MapGuid, in a sparse array at
subsystem+0x138. It then stamps each campaign map's entry with its
campaign's id (+0x120).

A row added without that entry loads the world, but the simulation stays "not
in a game" (`mjolnir live arrays`). With the entry, the map plays. So there is
no limit on how many hub maps a player can install. Only maps registered at
boot or added this session can start, and every start path adds the map
first.

## The pieces

**Launcher, `--install-map <CODE> [--release <id>] --progress <file>`** (`hub::run_live_install`).
This is the ordinary install (`install_one`), run with no window:

- It checks the hub's sha256, the platform signature when there is one, and
  the author signature.
- It writes the same cache, `hub_state.json` and active profile, and uses the
  same Paks file names. The next launch therefore copies nothing and rebuilds
  the registration container, because its record lacks the new code.
- Since launcher 0.14.0 it writes every file under the pack's `map/` (a
  remastered map's foliage file and `decals/`). Since 0.14.1 a map that is
  installed but missing one of the files its level names is fetched again at
  the release it has, and its containers in Paks are left as they are.

What it leaves out, because the game is running:

- It never rewrites a container the game holds open: an update of a mounted
  map is written beside it under a patch name, and the game swaps them
  ([below](#versions-and-updating-a-map-the-game-has-loaded)).
- It doesn't install or update code mods: their DLLs are loaded.
- It treats a missing dependency (the CE runtime pack) as an error, and
  since launcher 0.14.0 one older than the floor of the pack's range too,
  naming the range and the installed version.
- It doesn't rebuild the registration container: it is mounted.

It decides everything that can stop it before it writes a container, so a
refusal leaves Paks as it was, and a write that fails takes back what it
wrote. A map that downloaded but cannot be loaded into the running game (a
pack it needs is already loaded in another version, or Paks written for
another profile holds another mod's shader library under its number) stays
installed and enabled. The message then says to quit and start the game
again from the launcher, and that launch writes the map with everything
else. A container that only shares a chunk number with one already mounted
is not such a case
([docs/chunk_numbering.md](chunk_numbering.md)).

Progress goes to `<file>` as one JSON object, replaced as it changes:

- `{"stage":"start","code":...}` first.
- `{"stage":"download","received":n,"total":n}`, where the total comes from
  the hub listing, since the archive is streamed without a length.
- Then `{"stage":"done","mount":[...],...}` or `{"stage":"error","message":...}`.

The launcher records its own path in `launcher_exe.txt` in its config folder
each time it starts. A launcher from before live installs records nothing, so
the game says to update it instead of opening it.

**MJOLNIRLobby's native half** (`native/lobby`):

- `mjolnir_map_install` starts the launcher for a code (`[A-Z0-9]{3}` only).
- `mjolnir_map_install_status` says whether the launcher is still running.
- `mjolnir_hub_call` gained a `FILE` method that saves a hub response to
  `MJOLNIRMaps\_covers\<name>`; the name is a plain file name.

**MJOLNIRLevelLoader's native half** (`native/map_registry`):

- `mjolnir_mount_paks` calls `FCoreDelegates::MountPak`. The storage is at
  exe 0xD349040; the bound instance holds the `FPakPlatformFile` at +0x18 and
  `HandleMountPakDelegate` (0x4694C00) at +0x20, and the method is checked
  before the call. It mounts each `.pak`, then its IoStore sibling with the
  IoDispatcher and the package store, and fires `OnPakFileMounted`. Then it
  re-reads the world index.
- `mjolnir_scenario_add` does the following:
  - clones a template row (B40, as the cooked rows do) with the codename's
    world, `ScenarioName` and MapGuid (`blam_pack::scenario::map_guid`);
  - adds it to `DT_Scenarios`' `RowMap`;
  - appends the `ScenarioList` handle;
  - calls the frontend levels insert and copies the campaign id from the
    template's entry.

  Every allocation goes through `GMalloc` (exe 0xD4B7428: Malloc at vtable
  +0x28, Free at +0x48), so the engine frees them at shutdown like its own.
  An FText copied by value takes a reference (`+8` of its text data).

Both are CU4-only, with one set of exe addresses per build picked by the
exe's PE timestamp (`exe_profiles`). The exe RVAs in this note are the Steam
exe's; the Xbox app's CU4 exe has its own set (PR #179,
[game_pass.md](game_pass.md)).

**MJOLNIRLobby** (`Scripts/maplive.lua`, wired into `main.lua`):

- `MapLive.refresh` / `info` read the hub listings (`GET /maps`,
  `/maps/{code}`).
- `MapLive.cover` / `texture` keep each map's cover on disk and read it with
  `KismetRenderingLibrary.ImportFileAsTexture2D`. Textures are kept by name
  and found again with `StaticFindObject`, never kept by reference: a
  transient texture no brush holds any more is collected.
- `MapLive.install` starts the launcher, polls its progress, mounts, then
  registers.
- `MapLive.register` adds a map's scenario records unless they are there
  already. It runs before every start (`startGame`), before a join from
  FIND GAMES, and when a client hears the host's map.

## The flows

- **FIND GAMES:**
  - A game on a map you lack offers **DOWNLOAD AND JOIN**. The download
    screen explains why, and once the map is in, the join runs as usual.
  - The details panel shows the map's screenshot and download size.
  - QUICK JOIN still only picks maps you have.
- **The host picks a map a client lacks:**
  - The client's lobby offers the download once; after that, the lobby's
    START button reads **DOWNLOAD MAP**.
  - The client reports `mapstate <code> prompt|download <pct>|ready|declined|error`
    to the host.
  - While someone is deciding or downloading, the host's lobby footer says
    so. A first START warns; a second START within ten seconds starts
    without them.
- **The post-game vote picks a map a client lacks:**
  - Vote options on maps you lack read `/ DOWNLOAD`.
  - When the vote ends on one, the client gets the download screen.
  - The host's countdown waits while anyone is deciding (up to 25 s
    without word) or downloading (`Live.DOWNLOAD_WAIT`, 180 s), and the
    post-game footer says who it is waiting for.
- **Test verbs:**
  - `mjolnir_auto download <CODE>` opens the screen.
  - `mjolnir_auto install <CODE>` installs with no screen.
  - `mjolnir_auto join` downloads the listed game's map first.

## Versions, and updating a map the game has loaded

Every player has to run the host's release of the map. The host sends it,
as its hub release id and version (read from the launcher's
`hub_state.json`, `MapLive.release`):

- in the lobby message (fields 5–6);
- in the vote message (fields 7–8);
- in `starting`;
- in the hub listing (`map_release_id` / `map_version`, migration 0016).

A guest with another release, older or newer, gets the download screen as
an update: "ANOTHER VERSION OF THIS MAP — The host runs WIZARD 1.4.0; you
have 1.1.0", with UPDATE (or UPDATE AND JOIN in FIND GAMES). It installs the
host's exact release (`--install-map <CODE> --release <id>`), even one older
than the newest. A guest that won't update is treated like one without the
map: named on the host's first START, sent back on the second.

**The swap happens in the running game.**

- The engine holds a mounted `.ucas` open, so the launcher writes the new
  release beside it as `<name>_2_P`, `_3_P`, and so on.
  `FPakPlatformFile::Mount` gives a `_<n>_P` pak 100·n more order than a
  plain `_P` one, so the update wins even where a later Steam launch mounts
  both. The next launch from the launcher removes the patch files
  (`paks_strays`) and writes the release under its usual name.
- The launcher also removes, or lists for unmounting, any other copy of the
  map in Paks: an earlier patch, or a load-order number the profile no
  longer uses. Two releases mounted together mix their packages.
- The game unmounts the old containers through `FCoreDelegates::OnUnmountPak`
  (exe 0xD349248 → 0x4694CC0, `mjolnir_unmount_paks`). That drops each pak
  and its IoStore container from the package store and the IoDispatcher.
  The game then collects garbage, mounts the new release, and rescans.
- Verified on one PC: Wizard 1.1.0 was played, then updated to 1.4.0 from
  the frontend.
  - Before the update, a texture only 1.4.0 has (`…_sunshare`) didn't load;
    after it, it did.
  - The updated map then played with its baked lighting.
- Verified on two PCs: PC 2 downgraded live to 1.1.0, joined PC 1's 1.4.0
  lobby, got the update prompt and updated.
  - A 1.1.0-only texture no longer resolved there, and the 1.4.0 one did.
  - Both played.

**Not tested yet:** FIND GAMES comparing releases before the join. The
listing fields need the hub deploy and migration 0016. Until then a joiner
compares once the host's lobby message arrives, which the two-PC test used.

## Joining from a link

A website links a listed game as `mjolnir://join/<lobby id>` (the hub's
lobby id). The launcher registers the `mjolnir` scheme (its `src/links.rs`
also takes `mjolnir://mod/<slug>` and `mjolnir://map/<CODE>`, which only
open the launcher's pages, and `mjolnir://update`, the game's out-of-date
prompt, [update_check.md](update_check.md)). A join that has to start the
game runs the launcher's launch check first, as Launch does.

- **The launcher** (`hub_join_lobby`) checks multiplayer is installed: the
  four map code mods present and on, and the CE runtime pack installed and
  on. If not, it offers Install multiplayer instead. Otherwise it writes
  `MJOLNIRLobby\native\pending_join.txt` (a temporary file renamed over it)
  and starts the game if no game process is running:

  ```
  lobby=<lobby id>
  at=<unix seconds>
  ```

- **MJOLNIRLobby** reads the file from the main menu's poll (every 1.5 s),
  only once the player is signed in (a main menu has been up) and in the
  frontend. During a match the file waits. It deletes the file on reading,
  and drops a join older than ten minutes or one it can't read. It then
  opens FIND GAMES and, when the list arrives, chooses the game with that
  id and joins it as JOIN does, so DOWNLOAD AND JOIN, a full game and
  another version are handled as usual. A game that is not listed reads
  "That game has ended or is no longer listed."

**Not tested yet:** all of it in game. The launcher side is unit-tested.

## What was still open on 2026-10-09

**Update 2026-10-21:** both items below are done; they were verified on two
PCs on 2026-10-09 (eced8a14).

- **A guest that can't get the map.** One left in the fireteam holds
  everyone's start. Two PCs showed the host waiting forever on Gephyrophobia
  because the guest had declined it. So:
  - The host's first START names who doesn't have the map. A second START
    sends them back to their own menu, and the post-game vote does the same
    once its wait is over.
  - A guest told `starting <code>` for a map it lacks leaves by itself.
  - In the lobby the leave is `MeteoritePlayerViewModel.LeaveFireteam`.
    `BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem.LeaveGame`, which the kick used, only
    leaves a match.
  - Verified: the guest left before the countdown, and the host's match
    started alone.
- **Joining a match under way on a map this PC lacks** works. On two PCs, PC
  2 used DOWNLOAD AND JOIN on PC 1's running Gephyrophobia game. Its held
  join asked `where`, got `mapindex` back at once, moved the map from index
  18 to 19, and joined: the host's game had 2 players. A match started
  private with the host alone used to play offline and could never be listed
  later. Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.24.0 a host stays online alone, and the match
  can be made public mid-match ([multiplayer_servers.md](multiplayer_servers.md)).

notes.title: Update checks, the launch check and unsupported mods
notes.summary: Three pieces keep a player's game in step with what the hub ships, so a fireteam is never split by versions or by somebody else's mods:
notes.body:
Three pieces keep a player's game in step with what the hub ships, so a
fireteam is never split by versions or by somebody else's mods:

1. **The launch check.** Launch in the launcher checks for updates, checks
   the installed files, looks for mods MJOLNIR did not install, and only
   then starts the game.
2. **The in-game prompt.** At the main menu, the game asks the launcher what
   is out of date. If anything is, it offers UPDATE AND RESTART.
3. **Unsupported mods.** Pak and UE4SS mods from elsewhere are found and,
   on the player's say-so, moved aside for the session and moved back after.

## What counts as out of date

`preflight::check` (apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/preflight.rs) asks four
sources side by side and reports each one it could not reach:

| Source | Compared | Out of date when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The launcher (`check_launcher`) | this launcher's own version | `/api/releases/latest` (what the Tauri updater reads) names a newer one. A newer build on disk is not out of date. `MJOLNIR_LAUNCHER_LATEST_URL` points it elsewhere, for testing. |
| Code mods (`hub::code_mods_outdated`) | each MJOLNIR mod in `ue4ss/Mods` that is in the signed set: its own `mod.json` version | the signed set's version is newer. A newer version on disk (a development build) is not out of date. |
| Runtime bundle (`modpack_update`) | the cached runtime manifest | the bucket publishes another version |
| Hub mods (`hub::check_updates`) | each installed hub mod: the CE runtime pack and every map | the hub has a newer release, or a map's install is missing files (the same release again) |

The Updates screen asks the same sources. It judges code mods by this
launcher's install record, not by `mod.json`, so it can offer a few more.

## The launcher updates first

Any run that includes the launcher installs the launcher alone, first. The
updater plugin's NSIS installer (update mode) closes the launcher and starts
the new one, which checks again and installs the rest with its own code. So
a fix to how updates are installed reaches players before it is needed.

The run is handed over through `resume_after_update.json` in the launcher's
config folder, written just before the launcher installs and read (and
deleted) by the next launcher at startup (App.tsx):

- `{ "launch": true }` from a launch or the game's update link: the launch
  check runs again in update mode (as for `mjolnir://update`): it installs
  what is still out of date and starts the game.
- `{ "launch": false, "keys": [...] }` from the Updates screen: it opens
  Updates and applies the rest of what was selected, if still offered.

It is never a replay: what is out of date is checked afresh. A failed
launcher install deletes the note, and a note older than an hour is ignored.

## A mods release waits for the launcher

Because the launcher updates first, a mods release only has to suit the launcher
players are offered, but it does have to suit that one. A launcher compiles in
its variant validator: `check_mglo` (apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/hub.rs) runs
`Variant::validate` from the `crates/blam-megalo` it was built with, and refuses
a mod holding a `.mglo` that validator cannot read. A mods tag built from newer
Megalo code can therefore ship game types that launcher refuses, and the launch
check has no way to launch out of date.

`mods-v0.44.0` did this on 2026-11-05. Launcher 0.21.0 refused 8 of its 13 game
types (`not modelled: number operand kind 1/6`), so players could start the game
from Steam but not through the launcher.

So `release-mods.yml` tries it first. Once `build-game-types` has written the
game types, it checks out the released launcher's tag and runs that tag's own
validator over every `variants/*.mglo`, through the `validate_mglo` example in
`crates/blam-megalo`. A refusal fails the job, naming each file and the error,
and the `release` job that signs and publishes never starts.

- **Released means offered to players.** The check asks `/api/releases/latest`,
  the endpoint the updater and `check_launcher` read, rather than taking the
  newest `launcher-v*` tag. A tag exists from the moment it is pushed, and its
  GitHub release goes public before the R2 upload that reaches players, so if
  that upload failed GitHub would show a fix players cannot get. A stale answer
  names the older launcher, so it can only hold a release back, and no answer
  stops the release as well.
- **When it fails, the launcher goes first.** Nothing was signed or published, so
  the mods tag can stay. Tag the launcher, wait for `/api/releases/latest` to name
  it (a minute or two after its release workflow finishes), then re-run the
  mods workflow, which checks against whatever is released by then:

  ```bash
  gh run rerun <run id> --failed
  ```

## The launch check

Every Launch goes through `launch/PreflightProvider.tsx`. So does a
`mjolnir://join` link that has to start the game. A join the running game
picks up skips it, since nothing can change under a running game.

1. If the game is already running, it launches at once. Steam only brings
   the game forward.
2. It runs `preflight_check` (above) and `preflight_verify` together.
   `preflight_verify` needs no network:
   - **runtime bundle:** each file against the cached manifest
