     (`verify_install`). The player's own config files are skipped.
   - **hub mods (maps, the CE runtime pack):** a quick pass,
     `hub::verify_quick`. Hashing every map's containers on every launch
     read gigabytes, and it took minutes on a slow disk. The launcher keeps
     each cache file's size and modification time from when its hash was
     last known good (`verify_stamps.json`, written by every install and by
     the Library's full Re-check). A launch only looks those up, and reads a
     file only when either changed: it is re-hashed against
     `container_hashes`, and a mismatch is reported.
     - A file never stamped (installed before launcher 0.17.0) is stamped
       as it stands on first sight. Its download was hash-checked; from
       then on it is watched.
     - Missing files are always caught.
     - On this PC (25 hub mods, 248 cache files): 0.4 s, against 29 s for
       the full hash.

     The Library's **Re-check** still reads every byte
     (`hub::verify_installed`).
   - **code mods:** each file the release shipped against the hash recorded
     when this launcher installed it (`hub::code_mods_verify`, the
     record's `shipped` list). Files a mod writes into its own folder while
     the game runs (MJOLNIRBlamConsole's `native\status.txt`) are not looked
     at, so a mod that has been used does not read as damaged. Mods
     installed by a launcher before 0.17.0 have no list and are skipped, as
     is a mod whose `mod.json` names another version than the record.
3. When nothing is found, it launches. Otherwise a dialog lists:
   - the updates;
   - the damaged installs (a repair reinstalls the same release);
   - the unsupported mods, with *Move them aside while the game runs*
     ticked;
   - any source it could not check.

   The buttons are **Update and launch** (**Update the launcher** when the
   launcher is behind: see above) and **Cancel**. There is no launching
   out of date: one player on old versions splits the fireteam. When only
   unsupported mods or unreachable sources were found, the button is
   **Launch**.
4. The steps run one at a time, since they write to the same game folder,
   each with its download's bytes as they arrive. A failure stops the launch
   and offers **Try again**, which runs the whole check again.
5. When anything was installed, the installed files are checked again, item
   by item, before the game starts. A file that still differs offers
   **Try again** too.

The gate covers launches through the launcher. A game started from Steam
directly gets the in-game prompt below, which can be put off, but cannot
play multiplayer with unsupported mods (see "Multiplayer needs an
unmodified game").

While it checks, the dialog shows every item it looks at as a live
checklist under one progress bar (`launch/Checklist.tsx`): the core, each
code mod, each hub mod's update, each hub mod's files, and the unsupported
mods scan. The backend reports each item as it is queued, started and
finished (`preflight-progress` events, `preflight::Step`). Hub mods are asked
about four at a time, and the active row stays scrolled into view. With the
quick file pass, the slowest part is waiting on the hub's answers.

Being offline never blocks a launch. A source that can't be reached is
listed, and Launch still works.

Paks gaps (a hub container deleted by hand) are not reported. `launch_game`
puts them back from the cache anyway (`hub::prepare_launch`).

## The in-game prompt

`mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/outdated.lua` runs from the main menu's poll in
`main.lua`. That poll runs every 1.5 s in the frontend and not at all in a
match.

- **When it checks.** A poll after a gap of more than 10 s starts a new
  visit: the first main menu after start, or the return from a match. A visit
  asks for a check unless the last answer is under 10 minutes old.
- **How it asks.** It writes `check` to `native\launcher_request.txt` and
  calls the native export `mjolnir_launcher`. The native half starts the
  launcher with no window: `--check-updates --out
  native\update_check.json`. The launcher writes the `preflight::check`
  answer there, whole (a temporary file renamed over it). The game polls for
  it and gives up after 180 s.
- **What it shows.** When there are updates or unsupported mods, it pushes
  a screen with the campaign-menu kit (`UI.push`, no cooked widget needed),
  at most once a visit, and only while the main menu is the top screen. The
  screen lists up to six items and counts the rest. Its buttons are
  **UPDATE AND RESTART** (**OPEN LAUNCHER AND RESTART** when only unsupported
  mods were found) and **NOT NOW**.
- **UPDATE AND RESTART.** It writes `update` and calls `mjolnir_launcher`,
  which starts the launcher with the link `mjolnir://update`. That reaches a
  launcher that is already open too (the single-instance hand-over). The
  game quits 2.5 s later, from the frontend only: quitting from a match
  hangs.
- **In the launcher**, the link goes to Updates and runs the launch check in
  update mode:
  1. It waits for the game to close.
  2. It applies every update and repair without asking. It asks only when
     there are unsupported mods to move.
  3. It starts the game again.

The game reaches the network only through the launcher, which already holds
the signed sets' keys. The game process gains no network client.

### Launcher features

An older launcher would ignore both requests and open its window. So
`hub::record_exe_path` now also writes `launcher_features.txt` beside
`launcher_exe.txt`, one word a line: `check-updates`, `update-link`. The
native half starts the launcher for a request only when its word is listed;
otherwise the request fails with "the MJOLNIR launcher is too old". It is a
separate file because an older MJOLNIR Lobby reads `launcher_exe.txt` whole
as the path.

### The check's file

```json
{
  "checked_at": 1792825712,
  "items": [
    { "kind": "code", "id": "MJOLNIRLobby", "name": "MJOLNIRLobby",
      "installed": "0.14.0", "latest": "0.15.0", "release_id": null, "repair": false }
  ],
  "unreachable": ["the hub: ..."],
  "unsupported": [
    { "kind": "pak", "name": "z_Mod_P", "files": ["Meteorite/Content/Paks/z_Mod_P.pak"], "bytes": 123 }
  ]
}
```

`kind` is `launcher`, `core`, `code` or `content`. `release_id` is the hub
release to install, for `content`. MJOLNIR Lobby shows a kind it does not
know by its name alone.

## Unsupported mods

`apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/unsupported.rs`.

**In `Meteorite/Content/Paks`**, every `.pak`, `.utoc`, `.ucas` and `.sig`
is looked at, subfolders included: the engine mounts `~mods` and `LogicMods`
too. Names are compared case-insensitively. These are known:

- **the game's own:** `pakchunk<N>[optional]-Windows` or `-WinGDK`, and
  `global.utoc`/`global.ucas`, in Paks itself only. No store puts a file list
  in the install, so this is a name rule, and both stores' paks follow it.
- **MJOLNIR's:** `pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIR…`, in Paks itself only (MJOLNIR
  installs and mounts nothing in a subfolder; a `pakchunk1-MJOLNIRx` in
  `~mods` used to pass). That covers the hub's containers
  (`pakchunk9NN-MJOLNIRHUB-<slug>-<j>_P`, and their `_<n>_P` patch names)
  and those MJOLNIR's tools place (MJOLNIRREG, MJOLNIRMENU, MJOLNIRLAND, …).

Everything else is unsupported. A container's files are grouped by name.

**In `ue4ss/Mods`**, a folder UE4SS would start (`mods.txt` says `1`, or
it has `enabled.txt`) is unsupported unless it is one of these:

- named `MJOLNIR…`;
- a code mod this launcher installed;
- a folder of the runtime bundle (from the cached manifest);
- one of the mods UE4SS itself ships (BPModLoaderMod, Keybinds, shared, …).

**Moving aside** is a rename into
`<install>/MJOLNIR-set-aside/<unix time>/<same relative path>`:

- It stays on the game's own volume, so it is instant and cannot half-copy a
  large container. Nothing in the game reads that folder.
- Each move is written to `set_aside.json` in the launcher's config folder
  (`%APPDATA%\com.devnull9090.mjolnir-launcher`) before the next one, and
  logged to `set_aside.log` there.
- A file the game holds open is left in place and reported.
- Nothing is ever deleted.

**Moving back** happens three ways:

- **When the game exits.** `launch_game` starts a watcher whenever the
  ledger has entries. It waits up to 5 minutes for the game to appear, then
  for it to go.
- **On the next launcher start**, if the game is not running. This covers a
  launcher that was closed or crashed while the game ran.
- **Before every launch check**, with the `unsupported_restore` command, so
  the check sees the mods and no late watcher moves them back under the
  next game. Moves aside and back hold one lock, so two never overlap.

A move back that would land on a file of the same name (the player put the
mod back by hand) keeps the set-aside copy and its ledger entry, and says
so. Folders the moves emptied are removed with `remove_dir`, which only ever
removes an empty folder.

## Multiplayer needs an unmodified game

A mod works in a match: in the 2026-11-21 playtest players with a
faster-firing weapon mod fired faster in matches. So in game the unsupported-mods
finding is a gate (`mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/outdated.lua`,
`Outdated.mpBlock`):

- **No joining and no public listing** (`Games.join`, `Games.setPublic`)
  while the last check found unsupported mods, or before a check has
  answered. The check is asked for if none is running; one that cannot run
  (no launcher) keeps the player out with a line saying to start from the
  launcher.
- **The host sends back** (its 5 s watch, `Live.modsToRemove`) a member
  whose game reports mods, one that sends no report for 90 s, and one still
  "unchecked" after 240 s. Every client sends its verdict (`modcheck|clean`,
  `modcheck|unchecked`, `modcheck|mods:<n>`) each 20 s and whenever it
  changes. This is what covers joins that skip FIND GAMES (Steam invites).
- **A client leaves a host with mods.** The host tells each member its own
  verdict (`hostcheck|…`) when it changes.

Limits: the kick is the lobby's own (the kicked game's MJOLNIR Lobby leaves),
and the verdict is what the player's game says about itself. This stops
paks and UE4SS mods dropped into the game folder, which is what the launcher
sets aside. It does not stop someone who edits MJOLNIR Lobby's scripts or
its answer file, or changes the game's memory.

## Testing

- `cargo test` in `apps/launcher/src-tauri`. The `unsupported` tests cover
  the name rules against this PC's real Paks listing, a scan, and a move
  aside and back that will not overwrite (with a scratch ledger).
  `links` covers `mjolnir://update`.
- `lua5.4 tools/tests/test_outdated.lua`. It checks when the prompt asks,
  what it shows, that it shows once a visit and not over another screen,
  and the update request.
- By hand: run `mjolnir-launcher.exe --check-updates --out check.json` and
  read the file.

notes.title: Crash reports
notes.summary: When the game crashes, the launcher notices, asks the player whether to send a report, and uploads a small bundle to the hub. The hub groups reports by where the game crashed, and asks for the full memory dump only for crashes it has not seen enough of. Status as of 2026-10-17:…
notes.body:
When the game crashes, the launcher notices, asks the player whether to send
a report, and uploads a small bundle to the hub. The hub groups reports by
where the game crashed, and asks for the full memory dump only for crashes it
has not seen enough of. Status as of 2026-10-17: both sides are built, the
launcher in `apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/crash.rs` and the hub in
`hub/src/lib/api/crashes.ts` (migration 0019, admin section on
`/moderation`). Tested end to end against a local hub with this PC's real
crashes; not deployed, and the real launcher has not run it yet.
**Update 2026-10-21:** shipped. The launcher side is in launcher-v0.15.0
(PR #196); the hub side reached main with PR #194, and the hub deploys from
main. Migration 0019 was applied to production during PR #194's deploy,
and the `mjolnir-mods` bucket expires `crashes/` after 100 days (c05e2de4).

## Where crashes land

| Location | What is there |
|---|---|
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Meteorite\Saved\Crashes\UECC-Windows-<GUID>_<n>\` | One folder per crash, from UE's crash handler: `CrashContext.runtime-xml`, `UEMinidump.dmp`, `CrashReportClient.ini`, for GPU crashes `Breadcrumbs_*.txt` and a `.nv-gpudmp`, and an 8-byte `.film-unreal` whose name carries the mode and map |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Microsoft.198377053870B_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalCache\Local\Meteorite\Saved\Crashes\` | The same, if the Xbox app's build is sandboxed. Unverified: the dev box has the Xbox build's `Saved\Config\WinGDK` in the plain folder above, so both are scanned |
| `...\Binaries\Win64\ue4ss\crash_*.dmp` | UE4SS's own dump. Not collected: UE's folder has the same crash |
| `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive\AppCrash_HaloCampaignEvol_*` | Windows' record of the crashes UE's handler missed, no dump. Not collected |
| `...\Binaries\Win64\ue4ss\UE4SS.log` | The only useful log (`Saved\Logs\Meteorite.log` is near empty in Shipping). Overwritten on every launch |

UE never deletes crash folders: the dev box had 117 of them, 19 GB. The game's
own crash reporter posts to 343's BugSplat (`DataRouterUrl` in
`CrashReportClient.ini`); the launcher leaves that alone. Whether a successful
BugSplat send deletes the folder is unverified, since every send on the dev
box failed.

What the files are worth:

- **The XML call stack is junk**: frame 0 is "UE4SS", then `ntdll+160e44`
  over and over. The useful facts are `CrashType`, `ErrorMessage`,
  `BuildVersion`, `SecondsSinceStart` and `TimeOfCrash` (UTC .NET ticks).
- **The minidump** (~172 MB, flags `0x201045`: data segments, indirectly
  referenced memory, handle data) is almost all MemoryList. The thread stacks
  are about 0.6 MB of it. Its exception record and module list give the
  faulting module and offset, which is what groups crashes. It also carries
  the XML again, as a UTF-16 user stream (type `0x10000`).
- **Asserts and GPU crashes** fault inside `KERNELBASE.dll` (UE raises them
  with `RaiseException`, codes `0x4000` and `0x8000`), so their address says
  nothing; their `ErrorMessage` does.
- The XML carries `MachineId`, `LoginId` and `EpicAccountId`.

## Reading a crash

`tools/crash/analyze.py` reads the dumps with no debugger and no symbols:

    python tools/crash/analyze.py --last                 # the newest crash, in full
    python tools/crash/analyze.py <crash folder>         # one crash (or an unzipped report)
    python tools/crash/analyze.py --since 2026-11-14     # every crash since, grouped

For each crash it finds the thread that failed (the exception's, or for an
assert the one that raised it), takes the return addresses on its stack that
follow a call instruction in a module's code (checked against the module's
file on disk), drops the crash handler's own frames above the raise, and
names each frame by its function: `FUN_<address>` from the module's unwind
table, as Ghidra names it in the analysed exe (`tools/ghidra/decompile.ps1`
decompiles one), or a name from `tools/crash/names.json`. Crashes group by
error message or exception code plus the first frames below the fatal-error
helpers (`_skip` in names.json). Stack scanning can keep a stale address;
the call check drops most of them.

Some dumps carry no thread records at all (zero stacks and registers: 12 of
the 2026-11-14 crashes); for those only the exception record's address is
known, and the census marks them "no stack in dump".

**The Level Loader's breadcrumbs** (MJOLNIRLevelLoader 0.13.16,
`breadcrumbs.lua`): `ue4ss/Mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/breadcrumbs.txt`, started
afresh at each map load, one line before every load step and every asset it
loads from disk, written unbuffered so the last line survives a crash. A
Blood Gulch load writes about 315 lines (185 assets). analyze.py prints the
last lines beside a crash written within a minute of the file. Shipping
compiles Unreal's own log out, so this is the only record of what a load was
doing.

## The launcher

**Detection.** The launcher starts the game through `steam://` or the Xbox
app, so it has no process to watch. It scans the crash folders instead: once
at startup and every 10 seconds while open. A folder counts once its files
have stopped changing for 15 seconds. Crashes are remembered in
`crash_reports.json` in the launcher's config folder. On the first run every
crash already on disk is recorded as old, so only crashes after that prompt.

**The log.** `UE4SS.log` is copied into `crash-reports\<crash id>\` as soon as
the crash is seen, and again checked in `launch_game` before the game starts.
It is taken only when it belongs to the crashed session: its first line
(local time, converted with the offset between its last line and its
modified time) is no later than the crash, and it was last written after that
session started (`TimeOfCrash - SecondsSinceStart`).

**The prompt.** A banner names the crash ("The game crashed 3 minutes into a
multiplayer game on BCK") and offers Send report and Not now. Nothing is sent
without that click. Sending needs the launcher signed in to the hub. Settings
lists recent crashes with a Send button each, for one dismissed earlier.

**The bundle** (`crash-<id>.zip`, typically well under 1 MB):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `report.json` | The summary below, plus launcher version, installed hub mods (slug, version, enabled), code mods and versions, `mods.txt` |
| `CrashContext.runtime-xml` | With `MachineId`, `LoginId`, `EpicAccountId` and `UserName` emptied and Windows user names masked in paths |
| `UEMinidump-slim.dmp` | The dump with every memory range dropped except thread stacks, the handle data and the XML user stream removed, and user names masked in module paths. Same layout and size, the dropped bytes zeroed, so it still opens in WinDbg and compresses to almost nothing |
| `UE4SS.log` | The crashed session's log, last 4 MiB, user names masked |
| `Breadcrumbs_*.txt` | GPU crashes only |

User names are masked as `C:\Users\<user>\` (either slash) in the text files,
and as underscores of the same length inside the dump (module paths, and path
strings found on the kept stacks, ASCII or UTF-16).

The bundle is built as soon as the crash is seen and kept in
`crash-reports\<id>\` with the crash's summary in `crash_reports.json`. If the
game's crash reporter deletes the folder before the player answers, the report
can still go; only the full dump cannot. While the folder is there, sending
builds the bundle again, since the log may have been kept since.

**The signature** groups crashes:

```text
build_version | crash_type | fault
```

`fault` is `MODULE.dll+0xOFFSET (0xCODE)` for a `Crash` outside
`KERNELBASE.dll`, and otherwise the `ErrorMessage` with user names masked and
hex numbers replaced by `0x?` (asserts and GPU crashes). `signature` is the first 16 hex digits of
the SHA-256 of that string. The game's offsets move every CU, hence the build.

## Hub API

`hub/src/lib/api/crashes.ts`. All under `/api/v1`, with the launcher's paired
key. Any valid key will do: there is no crash scope, so every launcher signed
in before this existed can send. Each key has an hourly budget: 20 reports,
40 bundle uploads, 6 dump uploads (admins have none).

### `POST /crashes`

```json
{
  "crash_id": "UECC-Windows-A13FF88D473CDE7854D7F18E02EFDA14_0000",
  "signature": "ccfab15f14e59877",
  "build_version": "2026.08.11.1121610.2-Rel-i343-Meteorite-2607-CU4",
  "crash_type": "Crash",
  "fault": "UE4SS.dll+0x2580d7 (0xc0000005)",
  "error_message": "Unhandled Exception: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading address 0x0000000000000018",
  "crashed_at": "2026-10-17T04:28:33Z",
  "seconds_since_start": 175,
  "mode": "multiplayer",
  "map": "bck",
  "role": "server",
  "launcher_version": "0.14.0",
  "bundle_bytes": 327222,
  "bundle_sha256": "<hex>",
  "dump_bytes": 176604251
}
```

`error_message`, `mode`, `map`, `role` and `launcher_version` are cut to
length rather than refused. `crash_id` is the folder name, unique per crash,
so a retried send gets `200` with the report already made instead of a
second one. A new report gets `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "<report id>",
  "bundle_upload": { "method": "PUT", "url": "/crashes/<id>/bundle", "max_bytes": 8388608 },
  "wants_dump": true,
  "dump_upload": { "method": "PUT", "url": "/crashes/<id>/dump", "max_bytes": 94371840 }
}
```

`bundle_upload` is left out when the bundle is already stored. `wants_dump`
is true when the launcher has a dump (`dump_bytes` > 0) and the hub holds
fewer than three full dumps for that signature and build. A dump a player
declined does not count, so the next player is asked. `dump_upload` is
present only then. Its `url` is a hub path (the launcher adds its key) or an
absolute presigned URL (sent without the key); the hub uses paths today.

### `PUT /crashes/{id}/bundle`

The zip, `Content-Type: application/zip`, at most 8 MiB. Only the report's
owner may upload it; anyone else gets `404`. Refused with `400` when it is
not a zip or its SHA-256 is not `bundle_sha256`. `200 {sha256, bytes}`.

### `PUT /crashes/{id}/dump`

The untouched `UEMinidump.dmp` zipped (deflate, about 30% of its size: 52 MB
for a 176 MB dump), at most 90 MiB (`MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES`). The launcher sends
it only after a second, separate yes from the player, because the full dump
is a copy of the game's memory. `409` when the hub did not ask this report
for it or already has it. `200 {sha256, bytes}`.

### Reading them (admins)

- `GET /admin/crashes`: signatures grouped by signature and build, most
  recently filed first, with report, player and dump counts, maps, first and
  last seen. `?build=` narrows to one build.
- `GET /admin/crashes/{signature}?build=`: its reports, newest first.
- `GET /admin/crash-reports/{id}/bundle` and `/dump`: the files, as
  downloads.

Admins only, not moderators: a bundle carries a player's log and a dump is
their game's memory. The page is the Crashes tab of `/moderation`
(`/moderation#crashes`), shown to admins.

### Storage

A `crash_reports` row per report (migration 0019), and R2 objects in
MODS_BUCKET under `crashes/<id>/bundle.zip` and `crashes/<id>/dump.zip`.
Nothing serves that bucket directly. Each new report also sweeps up to 50
reports older than 90 days, rows and objects. An account deleted from
`users` takes its rows with it (cascade) but leaves its objects, so an R2
lifecycle rule on the `crashes/` prefix (about 100 days) is the backstop,
set on `mjolnir-mods` since the deploy (c05e2de4).

### Testing locally

`pnpm db:migrate`, seed a user and an API key into the local D1, run
`pnpm dev`, then send this PC's newest crash from the launcher code:

```bash
MJOLNIR_CRASH_HUB=http://localhost:3000/api/v1 MJOLNIR_CRASH_KEY=mjc_... cargo test --lib real_crashes -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Without the two variables the same test sends to a stand-in hub inside the
test and checks every request against this contract.

notes.title: Discord Rich Presence and public game invites
notes.summary: MJOLNIR publishes its current game to the running Windows Discord desktop client as MJOLNIR Core, using application 1533237469259104458. The game owns the connection, so closing the launcher does not stop presence. The launcher registers Discord's launch protocol so an invite…
notes.body:
MJOLNIR publishes its current game to the running Windows Discord desktop
client as **MJOLNIR Core**, using application **1533237469259104458**. The
game owns the connection, so closing the launcher does not stop presence.
The launcher registers Discord's launch protocol so an invite can start
MJOLNIR when the game is closed.

The code-mod update consists of MJOLNIRLobby 0.17.0 (including its rebuilt
native DLL) and MJOLNIRHud 0.12.0. Ship them together, plus the launcher
change for cold starts. These version increments let the existing updater
recognize the changed code mods.

## Discord setup

There is **no Social SDK download, bot token, OAuth client secret, redirect
URI, or Public Client setting required for this implementation**. It uses
Discord's documented local RPC over IPC transport for Rich Presence and
the `ACTIVITY_JOIN` event. The app's existing Hub OAuth configuration can
stay as it is. The activity explicitly sends `name: "MJOLNIR Core"`; the
developer portal application can remain named MJOLNIR Hub.

Players need the Discord desktop application running and signed in, with
activity sharing enabled for their intended audience. The browser-only
Discord client cannot receive the game's local IPC connection. They also
need the MJOLNIR launcher installed and run once to register the launch
protocol. Joining continues to use MJOLNIR's existing Hub sign-in and map
installation/version checks.

The app's Rich Presence Art Assets page initially contains no assets. Map
names and stats work without uploaded artwork. Artwork is optional and
must use asset keys actually uploaded to this application; do not publish
guessed map keys. Custom artwork is unset by default. To enable it, create
`MJOLNIRLobby/native/discord_assets.json` with a `default` image and optional
lowercase map codes mapped to uploaded keys (or supported external image
URLs), for example:

```json
{"default":"mjolnir_logo","bgl":"blood_gulch"}
```

If a future feature needs the full Social SDK (for example an in-game
Discord friends list), complete **Games > Social SDK > Getting Started**
in the developer portal, accept Discord's terms, download its Windows C++
SDK, and integrate/package `discord_partner_sdk.dll`. That is a separate
integration; adding the SDK DLL alone does not enable new features here.

## Presence and statistics

The lobby publishes the current menu, public/private lobby, loading,
match, and post-match state. The HUD contributes the current map, game
type, local player's observed kills/deaths, and session start time through
a bounded, fresh snapshot. Kills for presence are counted separately from
the Team Slayer score's betrayal penalty. These are observed local-session
statistics, not a replicated authoritative match total; a late join
cannot reconstruct earlier incidents.

Lua refreshes `MJOLNIRLobby/native/discord_activity.json` and calls the
native export `mjolnir_discord_update` once per second. The native half
copies the snapshot, then handles Discord I/O on a worker thread. It
coalesces routine changes, reconnects when Discord starts/restarts, and
clears stale presence if the game stops refreshing it. The payload uses
the game process ID, never the launcher's PID.

To opt out locally, create `MJOLNIRLobby/native/discord_disabled.txt`.
Remove that file to enable presence again. Discord's own activity-sharing
settings also control its visibility.

## Public Join Game

Only a confirmed public, fresh, non-full, joinable session publishes a
join secret. The host's public session identity is shared with its
participants so their cards can expose the same game. Private/offline
sessions, stale listings, full games, and matches with joining disabled
do not advertise Join Game.

The secret is `mjolnir:v1:<public hub lobby ID>`. It contains no account
key, host token, or PlayFab connection string. A received secret is
validated, then queued as `MJOLNIRLobby/native/pending_join.txt` using the
same `lobby=...` / `at=...` format as website join links. No secret is
executed as a command. The game's existing main-menu consumer fetches
the current public list and joins through the authenticated Hub endpoint;
an old invitation cannot bypass private/full/stale session checks.

The launcher registers `discord-1533237469259104458://` as a launch-only
protocol. Discord retains the actual join and delivers it over IPC once
the game connects. Launch intent passes through the normal launcher
preflight; a running game is not started again. If the player is already
in a match, the existing pending-join consumer waits until they return to
the signed-in main menu. It does not interrupt their match. Discord holds
a cold-start invite for about 180 seconds: if installation/preflight or
startup takes longer, click Join again after the game is ready. Once
received by the game, the existing pending-join queue expires after ten
minutes.

## Verification

Run the Lua presence/session tests, native Discord transport tests, and
launcher link tests before shipping:

```powershell
lua54 tools/tests/test_discord_presence.lua
./native/lobby/test-discord.ps1
cargo test --manifest-path apps/launcher/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib links::tests
cargo test --manifest-path apps/launcher/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib discord
```

The native tests use a private mock pipe and do not change a real Discord
account's activity. CI runs the Lua, native transport, and launcher tests; a production
lobby build includes the Discord source in the existing DLL and release
artifact, with no additional runtime DLL to distribute.

Live acceptance requires two Discord accounts on two machines:

1. Run the updated launcher once, then start the updated game with Discord
   open. Inspect the profile from the second account for MJOLNIR Core,
   current map/mode, observed kills/deaths, player count, and elapsed time.
2. Host a public game with space. Join from the host's card and from a
   participant's card. Verify the usual sign-in and map-download/version
   prompts still work.
3. Repeat with the joining game closed and with the launcher already open.
   Verify only one game starts and the pending join survives startup.
4. Make the game private, full, or unavailable for joining during a match;
   verify the join action disappears after the presence update and an old
   invite cannot bypass the current Hub checks.
5. Restart Discord, return to the main menu, leave the session, disable
   presence, and exit the game. Verify recovery and removal of old stats
   and join availability.

Automated tests do not establish Discord's visual presentation or an
end-to-end Steam/Xbox network join. Record those two-account results
separately before announcing live verification.

On 2026-10-24, a live local Discord desktop IPC check accepted application
1533237469259104458, acknowledged the `ACTIVITY_JOIN` subscription, and
echoed `name: "MJOLNIR Core"` and `supported_platforms: ["desktop"]` in its
successful `SET_ACTIVITY` response. The temporary activity was labeled
"Integration test" and then cleared with an acknowledged null activity.
This verifies these wire fields against the desktop client; it does not
replace the two-account game test above.

## Protocol references

- [Discord RPC over IPC, SET_ACTIVITY, SUBSCRIBE, ACTIVITY_JOIN](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rpc)
- [Rich Presence fields and unauthenticated desktop presence](https://docs.discord.com/developers/discord-social-sdk/development-guides/setting-rich-presence)
- [Invite configuration, launch registration, and pending joins](https://docs.discord.com/developers/discord-social-sdk/development-guides/managing-game-invites)
- [Discord's Windows launch registration implementation](https://github.com/discord/discord-rpc/blob/master/src/discord_register_win.cpp)

notes.title: The Xbox app (Game Pass) build
notes.summary: The Xbox app ships the same version of Halo Campaign Evolved as Steam (CU4, 1.112.1610.0), built for the WinGDK platform. MJOLNIR's Lua mods and cooked containers run on it unchanged; the native halves did not until 2026-10-10, because they call into the exe at addresses…
notes.body:
The Xbox app ships the same version of Halo Campaign Evolved as Steam (CU4,
1.112.1610.0), built for the WinGDK platform. MJOLNIR's Lua mods and cooked
containers run on it unchanged; the native halves did not until 2026-10-10,
because they call into the exe at addresses measured on the Steam build.

## What differs

| | Steam | Xbox app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install root | `steamapps\common\Halo Campaign Evolved` | `XboxGames\Halo- Campaign Evolved\Content` |
| Binaries | `Meteorite\Binaries\Win64` | `Meteorite\Binaries\WinGDK` |
| Exe | `HaloCampaignEvolved.exe`, PE timestamp `0x8a03f777` | `HaloCampaignEvolved.exe`, PE timestamp `0x3d94a571` |
| Simulation DLL | timestamp `0x6a7a740a` | timestamp `0x6a7a741d` |
| PlayFab / Party | `PlayFabMultiplayerWin.dll`, `PartyWin.dll` | `PlayFabMultiplayerGDK.dll`, `Party.dll` |
| Online subsystem | Steam | GDK (Xbox Live) |
| Containers | `pakchunk<N>-Windows.*` | `pakchunk<N>-WinGDK.*` |

- **The simulation DLL is the same code.** The two copies differ in 29 bytes
  (timestamp, checksum, debug id) plus Steam's signature. Every simulation
  RVA and byte patch holds for both.
- **The exe is a separate link of the same engine code.** Engine functions
  match instruction for instruction at other addresses. Platform code differs:
  the Xbox app's exe has no Steam subsystem.
- **The exe cannot be read on disk.** The Xbox app's file protection refuses
  even an administrator. The DLLs beside it can be read. To study the exe,
  dump it from the running game: `OpenProcess` + `ReadProcessMemory` over
  `SizeOfImage` from the module base. The image comes out relocated to the
  load base, so for Ghidra rewrite each section's raw pointer and size to its
  virtual ones, and set `ImageBase` to the load base.
- **The game is a packaged app.** It starts through
  `shell:AppsFolder\Microsoft.198377053870B_8wekyb3d8bbwe!AppHaloCampaignEvolvedShipping`.
  The launcher derives that id from the install's `appxmanifest.xml`. No
  `ms-xbl-<product id>://` link is registered for it. `C:\Program
  Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.198377053870B_…` is a junction to the
  `XboxGames` folder, so files installed there are what the game sees.

## Porting addresses

`native/map_registry` keeps one address set per exe (`exe_profiles`, keyed by
the PE timestamp). The Xbox app's set was found from Steam's with
`native/signatures/port_rvas.py`:

```
python -P native/signatures/port_rvas.py <steam exe> <dump> --dump 36D29F0 ... gD349040 ...
```

All eight functions matched whole. The three globals were read back from 5
to 8 functions each. `FModuleManager::Get` needs a longer pattern than the
script's first try, because it differs only in a thread-local slot index
(`0x154` on Steam, `0x13c` on the Xbox app). Do the same after a game
update.

| | Steam | Xbox app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FModuleManager::Get` | `0x36D29F0` | `0x32EBF10` |
| `FModuleManager::GetModule` | `0x36D3540` | `0x32ECA60` |
| FName hash | `0x3709650` | `0x33214B0` |
| FName from a view | `0x36FCC60` | `0x3316080` |
| `FCoreDelegates::MountPak` | `0xD349040` | `0xC31C940` |
| `HandleMountPakDelegate` | `0x4694C00` | `0x4239420` |
| `FCoreDelegates::OnUnmountPak` | `0xD349248` | `0xC31CB48` |
| `HandleUnmountPakDelegate` | `0x4694CC0` | `0x42394E0` |
| `GMalloc` | `0xD4B7428` | `0xC47DF60` |
| levels glue `Get` | `0x7B7DFC0` | `0x7749E60` |
| levels glue row insert | `0x7BAC140` | `0x7777F20` |

The AssetRegistry's `GetFirstPackageByName` is slot 30 on both builds.

`native/lobby` finds everything by code pattern. On the Xbox app every
pattern matches once, as on Steam, except two. One is the Steam join hook,
replaced as described below. The other is the presence session's 4-player
literal, which does not exist on the Xbox app, so the lobby DLL searches for
it only on Steam. The fireteam still shows 16 slots there.

## Joins by connection string

On Steam a join is the task manager's own `GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t`
handler, called from `OnlineTick` (docs/multiplayer_servers.md). The Xbox
app's counterpart is the invite handler that `FOnlineSessionGDK` registers
with `XGameInviteRegisterForEvent`:

- **The handler** (`0x663bf40`, `(session, const char *uri)`). It reads
  `connectionString`, `sender` (or `joineeXuid`) and `invitedUser` (or
  `joinerXuid`) from the URI's query: `name=` up to the next `&`, with no
  URL decoding. It then queues the join on the subsystem's next tick. That
  path is taken while a console variable reads true (it does in CU4). The
  other path reads an MPSD `handle`.
- **The invited user** must be a signed-in user. The queued task looks the
  XUID up with `XUserFindUserById`. A miss starts `XUserAddByIdWithUiAsync`
  and waits for it on the game thread.
- **The queued task** stores a pending invite (sender, the user handle, the
  connection string), which the session acts on later. The sender XUID is
  only stored.

`mjolnir_lobby` delivers the request from the GDK subsystem's own tick:

- `FTSTickerObjectBase::Tick` at `subsystem+0x70` (`0x6686270`), whose first
  act is to service the invite's task queue.
- The session is at `subsystem+0xF8`, and points back at `+0x2D8`.
- The player's XUID is the first live key of the subsystem's XUID →
  `XUserHandle` map at `+0x208` (0x38-byte elements).

The URI it sends is
`ms-xbl-mjolnir://inviteHandleAccept/?invitedUser=<xuid>&sender=<id>&connectionString=<string>`.
PlayFab connection strings (`cv2:<lobby>|<n>|kv1:<key>`) contain no `&`.

### Why a delivered invite went nowhere

Delivering the invite was not enough. Every join from the Xbox app stopped
after `join: delivered`, with no `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` and no error, and
the player saw nothing happen. The GDK subsystem does its whole part, all in
one tick: the task parks the invite (`0x664bb80`), the tick builds a search
result and hands it on (`0x664bd60`), and the session raises
`OnSessionUserInviteAccepted` (IOnlineSession vtable `+0x348`) with
success. Two things then lose it:

- **Nobody listens there.** The GDK session's only listener is its Online
  Services adapter, and nothing subscribes to the join event that adapter
  re-raises. The game listens on the other session interface, PlayFab's.
  Its adapter is bound with the same delegate type, and its join event has
  one handler.
- **The key is the GDK one.** The result carries the connection string as
  `CUSTOMJOININFO`. PlayFab's join reads `CONNECTIONSTRING`. Raised on the
  PlayFab session with the GDK key, the game left its fireteam and showed
  FAILED TO JOIN without calling PlayFab.

So for a join it delivered (within 30 s), `mjolnir_lobby` hooks the GDK
session's trigger slot and does two things instead. It renames the setting
in place. That is safe while the settings map has a single hash bucket
(fewer than four settings), where a lookup walks every element. Then it
raises the invite on the PlayFab session. It finds that session by its
adapter's delegate instance: a heap scan for the vtable of the GDK
session's own listener, once per game. The adapter is the instance's
`+0x18`, and the session is the pointer the adapter holds whose invite
listeners include that instance. Every other invite reaches the GDK session
as shipped.

A real Xbox invite raises the same event on the same session, so it
probably goes nowhere in the shipped game either. That is untested.

Verified 2026-10-10 on the Xbox app with a dummy connection string: the game
left its fireteam, called `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` with the string (returned
0) and showed its own FAILED TO JOIN when PlayFab refused the fake key. That
is what the Steam build does with the same string.

Verified 2026-10-10 between two real players: a Steam player joined a game
hosted on the Xbox app.

## Crossplay

Steam and Xbox app players share one PlayFab lobby service, so either can
host and the other joins from FIND GAMES or a link. The game refuses a
player from another platform when crossplay is off for either side. On the
Xbox app that follows the Microsoft account's "You can join cross-network
play" privacy setting. A Steam joiner dropped a few seconds after connecting
to an Xbox app host points at that setting.

notes.title: Fireteam join path and player cap (CU4)
notes.summary: Measured 2026-10-01 on CU4, statically (the exe disassembled with capstone) and by live reflection. Nothing was patched or tested with a second player. Exe RVAs are relative to 0x140000000, the simulation DLL's to 0x180000000. They move with each update. The CU3 study before it…
notes.body:
**Question:** can players join a host's converted-map game from our own lobby
service, on Steam and Game Pass alike, and can a game hold more than four?

**Short answer:** yes on joining. The PlayFab join needs only the lobby's
connection string, not an invite. Toward 16 players there are four separate
caps to raise, none of them known to be impossible.

- Measured 2026-10-01 on CU4, statically (the exe disassembled with capstone)
  and by live reflection. Nothing was patched or tested with a second player.
- Exe RVAs are relative to `0x140000000`, the simulation DLL's to
  `0x180000000`. They move with each update.
- The CU3 study before it is on the `mjolnir/coop-lobby-8-players-de2bcd`
  branch (`docs/coop_player_cap.md`, `tools/pe/lobby_size_hook.py`).

**Update 2026-10-21:** the caps were raised and tested on two PCs on
2026-10-02 ("Raising the caps in game" below). Fireteams of up to 16
shipped in mods-v0.10.0 (PR #120, #121), and the host's MAX PLAYERS in
mods-v0.16.0 (PR #143). Our lobby service took route step 2: FIND GAMES
hands the string to the game's own join handler (mods-v0.11.0, PR #127;
[multiplayer_servers.md](multiplayer_servers.md)).

## The stack

The session layer is Microsoft's OnlineSubsystemPlayFab:
`DefaultPlatformService=PlayFab`, `NativePlatformService=Steam`. Two PlayFab
libraries sit under it:
- **PlayFab Multiplayer lobbies** carry membership and the connection string.
- **PlayFab Party** carries the network traffic.

The Friends roster (`WBP_Roster_C`) lists Xbox, PlayStation, Steam and WinGDK
friends, each `Joinable` or `NotJoinable` (`ERosterJoinability`). The game
can join a friend's fireteam from the roster, without an invite. Invites are
platform-native: `PFMultiplayerSendInvite` is not imported.

## Joining

| What | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The one `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` call | `0x6f41e7c` in `0x6f417c0`; the string is the session setting `CONNECTIONSTRING` | Verified |
| Reached from IOnlineSession::JoinSession | `0x6f1fcd0`, `0x6f1fa10` (vtable `0xbde6c10`) via `0x6f1f210` | Verified |
| Steam invite accepted | `0x6aa6960` (`FOnlineAsyncEventSteamInviteAccepted` vtable `0xbc83420`). A URL without `SteamConnectIP=` is stored whole as `CONNECTIONSTRING`, then "invite accepted" is raised | Verified |
| Steam rich presence `connect` = the host's connection string | `0x6aaa4cd`, from `0x6aabf20` | Inferred |
| `+connect X` on the command line | becomes `-SteamConnectIP=X` (`0x6aaba07`): the IP path, not a lobby | Observed |
| Reflected entry points | stock `JoinSessionCallbackProxy`/`FindSessionsCallbackProxy` (the result struct is opaque to Blueprint); `MeteoriteLobbyNotifier.AcceptInvite(ToastInitData)` (no connection string in reflected fields); `UBlamOnlineSessionSubsystem` (`0x7abee20`–`0x7ada000`) has `PendingInvite`, `DeferredInvite`, `JoinRemoteSession` natively, with only `IsReadyToPlay` reflected | Observed |

**Route for our lobby service.**
1. The host publishes its lobby connection string. It can come from
   `PFLobbyGetConnectionString`, or from its Steam rich presence `connect`.
2. A joiner's native mod hands the string to the game's own invite-accepted
   flow, the way a Steam invite does. `UBlamOnlineSessionSubsystem` then
   leaves and joins as it would for a real invite.
3. The fallback is calling JoinSession with a search result whose settings
   hold `CONNECTIONSTRING`.

The PlayFab half is the same on Game Pass. Joins there take the GDK invite
route instead of Steam's (docs/game_pass.md); a Steam player joining an Xbox
app host was verified 2026-10-10.

## Finding lobbies

- `PFMultiplayerFindLobbies` is called at `0x6f1a347`, from FindSessions
  (`0x6f19210`). It builds OData filters (`lobby/memberCount`,
  `lobby/amMember`, search keys).
- Lobbies are created at `0x6f40aaf`–`0x6f40ade`:
  - owner migration: none;
  - access: **Private**, unless the session is advertised, then Public (or
    Friends with presence-join friends only);
  - search properties `string_key1`, `string_key2`, plus `PlatformId`,
    `PlatformModel=WIN64`, `OWNERNICKNAME`, `_flags`.
- Co-op lobbies are Private, so a search never finds them. A Private lobby
  can still be joined by its connection string, which is why our own service
  is the place to list games.

## The caps

| Layer | Where | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlayFab lobby `maxMemberCount` | `CreateAndJoinLobby` at `0x6f4156e` in CreateSession `0x6f40880`: from `FOnlineSessionSettings.NumPublicConnections` (settings+8) | 4 today; the game code supplying it not traced | Verified |
| Native (Steam) presence session after a PlayFab join | `0x6f2007b` | `NumPublicConnections = NumPrivateConnections = 4`, a literal | Verified |
| PlayFab Party network | `PartyCreateNewNetwork` `0x6f375dc`; fields loaded at `0x6f2eecb` from `[OnlineSubsystemPlayFab]` MaxDeviceCount, MaxUserCount, MaxUsersPerDeviceCount, MaxDevicesPerUserCount, MaxEndpointsPerDeviceCount | ini values unread (in the Oodle-compressed paks); read from the call on 2026-10-02 (below) | Verified as ini-driven |
| Unreal `GameSession.MaxPlayers` | `HaloOnlineGameSession` | 4, rebuilt every level; MJOLNIRLobby holds it at the host's MAX PLAYERS, 16 unless the host picks fewer (below) | Verified (CU3) |
| Simulation players array | `0x181010` (sim DLL) | **16** of `0x4B0` bytes. CU3 notes read 32: `0x20` there is the name buffer, not the count | Verified |
| `k_maximum_campaign_players` | block definition `0x9bb460` | 4 | Verified |
| `net_maximum_player_count` | registered at `0x9a3dd8` | value unread | Verified present |
| Network co-op refusal | `error_too_many_players_for_network_coop` = `0x50000a` (table `0x8384e8`) | where it is raised not found | Verified present |

**Route toward 16:**
1. Raise `NumPublicConnections` before CreateSession (or the CU3 IAT stub on
   `PFMultiplayerCreateAndJoinLobby`, CU4 IAT slot `0xa8bb630`).
2. Patch the presence session's literal 4 at `0x6f2007b`.
3. Make Party's MaxUserCount and MaxDeviceCount at least 16.
4. Keep raising `GameSession.MaxPlayers`.
5. Find the simulation's network co-op check.

## Unknowns

- ~~PlayFab may reject a larger `maxMemberCount`, depending on the title's
  configuration.~~ It took 16, and a fifth player joined (2026-10-02, below).
- ~~The Party ini values.~~ Read 2026-10-02 as the game creates its network:
  users 4, devices 4, users/device 2, devices/user 1, endpoints/device 3
  (`fireteam.log` below).
- Where the sim raises `0x50000a`, and `net_maximum_player_count`'s value.
- Whether Steam presence lobbies cap at 4 elsewhere.

None of this can be settled without a second machine or account in the
lobby. **Update 2026-10-21:** the first two were settled on two PCs on
2026-10-02; the other two are still open.

## Other CU4 RVAs

IAT: `PFMultiplayerJoinLobby` `0xa8bb5f8`, `PFMultiplayerCreateAndJoinLobby`
`0xa8bb630`, `PFMultiplayerFindLobbies` `0xa8bb608`. Party connect `0x6f37900`.
Steam command-line parser `0x6aab2a0`.

## Raising the caps in game (2026-10-02, two PCs)

MJOLNIRLobby's native half (`native/lobby`, `mjolnir_fireteam_open`) now does
three things at startup, all found at runtime by import name or byte pattern:
- hooks `PFMultiplayerCreateAndJoinLobby` (IAT) and raises `maxMemberCount`;
- hooks `PartyCreateNewNetwork` (IAT) and raises the Party limits;
- patches the presence session's two literal 4s (the unique 24-byte pattern
  at exe RVA `0x6f2007b`).

MJOLNIRLobby holds `GameSession.MaxPlayers` at 16. `native\fireteam.log`
records each call:

```text
party: users 4 devices 4 users/device 2 devices/user 1 endpoints/device 3 (options 15)
party: users 16 devices 16
lobby: maxMemberCount 4 -> 16
```

The incoming Party values match the shipped `[OnlineSubsystemPlayFab]`
section (MaxUserCount 4, MaxDeviceCount 4, MaxUsersPerDeviceCount 2,
MaxDevicesPerUserCount 1, MaxEndpointsPerDeviceCount 3), which confirms
`PartyNetworkConfiguration`'s field order. Both calls happen at sign-in.
A user `Saved/Config/Windows/Engine.ini` is deleted by the game at startup,
so the ini route is closed.

**Results:**
- **More than four players join.** PC 2 joined a host that already had three
  `CreatePlayer` guests: five players in `GameState.PlayerArray`, five
  player states, one `PlayFabNetConnection`.
- **Keep Party's per-device limits as shipped.** Raising users/device to 4
  and endpoints/device to 5 made every remote join time out, with or without
  guests: `ClientTravel` to the Party address (`0.0.0.0:5000`) gives up after
  exactly 20 s with "CONNECTION LOST / Disconnected from host", although the
  lobby join, the Party connect, authentication and endpoint creation all
  return 0 on the client and the host's lobby sees the member arrive.
- The host has no net driver at the frontend. It creates a
  `PlayFabNetDriver` when the first remote player arrives.
- **Local guests added before the first remote player block that join**
  (the same 20 s timeout). Guests added after a remote player has joined do
  not block later joins, up to four local players. `CreatePlayer` guests
  never pass through `UBlamOnlineSessionSubsystem::AddSplitscreenPlayerToSession`;
  the game's own `HaloOnlineGameInstance:LoginSplitScreenPlayer` does nothing
  without a second input device.
- **More than two local players on one PC freeze a match at its start**:
  black screen on every machine, nothing responds, `player_spawn` still
  fires. This happens offline too (host plus two guests, no remote player),
  so it is a splitscreen limit, not the fireteam's. Host, one guest and one
  remote player play Slayer normally.
- CTF with three players raised `game_over` (cause -1) about 15 s in; Slayer
  did not.

So a five-player match needs five machines, or a fix for three local players
on one; two PCs reach four players at most (two per machine).

### The FIRETEAM panel

`MeteoriteSquadLobbyViewModel.SquadMembers` always holds four slots: the
players, then blank INVITE + rows. A fifth player gets no row and the header
reads "n/4". MJOLNIRLobby's `squadpanel.lua` rebuilds the difference after
the panel's own `BackingDataChanged` and `UpdateHeader`: a row for every
player in the game state, one INVITE + row while there is room, and
"Fireteam n/16" (since 2026-10-04, on the host, n over its MAX PLAYERS).
- A row's widget class travels with its item in a native field. The list's
  `EntryWidgetClass` is only the fallback, read whenever the list builds the
  row, so a fresh item gets whichever class happens to be set by then.
  Player rows are therefore constructed with one of the view model's own
  player items as the template, which carries the class.
- An added row's `MeteoritePlayerViewModel` holds the name, platform and
  player state. `CanKickFromFireteam` returns true on it, so its menu offers
  Kick.

Removing a `CreatePlayer` guest with `GameplayStatics:RemovePlayer` crashed
the game.

## MAX PLAYERS (host choice, 2-16)

The lobby's MAX PLAYERS row (`-`, the number, `+`; host only) narrows the
fireteam below 16. Nothing raises it past 16: the simulation's players array
is the ceiling, so a larger PlayFab lobby would only let a seventeenth player
into a lobby the simulation then refuses.

- **PlayFab lobby.** `mjolnir_lobby_max` (native\lobby_max.txt) sets
  `maxMemberCount` on the lobby the host owns, through `PFLobbyPostUpdate` as
  its owner (`PFLobbyGetOwner`). It is kept for every lobby the game creates
  later (the create hook uses it), and an update the game posts with its own
  size is rewritten to it. This is the one layer every join passes, invite or
  FIND GAMES. PlayFab answers asynchronously; `mjolnir_lobby_connection`'s
  `max` line shows what took. The choice never goes below the players already
  in the fireteam.
- **Party and presence** stay at 16: they only have to be at least the lobby.
- **`GameSession.MaxPlayers`** is held at the choice (it was raised to 16).
- **The hub listing** sends it as `max_players` on create and heartbeat, and
  reports `full` at that many players; `/join` refuses a full game.
- The choice is saved in `MJOLNIRLobby\max_players.txt` and applied at startup,
  before the game creates its lobby at sign-in.

Not yet tested on two PCs: a join refused by a full lobby should reach the
joiner as "This fireteam is full", the same message a locked lobby gives.

meta.label: Question
meta.value: can players join a host's converted-map game from our own lobby service, on Steam and Game Pass alike, and can a game hold more than four?

meta.label: Short answer
meta.value: yes on joining. The PlayFab join needs only the lobby's connection string, not an invite. Toward 16 players there are four separate caps to raise, none of them known to be impossible.

notes.title: Forge
notes.summary: Forge lets you build with a map's palette, change object properties and save layouts for play. F3 selects physics modes, F4 sets the position grid and F10 selects rotation increments. Custom packs add modular building pieces and utilities. Forge editing is host-only.
notes.body:
Forge lets you build with a map's palette, change object properties and save
layouts for play. **F3** selects physics modes, **F4** sets the position grid
and **F10** selects rotation increments. Custom packs add modular building
pieces and utilities. Forge editing is host-only.

Use the mods the launcher installs (mods 0.45.0 or newer: **MJOLNIRForge 0.4.2**,
**MJOLNIRLobby 0.21.0**), with the matching CE runtime and map dependencies.

New to building? Start with [Your first Forge build](forge_guide.md), a raised
courtyard walkthrough with doors, lifts and teleporters. This page is the
complete control reference. See [how the engine works](re/forge_engine.md)
for implementation details.

Halo Reach's Forge is still inside Halo: Campaign Evolved's simulation.
MJOLNIR switches it on: you turn into the Monitor, fly around the map, and
pick up, move, drop and delete its objects. The game's own Forge engine does
the work; MJOLNIR gives it keys and a HUD. As the Monitor you can also
place new objects from the map's palette: weapons, vehicles, equipment and
scenery.

Community model sets use [Forge packs](forge_packs.md). Maps declare their
supported pack pieces when baked; the Hub catalog and launcher handle their
releases and dependencies. That guide includes the original Foundry set,
authoring commands and saved-layout compatibility checks.
For a model-to-pack walkthrough, see [Community pack authoring](forge_pack_authoring.md).

## Starting a Forge game

After a fresh launch, press **Enter** at the title screen and wait for sign-in
to finish and the main menu to appear.

1. MULTIPLAYER → HOST GAME, pick a map.
2. Pick **FORGE** as the game type. It is listed once MJOLNIRForge is
   installed and the CE runtime pack has the monitor fix.
3. Start. A panel at the top left says `FORGE`.

For scripts and tests: `mjolnir_auto host <CODE> forge private` at the
console. Before issuing it after a fresh launch, wait for
`MULTIPLAYER is on the main menu` in the current `UE4SS.log`. Starting before
sign-in can load the Unreal world without starting the native simulation.

## The HUD

![Holding an assault rifle as the Monitor: the target card with the weapon's silhouette, the distance bar and the control bar](/docs-images/forge-hud-holding.jpg)

- **Top left:** FORGE, whether you are the Monitor or your Spartan, and the
  map.
- **Centre:** the Monitor's cursor. Blue when it rests on nothing, white
  on an object, green while you hold one.
- **Beside the cursor:** what you aim at or hold. It shows the kind of object,
  its name, the game's own picture for a weapon, and what the keys do to it.
  While you hold something, a bar shows how far out it is (1 to 60 m).
- **Bottom:** the main controls, dimmed when they do nothing right now, and a short
  note of what the last key did ("DELETED Shotgun").

![Aiming at a shotgun: WEAPON, Shotgun, and the keys that act on it](/docs-images/forge-hud-aiming.jpg)

![A Ghost just placed from the palette: the VEHICLES category on the right, the Ghost held at the cursor](/docs-images/forge-palette.jpg)

- **Right, as the Monitor:** the palette. The category (WEAPONS, VEHICLES,
  EQUIPMENT, SCENERY) between its keys, the object Insert places with its
  picture, and the category's list around it. A dimmed entry is one the map
  cannot place right now.

The HUD also shows the target's physics mode and keeps the
grid and rotation settings visible in Monitor mode. The palette header
shows the turn increment separately: snapping off still leaves comma and
period turning by 22.5°.

The HUD ships in the CE runtime pack (`pakchunk980-MJOLNIRFORGEUI-Windows`).
Without it, a plain text panel shows the same things.

## Keys

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| **B** | Turn into the Monitor, or back into your Spartan |
| **V** | Pick up what the cursor is on; press again to drop it |
| **Page Up / Page Down** | Push a held object away, or pull it in |
| **Delete** | Delete what you hold (or, holding nothing, what you aim at) |
| **N** | Duplicate the target at the cursor |
| **Insert** | Place the palette's selected object at the cursor; you hold it, ready to move |
| **Left / Right** | Previous / next palette category |
| **Up / Down** | Previous / next object in the category |
| **F5** | Save this map's layout |
| **F6** | Load the saved layout, replacing the objects on the map now. With no saved layout, the newest one in `layouts\history` comes back |
| **F2**, twice | Go back to the map's own layout (the saved one is kept in `layouts\history`). The first press asks; press again within 4 seconds |
| **K** | Team of the target: neutral, red, blue |
| **L** | Megalo label of the target (the map's labels in turn, then none) |
| **J** | Respawn time of the target: 0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 s |
| **O** | Spawn order of the target: 0 to 9 |
| **P** | Teleporter channel of the target: alpha through zulu, then 26–31 |
| **, / .** | Turn what you hold or carry, or the next marker you place, left / right; 22.5° with rotation snapping off |
| **F3** | Cycle the target's physics: Normal → Fixed → Phased |
| **F4** | Cycle the position grid: off → 0.25 → 0.5 → 1 → 2 → 4 m |
| **F10** | Cycle rotation snapping: off → 90° → 45° → 30° → 15° → 5° |

As the Monitor you move with your usual movement keys and the mouse; jump
flies up.

To use other keys, create `keys.txt` in the MJOLNIRForge mod folder with
lines like `grab=H` (actions `toggle`, `grab`, `duplicate`, `delete`,
`nearer`, `farther`, `place`, `prev_category`, `next_category`, `prev_item`,
`next_item`, `save`, `load`, `revert`, `team`, `label`, `respawn`, `order`, `channel`,
`rotate_left`, `rotate_right`, `physics`, `grid` and `rotation_snap`;
key names as UE4SS spells them, such as `PAGE_UP` or
`LEFT_ARROW`).
The defaults are keys the game does not use. G, C, Z and X are taken;
MJOLNIRFlyCam uses F7–F9 and the square brackets.

## The palette

A map's palette is its scenario's own Forge palette. Current converted maps
can offer the CE arsenal: 13 weapons, 6 vehicles (not the campaign's flyers),
grenades, power-ups, ammo and scenery such as spawn points, teleporters, flag
stands and health packs. A map with a smaller palette only offers its baked
selection. Adding installed assets does not change that selection.

A converted map's own vehicles start in place: a FORGE game shows the ones a
Slayer game on that map would place. Saving keeps them under the host's vehicle
settings, so a match still places what its VEHICLE SET pages say.

The **blocks** palette includes a Covenant crate and portable shield. Maps
can also include original namespaced model sets such as Foundry through
[Forge packs](forge_packs.md). Per-kind quotas and overall object capacity
still depend on the map and engine (*Budgets and quotas*).

## Object properties

Every object Forge places carries properties the game types read. K, L, J
and O change the target's (what you hold, else what you aim at); the target
card shows its team and label.

- **Team**: a red flag stand is where the red flag starts in CTF; spawn
  points with a team are that team's. Include neutral spawn markers for
  free-for-all Slayer; red/blue starts alone do not cover that mode.
- **Label**: what a game type looks objects up by. CTF finds flag stands by
  `ctf_flag_return` and team spawns by `ctf_spawn_red` / `ctf_spawn_blue`.
  The list is the map's own labels.
- **Respawn time** and **spawn order** for weapons, vehicles and equipment.

### Physics and snapping

Aim at an object or hold it, then press **F3** to change its physics mode.
These are the game's native Forge object properties:

- **Normal:** uses the object's normal physics. An unsupported piece can
  fall when dropped.
- **Fixed:** stays where you place it, including in midair.
- **Phased:** stays where you place it and allows overlap with other geometry.

For a platform that should remain suspended, choose Fixed or Phased before
dropping it. The target card shows the selected mode; saved layouts keep
the object's physics properties.

**F4** controls MJOLNIR's position grid. It starts off and cycles through
**0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 metres**, then off again. On placement or drop, the
object's origin aligns to the nearest grid point in world coordinates.
The grid is anchored at the map's world origin; it does not connect model
edges automatically. A Normal object can still move or fall after it lands
on the grid.

**F10** starts with rotation snapping off and cycles through **90°, 45°,
30°, 15° and 5°**, then off again. With a snap selected, comma and period
request a turn to the next angle on that world yaw grid.
With snapping off, they turn by **22.5°**. Turning is around the vertical
axis; pitch and roll controls are not available.

Use **Phased** for precise construction and check the angle after dropping.
A held Fixed object can resist a requested turn when it encounters collision,
and the game's hold motion can settle slightly off the requested angle even
in Phased mode. Rotation snapping is not a guarantee of an exact final angle.

The HUD shows the current grid, snap angle and turn increment. Grid and
angle choices are editing settings for the current session; a saved layout
records the resulting object positions and rotations.

## Markers: flag stands, spawn points, health packs, teleporters

These have no physics, so the Monitor cannot drag them the way it drags a
weapon. Forge handles them its own way:

- **Insert** puts one where the cursor is, facing the way , and . set.
- **V** on one picks it up: it leaves the map and the HUD shows you carrying
  it, properties and all. Turn it with , and . and press **V** again to put
  it down at the cursor. **Delete** while carrying throws it away.
- **N** copies one, properties included.
- They are invisible in game (the bases' stands are separate scenery).
  Aim close to the marker's position to select it.

A flag stand made this way works in CTF: on Blood Gulch, a red stand placed,
labelled `ctf_flag_return`, saved, and the map then hosted as CTF got the red
flag.

### Teleporters

The scenery palette can include **Teleporter Sender**, **Teleporter Receiver**
and **Teleporter 2-Way**. Place an entrance and exit with the same channel;
**P** changes the targeted marker's channel, shown on its target card. The
game's simulation handles travel, including the receiver's facing. Use different
channels for separate routes. A two-way pair uses the same channel at both ends.

New Insert placements start on alpha with a player-only cylinder about 1.07 m
in radius, 1.83 m above and 0.30 m below the marker. Moving, duplicating and
saving preserves the marker's channel and trigger dimensions. Keep the receiver
clear of walls and leave room for the Spartan. The engine supports 32 endpoints
in total, including both ends of each route. Foundry's portal frames and pads
are visible architecture; place functional teleporter markers separately.

### Pack lights

Foundry's light strip and warm/red/blue pylons have optional catalog light data.
MJOLNIRForge attaches a movable point light to each active piece's actor, so
light follows placement and rotation and is removed when the piece disappears.
This also runs in ordinary game modes and when a saved layout starts a match.
The first 64 active lights receive illumination; additional fixtures still
render. Lights currently cast no shadows. Colors and brightness are properties
of the piece's catalog, so use the red or blue variant for team bases.

### Automatic doors and lifts

These utilities need MJOLNIRForge **0.4.0**, MJOLNIRLobby **0.19.3** and
MJOLNIRLevelLoader **0.9.8** at least; the mods the launcher installs today are
all newer.

Foundry Wide's door frames and moving panels are separate pieces. Place the
panel in its closed position inside the matching frame. Use **F3** to keep it
**Fixed** or **Phased** for automatic opening; **Normal** disables automation.
Leave the panel's full upward travel clear: 4 m for the infantry panel and
6 m for the vehicle panel. Return to your Spartan with **B** and approach
the doorway to request opening. The panel waits two seconds after you leave
before closing.

Clear players and vehicles from the doorway before editing it. Entering
Monitor mode attempts to close the panel, but a blocked closing path keeps
it raised. Moving, copying, turning and changing that panel's physics wait
until it can close; the HUD asks you to clear the doorway. Other objects remain
editable. **F5** saves the authored
closed pose even while the live door is
open. Door saves require the host's known closed pose; client saves containing
enabled doors are deferred, and a migrated host must rehost before using them.

For a lift, place the station with open space above its central deck, then
walk up its ramps as a Spartan and steer onto a nearby landing during ascent.
Crossline demonstrates a landing at 4.5 m above ground, four metres above
the station deck. A green teleporter frame or pad still needs the separate
sender/receiver markers and matching **P** channel described above.
Their metadata and current limits are in
[Forge pack utilities](forge_pack_utilities.md).

## With your fireteam

**Forge editing is host-only.** Start it without fireteam members; the lobby
refuses a Forge session with members present. Forge sessions do not appear
in **Find Games**.

Save your layout, return to the lobby and choose the game type you want to
play with your fireteam. The hosted map uses your saved layout. Players need
the map's matching runtime and pack dependencies.

## Budgets and quotas

A map can limit what Forge places: a budget, a price per object, and a most
of each kind. The simulation enforces them, as Reach's Forge did: an object
over its quota or over the budget is refused ("THIS MAP CAN'T PLACE ANOTHER").
The palette shows `placed/most` and the price beside an object that has them,
and the budget spent in its title. The text panel shows the same.

Maps set them when they are built (`blam.forge` in the level file,
[level_format.md](level_format.md)). A map without prices or per-kind quotas
still has the engine's overall object capacity.

## Layouts

F5 saves what is on the map now, everything Forge can move, as a layout:
`layouts\<MAP>.mvar` in the MJOLNIRForge mod folder (Blood Gulch is
`BGL.mvar`). It works as the Monitor or as your Spartan, in a FORGE game.

**A map with a saved layout starts every game with it**: FORGE, Slayer, CTF
or any other game type on that map. Saving again replaces it; the one before
moves to `layouts\history` with the time in its name. To play the map as it
shipped, press F2 twice in a FORGE game (or move the file out of `layouts`).
Objects you have not saved are gone after that, but the saved layout is not:
F6 brings it back from `layouts\history` until you save again.

F6 puts the saved layout back on the spot, undoing everything since the last
save. Objects you are holding are dropped first.

A layout file is a Halo Reach map variant (`.mvar`), the same format MCC
uses, so `cargo run -p blam-megalo --example mvar_summary -- BGL.mvar`
lists what is in it. Layouts belong to one map: the file name says which.

Forge checks a layout file before loading it and refuses a malformed one with
the reason, for example "FRB.mvar refused: it has more than 256 labels". The
map then plays its original layout. Layouts saved in game always pass.

## Not there yet

- **Several layouts per map, and picking one in the lobby.** One saved layout
  per map for now; `layouts\history` keeps the older ones.
- **Layouts for your fireteam.** A saved layout is used when you host;
  players who join see the host's objects.
- **A Forge menu** (object lists, properties).
- **Tilting.** , and . turn about the vertical only.
- **Markers are invisible**: aim near where you put them.
- The cursor only reaches things in plain view: it stops at walls and the
  ground.

notes.title: Community Forge packs
notes.summary: A Forge pack is a normal .mjolnir content release with a validated catalog of namespaced building pieces. The Hub lists them in its /forge catalog; the launcher downloads published containers and exposes their catalog to Forge. A map declares which pieces it supports when its…
notes.body:
A Forge pack is a normal `.mjolnir` **content** release with a validated catalog
of namespaced building pieces. The Hub lists them in its `/forge` catalog; the
launcher downloads published containers and exposes their catalog to Forge. A map
declares which pieces it supports when its scenario is baked. A saved layout
records the pack releases and palette bindings it used. Packs can be
[updated](#updating-a-pack) without stranding the maps and layouts built with
them, and the format leaves room for [other kinds of content](#entry-kinds)
than building pieces.

For a practical first contribution, see [creating a community Forge pack](forge_pack_authoring.md).
For placing existing pieces, use the [Forge building guide](forge_guide.md).
This page describes the release format, build pipeline and dependency checks.

| Reference pack | Current version | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Foundry](../forge-packs/foundry/README.md) | 0.2.0 | 24 original pieces on a 2 m module, including portal frames/pads and warm/red/blue lights |
| [Foundry Wide](../forge-packs/foundry-wide/README.md) | 0.2.0 | 38 pieces on a 4 m module; the original 18 retain their exact geometry and catalog order, with 20 additions for larger floors, walls, ramps, junctions, glass, doors, a gravity lift and green teleporter housings |
| [Roadworks](../forge-packs/roadworks/README.md) | 0.2.0 | Ten road pieces with 16 m clear decks, 24/48 m straights, R40 curves and 48 m ramps rising 4 m; open and guarded variants |

[Crossline 0.3](../forge-maps/crossline/README.md) combines Foundry and Foundry
Wide in a **96 × 160 m** Red versus Blue arena and utility showcase. Raised
decks remain 4.5 m high inside a 9 m perimeter. Its 300 authored objects include
two stock Warthogs, eight team-owned starts and four neutral midfield starts;
351 native slots remain available. Original Foundry's lights retain their size.
The [Forge Canvas](../forge-maps/README.md) stays a blank 64 × 64 m deck using
Foundry, while [Roadworks Circuit 0.2](../forge-maps/roadworks/README.md) provides
a roughly 731 m course on a 320 × 320 m recovery deck with three stock Warthogs.

Road connectors describe exact source assembly; current Forge placement does
not automatically dock them. Separate namespaces, and the rule that a
compatible update keeps every existing piece, keep new geometry from silently
resizing old builds. Historical Roadworks 0.1
used 8 m lanes, and Crossline 0.2 used the 18-piece Wide 0.1 kit in a 48 × 80 m
arena; those layouts need an explicit compatible rebuild to use the larger sets.

[Design research](forge_pack_design.md) explains the piece selection. The
[validation record](forge_pack_validation.md) records the tested artifacts,
gameplay checks and remaining coverage. Full vehicle-route, surface-placement
lifecycle and second-machine utility checks remain separate work; a representative
live check is not an exhaustive review of every piece.

## Release contract

`mjolnir.json` keeps `type: "content"` so existing archive download and signature
handling applies. Its optional `forge_pack` block identifies the catalog:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "name": "Foundry",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "type": "content",
  "summary": "Modular industrial construction pieces",
  "forge_pack": {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "id": "foundry",
    "blocks": [
      {
        "id": "floor_2x2",
        "name": "Floor 2 x 2",
        "tag": "objects\\mjolnir\\forge\\foundry\\floor_2x2",
        "category": "floors",
        "dimensions_m": [4, 4, 0.5],
        "snap_m": 0.5
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

- The pack ID must equal the Hub mod slug: 2–64 lowercase letters, digits or
  hyphens, beginning with a letter or digit.
- Block IDs and categories are 1–64 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or
  underscores, beginning with a letter or digit. IDs are unique within a pack.
  Names contain 1–80 characters and cannot be blank.
- Every tag is exactly `objects\mjolnir\forge\<pack-id>\<block-id>`, whatever
  the entry's [kind](#entry-kinds). For a block it names a crate (`bloc`) with
  its associated model, physics and collision tags.
- A catalog contains 1–256 blocks. Dimensions and optional snap are finite,
  positive metres. They describe authoring metadata; they do not change engine
  collision or configure the editor's global snap setting.
- Release versions are exact SemVer, at most 96 bytes. Hub versions exclude `+build`
  metadata. A published version's bytes never change; see
  [updating a pack](#updating-a-pack) for what each kind of new version may change.
- Optional `deps` use the existing `{ "slug": "other-pack", "range": "^1.2.3" }`
  format. The launcher supports Rust SemVer requirements such as `^1.2.3`,
  `~1.2.3` and `>=1.2.3, <2.0.0`; a bare complete version is an exact pin.

### Entry kinds

Each catalog entry may name its `kind`. Without one it is a `block`, which is
all the format carries today. The names below are reserved so that packs can
carry other objects once the bake, the launcher and Forge handle them:

| `kind` | Object tag class | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | crate (`bloc`) | Supported |
| `scenery` | `scen` | Reserved |
| `weapon` | `weap` | Reserved |
| `vehicle` | `vehi` | Reserved |
| `equipment` | `eqip` | Reserved |
| `biped` | `bipd` | Reserved |

The Hub, the packer (`mjolnir forge pack`) and the launcher refuse an entry of
any kind they do not support. A launcher meeting a pack built for a newer one
says to update instead of installing it, so a weapon is never handed to Forge
as a building block. Forge's light, lift and material code also skips entries
that are not blocks.

An entry's tag path stays `objects\mjolnir\forge\<pack-id>\<entry-id>` for every
kind. The tags an object needs besides its own (projectiles, effects, sounds,
animations, a weapon's first-person model) belong below
`objects\mjolnir\forge\<pack-id>\` too, and Unreal assets below
`/Game/MJOLNIR/Forge/<pack-id>/`. A pack replaces nothing outside its own
namespace. The Hub enforces this for catalog tags today; checking every package
in a pack's containers against it is follow-up work before packs carry kinds
with dependency tags.

### Required features and new fields

Catalogs stay at `schema_version` 1 while they only gain optional fields;
2 is kept for a change older launchers must not read at all, and they refuse
it with a request to update.

A pack lists in `requires` any feature it needs beyond what schema 1 readers
understand, for example `"requires": ["turrets"]`. None are defined yet: the
Hub accepts only features it knows, and a launcher refuses a pack that needs
one it does not, asking for an update. A pack that uses no new feature stays
installable by every launcher. The rule for extending the format:

- A new field that changes what MJOLNIR does with a pack (a new utility, a new
  surface profile, a field inside `light`, `lift` or `door`) comes with a
  `requires` feature name, added to the Hub, the packer and the launcher in the
  release that supports it.
- A field that only describes the pack (a credit, a preview hint) needs none;
  older readers ignore unknown top-level and entry fields.

### Updating a pack

Releases follow SemVer, and maps and saved layouts accept any later release in
the caret line of the version they were built with:

| Line | Same line | New line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0.0 and later | the same major version: `1.4.2` serves a map built with `1.2.0` | `2.0.0` |
| 0.x | the same minor version: `0.2.7` serves one built with `0.2.0` | `0.3.0` |

Within a line, a release must keep every entry of the earlier ones: the same
ID and kind, dimensions and snap, origin, and the heights where pieces meet.
It may fix an entry's look and collision within that shape, and add new
entries. In 0.x the patch number carries both fixes and additions. The Hub
refuses a release that drops an entry of an earlier release in its line, or
changes one's kind, dimensions or snap; origin and joins are the author's to
keep. Anything else starts a new line, or a new pack: Foundry Wide is its own
pack so that its larger pieces could never resize a Foundry build.

Maps record `^<version>` for each pack they were baked with. When the launcher
has to download a pack it takes the newest release of that line, and updating
an installed pack within the line is allowed while maps that use it are
enabled. A saved layout records the version
it was saved with and loads with it or any later release of the same line; the
palette entry must still be the saved tag path exactly. Two maps or layouts
that need different lines of one pack cannot be enabled together.

A block may also contain a data-only `light` object (omit it for ordinary
pieces; `null` is also treated as absent):

```json
"light": {
  "offset_m": [0, 0, 3.1],
  "color_rgb": [1, 0.05, 0.03],
  "intensity_cd": 70,
  "radius_m": 8
}
```

Offsets are relative to the piece's authored origin, in the
same right-handed Z-up metres as its geometry. Each component must be finite
and within −100..100 m. Linear RGB components are within 0..1. Intensity is
positive and at most 10,000 candelas; radius is positive and at most 100 m.
Unknown light fields are rejected. Hub, packer and launcher validate the same
bounds. Forge derives the actor class from the pack/block IDs, attaches a
movable inverse-square point light to its root, and converts metres to Unreal
centimetres with Y reflected. It does not execute pack code or accept an
arbitrary actor path. Illumination is capped at 64 active fixtures, is currently
shadowless, and has no exposure multiplier. Deleted/pooled actors and world
changes remove their attached lights. See [Forge utilities](forge.md#pack-lights).

Optional `lift`, `door` and `surfaces` fields provide the additional bounded
features used by Wide 0.2. See the [utility contract](forge_pack_utilities.md)
for their schemas and runtime limits, and [material authoring](forge_pack_materials.md)
for pack-owned glass/portal assets and the shader chunk a pack's material container is cooked under. A portal
surface is visual; native teleporter markers still perform travel.

The archive contains `mjolnir.json`, cooked `.utoc`/`.ucas` pairs under
`content/`, optional `docs/README.md` and `changes.json`, and author signatures
when signed. Source `.blend`, glTF and collision JSON files are authoring inputs,
not directly installable content. The launcher generates container `.pak` stubs.
