The generated Foundry release uses original visual geometry and collision with
game-specific actor/tag templates and shipped material references; its cooked
outputs require the supported game installation.

The Hub validates the catalog during the normal upload/scan/publish flow and
stores it on the release. `GET /api/v1/releases/{id}/forge-pack` returns the
published catalog, release version, archive SHA-256 and dependencies. The mod
detail page displays piece names, dimensions and snap. Choosing the Forge
category alone does not put an unvalidated archive in the Forge catalog.
Publishing still uses the existing registered author-key requirements and
review rules. Forge packs are live: the hub lists them at
[/forge](https://mjolnircore.com/forge), and launcher 0.21.0 or newer installs
them with the maps and layouts that need them.

## Build the Foundry content

Run these commands from the repository root. `$paks` is a developer's installed
game directory, and generated donors/cooked content remain local under ignored
`build/` directories. The examples use the debug tool builds for iteration.

```powershell
$paks = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Halo Campaign Evolved\Meteorite\Content\Paks'
$cli = 'target\debug\mjolnir.exe'

cargo build -p blam-cli
cargo build -p ue-asset --example mesh_rewrite --example forge_actor
cargo build -p blam-pack --example package_add

python forge-packs/foundry/generate.py
python forge-packs/foundry/validate.py
& 'C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe' `
  --background --factory-startup `
  --python forge-packs/foundry/build_blender.py -- --render

& $cli extract --paks $paks --group collision_model --filter crate_space_a `
  --shipped-only --verify --out forge-packs/foundry/build/donors
cargo run -p blam-sbsp --example forge_collision -- `
  forge-packs/foundry/source/geometry.json `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/donors/objects/props/covenant/crate_space_a/crate_space_a.collision_model `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/blam-collision
python tools/forge/build_collision.py forge-packs/foundry/source/geometry.json `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/blam-physics --mjolnir $cli --paks $paks `
  --payload-out forge-packs/foundry/build/blam-collision

python tools/forge/build_pack.py forge-packs/foundry --paks $paks
& $cli forge pack forge-packs/foundry/build/game/all/mjolnir.json `
  --content forge-packs/foundry/build/game/all/content `
  --readme forge-packs/foundry/README.md `
  --changes forge-packs/foundry/build/game/all/changes.json `
  --out forge-packs/foundry/build/foundry-0.2.0.mjolnir --sign
```

`--sign` uses the existing local author device key registered with the Hub.
`--sign-seed <file>` uses an explicitly supplied key instead. Omit signing for an
offline build; the Hub does not accept an unsigned public upload. The packer
validates the catalog, container pairing and basic IoStore structure before it
writes the archive. The Hub independently scans the submitted archive.

`build_pack.py --only <block-id>` produces a reduced diagnostic inventory in
`build/game/<block-id>/`; package that directory only for local tests. Do not
publish a reduced diagnostic build with the same version as the full set. Use
a fresh output directory when changing the set's inventory: these
builders retain prior outputs.

The visual cooker writes a namespaced mesh and synchronized actor per piece.
Blender/glTF geometry is converted to the game's units; the actor restores each
piece's authored transform after mesh normalization: Foundry uses a bottom-centre
origin, while Roadworks uses its entry floor. Actor visual
collision is disabled so the simulation owns collision. The collision cooker
builds triangle collision BSPs/MOPPs and fixed Havok polyhedra from the same
source hulls. Composite pieces keep separate hulls so doors and windows remain
open. The pack builder then creates namespaced collision, physics, model and
crate tags and packages their visual dependencies.

## Add a pack to a map

Add the desired subset to the level JSON before a `level bake --standalone`
build. Forge pack palettes currently require a standalone map; canvas overrides
are rejected because they do not install the new package preloads. Keep the
pack's cooked containers available in the bake's input Paks view so tag
references and preload dependencies resolve.

```json
{
  "blam": {
    "map_variant": true,
    "forge_packs": [
      {
        "slug": "foundry",
        "version": "0.2.0",
        "blocks": [
          {
            "id": "floor_2x2",
            "tag": "objects\\mjolnir\\forge\\foundry\\floor_2x2"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

This is a fragment to merge with the existing level definition. The bake adds
one custom Forge palette in the authored pack/block order. There is **no global
slot assignment**: independent maps choose their own subset and order. At most
63 packs and 200 custom references are accepted, and the completed palette must
fit the engine's 255-entry total including standard objects. The baker checks both
limits. It also adds each custom crate to the scenario wrapper's preload list,
dependency bundle and container package-store imports, preserving the donor
wrapper. A declared crate absent from the input Paks fails the bake.

Package the newly baked map with the existing `mjolnir map pack` command.
It preserves `blam.forge_packs` in the archived level JSON and adds a `^0.2.0`
dependency on each listed pack (see [updating a pack](#updating-a-pack)).
Installing the map through the
launcher resolves those dependencies, selecting a compatible published release
rather than blindly installing each dependency's latest version. The launcher
validates the enabled profile's dependencies before mounting content. A first
live map installation can mount new Forge pack dependencies before the map;
replacing an already installed pack requires a restart.

Installing a pack does **not** add slots to an already baked map. Such a map
must be rebaked and repackaged with `blam.forge_packs` before those pieces can be
placed. There is no automatic rebake or arbitrary runtime palette injection in
this implementation. Keep pack/block ordering stable when updating a map if
its existing layouts should continue to load.

## Saved layouts and downloads

The launcher writes generated catalog files beneath
`ue4ss/MJOLNIRForgePacks/`: `installed.json` for the editor's display metadata and
`installed.txt` for the native identity check. These represent enabled,
verified releases and include exact archive SHA-256 values. Forge labels match
full tag paths, so two packs may use the same block ID without ambiguity.
At most 4,096 catalog blocks may be enabled across a profile, matching the
native inventory reader's bound; each map still has its smaller palette limit.

Saving a layout writes both `<MAP>.mvar` and `<MAP>.mvar.packs` beneath
`ue4ss/Mods/MJOLNIRForge/layouts/`. Keep the pair together when copying or sharing
a layout. The sidecar starts with `forge-packs 1`; each following tab-separated
row contains:

```text
flat-palette-index    full-tag-path    pack-slug    saved-version    archive-sha256
```

The archive SHA-256 records which bytes the layout was saved with, for
diagnosing a report; it is not a load condition.

Only custom pieces actually used by the layout produce rows. Every new `.mvar`
contains an `fpk1` marker, including saves with no custom pieces, so removing
its sidecar cannot make it appear to be a legacy layout. Old layouts without
the marker remain usable when they do not reference custom pack tags.

Before launch, the launcher reads saved-layout pack requirements. A pack
installed at the saved version or a later one in its line serves the layout
as it is; otherwise the launcher downloads the newest release of that line
through the normal verified Hub install flow and enables the dependency
closure. Layouts saved with different releases of one line need the later
one. Layouts or enabled maps that need different lines of one pack are
written to the launcher log, and the launcher still restores everything else;
move the affected layout pair aside or use compatible map/pack versions.
Orphan sidecars without a matching `.mvar` and files in layout history do not
trigger downloads.

Before the engine recreates saved objects, native Forge checks each recorded
flat palette index against the current full tag path and the installed pack's
version. Missing inventory, a different palette binding, a missing sidecar on
a new save, or an installed release outside the saved one's line (or older
than it) refuse the layout. These checks prevent a saved custom index from
becoming an unrelated object after a profile or map change. They do not
migrate a layout to a different palette.

Downloads happen at launcher installation/launch time. Opening an incompatible
layout while the game is already running reports the dependency problem and
requires a launcher restart; the native DLL does not access the network.
Standalone Hub publishing of `.mvar` layout pairs and automatic map rebaking
remain follow-up work.

## Verification

The repository tests cover manifest/catalog rejection and Hub release
visibility, exact dependency selection and a local HTTP download fixture,
signature/archive round trips, IoStore bounds, and native identity mismatches.
Useful focused commands are:

```powershell
cargo test -p blam-cli forge
cargo test --manifest-path apps/launcher/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib
& native/forge/test-pack-bindings.ps1
python forge-packs/foundry/validate.py
python forge-packs/foundry-wide/validate.py
python forge-packs/roadworks/validate.py
```

Run the Hub's `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` from `hub/` when changing that
component. Geometry validation and the collision builder's ray checks verify
authored shapes offline. Before publishing
a playable pack, verify in game that each piece renders at its declared size,
ramps and platforms support players, apertures stay open, placement/duplication
and save/reload work, and a clean launcher profile fetches the exact dependencies.

notes.title: Modular Forge pack design
notes.summary: The first pack, Foundry, began as an original 18-piece industrial construction kit in 0.1.0; 0.2.0 adds six portal and lighting pieces for a total of 24. It provides a repeatable vocabulary for floors, elevation changes, enclosure, cover and trim. The models use no extracted…
notes.body:
The first pack, **Foundry**, began as an original 18-piece industrial construction
kit in 0.1.0; 0.2.0 adds six portal and lighting pieces for a total of 24.
It provides a repeatable vocabulary for floors, elevation changes, enclosure,
cover and trim. The models use no extracted Halo assets. Construction shape
families are inspired by the usefulness of Halo's Forge palettes, not by copied
mesh geometry or textures.

## Reference research

Reach's structure palette groups building blocks, bridges/platforms, buildings,
decorative objects, walls/openings, inclines and natural objects. Its block family
spans several footprints and thicknesses; bridge lengths, corners and ramps let
players connect those footprints. The [Reach structure catalog][reach-catalog]
and [Bungie's original palette screenshots mirrored on ForgeHub][palette] provide
concrete examples of the categories. The original catalogue is an Xbox 360
reference, so it is not an exhaustive list of later MCC additions.

In a [2010 developer Q&A][ferrex], Bungie systems designer Tyson Green explained
that pieces were intended to abut, which avoids overlapping-surface flicker.
He also described inventory limits shared by object families. Both details
support investing in compatible dimensions and useful reusable pieces before
large one-off decorative prefabs.

The [official MCC July 2020 announcement][mcc] documents Halo 3's rotation snap,
coordinate snap, precision edits and world/local rotation axes. Reach received
axis toggling plus expanded Forge World and Tempest palettes. These are useful
editing expectations for our kit; exact MCC world dimensions have not been
assumed or copied.

The [Reach manual published by Microsoft][manual] says Bungie's own Forge World
variants use the same tools and objects as players. Community examples such as
[Tension Span][tension] use multilevel bridgework; [Pinnacle][pinnacle] illustrates
towers, ramps, landing platforms and a central structure. Our demonstration
level should similarly show the kit assembled into traversable play space.

## Foundry construction contract

The following dimensions are this project's design choices, not measurements
claimed for MCC objects. One module is 2 m; placement snap is 0.5 m. All assets
use metre coordinates, Z-up and a bottom-centre origin. Keep 90-degree turns and
cardinal docking planes predictable; do not place decoration outside the nominal
bounds. Small bevels soften the image while collision remains simple and exact.

| ID | Piece | Width × length × height (m) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block_1x1` | Cube block | 2 × 2 × 2 |
| `block_1x2` | Long block | 2 × 4 × 2 |
| `floor_1x1` | Floor tile | 2 × 2 × 0.5 |
| `floor_1x2` | Long floor | 2 × 4 × 0.5 |
| `floor_2x2` | Large floor | 4 × 4 × 0.5 |
| `bridge_straight` | Marked bridge deck | 2 × 4 × 0.5 |
| `bridge_corner` | L-shaped bridge | 4 × 4 × 0.5 |
| `ramp` | 1:2 ramp | 2 × 4 × 2 |
| `ramp_shallow` | 1:4 ramp | 2 × 8 × 2 |
| `wall` | Full wall | 4 × 0.5 × 3 |
| `wall_half` | Half-height wall | 4 × 0.5 × 1.5 |
| `wall_corner` | L-shaped wall | 2 × 2 × 3 |
| `doorway` | Open doorway | 4 × 0.5 × 3 |
| `window` | Open window wall | 4 × 0.5 × 3 |
| `railing` | Open guardrail | 4 × 0.25 × 1 |
| `column` | Support column | 1 × 1 × 4 |
| `cover` | Low cover | 2 × 0.75 × 1 |
| `stairs` | Eight-step staircase | 2 × 4 × 2 |

The material system uses warm concrete, dark gunmetal frames, inset deck panels
and amber markers. Colour is carried by four reusable PBR materials, avoiding a
texture dependency for the first release. Markers on ramps are separate adjacent
surface strips, not coplanar decals. Door/window openings remain empty in both
the visual geometry and the compound collision geometry.

Source scripts, portable JSON geometry and the rebuild instructions live in
[`forge-packs/foundry`](../forge-packs/foundry/README.md). Blender 5.2.3 LTS was
verified locally and against the [official release page][blender]. Direct
background Python automation is sufficient; no MCP update is needed for the
generator. Generated `.blend`, GLBs, collision exports and the actual rendered
contact sheet are kept in that folder's ignored `build/` directory.

## Foundry Wide and enlarged Crossline

The first Crossline playtest found the 24 × 40 m arena cramped. Crossline 0.2
expands its footprint to 48 × 80 m using a separate eighteen-piece
[Foundry Wide](../forge-packs/foundry-wide/README.md) structural kit. Each
piece doubles X/Y while preserving Z: floor tiles reach 8 × 8 m, bridges are
4 m wide, and 8/16 m ramps retain a 2 m rise. This also keeps cover at 1 m,
stair rises at 0.25 m, deck surfaces at 4.5 m and perimeter walls at 9 m.

Portal frames, landing pads, light fixtures, player shapes and weapon models
retain their original dimensions. The larger arena spreads out their positions
without enlarging the native teleporter trigger. Separate pack and tag names
avoid reinterpreting existing Foundry placements in Roadworks or saved maps.
Original Foundry 0.2 remains available alongside Foundry Wide 0.1.

## Roadworks vehicle kit

The separate [Roadworks pack](../forge-packs/roadworks/README.md) provides
vehicle-scale straights, connecting curves and eased ramps. Forge racing
remains an active design genre: official features include
[race courses in February 2026](https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/forge-features-february-3-2026)
and [Death Race in April 2026](https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/forge-features-april-23-2026).
These are references for the type of play; the Roadworks geometry is original.

The installed Warthog's assembled visual envelope is approximately
6.13 × 3.25 × 2.43 m; the Spartan's standing collision height is 1.981 m.
[The scale audit](../forge-packs/roadworks/SCALE.md) distinguishes visible bounds,
physics bounds and wheel contact measurements. Foundry's 2 m-wide bridges and
ramps suit infantry. **Roadworks 0.2.0** uses a 16 m clear deck, 0.8 m shoulders,
24/48 m straights and 40 m centreline-radius curves. Its 48 m ramp rises 4 m,
with 4 m flat noses, 8 m slope transitions and a maximum 12.5% grade. Each
piece has an optional guarded variant with 1.5 m barriers outside the lane.
Deck thickness remains 0.5 m. Curves use separate convex slices so their inner
space remains open. The stock vehicle and player dimensions are unchanged.

**Historical 0.1.0 dimensions:** 8 m clear width, 0.4 m shoulders, 12/24 m
straights, R20 curves, 24 m ramps rising 4 m at a maximum 25% grade, and 1 m
rails. Vehicle playtesting found that footprint too tight. Version 0.2.0 doubles
the XY footprint and raises the rails by 0.5 m, preserving deck/ramp Z heights
and the convex topology. Earlier game photos and driving checks document
0.1.0; they are not evidence of driving the enlarged release.

The [Roadworks Circuit](../forge-maps/README.md) connects those pieces into a
roughly 731 m driving fixture on a 320 m recovery deck, including a raised
section and a pit pad. Three stock Warthogs provide a scale reference: one
beside a Spartan and a true 2 m scale bar, and two facing opposite directions
in the track lanes. Normal road surfaces remain 3 m high and the raised
section 7 m high, so driving exercises the pieces' collision above the recovery
floor. Connector positions and tangents drive the assembly and are checked
for closed loops, matching edges and reversed ramp joins. This source metadata
does not add automatic connector snapping to the current Forge editor.

Offline checks cover the enlarged geometry, exact joins, two-car static
footprint clearance and native collision rays. Updated in-game steering,
suspension, passing and rail-contact checks remain pending. The prior 0.1.0
fixture was roughly 366 m long on a 160 m recovery deck with two Warthogs.
The user reported the enlarged Roadworks scale was much better. Crossline's
subsequent enlargement uses Foundry Wide as described above; Forge Canvas
retains its original 64 × 64 m deck and Foundry dependency.

## Further visual sets

These are design directions, not delivered model packs:

| Set | Visual direction | Suitable spaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relay | Pale alloy, dark inset panels, narrow cyan channels and angular cuts | Elevated platforms, clean sci-fi arenas |
| Frontier | Weathered basalt, oxidized braces and muted ochre panels | Outdoor ruins, excavation sites, rugged outposts |

Reuse the same module, origins and docking planes across sets so creators can mix
them. A second set should change silhouettes and material treatment while keeping
the same traversal clearances and connector heights.

## Demonstration and runtime checks

The delivered [Crosswalk assembly fixture](../forge-packs/foundry/demo/crosswalk.layout.json)
places 54 instances of all 18 types inside 16 × 16 m. Its
[actual Blender render](../forge-packs/foundry/art/foundry-crosswalk.png) shows
two facing upper platforms, a bridge, lower routes, ramps, stairs, cover and
rails. Main walking surfaces are 4 m apart, with 3.5 m clear beneath the bridge.
This portable metre/Z-up authoring layout still needs a runtime adapter or bake;
it is not a native save or proof of playability. Verify floor seams by walking
and driving over them; walk through the doorway and fire through the window;
test ramp endpoints and stairs; duplicate, rotate, save, reload and delete parts.
Finally load the variant on a client without the pack, confirm the pinned pack
downloads before loading, and confirm missing/corrupt dependencies produce an
actionable failure instead of silently dropping placed pieces.

The source validator proves the mesh/collision construction invariants. The
render proves the exported geometry and authored material appearance. The game
build currently uses stock material references. Separate
[CU4 validation evidence](forge_pack_validation.md) records all 18 types placed,
representative rendering, movement, collision, ramp climbing and save/restart
checks, with the remaining traversal, visual and multiplayer work explicitly listed.

notes.title: Forge building blocks
notes.summary: A Forge block is an object tag the simulation can place from a map's palette and players stand on. Four things, all checked in CU4:
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-11-01, a research note. Three reference packs exist today (Foundry with 24 pieces, Foundry Wide with 38, Roadworks with 10); the 18-piece set below is the first Foundry build, which this note validated. For the pack format see [forge_packs.md](forge_packs.md); to make a pack, [forge_pack_authoring.md](forge_pack_authoring.md). Two shipped blocks are included on newly baked maps
(a Covenant crate and the Covenant portable shield). The original 18-piece
Foundry source set and community pack catalog, packaging, dependency and layout
binding support are implemented. See [forge_packs.md](forge_packs.md) for the
current architecture, reproducible build and runtime verification status.
The [local CU4 evidence](forge_pack_validation.md) records all 18 types placed,
representative rendering and collision, restart persistence, and save/load identity guards.
**See also:** [forge.md](forge.md), [re/forge_engine.md](re/forge_engine.md)
(placing, the grab crash, markers), [level_format.md](level_format.md)
(`blam.map_variant`, `blam.forge`).

## What a block needs

A Forge block is an object tag the simulation can place from a map's palette
and players stand on. Four things, all checked in CU4:

| Need | Why | Where |
|---|---|---|
| A collision model (`coll`), ideally a physics model (`phmo`) | The simulation does all collision. Unreal geometry is visual only. | the tag's `model` |
| A multiplayer object block | The placement check (`0x3049e0`) refuses a tag without one (root `+0x124`) | the object definition |
| An Unreal actor | Each object tag's wrapper package holds an `AssetReference` to an actor Blueprint, and the game binds a pooled actor of that class to the object. Without one the object is invisible, like MJOLNIR's flag stands and spawn points. | `/Game/Tags/<path>-<group>`, `BlamCrateTagDataAsset` and the like |
| *Phased physics in forge* (multiplayer flags bit 1) | Otherwise placing looks for room at the cursor and refuses anything resting on the ground | MJOLNIRForge sets it in memory on palette tags |

## What ships

CU4 ships **no Forge blocks**. Nothing of Reach's Forge World palette
survives: a search of all 12,508 tags and 144,482 Unreal packages for
forge, block, wall, ramp, bridge, platform or column names found campaign
geometry only. What comes closest (surveyed 2026-11-01; every row has a
collision model, a physics model and a Blueprint with a mesh):

| Tag | Use | Size (m) | MP block | On B40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `objects\props\covenant\crate_space_a\crate_space_a` (crate) | crate, cover | 1.4 × 1.6 × 2.25 | yes | yes |
| `objects\props\covenant\cov_portable_shield\cov_portable_shield` (scenery) | barrier (the panel can be shot down and recharges) | 2.4 × 1.2 × 2.9 | yes | yes |
| `crate_comm_a`, `crate_comm_b` (crate) | wall, column | 2.9 × 2.6 × 4.2; 1.8 × 2.5 × 4.2 | no | yes |
| `objects\levels\halo1\solo\b40\bridge_glass\bridge_glass` (scenery) | bridge (breaks at once: vitality 1) | 14.7 × 2.6 × 0.25 | no | yes |
| `light_bridge_b40` (machine) | bridge | 27 × 3.7 × 0.5 | no | yes |
| `elevator_a/b/c_b40` (machine) | platform | 6.5 × 6.6 × 0.5 | no | yes |
| Forerunner doors (`acr_big_angle_door`, `for_door_a`, `acr_control_room_door`, `chasm_door`) | walls | various | no | yes |

More is shipped but not loaded by B40: C20's light bridges (4 × 22 m and
4 × 28 m), E30 wreckage, small UNSC crates and doors. A palette entry that
names one loads it by name. Machines follow their device animation, so where
a door or a light bridge rests once placed on its own has to be seen in game.

`defs/level/palette-map.json` `blocks` lists the two with a multiplayer
block, so every map baked with `map_variant` gets a **blocks** palette. The
others need a multiplayer block grafted in, which makes new tags (see
*Making blocks* below).

VERIFIED in game (BGL, 2026-11-01): with `crate_space_a` put in a palette
entry at run time, it placed from the palette, Unreal drew it, it was saved
in the layout, and a Slayer game started with it. Not checked: standing on
it (the Monitor flies through everything).

## Run-time palette slots: `slots.txt`

A palette entry's object is the tag index in its first variant (`+0x10`).
The simulation reads it every time it places from the entry (`0x32f450` →
`0x5ee570`). MJOLNIRForge points entries at other tags when it reads the
palettes, and again at each new map before a saved layout is applied, from
`MJOLNIRForge\slots.txt`:

```
# palette:entry = tag path (an object tag the map loads)
3:1 = objects\props\covenant\crate_space_a\crate_space_a
```

- The tag must be loaded: referenced by the map, or by anything the map
  loads.
- The entry changes for the whole game. Objects the map itself placed from
  it change too: pointing BGL's health-pack entry at a crate turned every
  health pack into a crate.
- A saved layout's engine payload names entries. New community-pack layouts
  also save tag/version bindings and refuse an entry whose tag or pack line changed; see
  [saved-layout checks](forge_packs.md#saved-layouts-and-downloads).

## Community packs

The earlier proposal for 32 global slot tags and Hub-assigned slot ranges is
retired. Packs now own `objects\mjolnir\forge\<pack-id>\<block-id>` tag paths.
Each map declares its supported subset and order in `blam.forge_packs` before a
standalone bake. The scenario includes these references and their package
preloads; the map archive depends on the corresponding Hub release lines.
There is no shared global slot allocation and installing a pack does not
automatically add it to an existing map.

The Hub's Forge catalog displays validated content releases. The launcher
downloads map dependencies and missing releases required by saved layout
sidecars. Native Forge checks each saved index against its tag path and pack
line before recreating objects. The complete contract and
current limits are in [forge_packs.md](forge_packs.md).

## Making blocks

The [Foundry build](../forge-packs/foundry/README.md) uses these tools to produce
new namespaced meshes, synchronized actors, tags and exact collision hulls.
Cooked artifacts are generated locally from the supported game installation.

- **The tag:**
  - `mjolnir new-tag --group crate --from objects\props\covenant\crate_space_a\crate_space_a --to <namespaced block path>`;
  - `--graft "object.multiplayer object=crate:crate_space_a-crate:object.multiplayer object"` for a donor without the block;
  - `--asset-reference /Game/.../BP_Thing` for the actor;
  - `--payload` for a model, collision and physics of its own.
- **Collision:** `forge_collision` builds triangle collision BSPs and MOPPs;
  `tools/forge/build_collision.py` builds fixed polyhedra from the same hulls.
  Composite pieces retain separate hulls to preserve openings.
- **The Unreal mesh:**
  - rewrite a shipped mesh's LOD in place (`mesh_rewrite` + `package_add`,
    docs on UE mesh writing); or
  - cook in the MJOLNIRMaterials editor and retarget (`tools/ue/cook.ps1`,
    `ue retarget`); or
  - draw it the way the Halo 2 machines are drawn: the level loader's
    `follow` attaches a mesh to the donor's actor and hides the donor's own
    (`mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua`, `follow`).
- **From Halo Reach (MCC):** `mjolnir cache info forge_halo.map` identifies
  the map, but no stager reads Reach caches yet. One would be modelled on
  `crates/blam-cache/src/h2`. The first check is whether Reach's
  collision and physics model layouts match CU4's, by comparing
  `mjolnir fields` for each group. Forge World's blocks are mostly
  scenery with a Havok physics model, which CU4's crates use too.
- **Modelled new:** a mesh plus collision hulls (boxes and ramps are their own
  hulls), through the same pipeline. Each physics hull must be convex; a
  doorway or other compound piece uses multiple hulls.

notes.title: Original Forge canvas collision
notes.summary: crates/blam-sbsp/examples/forge_canvas.rs builds an original rectangular slab and an open build volume. It does not use Blood Gulch or another converted map's geometry. The local shipped BSP_03_1_Chasm_old tag supplies the engine's structure and physics wrappers; extracted and…
notes.body:
`crates/blam-sbsp/examples/forge_canvas.rs` builds an original rectangular slab
and an open build volume. It does not use Blood Gulch or another converted
map's geometry. The local shipped `BSP_03_1_Chasm_old` tag supplies the engine's
structure and physics wrappers; extracted and generated game data stays in
ignored build folders.

```powershell
cargo run -p blam-sbsp --example forge_canvas -- `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/donors/Levels/Halo1/Solo/B40/_Generated_/BSP_03_1_Chasm_old.scenario_structure_bsp `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/canvas/blank.sbsp

cargo run -p blam-sbsp --example forge_canvas -- `
  forge-packs/foundry/build/donors/Levels/Halo1/Solo/B40/_Generated_/BSP_03_1_Chasm_old.scenario_structure_bsp `
  forge-packs/foundry-wide/build/canvas/crossline.sbsp --width-m 96 --depth-m 160 --extent-m 96
```

The output directory must exist. Options, all in metres:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `--width-m` | 64 | Slab width on X, centred at zero |
| `--depth-m` | 64 | Slab depth on Y, centred at zero |
| `--thickness-m` | 1 | Slab extends from `-thickness` to Z=0 |
| `--extent-m` | 64 | Playable X/Y range is `-extent` to `+extent` |
| `--below-m` | 8 | Playable volume extends to `-below` on Z |
| `--height-m` | 64 | Playable volume extends to `+height` on Z |

The output uses Blam world units (metres divided by 3.048) and BSP index zero.
The sibling `<output>.canvas.json` records the exact bounds for the scenario
and centimetre dimensions for a matching visible slab. World bounds, cluster
bounds and every supernode AABB cover the build volume, independently of the
floor's vertex bounds. Two unreferenced vertices at the volume's minimum and
maximum extend only the world shell's query bounds; they have no edges or
surfaces and are added after building the actual floor's Havok collision.
The floor definition stays compact. The volume has no ceiling or boundary
walls.

This is required for selection above a flat floor: the engine rebuilds its
global ray-query box from all shell vertices, unions instance bounds and
adds 0.1 world units (CU4 `0x2c1aa1..0x2c1e20`). It does not use the authored
world bounds for that initial rejection. Without the extra vertices, a ray
above Z=0.1 was rejected before dynamic objects were tested, although a direct
ray against the same Forge block hit. The regression preserves every
collision table except the two added vertices and checks that elevated space
remains open.

Bot navigation is not provided by these maps. The shell's two extra vertices
also prevent the current `pathfinding::copy_drops` matcher (which requires
equal vertex counts) from recognizing the compact floor instance, so the bake
does not apply its usual 0.001-wu copy lowering. Future navigation support
must account for unreferenced bounds vertices when matching collision copies.

For a standalone B40-based level, use `active_bsps: [8]`, `single_bsp: 8`, the
reported bounds at scenario BSP index 8, `--bsp 8=<output>`, and the bare
`defs/level/empty_world.umap`. The bake renumbers the scenario to the BSP's
index zero. Supply original rendering, valid multiplayer spawn scenery,
lighting, and a kill floor separately. Decorative meshes do not supply Blam
collision. Forge pack palettes require `blam.map_variant: true`, the pack
references, and the pack containers available during the bake.

Each build checks the source collision and both emitted collision trees with
13,068 floor, edge and elevated-space probes, then verifies the emitted volume
bounds. It fails before writing if geometry or bounds disagree. Pure tests
cover square and rectangular slabs, packed collision, and invalid dimensions:

```powershell
cargo test -p blam-sbsp --example forge_canvas
```

These are offline checks; traversal and object placement still need a game
test of the final standalone map.

notes.title: Forge pack materials
notes.summary: Foundry Wide 0.2 adds two self-contained surface profiles to the existing seven shipped-material mappings. The original eighteen Wide pieces keep their previous mesh/material path. New glass and portal pieces use their own cooked masters, textures and shader library; they do not…
notes.body:
Foundry Wide 0.2 adds two self-contained surface profiles to the existing seven
shipped-material mappings. The original eighteen Wide pieces keep their previous
mesh/material path. New glass and portal pieces use their own cooked masters,
textures and shader library; they do not require the TST map to be installed.

## Inputs and provenance

The canonical profile data is
[`material_profiles.json`](../mods/MJOLNIRForge/Scripts/material_profiles.json).
`glass_cyan` is an original two-sided, lit translucent material: RGB
`[0.12, 0.55, 0.65]`, opacity `0.24`, roughness `0.12`, specular `0.7`.
Its pane collision stays solid regardless of opacity.

`teleporter_green` reproduces the Halo CE shader tag
`levels\test\tutorial\shaders\example_tutorial_teleporter`, using the existing
[`shader_transparent_chicago` graph](../unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_materials.py).
The numeric stage parameters were taken from the local TST conversion's
`materials.spec.json`, produced by
[`ce_material_spec.py`](../tools/level/ce_material_spec.py). Four stages sample
two textures: dust in stages 0/1 and mask in stages 2/3. The profile retains
their UV animation functions, periods, phases, scales and color/alpha combiners;
TST's map-specific fog parameters are omitted. Animation uses GPU material time,
not a Lua timer. The visual field has no collision and does not itself teleport
a player; native gameplay markers provide travel.

The material cook requires these **local** CE-conversion DDS files in the
directory supplied to `--ce-textures`. They are the bitmap/mip-chain exports
described in [CE map conversion](ce_map_conversion.md), not Blender previews or
replacement PNGs:

| Filename | Reference SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `scenery_teleporter_shield_bitmaps_teleporter_shield_dust.dds` | `087075684f5f8793ccc68df8f9032f8e493fffa51f32a008225875636009704d` |
| `scenery_teleporter_shield_bitmaps_teleporter_shield_mask.dds` | `84a9e25d316c8707f275b92aa9c1492cdc2a35cb3fafe9bded658fca844bcd31` |

The repository's original geometry and implementation are MIT-licensed. The CE
texture inputs retain their separate game-asset provenance; the repository's
MIT license is not a license grant for those textures. No proprietary texture
files are checked into the authoring source. The built archive **does** include
the converted portal textures. The design concept image is generated artwork;
the contact sheet is a Blender render. Neither is evidence of native rendering.

## Build and distribute

Use the project's Unreal 5.5 editor and fork shader/layout plugins. A fresh
checkout needs the `MeteoriteEditor Win64 Development` and
`Meteorite Win64 Shipping` targets built for
`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Meteorite.uproject` before the commandlets run. The
`mjolnir` CLI must be built too: `tools/ue/cook.ps1` retargets the cooked material
properties into the game's layout and the builder rejects a failed retarget.
Blender exports and native collision/physics are separate prerequisites, as
described in [Forge packs](forge_packs.md).

From the repository root, with local paths substituted:

```powershell
$ceTextures = 'C:/local/CE-conversion/staging/textures'
$basePaks = 'C:/local/base-and-runtime-paks'
# Preparation alone writes a reviewable input specification.
python tools/forge/build_materials.py forge-packs/foundry-wide --ce-textures $ceTextures --chunk 967
# Import, cook, retarget, and fingerprint the material container.
python tools/forge/build_materials.py forge-packs/foundry-wide --ce-textures $ceTextures --chunk 967 --cook
python tools/forge/build_pack.py forge-packs/foundry-wide --paks $basePaks
target/debug/mjolnir.exe forge pack forge-packs/foundry-wide/build/game/all/mjolnir.json `
  --content forge-packs/foundry-wide/build/game/all/content `
  --readme forge-packs/foundry-wide/README.md `
  --changes forge-packs/foundry-wide/build/game/all/changes.json `
  --out forge-packs/foundry-wide/build/foundry-wide-0.2.0.mjolnir --sign
```

Cook under a shader chunk in `900..999` that your own installed packs do not
use (`build_materials.py` enforces the range). Foundry Wide uses **967**, as
`pakchunk967-MJOLNIRFORGEMAT-foundry-wide_P`: Unreal opens the shader library
whose number matches the container's. Asset paths are derived from the validated pack slug:
`/Game/MJOLNIR/Forge/<slug>/Materials/` and `.../Textures/`.

**Launcher 0.24.0 and newer** give each installed container its own number and
rename its shader library to match, so two packs cooked under the same number
install side by side ([chunk_numbering.md](chunk_numbering.md)). The rest of
this paragraph is what an older launcher does.

An older launcher checks the numeric reservation before installing an enabled
surface pack, applying a profile, launching, or copying live dependencies.
Different slugs do not make the same shader number safe. A conflicting active
pack or unrelated `.pak`/`.utoc`/`.ucas` in Paks is refused without modifying
game files. The same pack's existing container triple and updates are allowed.
Offline profile application can retire old launcher-managed files, but two
conflicting packs in the resulting profile are still refused. This check is
specific to `MJOLNIRFORGEMAT` libraries; ordinary pack load ordering is unchanged.

`build/materials/materials.spec.json` records profile values, source paths and
DDS hashes. `receipt.json` records the specification/profile hashes and the
three cooked sibling-file hashes. `build_pack.py` requires a matching, complete
receipt before including surfaces. A changed profile or specification,
modified/missing file, wrong slug, or mismatched shader chunk is rejected.
Changes to the graph implementation also require a fresh cook; the receipt
does not hash Python source files. Unreal-generated IDs may change across
cooks, so receipts identify a particular output, not a promise of identical
binary hashes on every machine.

Local build output contains `.utoc`, `.ucas` and the empty `.pak` mount sibling.
The `.mjolnir` archive stores the `.utoc/.ucas` pairs; the launcher creates the
mount siblings on installation. Keep the material pair and all visual/tag pairs
together. The Forge runtime must also include `materials.lua` and
`material_profiles.json` beside `main.lua`; the JSON is runtime data, not an
optional authoring file. Pack metadata carries only approved profile IDs and
slots, never executable code or arbitrary material paths.

## Runtime lifecycle and verification

The runtime reads the launcher's actual nested inventory:
`packs[].forge_pack.blocks[]`. It requires catalog schema 1, a matching
`forge_pack.id`/release `slug`, and the exact namespaced block tag. Profiles are
assigned on the existing retained game-thread callback, at the 500 ms surface
scan cadence. Both masters already contain their intended defaults, including
the portal textures and animation, so newly spawned pieces do not wait for a
Lua assignment to acquire their basic appearance.

Assignment identity includes world, actor address/name and the salted native
object binding. Hidden or unbound pooled actors are skipped. A reactivated
actor or changed binding receives a fresh material instance. Polling retains
only string keys and booleans for these objects: no Blueprint class, actor,
component, material instance or texture wrapper crosses a poll. Native engine
classes/CDOs are cached; Blueprint classes use the non-loading soft-reference
resolver instead of a global UObject scan.

Work is bounded to 64 surface classes and 256 active actors per poll. A failed
assignment suppresses that class until inventory or world changes and logs
once; this includes a temporarily unavailable component. Existing/baked master
materials remain in place. This avoids repeated loading on a broken catalog or
missing container, but is not a general background asset-retry mechanism.

Portable checks:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s tools/forge -p test_build_materials.py
lua tools/tests/test_forge_materials.lua
lua tools/tests/test_forge_dispatch.lua
cargo test -p ue-asset --lib
```

Foundry Wide contains eight material/texture packages, with all `/Game/`
imports inside its own pack namespace. The glass and portal masters are
two-sided translucent/additive respectively. Each surface mesh declares nine
slots in both its reflected `StaticMaterials` and native arrays, including
slots 7/8. `mesh_rewrite --asset-imports` writes both arrays and uses the old
reflected entries as an exact format guard ([serialization details](ue_mesh_write.md)).
Component overrides alone do not establish translucent renderer relevance.

Cold-load tests verified transparency and solid collision from both sides of
the glass, plus visible green-field animation and native teleport travel in
both directions. Appearance while moving, pooling and restoring surface
placements remains a separate live check. See the
[validation record](forge_pack_validation.md) for the tested artifacts and images.

notes.title: Forge pack utility metadata
notes.summary: Pack utilities are bounded catalog data. They do not install scripts from a community archive. The Hub scanner, CLI packer and launcher validate the same fields; the launcher preserves them in MJOLNIRForgePacks/installed.json. Old packs can omit them or use null.
notes.body:
Pack utilities are bounded catalog data. They do not install scripts from a
community archive. The Hub scanner, CLI packer and launcher validate the same
fields; the launcher preserves them in `MJOLNIRForgePacks/installed.json`.
Old packs can omit them or use `null`.

## Gravity lifts

A block can carry this optional specification, in its authored local axes and
metres (right-handed, Z up):

```json
"lift": {
  "offset_m": [0, 0, 0.45],
  "size_m": [4, 4, 3.5],
  "direction": [0, 0, 1],
  "acceleration_m_s2": 20,
  "max_speed_m_s": 4.5,
  "negates_gravity": true
}
```

`offset_m` is the trigger's bottom centre; `size_m` is its full box size.
The trigger follows the piece's live translation and full rotation, independently
of its visual mesh normalization. The example overlaps a 0.5 m deck by 5 cm to
avoid a floating-point gap. Foundry Wide uses this four-metre-rise preset: its
nominal column ends at 3.95 m, with an additional ballistic rise after exiting.
Verify the trajectory and landing in your own layout; the speed is not a
guaranteed landing height. Horizontal steering is preserved.

Offsets are limited to ±100 m per axis; sizes to 0.1–100 m. Direction must be a
unit vector (squared-length tolerance 0.001). Acceleration is 0.1–100 m/s²,
speed 0.1–30 m/s, and `negates_gravity` must be a boolean. Unknown fields are
rejected. Runtime discovery uses at most 16 class definitions, selected by
sorted class path, and 64 active lift actors; additional definitions are ignored.

`MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/pack_lifts.lua` converts these boxes to the existing
Halo 2 phantom format, and `lifts.lua` hands them to MJOLNIRLobby's DLL with
the level's own phantoms. The DLL pushes with the same acceleration, gravity
compensation and `object_set_velocity` as Lockout's lifts, once per
simulation tick (`native/lobby/lifts_runtime.h`). Each peer pushes only its
own players, on foot, in Forge and Slayer. Saved-layout actors and later
duplicates are discovered from their current Blam bindings; hidden or pooled
actors without a binding do nothing.

Discovery uses Unreal's native actor-class lists and nonloading soft-class
resolution, every 500 ms while an installed pack has a lift block, and the
DLL is sent the set again only when a lift moves, appears or goes. It never
performs a periodic UE4SS global object scan or retains a Blueprint
class/actor wrapper between calls. Travel sends an empty set, and the DLL
drops each player's carried velocity on a new game.

## Automatic doors

Panels may declare:

```json
"door": {
  "travel_m": 4,
  "speed_m_s": 4,
  "trigger_size_m": [8, 16, 6],
  "hold_open_s": 2
}
```

Travel is along local +Z. Travel must be positive and at most 16 m, speed
positive and at most 8 m/s, trigger dimensions positive and at most 32 m,
and hold time 0–10 seconds. Door panel `dimensions_m` may not exceed 64 m
on any axis. Unknown fields are rejected. The infantry preset above travels
4 m; the vehicle preset travels 6 m with a `[12,20,8]` trigger, the same
4 m/s speed and two-second hold.

### Native behavior

Use **MJOLNIRForge 0.4.0**, **MJOLNIRLobby 0.19.2** and
**MJOLNIRLevelLoader 0.9.8** or newer together; doors outside Forge need
**MJOLNIRLobby 0.19.3**. Lobby checks the Forge native
utility API marker and waits for a compatible native Forge module before
animating. It refuses door automation with an older loaded Forge
DLL, whose save path would otherwise serialize the animated position.

`native/lobby/forge_doors_runtime.h` runs on the authoritative simulation
thread in Forge and ordinary multiplayer modes, including Slayer. It operates
on the native crate and its collision body through the engine's transform
setter, rather than moving only its Unreal visual. Players approaching the
rotated local trigger request opening along the panel's local +Z. After they
leave, the panel waits for `hold_open_s` and closes. **Fixed** and **Phased**
enable automation; **Normal** disables it and leaves ordinary physics in control.
Fresh scenario construction and **Revert** seed installed door panels to Fixed,
because scenario placements do not encode this physics choice. This happens
before the objects are created. Loading a saved layout replaces those defaults
with its saved properties, including an explicit Normal choice; other pieces
and existing Fixed/Phased choices are unchanged.

Forge mode keeps a panel inside the map variant's bounds. Other modes leave
those bounds empty, so no box applies there; travel is still limited by the
pack's `travel_m`.

The runtime checks a conservative sphere against the panel's swept box before
closing. Bipeds, vehicles and movable Normal crates can keep a door open or reopen it.
Opening also stops beneath a dynamic obstacle. Entering Monitor mode, or
requesting an edit, attempts to close the panel only if its entire closing
path is clear. A parked vehicle can therefore leave the panel raised while
editing. Grabbing, duplicating, rotating or changing the physics of that raised
panel is deferred with a message to clear the doorway; unrelated objects remain
editable. These checks do not test
the static world, Fixed/Phased construction pieces, or unparented crates whose
native physics model contains only fixed bodies. The last classification is
cached per world and salted tag; keyframed, mixed and unknown bodies remain
obstacles. Authors must leave
space above and beside the panel for its full travel.

Motion advances once per changed simulation tick, using the native tick rate;
paused redraws do not consume hold time. Catch-up frames advance at most one
tick. There are at most 128 active automated panels and 256 installed door
definitions. The adapter scans native object arrays once per tick, with no
Unreal global-object polling. It accepts only supported CU4 builds and rejects
parented panels, invalid transforms, stale object handles and unmatched pack
identities. Unsupported builds or invalid inventory disable automation.

### Editing, saves and multiplayer limits

Forge's native update reapplies each map-variant pose every tick. The adapter
therefore publishes the animated position in the live map variant and keeps
the authored closed pose in a private cache, keyed by world instance, full
object handle and entry identity. Deletion, travel and replaced objects discard
stale cache entries; an external authored pose change establishes a new baseline.

**F5** projects verified closed poses into Forge's temporary serialization copy.
Saving does not close the live door or modify the active animation. If a panel
has no verified closed baseline, saving is deferred rather than recording its
raised pose. This includes enabled door panels on fireteam clients. Ordinary
layouts without those panels retain the existing client-save behavior.

A client that becomes host cannot reconstruct the closed origin of a door it
joined while open. Automation and saves requiring that missing baseline remain
disabled until the game is rehosted. Closed-origin state is not separately
replicated. The engine's object-transform updates are used in Slayer; map-variant
dirty updates apply in Forge. Client visual/collision replication, host migration
and driving a vehicle beneath an operating gate still require in-game
verification. The
[validation record](forge_pack_validation.md) reports the narrower local
save/reload, visible opening/closing and nearby-vehicle obstruction results.
The implementation and portable tests are not live evidence.

### Installed companion

The launcher emits a companion `MJOLNIRForgePacks/doors.txt` for the native
reader. Its header is `forge-doors 1`; each row has ten tab-separated fields:
tag, travel, speed, trigger X/Y/Z, hold time, panel width/depth/height. All
measurements are metres or seconds, using decimal dots. There are at most
256 definitions across enabled packs. The native reader must match each
tag against current `installed.txt` bindings. Panel dimensions come from the
validated catalog, not a guessed donor bound. The trigger is centred on the
panel in X/Y, with its vertical interval from −0.5 m to trigger Z above the
authored bottom origin.

The launcher prepares all inventory files before replacing each atomically,
publishing the identity bindings last. Disabling/uninstalling packs also
rewrites the companion; no door entries leaves a header-only file.

## Surface profiles

`surfaces` is an optional list of up to 16 strict `{slot, profile}` objects.
Slots are unique integers 0–15. Profiles are the fixed names `glass_cyan`
and `teleporter_green`; arbitrary material paths or code are not accepted.
The material implementation supplies the approved textures, animation and
shader parameters. The green visual does not replace native teleporter
sender/receiver/two-way markers and their channel settings.

The CLI packer and Hub scanner require these cooked packages inside the
archive's installed `content/` containers, under `/Game/MJOLNIR/Forge/<pack-id>`:

| Profile | Required package paths below the pack root |
|---|---|
| `glass_cyan` | `Materials/M_ForgeGlassCyan` |
| `teleporter_green` | `Materials/M_ForgePortalGreen`, `Textures/T_PortalDust`, `Textures/T_PortalMask`, `Materials/T_CE_BlackCube` |

The check uses Unreal package IDs and requires export-bundle chunks; bulk-only
chunks, another pack's copies and containers outside `content/` do not satisfy
it. Packs without surface profiles do not need these assets. The Hub's bounded
package-ID hash and the Rust implementation share 15 test vectors spanning
minimum, ordinary and maximum pack slug lengths.

This is a presence check, not proof of valid material exports, complete shader
code, matching mesh slots or gameplay collision. Door/lift metadata validators
check their bounded data shapes; they do not decode tag payloads to prove a
compatible native crate and Blueprint binding. The authored cook checks and
live runtime checks remain necessary, as does testing the installed pack.

## Checks

Portable tests cover transformed trigger planes, source-to-Unreal coordinates,
the standing-deck overlap, player ownership, actor pooling, class lookup cost
boundaries, world travel and use of the shared script writer. Existing Halo 2
math tests remain unchanged. Hub/CLI/launcher tests cover schema limits,
unknown keys, normalized inventory round trips, companion fields and stale-row
removal. Live gameplay coverage is recorded separately in the
[validation record](forge_pack_validation.md).

`native/lobby/test-forge-doors.ps1` runs the portable door parser and movement
tests with MSVC warnings treated as errors. They cover field limits, rejected
row isolation, translated/rotated triggers, sphere-versus-swept-panel clearance,
opening/closing, hold time and paused or invalid time steps. The same C test
also builds with a C11 compiler on other platforms. CI runs it alongside the
three lift Lua suites and the launcher Forge inventory tests.

notes.title: Forge layout sharing
notes.summary: Players build with Forge today, but a build stays on their PC: F5 keeps one layout per map, and the only way to give one to someone is to copy two files by hand. This document plans several named layouts per map, a lobby choice of which one a match starts with, a hub listing…
notes.body:
**Status:** design, 2026-11-03. Nothing here is built unless a line says so.
Phase 0 (checking layout files) is built and tested in game on branch
`work/forge-mvar-bounds`.

Players build with Forge today, but a build stays on their PC: F5 keeps one
layout per map, and the only way to give one to someone is to copy two files
by hand. This document plans several named layouts per map, a lobby choice
of which one a match starts with, a hub listing that players publish to and
download from, and an in-game layouts menu.

## What exists

| Piece | Today | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Save, load, revert | F5, F6, F2 in a FORGE game only (the sandbox tick runs them) | `native/forge/mjolnir_forge.c` `layout_save` 1083, `layout_load` 1154, `layout_revert` 1175; `hooked_tick` 1999 |
| Files | `Mods\MJOLNIRForge\layouts\<CODE>.mvar` and `<CODE>.mvar.packs`; the previous pair moves to `layouts\history\<CODE>-<time>-<serial>` | `derive_paths` 315, `layout_history_paths` 718; two-file commits in `layout_files.h` |
| Sidecar | `forge-packs 1`, then `flat⇥tag⇥slug⇥version⇥sha256` for each pack palette entry used | `layout_packs` 795; `pack_bindings.h` 148 |
| Match start | the host's DLL reads `<CODE>.mvar` at new-map (any game type) and adopts it; clients never read a file, the engine replicates the objects | `layout_new_map` 1197 |
| Pack check | same major, not older (the caret line); refused with a reason shown for 10 s | `forge_version_accepts` in `pack_bindings.h` 104; `Hud.layoutWarning` |
| Launcher | before a launch, installs the packs every top-level `layouts\*.mvar.packs` names; two sidecars pinning different lines of one pack fail the launch | `apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/hub.rs` `saved_layout_pins` 632 (`read_dir`, not recursive); `forge_packs.rs` `merge_layout_pin` 352 |
| Hub | no layout type. The manifest allows `content` and `map` only, the scanner refuses `.mvar` and any release without a container, and uploads must be signed | `hub/src/lib/api/manifest.ts` 28; `scan.ts` 39, 344, 424; `wrangler.jsonc` 42 |
| Game ↔ hub | the lobby DLL's WinHTTP worker sends JSON with the launcher's key; downloads only go to `MJOLNIRMaps\_covers`; installs run the launcher (`--install-map`) | `native/lobby/mjolnir_lobby.c` 4560, 4754; `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/maplive.lua` |
| Credentials | the launcher's device key has `mods:read`, `ratings:write`, `comments:write`, `lobbies:write`; the tag editor pairs with `mods:write` and signs with a DPAPI Ed25519 key | `hub/src/lib/api/device.ts` 40; `apps/tag-editor/src-tauri/src/hub.rs` 113, `keystore.rs` |

## Phase 0: checking layout files (built)

A hub hands everyone who downloads a layout a file its author chose, so every
reader checks a layout before the game sees it:

- **Forge DLL** (built): `native/forge/layout_bounds.h` checks a layout's
  labels and label names, and Forge refuses a malformed file with the reason.
- **Hub and launcher** (planned): the validator below, on upload and on
  install.

## The validator

One Rust function, `blam_megalo::layout::validate(bytes) -> Result<Summary>`,
used by the hub (built to WebAssembly), the launcher and the tag editor
(native). A second implementation in TypeScript would be a second grammar to
keep in step.

It accepts a file when:

1. The envelope is the one Forge writes: `_blf` 1.2, one `mvar` 31.1 with a
   payload of at most 0x7000 bytes (the DLL's buffer), an optional `fpk1`
   1.0, `_eof`, then only zero padding.
2. The payload decodes completely with `crates/blam-megalo/grammar/megalo_cu4.json`,
   with fewer than 8 bits left over.
3. Content type 5 (map variant) and encoding version 31.
4. At most 256 labels, at most 0x1000 bytes of label names (the declared
   size, the compressed stream's prefix and the inflated bytes), and at
   most 256 quotas.
5. It encodes back to the same bytes, so nothing the grammar does not name
   travels in it.
6. Every placed object's palette index is inside the palette (to confirm
   against the decoder before relying on it).

`Summary` carries what the hub and launcher store: title, description, map
id, object count, labels, and the palette entries used. The sidecar is parsed
by the parser the launcher already has (`forge_packs::layout_pins`).

**WebAssembly on the hub works.** A spike on 2026-11-03 built `blam-megalo` for
`wasm32-unknown-unknown` (382 KB, grammar included) and imported the `.wasm`
from a route. OpenNext bundled it, `wrangler dev` ran it on workerd, and the
route returned the right label counts for a MJOLNIR save (0) and Reach's
Asylum (13), about 2 ms a file. A local Cloudflare build on Windows needs
`pnpm install --config.node-linker=hoisted`, because OpenNext's file copy
cannot create pnpm's symlinks without Developer Mode. CI builds on Linux and
is unaffected.

## Phase 1: named layouts

### Files

```
Mods\MJOLNIRForge\layouts\
  FRB.mvar, FRB.mvar.packs      active: what every match on FRB starts with (unchanged)
  FRB.active                    the library entry the active pair came from, if any
  history\...                   unchanged
  library\FRB\<id>\
    layout.mvar
    layout.mvar.packs
    layout.json                 title, description, created, updated, map version,
                                source (local, or hub slug + version + release id)
    preview.png                 optional
```

The active pair keeps its name, so everything that reads it today (match
start, F6, the launcher's pins, history) is unchanged. The launcher scans
`layouts\` without recursing, so library entries never take part in the
launch-time pins. A downloaded layout built against a newer pack line
cannot block a launch. An entry whose packs are missing or on another
line is refused when it is loaded, by the same caret check, with "restart
through the launcher".

### Operations

| Action | What happens |
|---|---|
| Save (F5) | as today; if `FRB.active` names an entry, the entry is updated too |
| Save as | F5, then the active pair is copied into a new entry; the id comes from the title plus a number, and the title can be changed later without moving files |
| Use | the active pair goes to history, the entry's pair becomes active, `FRB.active` names it; in a FORGE game the objects are replaced as F6 does |
| Original (F2) | as today; `FRB.active` is cleared |
| Rename, delete | `layout.json` only, or the entry's folder |

The DLL does the file work, because `layout_files.h` already commits two
files safely and never overwrites. Its exports take no arguments, so the
menu writes a request (`layouts\request.txt`: an operation, map code, entry
id and title, one per line) and calls a new `library` export. The DLL
answers in `layouts\library.txt`: one line per entry, with id, title,
objects, packs and when it was saved. Library requests run from `pump`
rather than the sandbox tick, so the lobby can use them outside a FORGE
game. Use, F5 and F6 still need the sandbox.

### The lobby choice

The map select shows **Layout: Original** and the map's library entries
when the chosen map has any. START GAME makes the choice active before
`startGame` writes `pending_variant.txt`, so the existing match-start path
does the rest. The lobby broadcast gains a seventh field, the layout's
title. Older clients read six fields by position and ignore it. The vote
after a match keeps each option's layout.

## Phase 2: the hub and the launcher

### Archive

```
mjolnir.json        type "layout", a `layout` block, deps
layout/layout.mvar
layout/layout.mvar.packs
layout/preview.png  (or .jpg / .webp, at most 1 MiB)
docs/README.md      optional
signature.json
```

`mjolnir.json`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "type": "layout",
  "name": "Crossline Towers",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "summary": "Two towers over the vehicle lane.",
  "layout": { "map": "FRB", "objects": 312 },
  "deps": [
    { "slug": "crossline", "range": "^0.3.0" },
    { "slug": "foundry-wide", "range": "^0.2.0" }
  ]
}
```

The base map is the dependency whose map listing has the code in `layout.map`.
Every pack in the sidecar must be a dependency at the caret line it names.

### Hub

| Change | Where |
|---|---|
| Manifest | `type` gains `"layout"`; the `layout` block is required for it alone (`manifest.ts` 28, 74) |
| Scanner | for a layout only: allow the four `layout/` files and skip the container rule (`scan.ts` 39, 344, 424); run the validator; compare the manifest's map and object count with the file's; check the sidecar against `deps`; cap the archive at 2 MiB |
| Validator | `blam-megalo` built to `.wasm`, imported by `scan.ts` |
| Complete | category forced to `layouts`; deps into `release_deps`; a `layout_listings` row (`publish.ts` 693-738) |
| Schema | migration `0025_forge_layouts.sql`, additive: `layout_listings (mod_id PK, map_code, base_slug, title, objects, packs JSON, updated_at)` and an index on `map_code`. Apply it before the merge |
| API | `GET /maps/{code}/layouts` and `GET /layouts?map=&sort=`, for the website, the launcher and the game |
| Website | a Layouts section on a map's page (`hub/src/app/mods/[slug]/page.tsx`), Community layouts on `/forge`, and `layouts` in `/mods/new`'s categories. The manage page's single PUT already fits |

**Review hold: a decision for the owner.** A layout carries bytes that
the engine decodes, which is a map's risk rather than a texture's.

- **Hold new authors** (as maps do: trust level below 2 waits for a
  moderator). Safe whatever the validator misses. Moderators would see
  the scanner's summary. The catch: `trust_level` has no writer in the hub
  today, so every new author waits on a person.
- **Publish on a pass** (as content does). Faster for players. It rests
  entirely on the validator: the full decode, the caps and the
  re-encode. Reports and yanking stay available.

The validator design favours publishing on a pass. Holding new authors
for the first releases is the cautious start.

### Launcher

- `install_one_as` (`hub.rs` 1085) learns the manifest type `layout`. A
  layout's hub mod is a `content` mod, so the trust-tier check (1112)
  already passes. For a layout it skips the container rule (1320) and runs
  the same validator natively before writing anything.
- It writes `library\<CODE>\hub-<slug>\` with `layout.json` naming the
  release, and installs the map and packs through the usual deps.
- Uninstalling removes the entry. If that entry is active, the active
  pair stays and `FRB.active` is cleared, so a match is never left without
  its layout.
- Library entries get a best-effort pin pass. Their packs are installed
  when they don't conflict with the active layouts. A conflict is noted on
  the Updates screen rather than failing the launch.
- `--install-layout <slug> [--release <id>] --progress <file>`, gated by
  `layouts` in `launcher_features.txt`, as `--install-map` is. Nothing
  needs mounting. A pack the game has not loaded still needs a restart,
  which the menu says.
- `mjolnir://layout/<slug>` opens the layout's page in Browse Hub, as
  `mod/` and `map/` links do (`links.rs` 79).

## Phase 3: the in-game menu

`WBP_MJOLNIRForgeLayouts` is a cooked widget in the Forge UI container
(`pakchunk980-MJOLNIRFORGEUI`, `build_forge_hud` in
`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_mjolnir_ui.py`), so it ships in a CE
runtime release.

- **Opening it:** in a FORGE game, from a FORGE LAYOUTS item in the pause
  menu (the HOST MENU pattern, `MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/main.lua` 3969) and from
  a key still to be chosen. F7-F9 belong to MJOLNIRFlyCam.
- **The list:** this map's entries in ten authored rows that slide over the
  list, the palette's pattern. Each row shows title, objects, packs and
  date, and the active one is marked.
- **Buttons:** Load, Save as, Rename, Delete, Use for matches, Publish, Get
  more.
- **Names:** an `EditableTextBox`, focused the way chat focuses its input
  (`MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/chat.lua` 433). Forge ignores its own keys while it
  has focus (`typingInChat`).
- **Get more:** lists the hub's layouts for the map
  (`GET /maps/{code}/layouts` through `Games.call`) with their covers (the
  existing `FILE` download into `_covers`), and installs through
  `--install-layout`.

## Phase 4: publishing

The game can't publish on its own. It holds no key that can write, and the
lobby DLL sends only JSON.

1. **Publish** in the menu writes `layouts\publish_request.json` (map,
   entry) and starts the launcher through the lobby DLL's existing launcher
   action, with `--publish-layout <CODE>/<id>`, window shown.
2. The launcher shows a publish form: title, summary, version (the next
   patch for an update), the preview, and what the layout depends on.
   Nothing is sent until the player confirms.
3. It builds the archive and signs it with a launcher signing key. That key
   is DPAPI-protected Ed25519, as the tag editor's `keystore.rs`, and
   registered once through `POST /account/signing-keys`. Then it uploads
   with the existing four calls.
4. **A new scope, `layouts:write`**, offered when the launcher pairs and
   shown on the device approval page. `requireScoped` accepts it only for a
   mod whose category is `layouts`, and `/complete` refuses anything but a
   `layout` manifest for a key that has only this scope. Giving the
   launcher `mods:write` instead would let every paired launcher publish
   any mod.

Two existing gaps this depends on:

- `POST /account/signing-keys` only authenticates (`account.ts` 224),
  despite its comment. It should require `mods:write` or `layouts:write`.
- Nothing checks that a joiner has the packs the host's layout uses. The
  lobby broadcast should carry the active layout's pins, and a client
  missing a pack should be told before the match, as for a missing map.

The tag editor can already publish with `mods:write`. A Publish layout
button there is the quickest working path, and it belongs with the
editor's Forge mode.

## Order and testing

| Phase | Ships as | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | MJOLNIRForge 0.4.1 (mods 0.43.1) | done in game, and in `native/forge/test_layout_bounds.c` |
| 1 | mods release (Forge, Lobby) | save as, use, rename, delete; START GAME with a chosen layout as Slayer and FORGE; F2 back to the original; the launcher still launches with conflicting library entries |
| 2 | hub deploy + migration, launcher release | validator tests on every MCC map variant, every MJOLNIR save and malformed files; scanner tests (`hub/scripts/test-scan.mts`); publish with a temporary key; a clean launcher profile installs a layout and its map and packs |
| 3 | CE runtime release (chunk 980) + mods | menu at 16:9 and 16:10; text entry beside chat; Get more installs without a restart when the packs are present |
| 4 | launcher + hub | publish from the game on a test account; refused for a key without the scope |

## Questions for the owner

1. Review hold for layouts from new authors, or publish on a pass?
2. Publishing from the game through the launcher (the new scope), or
   through the tag editor first?
3. The preview: should the launcher take a screenshot of the game window
   when the player publishes, or ask for an image?
4. Which key opens the layouts menu in a FORGE game?

notes.title: Forge mode in the tag editor
notes.summary: Forge in the game is one player with a cursor. The tag editor can show the whole map at once. Forge mode lets a builder place, move, turn and delete a layout's objects in the editor's 3D view, with real meshes and grid snapping. While the game runs a FORGE game on the same map,…
notes.body:
**Status:** design, 2026-11-03. Nothing here is built unless a line says so.
It builds on [forge_layout_sharing.md](forge_layout_sharing.md): the layout
library, the validator and the publishing flow.

Forge in the game is one player with a cursor. The tag editor can show the
whole map at once. Forge mode lets a builder place, move, turn and delete
a layout's objects in the editor's 3D view, with real meshes and grid
snapping. While the game runs a FORGE game on the same map, each edit
appears in the game on the next tick, and objects moved in the game move in
the editor. With the two windows side by side, the editor is the floor
plan and the game is the walk-through.

## What exists

| Piece | Today | Where |
|---|---|---|
| World view | BSP collision, a scenario's placements with real textured meshes (tag → `BP_` → `SM_`/`SK_`), trigger volumes, spawns; click to select; three.js `TransformControls` move/rotate; edits written to the scenario tag through `set_field` | `apps/tag-editor/src/components/ScenarioViewer.tsx`; `src-tauri/src/geometry.rs`; `lib.rs` `read_scenario_layout` 2692 |
| Meshes | Nanite or classic LOD decode, base-colour textures; the catalog indexes every top-level container in Paks, so the launcher's `MJOLNIRHUB` pack containers should be included | `lib.rs` `read_mesh` 2503; `src/lib/render-mesh.ts` `loadRenderGroup`; `catalog.rs` 303 |
| Live | attaches to the game with ReadProcessMemory/WriteProcessMemory and pokes tag fields | `src-tauri/src/live.rs`; `crates/blam-live` |
| Live objects | `blam_live::world::objects` reads every object's position, forward, up and scale; `mapvar_probe` reads the live map variant (`[TLS+0x250]+0x308`, 651 entries of 0x4c bytes from `+0x14fc`) | `crates/blam-live/src/world.rs` 254; `examples/mapvar_probe.rs` |
| `.mvar` codec | decodes and re-encodes a whole map variant as a tree (277 of 277 MCC files round-trip); world positions only in an example; no `.mvar` writer, no object API | `crates/blam-megalo/src/raw.rs` 1065, 1084, 1399; `examples/mvar_summary.rs` |
| Forge DLL | every command acts on the local player's held or aimed-at object; no outside command | `native/forge/mjolnir_forge.c` 159-184, `place_entry` 1466, `finish_grid_drop` 1573 |

What the editor lacks: it has no idea of maps by code or of Forge packs, it
doesn't read the scenario's `map variant palettes`, and it doesn't link
`blam-megalo`.

## The parts

### 1. A layout model in `blam-megalo`

A `layout` module over the existing tree:

```rust
pub struct Layout { pub header: Header, pub bounds: Bounds, pub objects: Vec<Placement>, /* the rest kept as tree */ }
pub struct Placement {
    pub entry: u16,            // 0..651, stable across edits
    pub palette: u8,           // flat index across `map variant palettes`
    pub variant: Option<u8>,
    pub position: [f32; 3],    // world units
    pub yaw: f32,              // radians
    pub up: Option<u32>,       // packed, carried as read (see below)
    pub flags: u8,
    pub properties: Properties, // physics, team, spawn order, label... carried exactly
}
impl Layout { fn decode(mvar: &[u8]) -> Result<Self>; fn encode(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>>; }
```

- **Positions:** decode with the widths `position_widths` already computes,
  `lo + span / 2^bits × (raw + 0.5)`. Encoding is the inverse, rounded,
  so a position moves by at most half a step. That is under a millimetre
  on a Forge map, as in the game.
- **Turning:** yaw is 14 bits (radians = raw × 0.000383495 − 3.141401). The
  20-bit `up` vector (`0x3f57d0`) is not modelled, so an edited object
  keeps its `up` as read. The game turns about the vertical only, so
  nothing is lost.
- **File writer:** the envelope the DLL writes (`_blf` 1.2, `mvar` 31.1 with a
  zero hash, `fpk1`, `_eof`). The sidecar writer uses the launcher's
  format.
- **Every save passes the validator** in the layout sharing design, so the
  editor can never write a file the game refuses.
- **Tests:** decode → encode is byte-identical on every MJOLNIR save and
  every MCC map variant. Moving one object changes only that entry. The
  DLL's own reader (`test_layout_bounds.c`) accepts what the writer
  produces.

### 2. The Forge view (offline)

- **Open a map by code.**
  - The editor reads the installed maps the way the game does
    (`ue4ss\MJOLNIRMaps\maps.json`, then the loader's `maps.json`).
  - It finds the map's scenario in the catalog and shows its world as
    the World view does.
  - MJOLNIR's own Forge maps also have floors that MJOLNIRLevelLoader
    spawns at runtime from `map/level.json` (`decor`: Crossline's slab,
    Forge Canvas's deck). Forge mode draws those as plain shapes, so the
    map isn't floating in space.
- **Palette.** The scenario's `map variant palettes` block, read in
  `geometry.rs`, gives each flat index a tag.
  - Pack pieces are named from `MJOLNIRForgePacks\installed.json` and
    grouped by pack and category, as in the game's palette.
  - Each piece's mesh comes from `loadRenderGroup`. If a pack mesh doesn't
    resolve, its catalog box (`dimensions_m`) stands in, so a missing mesh
    never hides a piece.
- **Open a layout.** Choose a library entry, the active layout, or the
  map's own. Objects are drawn at their decoded transforms and selected by
  click or from a list, with a box select.
- **Edit.**
  - Move with the gizmo, on a grid of 0.25 to 4 m (the game's steps), and
    turn by the game's angle steps.
  - Duplicate, delete, and place from the palette.
  - Physics mode, team, spawn order and label use the same values as the
    game's property keys.
  - Undo goes through the editor's existing journal.
- **Budgets.** The palette shows placed and maximum counts and the price,
  as the game's HUD does, and refuses a placement over the maximum.
- **Save.** Saving goes to a library entry (Save, or Save as), never
  straight over the active layout. In the game, Use or F6 puts it on the
  map.

### 3. The live link

**Reading needs no game change.** While the game runs a FORGE game on the
same map:

- The editor reads the live entry table about ten times a second, through
  `blam-live` as `mapvar_probe` does.
- It moves its copies of anything that changed, so an object the player
  carries in the game moves in the editor.
- It marks the object the player is holding (`forge_state.txt` names it)
  and locks it against editing while it's held.

**Writing needs the game thread.** Writing the entry table from outside
would not move the objects, because the engine moves them through
`object_set_pose` and its dirty marks. It would also race the simulation.
So the Forge DLL gains a small command server:

| Piece | Design |
|---|---|
| Transport | a named pipe, `\\.\pipe\mjolnir-forge-<pid>`, created by the DLL with an ACL for the current user only. One client at a time |
| Operations | `snapshot` (entries with palette, transform, flags, and a generation number); `move <entry> <pos> <yaw>`; `place <palette> <pos> <yaw>`; `delete <entry>`; `highlight <entry>` |
| Execution | a reader thread queues operations, and the sandbox tick runs them (the slot 113 hook, as Lua's commands do), at most a few per tick |
| Reuse | `place` uses `place_entry`. `move` uses the pose sequence of `finish_grid_drop`: `0x5ec880` pre-move, `0x59f600` set pose, `0x59f470` modified, the entry's position, forward and up, then `mv_entry_dirty(entry, 2)`. `delete` is engine request 1 |
| Answers | each operation replies with the entry's pose as the engine left it. Fixed and Phased objects take the pose exactly, while Normal physics may settle |
| Guards | host only, FORGE games only, refused on a fireteam client. An operation names the layout generation it was made against, and the DLL bumps the generation when a layout is replaced (F6, F2, Use), so stale edits are refused. Nothing runs while the player holds that object |

Why not MJOLNIRBridge: players don't have it enabled, and it runs any Lua
it's sent. A pipe with five typed operations, local to the user, is much
narrower.

**Conflicts.** The last writer wins for each entry. The editor shows the
game's version whenever its snapshot disagrees with an edit that hasn't
been answered yet.

**Camera.** "Follow the game" moves the editor's camera to the player's
view (the player unit's position and aim, read through `blam-live`). It's
optional and comes later.

### 4. Publishing

The editor already pairs with `mods:write` and signs releases
(`src-tauri/src/hub.rs`, `keystore.rs`). Publish layout builds the
archive described in the layout sharing design from a library entry.
That makes the editor the first working path for publishing.

## Phases

| Phase | Ships as | Test |
|---|---|---|
| E1 codec and validator | crate only | byte-identical round trips on every MJOLNIR save and MCC map variant; single-entry edits; the DLL's reader accepts the writer's files |
| E2 offline Forge view | tag editor release | open Crossline, Forge Canvas and Roadworks Circuit by code; pack meshes draw; move, place and delete, save to a library entry, then F6 in game shows the same layout |
| E3 live read | tag editor release | carry a wall in game and watch it move in the editor; the held object is locked |
| E4 live write | mods release (Forge DLL) + tag editor | on Crossline, move a wall, place a ramp and delete a crate from the editor, and see each in game on the next tick; Fixed/Phased exact, Normal settles; stale generation refused after F6; refused on a fireteam client |
| E5 publish | tag editor release + hub layout type | publish a library entry to a test account; install it with a clean launcher profile |

E1 is shared with layout sharing's Phase 2. Building it first serves both.

## Risks

- **Pack meshes:** pack pieces are expected to draw through the catalog,
  but nobody has tried it. The box fallback keeps the view usable either
  way.
- **Map coverage:** MJOLNIR maps whose floors are runtime decor need their
  `level.json` shapes drawn. Converted CE maps also have a terrain mesh in
  their Unreal world that the World view doesn't load. Forge mode shows
  their BSP collision instead.
- **The live move sequence:** the order of calls `finish_grid_drop` uses
  works for a held object being dropped. Moving an object nobody holds by
  that path is untested; E4's first in-game test settles it.
- **One game at a time:** the pipe is per process, and the editor attaches
  to one game.

## Questions for the owner

1. Is a named pipe from the Forge DLL acceptable as the live channel, or
   should it be files beside `forge_state.txt`, as the Forge HUD's are?
2. Should Forge mode be a mode of the existing World view, or a separate
   Forge tab that starts from a map code?

notes.title: The MJOLNIR level format (`.level.json`)
