notes.title: Converting a Halo 2 Map
notes.summary: MCC's Halo 2 multiplayer maps (halo2/h2_maps_win64_dx11/*.map) become standalone Campaign Evolved maps the way classic CE maps do (ce_map_conversion.md): their own collision, render geometry, materials and lightmaps, player starts, pickups and markers, under the Megalo engine.
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-10-22. Lockout and Ascension convert through the same
command as the Halo 1 maps and start from MULTIPLAYER (`mjolnir_auto host LOK
slayer private`, `host ASC ctf private`): their own worlds, the Spartan
standing in the BSP, the pickups resting where Halo 2 put them, every
material applied. Lockout was played by a person on 2026-10-21; the glass,
snow and sky they found wrong are fixed (reflecting tinted glass, the
chambers' gas behind it, snow where Halo 2 puts it, cloud banks in place of
flat white planes). Ascension was compared side by side with MCC on
2026-10-22: its turning antennas and storm sky match. The Halo 1 pipeline is unchanged; its outputs for Chill
Out and TST are byte-identical before and after the Halo 2 work.

MCC's Halo 2 multiplayer maps (`halo2/h2_maps_win64_dx11/*.map`) become
standalone Campaign Evolved maps the way classic CE maps do
([ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md)): their own collision, render
geometry, materials and lightmaps, player starts, pickups and markers, under
the Megalo engine.

```bash
export HCE_PAKS=".../Halo Campaign Evolved/Meteorite/Content/Paks"
MCC=".../Halo The Master Chief Collection/halo2/h2_maps_win64_dx11"
tools/level/convert_ce_map.sh "$MCC/lockout.map" LOK out/lok --install
```

`shared.map` and `textures.dat` must sit beside the map (they do in an
install): every weapon, vehicle and most shaders live in `shared.map`, every
bitmap's pixels in `textures.dat`.

## Which game a map is from

`mjolnir cache info <map>` reads the header and names the game, the build and
the tool that stages it ([h2_cache_format.md](h2_cache_format.md), "Telling the
games apart"). `convert_ce_map.sh` asks it first:

| map | stager |
|---|---|
| Halo 1 PC or Custom Edition (version 7, 609) | halo2ue (HalcyonRing), unchanged |
| Halo 2 MCC (version 13, game index 1) | `mjolnir cache stage` (crates/blam-cache) |
| Halo 1 MCC, Halo 3, ODST, Reach, Halo 4, H2A | refused, by name, before anything runs |

The staging's `manifest.json` says which game it came from (`source`:
`halo_ce` or `halo2_mcc`), and the few steps that are CE's alone branch on it:
`ce_fog.py` and `ce_sounds.py` (they read the CE `.map` itself), the
lightmap solver (CE's radiosity: `LIGHTMAP_SCALE` defaults to 0, keeping Halo
2's own pages) and the foliage (CE detail maps: `FOLIAGE` defaults to 0).
`gen_ce_level.py` takes its tag map (`defs/level/h2-tag-map.json`), menu name
and description from the same field.

## What staging does differently

`mjolnir cache stage` writes the files halo2ue writes for Halo 1, in the same
units and axes, so every later step reads them unchanged:

- **Collision.** Halo 2's 16-bit tables are widened into the CE element layout
  (`collision_0.bin`, `layout: "ce_pc_v7"`). Instanced geometry, which CE never
  had, is placed in world space (scale, forward/left/up, position), each
  polygon fan-split into standalone two-sided triangles that keep their
  material and flags, and appended as the `scenery_surfaces` tail CE scenery
  uses; `merge_ce_collision.py` adds the props after it. Lockout: 3,162 BSP
  surfaces, 75 instances (7,312 triangles), 15 crates (840), more than one
  16-bit tree holds, so `level collision` puts the tail behind an instance of
  its own (as Timberland's trees).
- **Surface materials.** A Halo 2 shader names a global material
  (`hard_terrain_concrete`), not a CE material type; staging maps it onto the
  29 the game ships: the same name, else an alias (concrete is stone,
  `energy` is `energy_hologram`), else the name shortened a word at a time
  and tried again the same way (`hard_metal_thin_hum_grating` to
  `hard_metal_thin`), else `default_material`. Each substitution is printed.
- **Render geometry.** Clusters and instanced geometry go into one
  `bsp_0.gltf`, a primitive per (shader, lightmap page), with each cluster's
  and instance's page from the lightmap tag and Halo 2's lightmap
  coordinates. Halo 2's triangles already wind counter-clockwise, so their
  order is kept (CE's are flipped).
- **Shaders.** MCC keeps no shader parameter names; each template's bitmap
  slots and tiling are read in the template's order (`h2::render::template`),
  and what the compiled shaders do was read back from the DXBC in the
  shader pass tags ([h2_cache_format.md](h2_cache_format.md)). Opaque shaders
  become environment-master summaries (base, detail, second detail blended
  by the base's alpha where it is high, the reverse of CE's, bump,
  self-illumination; alpha tested for the alpha-test templates. The
  single-pass ones' compiled lightmap pass discards where the bump map's
  alpha rounds to 0: Zanzibar's palm fronds, beach bushes and tree foliage
  keep their outline only there, so their base map is staged with the bump
  map's alpha as `<stem>__cut.png`. The other `tex_bump_alpha_test*`
  shaders keep the outline in the base's alpha, the bump map's, or both
  (of the 26 stagings' fourteen: grates on Zanzibar and Foundation in the
  base; the temple vines on Sanctuary and Warlock, Derelict's vines,
  Headlong's girders, Midship's torn pillars and Terminal's generator in
  the bump map; Lockout's grate in both), so `<stem>__cut.png` takes the
  product of the two. Cut on the base alone, the bump-map ones drew as
  black quads, 2026-11-21 playtest).
  `tex_bump_plasma_one_channel_illum` (Zanzibar's fusion coil cores) is a
  lit base and detail plus the plasma pass's glow from bitmap 3: red times
  a band of its alpha around pixel constant 2's, plus green and blue each
  times a pink pixel constant. It becomes CE's three-channel
  self-illumination (`<stem>__glow.png`: green, blue, and red x the band
  baked at the shader's level, tinted by pixel constants 3, 4 and 5; a
  colour image in one channel drew white). Read as a detail map, its
  magenta channels drew a pink and black grid. `overlay` (Zanzibar's Camp Froman sign, the
  military crates' stencils) is 2 x base x tint, drawn as a double
  multiply. On Zanzibar the multiply master draws nothing in the after-DOF
  translucency pass (a black multiply on the sign stayed invisible, and
  appeared with `r.SeparateTranslucency 0`; the same black multiply draws
  on Chill Out's glass, cause not found), so the multiply is baked into an
  alpha-blended copy,
  `<stem>__overlay.png`: black at 1 - m where the overlay darkens the
  frame by m (exact), clear at neutral grey and where it brightens: no
  blend brightens whatever lies under it, and as its hue at (m - 1) / 2 a
  crack map's near-grey laid a pale sheet over Sanctuary's dark ceilings. `water_edge_blend` (Zanzibar's flat plane at sea level)
  writes its map's alpha into the frame's alpha only, a mask the water
  fades by; its geometry is left out (drawn opaque without a map, it was a
  big white patch on the beach). Water (`water_pool`, `water_pool_cube`:
  Beaver Creek's creek, Coagulation's cave pool, Sanctuary's streams) mixes
  the rippled frame behind with its reflection map by a fresnel term (its
  fresnel map's alpha: 0 looking straight down, 0.72 at a grazing angle).
  It goes in as CE's own water (`swat`, M_CE_Water): the reflection (a cube,
  or a 2D reflection map on all six faces) along the normal rippled by its
  ripple map (bitmap 0, a normal map as CE's ripples are, in two scrolling
  layers), added into the frame, weighted from 0 straight down to 0.72 at
  the edge (flag 0 over the master's white base). Drawn as a chicago cube
  blended over the frame, Beaver Creek's creek was an unmoving glossy
  picture of its reflection map. Waterfalls (`waves`) are
  min(1, mask x A + mask x B) x C, each scrolling: CE's four-stage chain
  as (A + B) x mask x C. `tex_bump_illum_3_channel` (Backwash's blue lights)
  has a grey detail before its base, and its glow map's channels tinted by
  pixel constants 4, 6 and 7 as CE's three self-illumination colours. An
  alpha-tested template that cuts out on its bump map keeps a placeholder
  base (Backwash's canopy, color_black), taken to the bump map's size.
  `tex_detail_blend` (Sanctuary's ground, the Mombasa trees) is a base and
  two details blended by its alpha, the details' scales in vertex constants
  2 and 3; `tex_illum` and `tex_illum_bloom` (Backwash's fungus,
  Triplicate's lights) a base, a detail and a glow map; `decal_simple`
  (Street Sweeper's road stripes, Headlong's signs) its one map alpha
  blended. A template with no slot layout falls back to the shader's
  runtime diffuse map, drawn opaque, which is how these lost their details,
  glow and cut-outs.
  Halo 2 tiles each map by a u and a v scale, and many are uneven (the palm
  bark's detail and bump 2 x 12, the beach's sand 128 x 64); CE's
  environment shader takes one scale per map. The base map's tiling is in
  the UVs; a detail or bump map tiled unevenly relative to it is staged as
  a copy repeated to the ratio (`<stem>__x<nu>y<nv>.png`, at most 16 a
  side) and drawn at the smaller scale. Read as u alone, the palm's detail
  was stretched six times along the trunk.
- **Decals.** The scenario's decals (Zanzibar's 40 caution, safety and
  warning signs, the CAUTION over the beach gate) go to the placement's
  `decals` with their bitmap, radius and the bitmap's aspect.
  tools/level/gen_ce_level.py lays each as a quad on the nearest surface
  within 3 m, by true distance over every triangle whose bounds come that
  close (by centre, the flywheel room's sign missed its big wall triangle
  and went onto a slanted face, tilted and half buried), its longer side twice the
  radius, drawn with the transparent alpha master over the cooked bitmap;
  tools/level/ce_material_spec.py cooks the bitmaps with the map's. By
  layer: lit alpha blend (0, 1) as it is; multiply (3) and double multiply
  (2: bullet holes, scorches, Desolation's and Warlock's team emblems) with
  the multiply baked into an alpha-blended copy (`<stem>__mul<gain>.png`,
  as the overlays, times the bitmap's alpha); max (4) and add (5) on the
  additive master. Drawn as plain alpha, the rust decals were orange blobs
  and the emblems solid bars. Glass (`one_alpha_env`) becomes CE's glass shader: the base
  map tinted by the albedo and facing tints, blended by its alpha, unlit, and
  the environment cube map reflected through the specular mask with the
  environment tint; the cube's six faces are staged in D3D order. The
  two-layer glass (`two_alpha_env_illum`: Turf's storefront and stairwell
  doors, Triplicate's glass rails, the medical tent's panels) has the same
  slots and pixel constants, a second glass layer in slot 4, and goes in
  the same way; `two_alpha_env_detail` (the Forerunner "invisible" glass)
  has only placeholders and draws nothing. Read through the transparent
  catch-all, slot 0's reflection cube was drawn as a picture: Turf's
  stairwell door was an opaque dark sheet with nothing behind it to stop
  a player. `tex_bump_env_alpha_test_combined` cuts out on the base's
  alpha times bitmap 1's (Turf's damaged stucco: a solid door base, the
  splintered boards in `base_stucco1_damaged_01_alpha`; the chainlink
  fence keeps its holes in the base, alpha_white in slot 1).
  Change colours (`tex_bump_one_change_color`: Turf's panel trucks and
  crates) are base x lerp(1, the object's colour, bitmap 2) in the compiled
  lightmap pass; the mask goes in as CE's shader_model multipurpose alpha
  (`<stem>__mp.png`) and each prop placement carries its object's colour
  permutations (obje +0xAC) as `change_colors`, Halo 2's weights (shares:
  the truck's off-white 0.4, red 0.2, tan 0.2) summed into CE's running
  cut-offs, so tools/level/merge_ce_scene.py draws one per placement into
  the object lighting page as it does for CE scenery; a placement's own
  colours (active bits at +0x38, ARGB at +0x3C) win. Read without the mask,
  every truck drew its untinted off-white base.
  Self-illumination (`tex_bump_illum` and its kin) is a pass of its own,
  `default_self_illumination`: saturate(glow map x pass constant 1),
  added over the lit surface, not lit with it (Turf's light fixtures are
  black where they glow). The template's remapping table names the pixel
  constant (2 for tex_bump_illum, 0 for tex_bump_illum_no_specular); an
  animated parameter on descriptor 0x81 drives it instead, a periodic
  colour function going in as its wave between its darkest and brightest
  non-zero colour (the storefront signs jitter between 0.46 and 0.5). The
  environment master adds it after the fog when `SelfIllumAdd` is set. The "two
  plus two" shaders (the sky's cloud banks, the containment gas) are mask x
  layer x layer, tiled and scrolling as the shader animates them, alpha
  blended; the plasma shaders (`plasma_alpha`: Zanzibar's flywheel
  lightning, the teleporter beams, Lockout's grav lifts) draw with
  `M_H2_PlasmaAlpha` (`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_h2_materials.py`,
  `/Game/MJOLNIR/H2`, chunk 981 beside the runtime pack), the compiled
  shader as it is: noise A's blue and noise B's red, each scrolling, banded
  into a sharp ridge where they meet and twice more inside it, coloured
  between pixel constants 1 and 0 by the second band plus 3 on the
  innermost, faded by the mask's alpha, added. The staging keeps a chicago
  approximation beside it (`h2_plasma` in the shader summary; without the
  master, noise x noise x mask in the bands' mean colour drew soft clouds). All of these draw in the
  translucent mesh.
  Opaque `env` templates (the `tex_bump_env` family) reflect their cube map
  as Halo 2's lightmap pass does: the cube along the reflected eye vector,
  times a colour and a brightness each between the glancing and the facing
  value, masked by the albedo's alpha and dimmed with the light, added to
  the lit surface. The cube is whichever of the shader's bitmaps is one;
  the template's black placeholder cube reflects nothing. 22 of the 24 maps
  have such surfaces (Lockout only its grav pads; Ascension its Forerunner
  windows and panels).
- **Sky layers.** Besides the alpha and "two plus two" layers, Ascension's
  sky uses two more templates, read back from their compiled shaders: the
  cloud cover (`sky_two_alpha_clouds`: a cloud map tiled 8x and scrolling,
  times a cover mask, colour and alpha, alpha blended) and the sun shafts
  (`sky_one_add_illum_detail`: a mask's colour times its alpha, times a
  scrolling detail, tinted, added). Drawn as one map each, the cloud map
  covered the whole dome in flat grey and the shafts were white wedges.
  Additive clouds (`two_add_clouds`, `sky_two_add_clouds`: Tombstone's sky
  dome, Gemini's sky, the recharge stations' glow) are min(1, 2 x bitmap 0
  x bitmap 1), faded by pixel constant 0's alpha: CE's double multiply, or
  bitmap 0 alone where bitmap 1 is default_multiplicative (50% grey).
  The Covenant holo panels (`two_add_detail_masked`: Midship, Desolation,
  Gemini) compile to the same product of the panel map and a static map,
  plus a readout tiled 4 x through the panel's alpha; they go in as the
  clouds do, without the readout. Drawn from the static alone, they were
  solid white blocks.
  Lightning (Colossus, Triplicate) has that alpha at 0 and flashes by an
  animation the conversion doesn't carry, so it isn't drawn. The fusion
  coils' bloom (`two_add_env_illum`) is bitmap 3 tinted by pixel constant
  3, added; the storm layers and horizon gradients
  (`sky_one_alpha_env_clamped`, Colossus, Containment) take
  `one_alpha_env`'s slots. Read with the catch-all additive slots (bitmap
  1), these drew nothing or only their mask. `add_illum_detail` (Gemini's
  hologram halo: a ring map through scrolling scanlines) and
  `one_add_illum_detail` (the light volumes of Gemini, Containment and
  Waterworks) are the sun shafts' template outside the sky, drawn the same
  way; the facing colour's alpha (vertex constant 6.w: 1 on the sun shafts,
  0.15 on Gemini's white volumes) scales the tint, and `add_illum_detail`,
  whose five constants are only the maps' transforms, has no facing colour.
  Drawn from bitmap 1 alone, the halo was a solid grey ring of scanlines.
  These and the holo template fade by view angle: the vertex colour's
  alpha runs from a glancing alpha to a facing one by N.V (constants 7.w
  and 6.w; the holo template's 11.w and 10.w), so where the facing alpha is
  higher a volume seen edge-on vanishes. That goes in as CE's
  `framebuffer_fade_mode` 2 (|N.V|); without it Desolation's light shafts
  (a holo-template volume with a white mask) were solid white slabs. A
  transparent template's textures, transforms and scrolls are read the way
  halo2.dll reads them: a constant's descriptor names its texture slot
  (bits 10-12) and row (bits 5-9: 14 and 15, the 2D affine rows), the
  template's remapping table names each slot's bitmap, and an overlay's
  function is evaluated as the engine's evaluator does (identity,
  transition, periodic slide, linear with its own slope; the engine adds
  the translation, as CE's masters add their animation).
- **Sky.** The sky's lights (yaw, pitch, colour, power, diameter, whether
  the lightmaps used them), outdoor ambient and atmospheric fog go to the
  placement as halo2ue puts a CE sky's, so the level's sun, sky light and
  fog follow them. Halo 2 stores the ambient as a colour alone; it goes in
  at CE's usual power, 0.2 (at 1, Ascension's lit the player and weapons
  3.8 times too bright). Lockout's light lit nothing (its radiosity flags are
  clear; the sky model lit the lightmaps), so its sun comes from the
  lightmaps' incident directions, as for a CE map without one. Halo 2's
  atmospheric fog covers the sky as well: one at full density (Backwash's
  swamp, opaque at 20 world units) also gives the level `sky_fog`, so
  everything past the opaque distance, the black sky dome included, is the
  fog's colour (gen_ce_level.py `sky_and_weather`; Backwash's sky drew
  black above the fog).
- **Placements.** Halo 2 spawns every multiplayer pickup and vehicle through
  netgame equipment (item and vehicle collections): each becomes halo2ue's
  `netgame_equipment` or `vehicle` entry naming the collection's item.
  Netgame flags take CE's names where CE has the thing (`CtfFlag`,
  `OddballSpawn`, `HillFlag` with its hill index, `TeleportFrom`/`TeleportTo`
  paired by identifier); assault, territories and headhunter keep names the
  tag map leaves out. Halo 2 spawns by influence, so its player starts carry
  no CTF side (Lockout's are all team 0); each start takes the side of the
  nearer CTF flag spawn, so a CTF game has red and blue spawns. A start
  (0x34 bytes) lists four game types at `0x14` (CE's numbers, plus 6
  Headhunter, 7 Juggernaut and 8 Territories) and a spawn type for each at
  `0x1C` (0 both, 1 initial spawn only, 2 respawn only), staged as
  `game_types` and `spawn_types`. A start that lists no game type serves
  every one: Containment, Relic, Sanctuary and Warlock list none on any
  start, and Terminal's 88 untyped starts stand beside 61 All games ones.
  The level generator places them by game type ([ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md),
  "Spawn sets"); spawn types are not used yet. Props are
  scenery and crates (`bloc`), staged with their
  render and collision models. A prop with no collision model collides in
  Halo 2 by its physics model's solid shapes alone (the boxes, polyhedra
  and pills whose material is not a phantom's): Burial Mounds' and
  Elongation's and Gemini's invisible boxes, Zanzibar's beach bushes. The
  stage writes those as its collision (`crate::h2::phantom::solid_triangles`,
  each shape's planes closed into a triangle mesh; a pill as the box round
  it). The surfaces are in the built level (Elongation gains 96), but
  no difference has been shown in play: dropped on Elongation's first box
  a player lands on a real surface 0.2 world units above its top, with or
  without it. A prop with both keeps its
  collision model, which is what projectiles hit in Halo 2. Game-type props
  (the CTF and territory flag bases) are left out: the level's own CTF
  stands replace them.
- **Planar fog.** A BSP's fog plane (Ascension's cloud deck, Lockout's
  haze below the map, the water of Dune, Needle and Zanzibar) goes to
  `fog.json` as `ce_fog.py` writes a CE map's, so the masters fog what lies
  below the plane by its depth under it and its distance, as CE's planar
  fog does. Halo 2 draws planar fog per surface only (every opaque
  template's `fog_planar` pass; no fog-plane mesh, no full-screen pass), so
  that is all there is to it. The cloud sea MCC shows under Ascension's
  island, wisps drifting through it, is not fog: it is a transparent cloud
  plane in the BSP 12.6 wu under the fog plane (`ascension_clouds`, a
  `two_alpha_clouds` shader), a static disk of cloud puffs times a cloud
  tile scrolled over it, drawn unfogged over the sky's lower half. Drawn as
  one static grey map, it was the flat pale plane the rocks stood in.
  Halo 2's transparent templates other than glass have no fog in their
  compiled shaders, so they go in `fogged: false` and the material spec
  leaves their fog out. Where the view passes below the plane and finds no
  surface, MCC draws the fog's colour (its fog pass lays a depth copy for
  the engine's full-screen fog shaders): the rocks' fogged lower ends vanish
  into it, where ours stood out against the sky's dark lower edge. A level
  plane gets that as the loader's height fog at the plane, in the fog's
  colour, starting 1.5 km out past the cloud plane
  (`gen_ce_level.h2_fog_fill`, `environment.haze`). The plane names its fog through the scenario's
  planar fog palette; Beaver Creek's names an entry the scenario does not
  have and gets none.
- **Machines.** A gear whose device animation turns its one node about one
  fixed axis is placed like scenery, with its turn: the axis and the keys
  of its `device:position` animation as (seconds, degrees) over its
  position transition time, read by `crate::h2::animation` (the keyframe
  codecs 4-7, and codec 3, which stores every frame). That covers
  Ascension's three antennas (the big arms that swing around the central
  pillar every 40 s, about +Z), Zanzibar's big wheel, its blades and three
  flywheels (+Y; two flywheels are placed tilted) and Foundation's two fans.
  `merge_ce_scene.py --machines` writes each such placement as a mesh of
  its own (`scene_machine_<k>.gltf`, built as `SM_<code>_Machine<k>`; its
  transparent parts, such as the flywheels' lightning, as
  `scene_machine_<k>t.gltf`, since a rewritten mesh enters the translucency
  pass by its slot 0) with its pivot, keys and, when the axis is not the
  world's +Z, the axis in
  Unreal's axes beside it (`.motion.json`); the level's decor entry carries
  them as `motion`, and MJOLNIRLevelLoader turns the actor about the pivot.
  Every other machine's motion (doors, lifts, Triplicate's train, Backwash's
  monitor) is left out as before, listed in staging's notes: still, a
  closed gate or a parked train would block a way Halo 2 opens. A lift's
  push does not need its motion; see the next item.
- **Lifts, jump pads and vents.** Halo 2 pushes through physics model
  phantoms (`crate::h2::phantom`): shapes nothing collides with, each with a
  phantom type (accelerations and top speeds along a render model marker's
  forward, towards its axis and towards its point, and whether it holds off
  gravity). The stage writes every placed object's phantoms that push
  players to placement.json `lifts` (object space, whether or not the prop
  is drawn), `gen_ce_level.py` puts them in the level file in Unreal space
  (`lifts`: planes or a pill, a bounding sphere, the marker, the pushes in
  cm). MJOLNIRLevelLoader's `lifts.lua` hands them, in the simulation's
  units, to MJOLNIRLobby's DLL once a map, and the DLL sets the velocity of
  a player inside one through `(object_set_velocity (player_get N) ...)` on
  every simulation tick (`native/lobby/lifts_runtime.h`,
  [re/lift_push.md](re/lift_push.md)).
  Each game pushes its own players only: a joiner's motion is its own game's,
  and a push the host sends a joiner's unit does nothing (two PCs,
  2026-10-25). Maps with player lifts: Lockout, Midship, Cyclotron (Ivory
  Tower), Colossus, Coagulation, Headlong, High Plains (Tombstone, hvac),
  Backwash, Foundation, Warlock, Derelict (Desolation), Dune (Relic,
  watchtowers), Ascension and Gemini (jump pads).
  `lifts` is a key only the loader reads, so a published pack gets them
  without a rebake: `tools/level/add_lifts.py` stages the map, adds the block
  to the pack's level file and packs the next version, and checks nothing
  else changed (the bots stay as baked). Those 14 maps shipped this way at
  1.3.0 on 2026-11-04, with the gaps in testing listed in
  `docs/h2_lifts_release.md`. The other 11 maps have no phantom that pushes
  players and stay at 1.2.0.
- **Moving collision.** The simulation does all collision, never reads
  Unreal geometry, and its structure BSP cannot move: an arm's collision
  baked at rest stood where the arm only sometimes is. Rewriting a live
  object's transform moves the object but not its Havok body; a device
  machine moves its collision with its animation. So each turning part
  becomes a machine of the simulation's own (`tools/level/h2_machines.py`,
  run by `convert_ce_map.sh`), five tags cloned from B40's elevator, whose
  nodes and Havok layouts agree, each a container
  `pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-<k><g>` under `objects\mjolnir\<code>\`:
  - an animation graph whose one resource member turns the root by the
    part's keys, every frame with codec 3 (the shipped turning props' own;
    its header is Halo 2's), beside the static pose, node flags, an
    uncompressed copy and object-space frames the resource carries;
  - a collision model holding the part's own Halo 2 collision BSP, which
    staging writes as `collision/<part>.bsp.json` and `mjolnir level
    machine-collision` packs with its Havok MOPP. Bipeds meet a machine's
    collision model, not its physics model's shapes: a player dropped on an
    arm built of physics boxes alone fell through it;
  - a physics model of boxes over the part's triangles, for what moves
    through Havok (the elevator's lift phantom goes with it);
  - a model, and a gear machine whose "position transition time" is the
    rate 1 / period (the engine reads it as a rate: 40 ran the antennas 40
    times a second, aliased into a seven-second wobble). The engine shows a
    gear at frame position x N, held at the last frame (Halo 2 used N - 1),
    so frame f is the angle at f / N of the turn, one every 0.1 s: with
    Halo 2's five frames Zanzibar's wheel turned a full circle in 24 s of
    its 30 and stood still for 6.

  The generator places each machine where its part is, with its full
  rotation (`blam.objects`, group `machines`), and gives the part's mesh
  `motion.follow`; the merge leaves the part's collision out of the BSP
  (`merge_ce_collision.py --sim-machines`). The machine draws through the
  elevator's Blueprint, whose turning part follows the root; the loader
  hides that part's mesh, attaches the Halo 2 mesh to it, and fits the
  turn's phase (the simulation starts its gears about 25 s off the world
  clock) for the sounds. Checked on Ascension: a player dropped on an arm
  stands on it and is carried round as it turns.
- **Props that move and break.** A crate (`bloc`) whose physics model has
  a rigid body that is neither keyframed nor fixed moves in Halo 2; one
  with constraints (Zanzibar's hanging lights, crane, awnings) is held and
  stays still. `crate::h2::props` reads it from the tags and the stage
  writes it onto the placement: `h2_physics` (mass, motion type, bodies,
  constraints), `h2_damage` (the model's damage info, 0x60: vitality and
  every instant response with its effect, damage effect, and the sounds
  and decals the effect references, the sounds staged as one-shots) and
  `h2_functions`. `tools/level/h2_physics_props.py` turns every movable
  type into crate tags (a physics shape of the model's box, mass from
  Halo 2's, and a death response when Halo 2's kills it: the fusion coil's
  15 vitality), takes the props out of the merged meshes and builds their
  meshes; the level loader (props.lua) dresses each crate as the prop placed
  nearest where it first appears, so every type shares one crate actor
  class. Zanzibar: 11 types over 55 placements. A dying prop plays our
  fuel-rod explosion and fire, a plasma scorch and Halo 2's own death sound
  (`sound\visual_effects\fusion_coil_destroyed`, 13 variants; this game's
  Wwise events cannot be posted from a mod), and stays, burnt. A coil's
  core (`tex_bump_plasma_one_channel_illum`) is a one-channel mask lit by a
  colour running from its damaged pink-red (pixel constant 3) to its
  healthy orange with the object's `health` function; read as a picture
  its green channel drew the coils green. A prop's `overlay` stencil (the
  crates' MKT1 EMERGENCY FOOD) is drawn as masked paint on the prop: the
  level's darkening copy loses text that brightens. A door (machine type 1:
  Zanzibar's house gate) opens from its control (the keypad, staged as a
  `ctrl` placement; the two share position group 0). `crate::h2::door`
  reads its render model's nodes (0x48, 0x60 each: parent 0x04, default
  translation 0x0C, rotation 0x18) and decodes `device:position` for every
  node: keyframe codec 6, four turning and ten sliding nodes named by the
  three node bit fields that end the frame data, their frame info in node
  order (read last node first the gate's doors stayed shut while its bars
  slid across), sliding keys offsets added to the default translation.
  A vertex's node is its rigid-boned vertex's index byte through the
  section's node map (resource locator 0x68), staged as `_NODE`.
  h2_physics_props.py splits the door into a mesh a node (doors.json). The
  simulation opens it and Unreal moves it: every node with a collision BSP
  (staged `h2_door.collision`, one BSP a node; the gate's 14, its frame and
  four ramps among them) becomes a device machine with tags of its own
  (h2_door_machines.py: animation, collision, physics, model and machine,
  written into the layout of B40's elevator family). Its root follows the
  node exactly, turning and sliding at once (`h2_machines.pose_resource`:
  codec 3 with the root's rotation and translation both animated, so a
  ramp swinging about its hinge is one machine); its collision is the
  node's own BSP, its physics boxes cover the BSP's triangles. Each machine
  stands on a grid about the door's origin, 0.05 wu (15 cm) apart, every
  machine of a map on a cell of its own.

  **Each placed machine draws its own part.** Its machine tag (one a
  placement; the animation, collision, physics and model tags are shared)
  names an actor of its own (`--asset-reference`): B40's elevator
  Blueprint cloned by `write_actors` (crates/ue-asset/examples/
  vehicle_actor.rs, which renames the package, its generated class and
  default object) into `/Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/Machines/
  BP_<CODE>_Machine<n>`, all in `pakchunk987-MJOLNIRACT-<CODE>_P`. The
  Blueprint's mesh list (BlamMeshSynchronizationComponent `RuntimeRegions
  {default}.Permutations{default}.StaticMeshes`, which held the elevator
  floor on bone `platform`) names the node's part meshes instead, each on
  bone `Root` (the simulation's root node, bones `elevator_world`, `Root`,
  `Platform`) at its rest offset from the actor, turned by the placement's
  yaw. So Unreal draws and moves the part with no elevator to hide and no
  script attaching anything; the part meshes are not spawned as decor (the
  level's `doors` parts carry their mesh and materials instead). The loader
  (doors.lua) only finds each machine's actor by its class (one scan of the
  Blam object actors); it hides the keypad's switch panel's components (the
  actor's own hidden flag is reset by the game) and watches one machine at
  4 Hz (10 Hz while moving) only for Halo 2's sounds.

  The parts' materials are cooked, as the custom vehicles' are
  (machine_instances.py): when the map's cook runs, build_terrain_meshes.py
  gives each part mesh real slots (`mesh_rewrite --asset-imports`) naming a
  material instance per slot, `<root>/MachineMaterials/MI_<mesh>_n<slot>`,
  of the slot's prop_lit material; ce_vehicle_instances_editor.py makes them
  after build_ce_level.py and the cook ships them in the map's chunk, and
  `machine_instances.py check` reads every one back (in the chunk, no static
  permutation, its textures cooked beside it). The level's parts then carry
  no materials, so nothing is dressed at spawn. The Blueprint's own
  `MaterialOverrides` cannot do it: they match slots by name, and a mesh
  rewritten from the engine's cube keeps the cube's one slot
  (`WorldGridMaterial`) unless `--asset-imports` writes its own. Without a
  cook (CE_COOK=0), and on a level built before this, the loader dresses the
  parts once a world, as before.

  An upgraded map (upgrade_ce_map.py) does the same from its own stages.
  `h2_physics_props.py --instance-root /Game/MJOLNIR/MachineParts/<landscape>`
  builds the turning parts and the door parts naming instances in that
  folder and lists them in `<scene>/machine_instances.json`. The editor
  stage finishes each entry as assemble finished a part the loader dressed
  (the redrawn textures, `detail_fill`: `machine_parts_plan`, the same two
  helpers) and makes the instances after the landscape world, under a label
  of the folder's own (`PAL_MJOLNIR_<landscape>Parts`, the landscape's chunk,
  not recursive: the landscape's own labels are, and would take the masters
  into the chunk). The cook stage runs `machine_instances.py check` on the
  chunk (the conversion's cook container named for the textures it carries),
  and assemble leaves those gears without materials. Zanzibar: 21 slots,
  each equal to what the loader set before, checked entry by entry; in
  game all 21 draw `MI_ZAN_*` instances, in a second match on the map too.

  The cook stage also refreshes the map's own cook container
  (`refresh_map_cook`): textures imported into the map's folder after its
  conversion cooked (the door parts' and the props' stencils, by
  h2_physics_props.py) are in this cook's chunk, not in the conversion's
  container the install took, and Zanzibar's gate had drawn textured only
  beside a test container installed by hand. When the staged chunk holds
  everything the conversion's does and more, a copy in the work folder
  becomes the map's `MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>`. Run the stages with `HCE_PAKS`,
  `MJOLNIR` and `EXAMPLES` set (release builds): the bake's defaults are
  the debug examples, which may be older than the level schema.

  The map's own tag containers (its machines and control, their actors,
  the gears' and the movable props' crate tags) are one list,
  machine_containers.py, read by the install stage and by both pack tools
  (pack_local_map.py, pack_remastered.py), so a pack carries what the
  tested install did. The tags go in the pack folder's `machines/`, named
  `-MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-...` (a prop's `-MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-PROP-<leaf>-<g>`),
  where `mjolnir map pack` takes a map's tags from; the actors' containers
  end `-<CODE>_P` beside the map's own. Before this the packs carried none
  of them and the props' tags were in the game only as local builds
  installed by hand. Zanzibar: 123 containers, every one in a test pack
  (not signed, not published), and the map played from the pipeline's
  install alone with its 14 gate machines, 8 gears and 55 props. Two
  copies of the game (tools/remote/instances.mjs) agreed: every slot cooked
  and every prop present in both, and the gate opened by the host stood
  open in the client's own simulation and its own view.

  A placement's own flags go with it (scenario machine +0x38 device flags,
  +0x3C machine flags; the simulation's bits are Halo 2's). Containment's
  base gates are door-type machines (type 0) with no activation radius, so
  the simulation's door logic opens one for any unit within its bounding
  radius and shuts it after its open time. Halo 2 places them with
  machine flag 1, "does not operate automatically", so only their
  switches move them. Without that flag they stood open (2026-11-15).
  Zanzibar's gate parts are platforms (type 1), placed with no flags.
  Before, the fields were whatever B40 placement each map cloned (the one
  nearest its origin), and some of those are "initially open", "position
  reversed" or "does not close automatically". Of the Halo 2 machines,
  only Containment's carry a flag (`h2_machine_placements <map>` lists
  them); Gemini's, Triplicate's, Colossus's and Backwash's doors carry
  none and open for a unit nearby, as in Halo 2.
  Dressing state belongs to the world: a
  second match on the same map has the same world name and new actors, and
  parts kept from the first came back as bare grid (fixed 2026-11-15).

  The keypad gets B40's switch panel; machines and switch share one device
  group (`zan_group0`, Halo 2's position group 0, baked into the
  scenario), so a player pressing the keypad opens the gate, collision and
  all, for everyone in the match. The install stage installs every
  machine's containers (machine_containers.py).
  `device_group_set none zan_group0 1` opens it from the console.

  **Every machine that moves in parts is staged the same way**, whatever
  its type. Staging tries a one-node gear first (`gear_turn`); any other
  machine whose `device:position` decodes (keyframe codecs 4-7, and codec
  3, which stores every frame) is staged as `h2_door` with its own
  behaviour (`machine`: type 0x11C, flags 0x11E, door open time 0x120,
  automatic activation radius 0x118). A machine with no animation never
  moves and is staged as scenery with its collision (Dune's watchtowers).
  `h2_machine_census <maps>` lists every machine and whether it decodes. In
  MCC that is Containment's base gates, shields and switches, Gemini's High
  Charity doors and gravity columns, Triplicate's garage gates and train,
  Cyclotron's elevator, Waterworks' crusher, Backwash's monitor and Dune's
  collapsing teleporters; all seven maps build their machines
  (h2_door_machines.py). The rules, from the tags:
  - one machine a collision BSP, and one a node that moves without
    collision (no collision or physics model: Dune's teleporter legs);
  - the machine tag's type is Halo 2's: a door (0) opens by itself within
    its activation radius (proven on Zanzibar with Triplicate's garage
    gate: a Ghost parked inside its 5 wu opened it, as Halo 2 does), a gear
    (2) runs round by itself (Triplicate's train: all six parts' positions
    agree, 0.732 then 0.936 three seconds later), a platform (1) goes where
    its device group sends it;
  - a placement's machines stand on a 15 cm grid about its origin, so a
    door's parts measure its radius from nearly one point, every machine of
    the map on a cell of its own (Triplicate's train and its deathball are
    placed 3 cm apart; on shared cells the loader bound one actor twice and
    an elevator mesh rode the train's nose). The loader claims each actor
    once, nearest first;
  - a machine tag is built once and placed per placement (Triplicate's
    three garage gates);
  - Halo 2's position group number is the device group
    (`<code>_group<n>`), shared by every machine and control of that number
    (Containment's gate and its switch), each control placed once.

  A fresh conversion (`convert_ce_map.sh`) does the same as the upgrade
  pipeline: after `level collision`, `h2_door_machines.py <staging> <CODE>
  <out>/machines --transform <name>.sbsp.transform.json` builds every
  placement's machines (positions moved with the map) and writes
  `doors.json`; `merge_ce_scene.py --doors` takes the machines out of the
  static scene as a mesh a node (`scene_machine_d<k>n<node>.gltf` with a
  `.door.json` naming its staging entry and node, which
  build_terrain_meshes.py turns into a decor id); `gen_ce_level.py --doors`
  adds the machines, controls and device groups to the scenario and the
  level's `doors` for the loader (`level bake` keeps `doors` as opaque, as
  it keeps `lifts`). The machine containers sit with h2_machines.py's in
  `<out>/machines` and install with them. Triplicate (TRI, 2026-11-15):
  seven placements, 20 machines, 18 part meshes, all bound and attached;
  a garage gate rolled up when the player was teleported into its 5 wu
  radius. Halo 1 conversions (Chill Out) and Halo 2 maps without such
  machines (Lockout) merge byte-identically. The published Containment,
  Gemini, Waterworks, Backwash and Foundation will gain their machines the
  next time they are converted.

  A moving part is lit by Unreal (prop_lit.py's M_CE_PropLit, both
  pipelines): lit by the light baked where it was placed, Triplicate's
  trains, parked in a dark tunnel, drew black through the station. The
  trains themselves run as the tag says: a 15 s loop, moving for about 5 s,
  427 m at up to about 107 m/s. (A reading that looked frozen was the
  train parked at the end of its run for the other two thirds of the loop.)

  The game hides the actors of machines the player cannot see
  (`bHidden`, the skeleton not rendered) and gives them no pose until the
  player can; then it poses them at once where the simulation has them
  (Zanzibar, 2026-11-15: all fourteen gate machines hidden with the player
  at spawn, the gate opened, nothing moved; the player teleported to the
  gate, all fourteen shown and every part open). FlyCam does not count as
  the player's view: a part that stands still in a FlyCam shot while the
  player is elsewhere is this culling, not a fault. Judge machines from
  the player's own view. (This explains every "stuck" ramp, bar and
  "frozen" train reading earlier that day; un-hiding an actor by hand does
  not pose it, the game's own visibility does.) It is distance culling, as
  for every Blam object, judged by the object's bounding radius: with the
  player 20 wu from the gate none of its machines hid, at 35 wu 11 of 14,
  from 45 wu all. Since the parts are the actors' own meshes now, a culled
  part is not drawn, as a culled crate or weapon is not; Halo 2 culls the
  gate as one object (bounding radius 2.56 wu, object +0x04, offset +0x08),
  so every machine of a placement takes the placement's largest reach as
  its radius and the parts go and come together. Gears (h2_machines.py)
  were never hidden within 75 m of the player.

  Two copies on PC 1 (tools/remote/instances.mjs up 2, one simulation):
  each found and dressed all fourteen actors; the gate opened from the
  host's console showed open on the client; each copy culls by its own
  player, and each showed every part open once its player was at the gate.
  Opaque shaders that scroll their base map are staged as `base_scroll`
  (Zanzibar's rotating_metal, the drum under the spindle grates: one repeat
  in u every 2 s); the `h2_staging` map setting applies it to the level's
  slots as CE's environment scroll (BaseUAnim).
  Turning machines are lit by Unreal (their object page drew black, and a
  black flywheel turning read as one standing still); one riding a
  simulation machine whose Unreal part stops updating (the big wheel and
  blades: the simulation's position advances, the game stops copying its
  pose) leaves the part after 2 s and turns by the clock.
- **Teleporters.** Halo 2's teleporter scenery (Ascension's
  `2way_teleporter` bases) is placed like any other prop: the generator's
  working pads on the teleporter flags draw nothing. Its beam is a
  `plasma_alpha` shader, its glow a `one_add_illum` (the base map times
  pixel constant 0, added). The bases have no collision model.
- **Sound.** Halo 2's samples are not in the maps but in headerless
  `sounds_*.dat` files beside them (Opus and Xbox ADPCM;
  `docs/h2_cache_format.md`, "Sound"). `crate::h2::sound` stages them as
  `ce_sounds.py` stages a CE map's, `staging/sounds_out` (`sounds.json` and
  its files), which `convert_ce_map.sh` imports with `build_ce_sounds.py`
  and the generator plays: the BSP clusters' background loops (2D), the
  sound scenery and the loops placed objects carry (3D, at the object's
  origin), and the one-shots a turning machine's animation raises
  (Ascension's 12 antenna cues, at their frames). Opus packets go into an
  Ogg Opus file as they are, which the editor imports (Ascension's
  `antenna1` came in at its tag's 2.240 s); ADPCM is decoded to WAV. A
  sound's playback gain (dB) and random pitch bounds (cents) become the
  entry's `gain` and `pitch` (Ascension's humming light plays 5 semitones
  down); a loop's distance bounds come from its `lsnd` (most loop samples
  carry none) unless the sound scenery overrides them. Halo 2 adds its
  sound class's gain to the sound's own (halo2.dll 0x6e5bd0: the class's
  upper gain bound and the sound's scale bound at scale 1; -7 dB for the
  ambient classes, -11 dB for machinery), so the entry's `gain` carries
  it. The class also caps how many of one sound play at once ("max sounds
  per tag", 4 for these classes), which becomes the emitter's `max`: the
  loader gives each such sound a concurrency group that keeps the nearest
  playing (Elongation places its belt hum 100 times with two tracks; all
  200 played, at the tag's gain, with every cluster's background on top).
  A background loop belongs to BSP clusters: `zones` are the clusters'
  bounds with the set of loops each plays, and the loader fades to the set
  of the box the camera is in or nearest to, the smallest when boxes
  overlap (the clusters themselves are not boxes). An attachment scaled
  by an object function (the jump pads' launch loop, `phantom_power`) is
  left out: it sounds only while the object drives it.
- **Lightmaps.** Halo 2 keeps its pages at half their light and doubles
  them in the shader; the CE masters take a page as it is, so the pages are
  staged doubled (clamped). Without that Lockout's interiors were nearly
  black. Its 65 small pages would each bake at 2,048 under lightmap_bake's
  default 16x, so Halo 2 maps bake at most 4x (`BAKE_ARGS` default).
- **Render models** (the sky, props) store positions and texture
  coordinates in -1..1 across the model's compression bounds; read raw,
  Lockout's sky was a 3 m knot at the origin and drew nothing.
- **Weapons the game lacks** take the nearest role (`defs/level/h2-tag-map.json`):
  the battle rifle the assault rifle, the brute shot the fuel rod gun, the
  carbine, brute plasma rifle and sentinel beam the plasma rifle.

## Specular

A Halo 2 template's postprocess definition (stem +0x58) lists its passes,
each pass's implementations and what each implementation feeds its shaders
(`specular_constants` in render.rs reads it; the example
`h2_template_blocks` prints it). Most opaque templates draw
`default_light_combined_tangentspace_specular_sphere`. Its vertex shader
passes vertex registers 10 and 11, fed from two of the shader's vertex
constants, to the pixel shader, which adds sat(R.L)^8 x the light x
lerp(register 11, register 10, sat(N.L)) through the frame's alpha (R the
view reflected about the bumped normal, L the light's direction). The
template's lightmap pass wrote that alpha first:

- min(1, 2 x base alpha x the light) for `lightmap_tex_detail` and nearly
  every other lightmap pass (`tex`, the detail blends, two and three detail,
  illum, shiny, tiling, change colour, honor guard), so the base map's alpha
  is a specular mask;
- 0 for the env passes, `detail_overlay` and `detail_no_specular`: those
  surfaces never shine, whatever their passes;
- the cut-out or other terms for the alpha-tested passes. Only
  `alpha_test_no_bump`'s (the cut-out, which is the base alpha) matches
  what staging writes; the others are left without.

That is CE's lightmap specular (`SpecLightmap`: the lobe from the
lightmap's incident direction, masked by the base map's alpha), its colour
going from parallel to perpendicular by N.V rather than N.L: perpendicular
takes register 10's constant, parallel register 11's. A template that cuts
out on another map's alpha has the cut staged in the base's alpha, so it
would shine all over; it gets none. Nor does a base map with no authored
mask (alpha 1 everywhere): 157 of 552 specular shaders on the 25 maps,
Coagulation's cliffs, Turf's stucco garage doors, Backwash's tree trunks,
shone all over like plastic where Halo 2's surfaces read flat; the shaders
with an authored mask (Turf's brushed door frames) keep it. Turf's door frames and posts
(`metal_grey_dark` on `matte_grey`, brushed streaks in the alpha: vertex
constants 7 and 8, 1.0 and 0.75 grey) drew flat grey without it. Placed objects (lit from the object lighting
page) are left without: they have no incident direction per texel, so a
flat face took one and saturated white (Turf's dumpster). 25
templates take it, 61% of the multiplayer maps' triangles
(docs/h2_shader_census.md).

## Decorators

Halo 2 scatters grass, rocks, debris, litter and decals from its scenario's
decorator sets (`DECR`) over each structure BSP (`crates/blam-cache/src/h2/decorator.rs`;
the example `h2_decorators` prints a map's). The BSP's decorators block
(+0x234) is an octree of 8-unit cells around a centre (cells per side x 8
units across); each leaf names groups, and a group a run of placements in a
raw cache block, six words each. MCC's `halo2.dll` decodes them (0x979eeb;
no tag carries the finished geometry, so the decode was read from there):

- position: the leaf cell's corner + (bits 0-9 x 8/1023, bits 10-19 x
  8/1023, bits 20-31 x 8/4095) world units;
- internal word: bits 0-2 the class, 3-8 the permutation, 9-12 the yaw
  (v/15 of a turn), 13-15 the tint blend, 16-19 the scale (v/15 across the
  permutation's range), 20-31 an up vector the "align to normal"
  permutations turn to: the yaw then turns from Halo 2's own perpendicular
  to it (0x6fcf30: the smallest component zeroed, the other two swapped,
  one negated), and any other perpendicular turns every aligned piece by a
  fixed angle (Turf's cans lay 180 degrees round);
- tint and lightmap colours, two light directions.

On Zanzibar, Turf and Beaver Creek the decoded placements lie on the BSP's
surface (median 0.1 units). The 20 maps with decorators hold 38,600:
31,000 models, 6,300 floating decals and 1,300 camera-facing sprites
(Zanzibar's, all). A group's own type byte disagrees with its class's on
Turf, so the class's (`DECR` class +0x04) decides.

DXT1 bitmaps decode with their one-bit alpha (a three-colour block's
index 3 is transparent black, as D3D samples it). Read opaque, the debris
atlas drew each piece in a black box where Halo 2 cuts it out; elsewhere
one to five textures a map gain transparent texels (Coagulation's light
bands, Ascension's light strips, Zanzibar's hazard strips).

Model decorators are staged as scenery: each set's model
(`models/<set>__decorator<k>.gltf`, its run of the set's indices, double
sided, `decorator_tex` cut out on its base map's alpha), one placement entry
each with its rotation as `basis` (forward, left, up) and `scale`, which
merge_ce_scene.py places like any object, and its `light`.

Every decorator is lit and coloured as Halo 2 colours its vertices
(`halo2.dll` 0x7fa1d0): the permutation's tint 1 to tint 2 by the
placement's blend, times the placement's tint by the base map tint
percentage; times its light, the placement's lightmap colour by the
lightmap tint percentage, grey (0.5) for the rest. The decorator pixel
shaders draw 2 x texture x that colour. A model's entry carries the doubled
product as `light`; a decal's or sprite's vertices already hold the product
(their stored colour equals it on Turf and Coagulation to 8-bit rounding),
doubled into the mesh's `_LIGHT`. merge_ce_scene.py lights each from that
in place of the ground under it: one object page block a distinct colour
(in 32nds), the incident direction along the normal so it draws flat, as
Halo 2's does.

Decal decorators need no decode: the map stores them as geometry. Each
cache block carries decal vertices (locator 0x08: 0x20 each, position,
texture coordinate, a second coordinate, colour) and indices (0x10), 4
vertices and 6 indices a placement over its group's run (+0x0C vertex
start and count, +0x10 index start and count); `halo2.dll` draws them as
they are (0x9795c0). Their coordinates already point into the decal
bitmap's atlas. `decorator::decals` reads them; staging writes one mesh a
group and shader (`models/<set>__decals<group>_<shader>.gltf`, at the
quads' centre): `decorator_decal_paint` alpha blended,
`decorator_decal_paint_multiply` (stains, blast scorches) multiplying the
frame by the map where its alpha covers, baked into an alpha blend as the
overlay's is. Turf's 322 (posters, rubble, stains) draw in game. A group's
own type byte calls Turf's posters and rubble models; their class and
their decal vertices say decals.

The axis-rotating sprites (grass: Coagulation's 14,362, Relic's, Beaver
Creek's, Containment's) are stored the same way, in the block's sprite
vertices (locator 0x48: 0x30 each, base position, the corner's offset
across and along the axis, the axis, texture coordinate, colour) and
sprite indices (0x50), 4 and 6 a placement. Halo 2 turns each about its
axis to face the camera, and so does ours: each comes out as one card in
its rest pose (across Halo 2's perpendicular to the axis turned by the
placement's yaw) on `M_H2_Billboard`
(unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_h2_materials.py, chunk 981), the
masked two-sided environment master with a World Position Offset that
turns it. The vertex normal is the axis (the card draws flat lit, so it
needs no face normal), and two extra UV channels carry, in Unreal
centimetres, the way from the vertex to its base point on the axis
(TEXCOORD_2 x, y and TEXCOORD_3 x) and its offset across (TEXCOORD_3 y):
`_BILLBOARD` in the staged mesh, converted by merge_ce_scene.py, written by
mesh_rewrite as channels 2 and 3 when a mesh has them. A runtime pack
without the master draws the cards unturned (the level loader falls back
to `M_CE_EnvironmentMaskedTwoSided`). A group
draws from the sprite buffer when its block has one and its type says
quad, or it has no decal buffer. Zanzibar's "screen-facing quads" (group
type 3) are `foliage_earth` models by their class, and are placed as models.

merge_ce_scene.py merges every decorator primitive of a material into
one: each glTF primitive becomes a section of the terrain mesh, drawn in
every pass, and Coagulation's 2,639 pieces as their own sections drew
14,808 draws a frame (1,623 merged). Measured on PC 1 (RTX 5090, 3840x2160,
Epic, `mjolnir_bench` at a held view over the grass, 2026-11-11):
Coagulation without decorators 9.21 ms (GPU 6.53); with them as sections
10.34 ms; merged 9.63 to 9.84 ms (GPU 7.02), so the decorators cost about
0.5 ms, on the GPU. Their World Position Offset costs nothing measurable
(off: same frame, GPU -0.2 ms). All three were benched in sessions in PC 1's
slower state (the game thread on its V-Cache cores, by the 9 ms baseline;
docs/performance.md, "Reading the numbers"); a control in the faster state
read 7.80 ms.

## Breakable glass

Halo 2's glass (Turf's stairwell doors) is solid until shot, meleed or hit
hard, then breaks and lets players through, as in Halo 2.

- **Collision.** `mjolnir level collision` (Halo 2 sources only) makes the
  glass breakable surfaces of the sim's own kind
  (`blam_sbsp::convert::rebuild_breakable`): each polygon is a pane (its
  front and back), each connected sheet a set, closed at its edges so the
  sim's flood fill never reads a missing surface. `brittle_glass` takes the
  `brittle_glass_reinforced` material: plain `globals\glass` breaks at any
  touch, so walking into it broke it.
- **Drawing.** The sheets go beside the BSP (`<map>.sbsp.breakables.json`,
  world units); `tools/level/split_breakable_glass.py` moves each sheet's
  transparent triangles into mesh slots of their own, and the level entry
  lists them (`breakables`: sheet, box in cm, slots). The level loader
  hooks the game's break effect (`BP_BaseBreakableSurfaceEffect_C:Spawn`,
  which names the point it broke at): the sheet there loses its slots
  (`M_CE_Hidden`) and throws glass chips (`NS_Impact_Glass_Lrg` without its crack decal, over a 3 x 3
  grid). A sheet stays broken until the map loads again.
- Not done: the break's sound (the game's `HaloAudioSound` has no script
  call to play it), and glass in the structure BSP itself (the world shell's
  packing drops the breakable bit; Turf's is all instanced geometry).

## How the open items were closed

- A prop's collision on a child node (Zanzibar's crane and hinged lights,
  Derelict's trees) is placed by the render model's rest pose; a scaled
  placement (Zanzibar's bushes at 2x to 4x) gets a copy of the model and
  collision with the scale baked in (`<name>_x2__scen.gltf`).
- Every instance's incident light direction, and the light of vertex-lit
  instanced geometry (Lockout's 26 light fixtures), come from Halo 2's
  lightmap vertex buckets. A vertex-lit instance draws its vertices' mean
  light from a texel of its own on a page after the last (the CE masters
  sample light through lightmap coordinates, so per-vertex colour has no
  slot); the incident direction still varies per vertex.
- Cube maps and the scrolling shader animations (cloud banks, gas, grav
  lifts) are converted; see Shaders above.

## Not yet done

- Only BSP 0 is converted (every multiplayer map has one).
- Placed object models take each region's first permutation at its most
  detailed level.
- Specular's colour blends by the view (N.V) where Halo 2's blends by the
  light (N.L), and alpha-tested templates other than `tex_alpha_test` have
  none (see Specular).
- The sun shafts' fade towards edge-on (the vertex colour going from the
  facing colour to black as (N.V)^2) has no CE chicago equivalent; they draw
  at their facing colour.
- An env reflection's colour is one hue (the mean of the facing and
  glancing colours) baked into a copy of the cube, and its facing-to-glancing
  blend uses CE's squared view term rather than Halo 2's linear one.
- `plasma_alpha`'s fade comes from its vertex shader
  (`transparent_generic_reflection`), not read back: M_H2_PlasmaAlpha takes
  it as the facing term |N.V|, weighted by pixel constant 2's alpha as the
  pixel shader weights it. The level needs chunk 981
  (`pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2-Windows`) installed: without it the level
  loader finds no parent for the plasma's slots ("parent material not
  found").
- The loops' detail sounds (Ascension's thunder and wind gusts, at random
  periods and directions) are staged in `sounds.json` but not played; a
  loop attached to a marker plays at the object's origin.
- On maps other than Lockout, CTF sides and vehicle teams come from the
  nearer CTF flag and vehicle game types from Halo 2's; Lockout and
  Ascension have been started, Ascension only by a test camera.
- Install the way a local test map is installed (`level bake --install-test`
  and the map's 985/986 containers): `--install` also copies this project's
  material cook over chunk 988, which on a box with the hub's runtime
  replaces the runtime's masters.
- All 24 multiplayer maps stage; Lockout, Ascension and Zanzibar have been
  converted end to end and started.

## Remasters

A converted Halo 2 map goes through the same pipeline as the CE remasters
(`tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py`, configured in
`tools/level/ce_upgrade_maps.json`). Coagulation (`COA`) is the first, built
2026-11-12 and seen in game on PC 1 as local builds; it is not published.
Convert from the `.map` itself, not from a staging folder elsewhere: the
pipeline reads the staging beside the conversion (`<conversion>/staging`),
and the level takes the map's name.

- **Stages:** land, foliage, swap, editor, cook, bake, assemble, install.
  `collision` is skipped, so the bake uses the conversion's own BSP with its
  glass and physics-model surfaces; a swapped tree keeps Halo 2's collision.
- **Ground and cliffs by name.** Halo 2's detail bitmaps are not named
  `detail_grass` or `detail_cliff`, so the config names them: `shaders`,
  `cliff_shaders` (Coagulation's boulders, `coag_rocks`, among them, which
  draws them in the game's rock) and `details` (`ground_dirt_pebble` as
  sand, `coag_grass` as grass: the base map's alpha then says where each
  grows, as on a CE map).
- **A look of its own.** A landscape with no `MAP_LOOKS` entry in
  `build_landscape.py` gets Death Island's beach. Coagulation (`LCO`) takes
  Blood Gulch's: packed earth, stones on soil, its cliff mix.
- **A pond is not a sea** (`"sea": false`). The pipeline and the loader take
  any water mesh for the sea. Coagulation's pool by the cave sits 7 m up:
  grass grew only above it, so 1.8 of 2.2 million clumps stood on the
  plateau and none in the valley, and the valley floor drew as a beach
  (sand, ripples, shells).
- **`foliage_ceiling`** (cm): nothing is scattered on ground above it.
  Coagulation's plateau, 50 to 107 m up and out of sight, is left bare;
  the valley keeps about 290,000 clumps, Blood Gulch's count.
- **Light.** The conversion's sun stood at 28 degrees and the cliffs shaded
  the valley floor; the config raises it to 55, turns the baked sun mask
  off (`sun_mask: false`, as Blood Gulch) and sets `sun.lightmap_sun` to
  [0.35, 0.62]: Halo 2's ground lightmap is a lavender 0.6 where CE's
  sunlit ground is 1.0. Blood Gulch's skylight, exposure and clouds, and
  `haze: "ce"` (a Halo 2 slot carries its fog as a CE one does).
- **Halo 2's grass sprites are hidden** (`hide_materials:
  ["M_H2_Billboard"]`): the scattered grass replaces them. A decorator
  placement is ground cover, not scenery the grass keeps clear of or a
  boulder to swap (`decorator` in `placement.json`): Coagulation's 218
  decal fields cleared 20 m circles of grass until the scatter skipped them.
- **Trees.** Coagulation's trees are instanced BSP geometry, which
  `placement.json` never names. `mjolnir cache stage` writes every
  instance's name, frame, shaders and bounds to `bsp/instances.json`, and
  `instance_swap: {"redcedar": "tree_pine"}` has
  `tools/level/instance_scenery.py` turn the instances with such a shader
  into scenery entries for the swap: its three red cedars stand as A30's
  pines, sized to each cedar's height, their Halo 2 slots hidden.
- **Chunk 1001.** Halo 2 remasters take numbers from 1001 up
  (docs/chunk_numbering.md). The landscape container's library holds the
  same two shader maps as every CE remaster's, so a textured landscape on
  a machine with a CE remaster installed does not prove library 1001
  opened.
- **Desert biome** (`"biome": "desert"`). Coagulation's dirt and cliff feet
  are dressed from the game's dry-country plants and Poly Haven's
  Namaqualand pack (flowers, succulents, granite stones) instead of the
  beach's shells and driftwood: docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md. The pack
  cooks into the map's landscape container, so the map needs it in the
  editor project and a credit when published.
- **Zanzibar** (`ZAN`, chunk 1002, `"biome": "coast"`). A Fluid Flux coast
  at the fog plane's height, since the conversion has no water surface;
  sea life on the bed, sea campion, small palms at the walls' feet and
  the beach bushes as young palms. Its ground shaders list grass before
  sand, the reverse of CE: the bake and the mesh ground slots turn that
  over (docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md).
- **Containment** (`CNT`, chunk 1003, landscape `LCN`, `"biome": "snow"`,
  2026-11-16). Ice Fields' and Sidewinder's snow: B40's glacial rock on
  the cliffs (`containment_cliff_a` and the boulders' `containment_rock_medium`),
  Sidewinder's ground look, snowy stones and rubble scattered, the game's
  falling snow kept out of the bases (11,755 roof cells). Its terrain
  shader is not a blend, so it would have baked as one flat snow; with
  `real_base` the ground keeps its base map's own colour, which paints the
  tyre tracks and the dirt by the bases. Its bases are Forerunner, so the
  Forerunner plate stays on their metal (no `structure_metal: false`).
  Swap and collision are skipped: its scenery is 8 brambles and twig
  decals (the twigs are `M_H2_Billboard`, hidden). Its gates and switches
  come from the conversion's own machines, as a fresh conversion places
  them; the install takes their actors (`pakchunk987-MJOLNIRACT`) from the
  conversion's `machines` folder (tools/level/machine_containers.py). In
  game, solo and in two networked copies: all 8 machines start shut, a
  switch group opens its own gate in both simulations, and the 8 part
  slots draw their cooked instances.
- **Ascension** (`ASC`, chunk 1004, landscape `LAS`, `"biome": "desert"`,
  2026-11-16). Its ground is a blend of bare slate and pale sandstone
  paths, so both detail maps are `sand` (stones and dry plants): taking
  the slate for grass grew 2.3 million clumps on bare rock. Grass stays on
  the cliffs' up-facing faces, where the cliff master draws its turf, which
  greens the rock pillars' tops. Blood Gulch's look, as Coagulation's.
  Reconverted first (`ASC_flags`) so its machines carry their own
  placement flags. Its three antennas are the conversion's turning
  machines, cooked. In game, solo and in two networked copies: the
  antennas turn in step and draw their cooked instances; a frame takes a
  median 11 ms at 4K. A ground with no grass class had crashed the scatter
  where a cliff's turf met it (scatter_foliage.py).
- **Cladding only within reach.** Ascension first loaded in 4.2 s solo and
  7.3 s on a client (the hub copy: 0.7 and 2.3 s). The loader dresses each
  cladding rock, a mesh actor, with its group's material, and Ascension had
  120,427 of them: its pillars fall 150 m under the lowest spawn, and their
  walls took 80,000. The scatter now puts no rock more than 30 m under the
  map's lowest player spawn (`--clad-floor`, upgrade_ce_map.py's
  CLAD_BELOW_SPAWNS), which of all the remasters trims only Ascension and
  Gephyrophobia's chasm (3,905). Ascension: 40,390 rocks, 2.3 s solo, 3.5 s
  on a client. The loader's log now lists the queued jobs' time by kind
  (`load timing: queued jobs:`).
- **Structure surfaces** (`structure_surfaces`). Zanzibar's concrete and
  steel draw in Poly Haven PBR surfaces through the cliffs' master, each
  wall's Halo 2 base map kept as its colour and its lightmap as shade
  (docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md). The surfaces cook into the runtime
  container, so they too need a runtime release.
- **Still CE-runtime bound.** The cliffs' tessellated meshes cook into the
  trial masters' container (983), as for the CE remasters, and Halo 2's
  masters are in 981: publishing a Halo 2 remaster needs a runtime release
  with both.
- **Measured** on PC 1 at 4K, standing in the grass: 13.9 ms a frame, 2.5 ms
  of it the foliage.
- **Not done:** the pines against Halo 2's cedar collision is unchecked; no
  side-by-side from fixed cameras; `instance_swap` replaces the conversion's
  own scenery list for the swap, so a map with both kinds swaps only its
  instances.

notes.title: Distributing converted maps
notes.summary: Converted Halo CE maps (ce_map_conversion.md) reach players the way texture swaps and tag edits do. Each map is baked ahead of time, uploaded through the mod hub, stored in R2, and installed by the launcher. Players can publish their own maps the same way.
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-10-21. Format v1 is proven with Blood Gulch: a pack built by
`mjolnir map pack`, installed as the launcher will install it and registered
by `mjolnir level register`, plays CTF. Phases 1 to 4 are done, but for the
tag editor's map publishing: the hub takes map packs with a review queue, the
launcher installs them with their dependencies and registers them
(`apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/maps.rs`), and the 19 classic maps and the CE
runtime pack are published, the remastered maps as 2.x releases of the same
listings. The tag editor's map publishing and the Rust cook (Phase 5)
remain: see [Phases](#phases). **Update 2026-11-21:** Halo 2 maps, Custom Edition
conversions, Forge maps and Pelican Warfare are published the same way.

Converted Halo CE maps ([ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md)) reach
players the way texture swaps and tag edits do. Each map is baked ahead of
time, uploaded through the mod hub, stored in R2, and installed by the
launcher. Players can publish their own maps the same way.

Three rules shape everything below:

- **No game-derived bytes in git.** A baked map clones shipped tags (the
  canvas scenario, the donor BSP, object definitions) and carries CE's
  geometry, textures and sounds. These bytes live only in R2, behind the
  hub. The repository holds the tools, the code mods and the design.
- **No Unreal Editor on a player's machine.** Baking needs the editor today
  (the materials and sounds cook), so maps ship pre-baked. Player
  publishing waits on the Rust cook ([Phase 5](#phases)).
- **Anything executable still ships only from signed CI.** A map pack is
  data: containers, JSON, textures and Megalo variants (bytecode the game's
  own interpreter runs, sandboxed like a game type). The loader and lobby
  that read it are code mods, released by `release-mods.yml` as before.

## The pieces

| Piece | Kind | Published by | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| A map, e.g. `ce-blood-gulch` | hub `content`, with a map listing | map author | the map's containers, level file, registration record |
| `mjolnir-ce-runtime` | hub `content` | us | everything every converted map shares |
| MJOLNIRLevelLoader, MJOLNIRLobby | code mods | signed CI | the loader, the multiplayer menu, the game types (`.mglo`) |

### A map pack

A `.mjolnir` archive ([mjolnir_format.md](mjolnir_format.md)) of type `map`:

```
mjolnir.json                  manifest: type "map", plus the map block below
signature.json                added by `mjolnir map pack --sign` (below)
content/
  pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-<CODE>_P.utoc    the scenario, its BSP, and the map's own world
  pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-<CODE>_P.ucas
  pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMESH-<CODE>_P.utoc   the terrain mesh
  pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMESH-<CODE>_P.ucas
  pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>_P.utoc   the map's cooked CE textures, lightmaps and
  pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>_P.ucas   ambient sounds
  pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIRLAND-<CODE>_P.utoc   a remastered map's landscape world, with a
  pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIRLAND-<CODE>_P.ucas   shader library the launcher renumbers with it
  pakchunk996-MJOLNIRBANK-<CODE>_P/<id>.bnk   a vehicle's Wwise banks (below), beside
                                              that container's .utoc and .ucas
map/
  level.json                  the level file the loader reads
  registration.json           the bake's registration record (below)
  bots.json                   where the bot squads stand, for MJOLNIRHud (a map with bots; docs/bots.md)
  vehicle_sounds.json         a custom vehicle's sounds and lights, for the loader (docs/custom_vehicles.md)
  <foliage file>              the foliage placements the level file names
  decals/*.png                its decals' textures
docs/README.md                optional
```

Format rules (version 1):

- Every package a map adds lives under `/Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/`, so two
  maps never claim the same package. The level file names only `/Game`
  paths: either the map's own, or the runtime pack's.
- A map cooks into a chunk of its own, `10000 + int(CODE, 36)` (Blood Gulch,
  `BGL`, is 24853). A `PrimaryAssetLabel` at the map's root sets it, so the
  map's cook never mixes with the runtime pack's chunk 988.
- No `.mglo` and no code. The only loose files are the level's own data
  under `map/`, which the mods read beside the level file: the foliage file
  the level names (a remastered map's `foliage.bin`), its decals' textures,
  and a map with bots' `bots.json` (`mjolnir map pack` takes it from the
  bake's `<CODE>.bots.json`). A map's preview is its hub listing's cover
  image, not a file in the pack.

The manifest's map block:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "name": "Blood Gulch",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "map",
  "map": {
    "code": "BGL",
    "title": "Blood Gulch",
    "modes": ["slayer", "ctf"],
    "size": "large",
    "players": { "min": 4, "max": 16 },
    "vehicles": true,
    "game": "halo1"
  },
  "compat": { "min_build": "2026.08.11.1121610.2" },
  "deps": [{ "slug": "mjolnir-ce-runtime", "range": "^1.0.0" }]
}
```

- `code` is the three-character scenario codename. It is unique across the
  hub, which rejects a second map claiming a code someone else's map holds,
  whether that map is listed or [waiting for review](#players-maps).
- `modes` lists the game types the multiplayer menu offers. Each one must be
  a variant the loader ships (`slayer`, `ctf`, ...).
- `size`, `players`, `vehicles`, `origin` and `game` are optional catalog metadata,
  what players filter the hub's map list by ([below](#the-catalog)). A
  release that leaves one out keeps the value the listing already has.
  `origin` is `custom_edition` or `original`; `classic` is set by
  moderators only. `game` is the game the map comes from, `halo1` (Halo CE)
  or `halo2` (Halo 2). Field rules are in [mjolnir_format.md](mjolnir_format.md#map-archives).
- The registration record is what `mjolnir level bake --standalone` writes
  beside its output as `<CODE>.registration.json`: the codename, the canvas
  scenario it was cloned from, the title, the description and the world
  path. The launcher
  builds the shared registration container from these records
  ([below](#the-registration-container)).

A map pack carries no `.mglo`. Game types are code-reviewed scripts the
loader ships, so a map can only name them. Custom game types per map are
[Phase 6](#phases).

### A vehicle's banks

A vehicle built by `tools/level/ce_vehicle_audio.py` plays through Wwise banks. A
`.pak` can hold any file in the game, so an archive never carries one. `map pack`
takes the banks out of the `.pak` the build left beside the container and writes
them as bare members, `content/<container>/<id>.bnk`. The launcher builds the `.pak`
itself under its own mount name, so a bank can only land at
`Meteorite/Content/WwiseAudio/<id>.bnk`.

The hub's scan (`hub/src/lib/api/banks.ts`) and the launcher
(`crates/ue-iostore/src/bank.rs`) apply the same rules, and `map pack` holds each bank
to them as it writes the archive:

- A member sits at exactly `content/<container>/<id>.bnk`. The container is a plain
  name with its `.utoc` in the same archive, and the id is written as a plain number.
- The id is not in `defs/hce/shipped_banks.json`. A map pack must not change the sound
  of a stock vehicle on every other map.
- The bank is version 150 and its header's id is the one in its name. `BKHD` comes
  first, the sections are only `BKHD`, `DIDX`, `DATA` and `HIRC`, each once, and every
  section, media entry and `HIRC` record stays in bounds.
- A bank is at most 16 MiB, and a release at most 32 banks and 48 MiB of them. The scan
  holds them in memory.

These rules keep a member to being a bank. They don't prove Wwise reads one safely:
the record bodies go to Wwise's own parser, in every player's game. So anyone may
publish banks, but a new author's wait for a moderator, whatever the release's type
([review](#players-maps)).

Nothing checks two packs for the same id. Ids hash from names carrying the map's code,
so only a copied id collides, and then one map's bank shadows the other's.

**Installing.** The launcher keeps a release's banks at
`<release>/banks/<container>/<id>.bnk` in its cache and records each one's hash beside
the containers', so verify and repair cover them. Every write to Paks builds the `.pak`
again from the cache, so an update, a reorder or a repair keeps the banks, and uninstall
removes it with the rest of the triple. A bank gone from the cache counts as a damaged
install: it never turns into a silent stub.

**Older launchers.** Launcher 0.22.0 and older skip a `.bnk` under `content/`, as they
skip any member that isn't a container, and write a stub `.pak`. The map installs and
plays, and the vehicle has no engine or horn. Nothing warns the player: the hub has no
gate on launcher version, and `launcher_features.txt` is the game asking about the
launcher, not the hub.

**Release order.**

1. Release the launcher that takes banks, and let players update to it.
2. Deploy the hub with the scan (`ts-5`). Until then the hub refuses `.bnk` as a forbidden
   kind. Apply migrations 0025 and 0026 first: `/complete` writes `banks_json` and
   `map_json`, so without them every publish fails.
3. Publish maps with banks, and approve the ones waiting for review.

Step 2 lets authors upload banks, so moderators leave those releases pending until step
1 is done. The other way round, players on an older launcher get a silent vehicle with
no error.

This pack is published by us and updated when a shared piece changes (1.19.0
as of mods 0.46.1). It holds everything converted maps share. `tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh` builds most of it:
