notes.title: Container numbers and load order
notes.summary: Status: the engine behaviour proven in game on 2026-11-11 (PC 1, Steam CU4); rollout steps 1 to 4 built in the launcher the same day (see What was built). Steps 5 and 6 and the shared-library move remain (see Remaining).
notes.body:
Status: the engine behaviour proven in game on 2026-11-11 (PC 1, Steam CU4);
rollout steps 1 to 4 built in the launcher the same day (see *What was built*).
Steps 5 and 6 and the shared-library move remain (see *Remaining*).

## The problem

A container's file name starts `pakchunk<N>`. Today that one number does three
jobs:

1. **Shader library name.** The engine opens a mounted pak's shader library
   by the number in the file name: `pakchunk978…` opens
   `Meteorite_Chunk978`. A container with a library has to keep the number
   it was cooked with.
2. **Load order.** The launcher names hub containers `pakchunk9NN`, with
   `NN` the mod's place in the profile's load order, on the assumption that
   a higher number wins.
3. **Ownership.** The launcher treats `pakchunk9NN-MJOLNIR…` as ours and
   sets every other non-game container aside as an unsupported mod.

That gives every author, every tool and every installed mod one shared space
of 100 numbers:

- 966 to 999 are taken by our own shipped containers, and 969 to 979 by the
  eleven CE remasters. There is no number left for a twelfth.
- Hub load-order numbers start at 900 and PC 1 is at 965. The next installs
  reuse numbers our shipped libraries own.
- `order_number` clamps at 999, so every mod past the hundredth gets the same
  number.
- Two authors who cook a library under the same number cannot be installed
  together, and nothing tells them which numbers are free.

## What the engine actually does

Read from UE 5.5 source, then checked in game.

| Fact | Source | In game |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The number after `pakchunk` can have any number of digits. | `GenericPlatformMisc.cpp` `GetPakchunkIndexFromPakFile` | A container named `pakchunk20001…` mounts and its library opens. |
| A library's chunk ID is CityHash64 of lower-cased UTF-16 `<Project>_Chunk<N>-<format>`. Shader code chunks are keyed by content hash and do not depend on `N`. | `ShaderCodeArchive.cpp` `GetShaderCodeArchiveChunkId` | The computed ID matches the library chunk in all eleven remaster containers (format `PCD3D_SM6-PCD3D_SM6`). |
| So a library can be renamed to another number by rewriting one chunk ID in the `.utoc`. The `.ucas` is untouched. | n/a | TST's library renamed 968 → 20001 and mounted as `pakchunk20001…`: the map draws fully. The same file mounted as `pakchunk20002…` draws the default checker material on the same building. Blood Gulch's library cannot show this: its shader maps are in other installed libraries too. |
| Load priority is the folder's base order plus `100 × (v + 1)` for a name ending `_<v>_P` (plain `_P` counts as `v = 0`). The same value orders the IoStore containers. | `IPlatformFilePak.cpp` `FPakPlatformFile::Mount` | Two containers holding the same map: the one with the higher suffix loads, whichever has the higher chunk number: `_9_P` over `_P` both ways round, and `_3000_P` over `_2000_P` with the loser being the name that wins a plain tie. |
| With equal priority, the container mounted last wins, and files mount in reverse name order. So the name that sorts **lower** wins. | `IoDispatcherFileBackend.cpp` `FFileIoStore::Mount` | `pakchunk940-…_P` beat `pakchunk997-…_P` (twice), and the same container renamed `pakchunk900-…_P` beat `pakchunk940-…_P`. |
| A failed library open is retried on the next mount with that number. | `ShaderCodeLibrary.cpp` `OnPakFileMounted` | Not tested. |

The last-but-one row means the launcher's "higher number wins" assumption is
backwards. Today the mod listed **first** in a profile wins a conflict, and
any hub container beats our `99x` overrides on a shared chunk. This matches
the 2026-11-06 finding that a hub copy at 920 beat a local 996.

The launcher already uses the suffix once: a live update is written as
`…_<n>_P` beside the container the game holds open (`patch_name` in hub.rs).

The in-game check for "which copy loaded" scans the game's memory for byte
windows unique to each container's data file; it read 12 of 12 for the winner
and 0 of 12 for the loser in every run.

## Design

Split the three jobs.

### 1. Load order is the `_<v>_P` suffix

The launcher names each hub container `…_<v>_P`, where `v` comes from the
profile's load order: later in the list, higher `v`. This is the engine's own
priority field and it does not depend on name sorting. Thousands of mods fit.

Our shipped overrides (`990` to `999`: registration, flags, spawns,
teleporters) were to get suffixes chosen to reproduce what wins today. What
wins today was measured (next section) before choosing.

### 2. The chunk number is assigned on the player's machine

When the launcher writes a profile into Paks it gives every container a
number of its own from a wide local range (for example 10000 upward), and
for a container with a shader library rewrites the library's chunk ID to
match (`ue_iostore::shader_library::renumber`). The number an author cooked
with stops mattering once the container is installed:

- No registry, no reserved bands for authors, no coordination between games.
  Two mods cooked under the same number install side by side.
- A container without a library can share one number; it has nothing to open.
- Uniqueness only has to hold among the containers mounted on one machine,
  and the launcher sees all of them.

Our own runtime containers that Lua or tools name by number (980, 984, 985,
988 and the rest) keep their numbers. Those are a short fixed list in the
repo, checked by a test for duplicates.

### 3. Ownership is the `MJOLNIR` marker

`is_mjolnir_container` accepts any chunk number, and keeps requiring the
`-MJOLNIR` marker.

### 4. Remasters stop shipping duplicate libraries

Measured on PC 1: the eleven remaster libraries (969 to 979) hold two shader
maps between them. One is in all eleven, the other in five. Neither is in a
runtime container today. Shipping those two once in the runtime pack would
leave a remaster whose materials add nothing new with no library and no
number at all. Whether a Halo 2 remaster cooks to the same two maps has not
been checked. `shader_lib_overlap` reports this for any Paks folder.

## What wins today, measured

Measured 2026-11-11 on PC 1's active profile (55 entries, 582 cached
containers) plus every loose `MJOLNIR` container in Paks: every chunk two
containers share, with the bytes compared, and the winner by the rule above
(equal `_P` priority, lower name wins).

Where the shipped overrides live. On a player's machine the flag, spawn,
teleporter, bot and menu containers (`990` to `995`, `985`) are not loose:
they are containers of the `mjolnir-ce-runtime` hub mod, written into Paks
as `pakchunk900-MJOLNIRHUB-mjolnir-ce-runtime-<j>_P` (libraries at their
cooked 966, 981, 982, 983, 988). The only loose `99x` container the launcher
writes is the registration, `pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P` (`maps.rs`). The other
`99x` writers (`build_ce_runtime.sh`, `convert_ce_map.sh`, `upgrade_ce_map.py`
local installs, `build_spawn_point.sh`, `build_ctf_flag.sh`, `blam-cli` `ue`
and `level` commands) install loose files on developer machines only.

| Shared chunks | Between | Bytes | Wins today | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 11 packages (`M_CE_Ocean`, `M_CE_CliffTess`, `M_CE_Environment`, 8 textures) | runtime `WATER`/`CETRIAL`/`MAT` (982/983/988) and TST `COOK` (968) | differ: a 16-byte GUID, and in the materials a 20-byte shader-map hash | **TST** (the map) | 968 sorts below 982 |
| 128 packages (`MI_LTT_swap_*`) | TST `LAND` (969, library) and TST `ROCK` (no library) | differ: 598-byte stubs in LAND, full native clones in ROCK | **ROCK** | ROCK took load-order number 923, below 969 |
| 5 packages | TST `COOK` and TST `LAND` | identical | n/a | |
| none | `MJOLNIRREG` and any hub container | n/a | n/a | |
| any | a hub container and a loose `99x` `_P` override (developer install) | n/a | **hub** | 9NN below 99x; the 2026-11-06 "hub copy at 920 beat a local 996" |
| 1 package + library | runtime `H2` (981, fixed) and a loose `pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2TEST_P` (a hand-placed test build on PC 1) | differ | **loose** | same number, and `MJOLNIRH2…` sorts below `MJOLNIRHUB…` |

Everything else that overlaps is between a hub copy and a loose copy of the
same container that another session placed by hand on PC 1, where the hub
copy wins today.

So, reproduced on purpose:

- **Later profile entry wins.** The runtime is entry 0, maps come after it,
  so the map's copies of the runtime materials keep winning. This is also
  what the profile list in the UI says ("later entries win", "the lower
  entry wins them") and what `Profile`'s doc comment said; the launcher's
  9NN numbers did the reverse for containers without a library.
- **Within one entry, the later container wins** (TST: `ROCK`, index 2,
  over `LAND`, index 1).
- **Every hub container sits above loose `_P` containers**: `v` starts at
  1000, and a loose `_P` is `v = 0`. The registration never overlaps a hub
  container, so it stays loose at `v = 0`. This reproduces every hub-vs-loose
  case but one: a loose test build that shares a *fixed* number with a hub
  container and has a marker sorting below `MJOLNIRHUB` (PC 1's
  `pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2TEST_P`) beat the hub copy by name, and now loses.
  Plain `_P` keeps losing on purpose. Local development wins by being
  installed as a local build (next section), and anything still loose that
  loses is named by `mjolnir dev list` and in the launcher.

## Local builds take precedence over hub content

Decided 2026-11-11: local development must have a good way to win over
published hub content. A local build is
`pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIRDEV-<name>_<v>_P`:

| | Load-order suffix `v` | Chunk number `N` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loose `_P` (registration, hand copies) | 0 | as named |
| Hub containers (launcher) | 1,000 to 999,996, plus 3 for live updates | 10,000 to 4,999,999 |
| Local builds (`mjolnir dev install`) | 1,000,000 to 1,999,999, each install above the last | 5,000,000 to 5,999,999 |

The bands live in one place, `ue_iostore::paks`, with compile-time checks
that they do not overlap and that `100 × (v + 1)` stays inside the engine's
int32 priority. The launcher's `chunk_numbers` takes its hub values from it.

- `mjolnir dev install <container> --name <name>` writes the build above
  every hub container and every earlier build, replacing an earlier build of
  the same name (it keeps that build's number). A shader library is renamed
  to the build's own number, so it opens beside the hub copy's. The name is
  letters, digits and dashes; one carrying `MJOLNIRHUB` is refused (the
  launcher deletes those). With no `--name` the container's own name after
  its number is used, refused when it says nothing about which map
  (`pakchunk978-MJOLNIRLAND-Windows`).
- `mjolnir dev remove <name>`, `mjolnir dev list [--json]`. Install and
  remove change nothing while the game holds a file they would replace.
- `dev install` and `dev list` print every loose MJOLNIR container that
  loses chunks with different bytes to a hub container or local build
  (`paks::shadowed_loose`; byte-identical chunks are counted apart, shader
  code and container headers are left out, a library under the same number
  counts). This is the silent failure seen twice (a hub copy at 920 over a
  local 996, and H2TEST).
- The launcher never sets a local build aside, never renames or deletes
  one, and lists them under *Local builds* in the Library's content-mod
  panel with a Remove button, beside the same "loses to" warnings
  (`local_builds.rs`, `LocalBuildsPanel.tsx`).
- `tools/level/dev_paks.py` is the Python side: the install and remove
  commands, and the glob for the launcher's copy of a hub container under
  either name. `upgrade_ce_map.py`'s install stages use it: a local install
  of a new map, `--install` over an existing hub map (map, mesh and
  landscape), and the shared trial and water masters all go in as local
  builds instead of being copied over the hub's files.
  `tst_preview_swap.py` installs the staged TST containers as builds named
  `TST-PREVIEW-*`, swaps and backs up the map's data files as before, and
  restore removes the builds.
- A local build shadows the hub copy; it cannot delete it. A package the hub
  copy has and the build does not still loads from the hub. Overwriting the
  hub's files used to drop such packages; that no longer works anyway, since
  the launcher renames hub files and rewrites their libraries.

Checked in game 2026-11-11 (PC 1, Steam), with the hub profile written under
the new names and the same GUID memory scan as above (11 packages the
runtime and TST both carry):

| Paks | Copy that loaded |
| --- | --- |
| hub only | TST (later entry), 8 of 11, runtime 0 |
| + runtime's WATER, CETRIAL, MAT as local builds at 1,000,000 to 1,000,002 | runtime, 8 of 11, TST 0: the bottom of the band beats the hub |
| + a placeholder at 1,999,998, then TST's COOK as a local build, which took 1,999,999 | TST, 8 of 11, runtime 0: the top beats the bottom, no overflow |
| TST's hub entry off, its five containers as local builds (libraries 968 → 5,000,000 and 969 → 5,000,001) | TST loads and draws textured; COOK's 13 shader maps are in no other library |

`mjolnir dev list` on that Paks named PC 1's `pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2TEST_P`
as losing to the runtime's 981 container, the case it exists for. The
launcher's panel was not looked at in the running app.

## What was built

`ue-iostore`: `pack::rekey` and `shader_library::{library_id, renumber}`,
with the examples `renumber_container`, `shader_lib_id`, `shader_lib_overlap`.

Launcher (`apps/launcher/src-tauri/src`):

- `unsupported.rs`: `is_mjolnir_container` accepts `pakchunk<any>-MJOLNIR…`.
- `chunk_numbers.rs`: the numbers. A container's *position* is its place in
  the active profile, counting every entry's containers in order, disabled
  entries included, so enabling a mod or installing one (appended) renames
  nothing already mounted.
  - Suffix `v = 1000 + 4 × position`, capped at 999,996, below the local
    builds' band. The gap of 4 holds three live updates.
  - Chunk number `N = 10000 + position`, capped below the local builds' numbers: every container its own number.
  - `config/fixed_chunks.json`: the containers that keep their cooked number
    because Lua, a tool or the launcher names them by it (966 KOTH, 980
    FORGEUI, 981 H2, 982 WATER, 983 CETRIAL, 984 UI, 985 MENU, 988 MAT, the
    990 to 995 runtime overrides, 996 REG). A test fails on a name listed
    twice, two libraries under one number, or a number in the local range.
- `hub.rs`: `mount_plan` names each container
  `pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIRHUB-<slug>-<j>_<v>_P`. A container with a shader
  library named for its cooked number gets its library renamed to `N` as it
  is written into Paks (`Mount::utoc`); one whose library is not named for
  the number in its own file name keeps that number, as before. The cache is
  never changed, so `verify_installed` and the quick verify (which hash the
  cache) are unaffected; `paks_gaps` checks presence and `paks_strays` names,
  neither size nor bytes.
- Live updates (`patch_name`): a container the game holds open is replaced by
  `…_<v + n>_P`, n from 1, above the old one and below the next container. A
  library written while the game runs is refused when another mod's
  container in Paks carries a shader library under its number
  (`forge_shaders::library_free`). The engine opens one library per number
  and skips a number only once a library has opened under it
  (`FNamedShaderLibrary::OnPakFileMounted`, `PresentChunks`), so a container
  that shares the number and has no library takes nothing: the runtime's
  `pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU_P` beside a map's `pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>_P`
  is the everyday case. A library not named for the number in its file name
  is never opened and is not checked. Every check runs before the first
  container is written, and a refused map stays installed and enabled, so
  the next launch from the launcher writes it (`hub::write_live`).
- `forge_shaders.rs`: the Forge material check runs on the numbers assigned
  in Paks. Two packs cooked under the same number now install side by side;
  the 900 to 999 requirement is gone.

### Checked in game, 2026-11-11 (PC 1, Steam)

The active profile (53 entries; `h2-elongation` and `h2-turf` left out
because another session had their containers aside) was written into Paks by
this code (`mount_plan` plus `Mount::write`, the copy loop `materialize`
runs), with the game's own and hand-placed containers left in place:

- **TST draws textured** with its two libraries renamed 968 → 10158 and
  969 → 10159.
- **All 48 hub maps load** (hosted in turn with `mjolnir_auto host <CODE>
  slayer private`, each reaching "world <CODE> has level"), including the
  remasters whose libraries moved from 970–979 to 100xx and the Forge maps
  with `foundry-wide`'s material library at 10263. The remasters' and
  TST's screenshots show no default checker material. The Forge maps'
  pieces are plain grey either way, so the screenshots do not show whether
  `foundry-wide`'s one shader map found in no other library (per
  `shader_lib_overlap` on the cache) is in use; its `.utoc` renumbers
  cleanly (`a_cooked_library_renumbers`).
- **A conflict resolves by profile order, not by name.** The 11 packages
  shared by the runtime and TST (above) carry different GUIDs, so a scan of
  the game's memory tells which copy loaded. In the profile's own order
  (runtime first) TST's copies loaded: 8 of 11 of TST's GUIDs resident, none
  of the runtime's. With the runtime moved after TST it reversed: 8 of 11 of
  the runtime's, none of TST's. In that second layout TST's names
  (`pakchunk10120…`) sort below the runtime's (`pakchunk966…`), so name order
  alone would have kept TST: the suffix decided.

Not checked in game: live updates (`patch_name`, `library_free`), the
registration rebuild path of a full `materialize` (`sync_maps`, unchanged by
this work), suffixes above about 3,300, and the Game Pass build.

## The launcher gate and release order

Decided 2026-11-11: content that only works with local chunk numbers must
not reach a player on an older launcher silently; they get "update your
launcher" instead.

What needs a newer launcher. A release carrying a shader library cooked
under a number outside 900 to 999 (launchers before local numbers set that
container aside as unsupported), or under the same number as another mod's
library (they open only one of the two). The hub measures this when it scans
a release and records it as the release's `requires` list, entry
`local-chunk-numbers`; authors do not declare it. A library number already
used by another mod's ungated release gates the newcomer, never the
original.

What each launcher does.

- **This launcher and later** send `User-Agent: MJOLNIR-Launcher/<version>`,
  `X-MJOLNIR-Launcher: <version>` and `X-MJOLNIR-Features:
  local-chunk-numbers` on every hub request (`hub.rs`, `launcher_headers`).
  A release whose `requires` names a feature the launcher lacks is never
  chosen, never offered as an update, and refused at install or enable with
  "needs a newer MJOLNIR launcher … Update the launcher, then try again"
  (`needs_newer_launcher`). The feature list is compiled in
  (`LAUNCHER_FEATURES`), as Forge packs' `requires` is.
- **Launchers up to 0.23.0** send no User-Agent and no headers, which is how
  the hub tells them from browsers. The hub leaves gated releases out of
  their release lists and map listings, so they install the newest release
  they can use. When a mod has nothing else, the newest gated release stays
  listed and `GET /releases/{id}` reports its status as a sentence telling
  them to update the launcher, which they show as "Release is …, not
  published"; the download itself is refused. Browsers and other clients
  with a User-Agent see everything as before.
- **Not covered.** A player on an old launcher who joins a host running a
  gated release by its exact id reads "That release is not published". The
  test for an old launcher is the missing User-Agent: anything else that
  calls the hub without one is treated the same way. Releases scanned
  before the hub change is deployed carry no `requires` until scanned again.

Release order, for content cooked under a new number (Halo 2, Reach and
later remasters, community maps with their own libraries):

1. Ship this launcher (`launcher-v*`) and let it be adopted. Which version
   number that is, is the release's call; nothing stores it.
2. Deploy the hub with the `requires` scan and filtering.
3. Only then publish such content. Content cooked under 900 to 999 with a
   number nobody else uses needs no gate and works on every launcher.

## Rollout

1. `ue-iostore`: `pack::rekey` and `shader_library::renumber` (written,
   proven in game). **Built.**
2. Launcher: accept any chunk number as ours. This has to reach players
   before any content uses a new name, because older launchers set unknown
   names aside. Gate new-style content on a minimum launcher version.
   **Built** (the gate is not: see *Remaining*).
3. Launcher: suffix-based load order, with the shipped-override table.
   Decide which way the profile list reads and say so in the UI, since the
   order players have today is the reverse of what was intended. **Built:**
   later wins, which the UI already said.
4. Launcher: local numbering with the library rewrite; `forge_shaders`'s
   duplicate check moves to after numbering. **Built.**
5. Tools that install containers by hand (`upgrade_ce_map.py`,
   `pack_local_map`, the CLI install path, live map mount in Lua) take their
   names from one shared helper.
6. New remasters (Halo 2 first) cook to any number; the installer renumbers.

## Remaining

- **Tools not moved to local builds.** `tools/level/ce_vehicle.py` and
  `ce_vehicle_name.py` copy any `pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-*_P.pak` from Paks as
  a stub, which a machine with only hub maps does not have. The build
  scripts that copy runtime overrides in by hand (`build_ce_runtime.sh`,
  `convert_ce_map.sh`, `build_spawn_point.sh`, `build_ctf_flag.sh`, the
  `blam-cli` `ue` and `level` writers) still write plain `_P` names, which
  lose to the hub's runtime; `mjolnir dev list` names them.
  `pack_local_map.py` only packages archives and needed nothing. Tools that
  read Paks through `ue_iostore::load_all` do not apply mount priority when
  two containers hold one package. A comment in
  `mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/main.lua` still describes the old `pakchunk9NN`
  names (Lua finds hub containers by their cached names in
  `hub_state.json`, so its behaviour does not change).
- **Minimum launcher version gate** for content cooked under numbers outside
  9NN (older launchers set those aside as unsupported).
- **The two shared landscape shader maps** (design step 4): move them into
  the runtime pack so remasters ship no library.
- **Hub server**: nothing changed; the conflict preview (`/conflicts/check`)
  returns pairs and the UI already reads "the lower entry wins".
- Fixed numbers match by cached container name in any mod, so a community
  pack shipping a container named `pakchunk988-MJOLNIRMAT-…` would keep 988
  and share our library's number. Restrict the match to the runtime mod's
  slug if that matters.
- `install_stock_modes.ps1` matches `^pakchunk\d+(-MJOLNIRHUB-.+)$` and keeps
  working; comments in `teams.lua` and the Lobby's `main.lua` still describe
  `pakchunk9NN` names.
- A live update that changes how many containers a mod has shifts the
  positions of every later mod. Already mounted containers keep their
  priority until the next launch, which renames them; a library that would
  land on a number another mod has open is refused (`library_free`).

## Open

- Whether live-mounted containers (maps mounted without a restart) take the
  same suffix priority. Not tested.
- The Game Pass build shares the engine but was not tested here.
- Upper bound on open shader libraries: each installed library costs memory
  at launch whether or not its map is played. Step 4 of the design removes
  most of them; measure before thousands are installed.

notes.title: Custom Content in Community CE Maps
notes.summary: Community maps bring their own weapons, vehicles, scenery, devices and scripts. ce_map_conversion.md converts what the stock maps have. This page records what the community maps add on top, measured across the whole halomaps.org archive, and the order to support it in.
notes.body:
Community maps bring their own weapons, vehicles, scenery, devices and
scripts. [ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md) converts what the
stock maps have. This page records what the community maps add on top,
measured across the whole halomaps.org archive, and the order to support it
in.

The numbers come from the archive mirror ([tools/halomaps](../tools/halomaps/README.md)):
`python tools/halomaps/halomaps.py scripts` reads every map's scenario with
`tools/halomaps/cescript.py`, and `report` writes them up in `report.md`.
Figures are for the 4,264 multiplayer cache files, as of 2026-10-10.

## Where conversion stands

- **Weapons, vehicles and pickups** map by tag path to a type this game has
  (`defs/level/ce-tag-map.json` → `defs/level/palette-map.json`). An
  unlisted custom vehicle falls back to its CE vehicle type. Anything else,
  and a tag listed with no type, is dropped and logged.
- **Custom vehicles** can run as themselves: clones of a shipped vehicle
  with CE's model and numbers ([custom_vehicles.md](custom_vehicles.md),
  Yoyorast's Mongoose).
- **Scenery** is drawn and collides, as static geometry.
- **Machines and controls** are drawn in their rest pose by default. A gear's
  moving part is animated in the material. A map that goes through the device
  lanes gets real machines and controls
  ([ce_map_scripts.md](re/ce_map_scripts.md), Yoyorast and Sanctuary Final).
- **Scripts** of a map that isn't translated are not read: it runs the
  generated startup script, and the bake clears the blocks scripts name.
  `tools/ce_scripts/ce_translate.py` turns a map's own scripts into HSC the
  engine loads.

## What the archive carries

| | Maps |
|---|---|
| Custom weapons | 2,667 |
| Custom vehicles | 1,925 (595 with a custom aircraft, CE's `human_plane`) |
| Machines or controls | 1,087 (119 link them through device groups, 75 script them) |
| Scripts | 759 (median 3 scripts each) |
| Trigger volumes | 455 |
| AI encounters | 877 (83 script `ai_*`) |
| `switch_bsp` | 57 (Hugeass's day/night: a trigger volume switches to its second BSP) |

Many "custom" tags are the same few tags passed between maps. The energy
sword is in 456 maps, the SMG in 325, the battle rifle in 324, the LAAG
turret in 223, the Gauss Warthog in 198.

## This game has more than the canvas places

The canvas level (B40) places only part of the game's armoury, but the
game ships much more. The bake gives a type the canvas palette lacks an
entry of its own (the shotgun was played that way on 2026-10-03). Tags in
the containers with a full Unreal side (an animation Blueprint and a
`BlamWeaponComponent`, found with `mjolnir ue roundtrip --filter <Name>`):

- **Weapons:** battle rifle, SMG, shotgun, fuel rod (`flak_cannon`), energy
  sword, beam rifle. The campaign places the SMG (A15, A30, A50) and the
  beam rifle (A30, A50).
- **Vehicles:** Pelican, Seraph, Wraith, space Banshee, plus the Gauss
  Warthog turret.
- **Ammo:** battle rifle, shotgun and needler ammo, besides the four the
  canvas has.

The weapon group also lists Reach's DMR, needle rifle, concussion rifle,
grenade launcher, gravity hammer, Spartan laser, plasma launcher and focus
rifle. Most have no Unreal packages under their names, and none is known
to draw.

So the archive's most shared custom weapons now map to the game's own
(`ce-tag-map.json`): every energy sword, battle rifle and SMG variant
listed there, the Hunter fuel rod, the brute plasma rifle (as the plasma
rifle), the H2/H3 rifles, pistols, rockets and shotgun, and the H2/H3
grenades, power-ups and ammo. The battle rifle and SMG fall back to the
assault rifle. CE's own ammo pickups (assault rifle, pistol, rocket,
shotgun, needler) were not mapped at all and are now. Custom aircraft
(Coldsnap's jets and fighter-bombers, CE type `human_plane`) spawn as
Banshees, the one aircraft players fly here, until a clone of their own
replaces them ([custom_vehicles.md](custom_vehicles.md)); the shared
Pelicans and Wraiths as the game's own. Whether players can drive this
game's Pelican and Wraith is the open question for those two.

**Checked in game (2026-10-10, Night-Lockout, a 9.0-rated halomaps map with
the battle rifle, SMG, energy sword, beam rifle and brute plasma rifle):**
every placed weapon spawns in the simulation (`mjolnir live objects`), and
each has its own Unreal actor at its spot, drawn with the game's art
(`BP_BattleRifle_WeaponActor_C` with its scope and ammo display,
`BP_SMG_WeaponActor_C`, `BP_Shotgun_WeaponActor_C`,
`BP_EnergySword_WeaponActor_C`). Picking them up and firing them is still
to be played.

A vehicle with spawn flags 0 is in no game type's set: only a script
creates it. That covers wreckage and real vehicles alike, so the flags alone
don't decide. Coldsnap's and Hugeass's fighter-bomber wreck pieces and the
Mythos hull are vehicle tags of that kind (CE type `human_jeep` or
`human_tank`). They used to be placed as Warthogs and a Scorpion, and
`ce-tag-map.json` lists them with no type now. Yoyorast's Mongooses and
Hugeass's Scorpions have the same flags and are real vehicles, so they stay
placed, in every game type's set.

## Scripts

### Reading them

A cache file keeps no script source, only the compiled trees: `script
syntax data` (20-byte nodes) and `script string data` (every name token's
text). A call's first child is its function's name, so the source comes
back without CE's function table:

    python tools/halomaps/cescript.py --hsc maps/hugeass.map

Protected maps decompile too (Yoyorast Island V2: 51 scripts).
`tools/ce_scripts/ce_hs.py` does the same for the script work in
[ce_map_scripts.md](re/ce_map_scripts.md); `cescript.py` also reads a map's
devices and vehicle types for the archive's survey, and `--names` exports
what its scripts refer to.

### What they call

759 maps have scripts. Matched by name against this game's function table
(`defs/hce/console.json`, 1,695 functions), 352 (46%) call nothing this
game lacks. The gaps are concentrated, and most are cheap:

| Step | Maps covered |
|---|---|
| By name, today | 352 (46%) |
| Drop server, console, debug and save calls (`sv_say` alone is 154 maps) | 427 (56%) |
| Drop the engine globals with no use here (`rider_ejection` 109 maps, network rates, cheats) | 509 (67%) |
| Expand `object_create_anew_containing` and friends to the names they match, at compile time | 523 (69%) |
| HUD show/hide and help text | 548 (72%) |
| `vehicle_test_seat_list`, `unit_set_seat`, the flashlight (maps use it as a button) | 582 (77%) |
| `switch_bsp`, `structure_bsp_index` (needs a second BSP) | 618 (81%) |

What's left is mostly CE's encounter AI (`ai_dialogue_triggers`,
`ai_attach`, `ai_magically_see_players`), nav points and cinematic screen
effects.

A name in the table is not a working call. Arguments, value types and
behaviour need checking, and the reference for that is in hand: the MCC
editing kit has CE's original campaign `.hsc` sources
(`HCEEK/data/levels/*/scripts`), and this game's scenarios carry the
developers' ported campaign scripts (`mjolnir script --tag <CODE>
--decompile`), so the two show how each function was translated.

### Compiling them

`mjolnir compile` builds a tree from `.hsc` for this game, with full type
checking. Its vocabulary is the corpus the campaign's scripts call
(`defs/hce/scripting.json`, 483 functions) plus every function of the engine's
own table (`console.json` beside the corpus) that the campaign never calls,
with the signatures the engine declares. The engine compiles a scenario's
source at load, so that source is what a converted map ships
([ce_map_scripts.md](re/ce_map_scripts.md)).

Decompiled and compiled with nothing translated (2026-10-10), the pilot maps
failed only on the gaps in the table above:

| Map | Scripts | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| Hugeass | 11 | `vehicle_test_seat_list` 52, `switch_bsp` 2 |
| Coldsnap | 24 | `vehicle_test_seat_list` 198, `*_containing` 16, flashlight 6, nav points 8, `switch_bsp` 2, `structure_bsp_index` 1 |
| Yoyorast Island V2 | 51 | `*_containing` 2, `rasterizer_decals_flush` 2 |

`ce_translate.py` closes those gaps: drops, renames, seat labels and
`*_containing` expansion, with a report of what it left out. Where that stands,
map by map, is in [ce_map_scripts.md](re/ce_map_scripts.md).

## Devices

Most device placements need no script: CE doors open for whoever walks up,
and platforms and lifts run on their own. So the device work is making
machines and controls real simulation objects: a Blam machine tag (cloned
from a shipped one) with the CE model's collision, and an Unreal visual
that follows the object. Yoyorast and Sanctuary Final work this way on a
host ([ce_map_scripts.md](re/ce_map_scripts.md)).

## Vehicles and weapons of their own

New objects need two halves. The simulation's half is a tag, and the tools
already clone and edit tags (the health pack from battle rifle ammo, the
two-way teleporter, the Spartan fix). The visual half is a cloned Blueprint
with CE's model in it. [custom_vehicles.md](custom_vehicles.md) has the recipe
and [ce_native_support.md](ce_native_support.md) the direction: a CE object's
own tags decide what it does and how it looks. Weapons are still to come, and
walkers (Coldsnap's Mythos and Nirvash) stay out of reach: their legs are
animation only.

## Not converted yet

- Sounds a custom map keeps inside its `.map`.
- A map's second BSP (Hugeass's night).
- AI encounters (CE encounters; this engine has squads).
- The flamethrower: none ships.

notes.title: Custom vehicles
notes.summary: A Custom Edition vehicle runs here as two clones of a shipped one: its tags, which the simulation drives, and its Blueprint, which draws it. Halo CE's Mongoose from Yoyorast Island V2 was the first, driven in game on the test map VHT on 2026-11-04.
notes.body:
A Custom Edition vehicle runs here as two clones of a shipped one: its tags,
which the simulation drives, and its Blueprint, which draws it. Halo CE's
Mongoose from Yoyorast Island V2 was the first, driven in game on the test map
`VHT` on 2026-11-04.

    python tools/level/ce_vehicle_materials.py ...           # CE shaders as material instances
    python tools/level/ce_vehicle_mesh.py ... --instances    # CE parts as meshes, one per node
    python tools/level/ce_vehicle_numbers.py <map> <tags.json> <vehicle tag> <out>
    HCE_PAKS=... python tools/level/ce_vehicle.py <manifest.json> <out dir> --numbers <out>/numbers.json \
        --driver-pose ghost_d --driver-offset=-0.02,0,0.262 --passenger-offset=-0.407,0,0.097 \
        --skel-set-file tools/level/data/mongoose_rider_ik.sets

Everything lands in the out dirs; copy the containers to the Paks folder with
the game closed. One vehicle per code, and never a map's own code:
`convert_ce_map.sh` uses the same `985` and `986` container names, so a vehicle
built under `YOY` would replace the map's textures and terrain.

A level then places it with `tag` ([level_format.md](level_format.md)). A test
map's `level bake --install-test` registers only the maps in the loader's
`registry/`, so hub maps such as Yoyorast drop out of `pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P`
and `maps.json`. Run `mjolnir level register` after it, with the game closed: it
rebuilds both from every installed map.

## Donors

`--donor` names a profile in `tools/level/data/donors/`, default `warthog`: the
actor, its tags, the rig's export, the bone parts ride, the seats and the handling
type. `ce_vehicle_numbers.py --baseline-map` reads the baseline from another map
when the vehicle's own lacks it, as Coldsnap lacks every stock vehicle.

Coldsnap's `jet2_v2` is the first build on `banshee`, on the test map `JTT`. It
draws, boards and flies, but launches itself on boarding (the Banshee's cruising
throttle) and its pilot sits low:

    python tools/level/ce_vehicle_numbers.py coldsnap.map "" vehicles/jet2/jet2_v2 <out> \
        --baseline vehicles/banshee/banshee_mp --baseline-map bloodgulch.map
    python tools/level/ce_vehicle.py <manifest.json> <out dir> --numbers <out>/numbers.json --donor banshee \
        --code JET --name jet --label Jet --variant jet_35=35 --variant jet_91=ce

- **Fit.** There are no wheels to fit to. The hull is centred on the Banshee's
  physics box and stood on its floor, 52 cm below the origin, and every part rides
  `Hull_M`, 136 cm up. The jet is 1.68 times the Banshee's length, but the rig stays
  at 1 (`--rig-scale`): nothing in the simulation depends on it, and a rider is
  drawn at the rig's scale. The Banshee's effects stay at its own size for now.
- **Damage.** The hull region's five permutations each hold every part, and the
  other regions are empty.
- **Pilot.** The Banshee's seat is `invisible`, so the clones clear that bit. The
  `banshee_d` marker takes CE's `driver`. The two boarding seats stay: `--resize`
  reaches root blocks only.
- **Numbers.** Shipped value times CE jet over CE `banshee_mp`: acceleration 600,
  deceleration 562.5, turn rate 14.5, top speed 90.9 (`ce`) against the 35 clamp.
- **Stock parts.** Collision and physics stay the Banshee's (`"chassis": "stock"`),
  so boarding means aiming where the Banshee would be. `vehicle_mute` does not
  apply: the Banshee's graph has no `SoundVariant_EngineLoop` statement.

## How it works

- **Tags.** `new-tag` clones the donor's skeleton, model and vehicle. Model
  variant `none` drops the Warthog's turret.
- **Blueprint.** `crates/ue-asset/examples/vehicle_actor.rs` clones the donor's
  actor under `/Game/MJOLNIR/Vehicles/`, so stock vehicles stay stock.
- **Parts.** Every donor part leaves the actor's `RuntimeRegions`, and the CE
  parts go in. Each rides a bone by name with its own `Transform`. Tyres ride
  the wheel bones, yawed a quarter turn because a wheel bone spins about its X
  axis. Parts that do not turn ride `b_chassis`.
- **Size.** The rig is scaled (0.589 for the Mongoose on the Warthog), which
  lands the donor's wheel bones on the CE tyres. Parts divide by that scale.
- **Look.** CE's shaders become cooked material instances on the `M_CE_*`
  masters, named by the mesh slots, so nothing happens at spawn and joiners get
  the same parts. The masters come from the CE runtime, which must be installed.
- **Collision.** `level machine-collision --plan` writes CE's hull and tyre BSPs
  into the donor's collision model, in the regions the plan names. The physics
  model keeps the donor's bodies with its shapes shrunk to the CE vehicle.
- **Wheel boxes.** A wheel only pushes back while its marker is above the ground.
  The driven body's shape list is a box by each wheel and the polyhedron, and on
  the Warthog each box's foot sits 2.8 cm under its marker, so the body lands
  before a marker can pass the surface. The biggest box belongs to the second,
  proxy body, which does not touch the level, so it stops nothing. Stretching the
  boxes with the hull left the Mongoose's feet 24 cm over its markers, and rear
  boxes 43 cm ahead of the rear wheels: a hard landing put the wheels under the
  ground for good, with the vehicle riding on its boxes. `wheel_boxes` keeps each
  one by its wheel at the tyre's scale, and mass distributions stay, so handling
  does not change.
- **Handling.** Each number is the shipped Warthog's times CE Mongoose over CE
  Warthog: mass 1650, steering two thirds.
- **Lights.** The donor's lights ride VFX sockets of its rig, so they keep the
  Warthog's shape at the rig's scale and float off a CE body. Niagara components
  can't be edited in the cooked Blueprint (`NiagaraVariable` is refused), so
  `ce_vehicle_lights.py` adds a `lights` entry to `vehicle_sounds.json`, and
  `vehicle_sounds.lua` moves them onto CE's `headlight` and `taillight` markers at
  spawn and hides the Warthog's roof pair. That file sits in each level's folder.
  CE's markers can sit inside the model: the Mongoose's taillights are 3.4 cm
  behind their lamp faces, so a glow on the marker is buried and only the light on
  the ground shows. Pass `--bones` with `ce_vehicle_skin.py`'s `bones.json`, whose
  lights it moved clear of the body: 4.5 cm for the taillights, 10.7 cm for the
  outer headlights.
- **Name.** The prompt's `{ItemName}` comes from no tag and no string table: the
  Blueprint's `BlamVehicleComponent.VehicleUIDataAsset` is read by
  `WBP_InteractPrompt`. `ce_vehicle_name.py` clones the donor's asset with the name
  as literal text and repoints the actor at it, so `--label` takes any name.
  Weapons and equipment have the same asset (`WeaponDataAsset`,
  `EquipmentDataAsset`). Keep `enter seat string` empty: a key outside
  `BlamStrings.csv` draws `<MISSING STRING TABLE ENTRY>`.
- **Markers.** Wheel, seat and entry markers in the skeleton clone reach the
  simulation. A skeleton node's translation does not reach the drawn bones.

## What was measured

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Vehicle tag clone, stock Blueprint | loads, boards, drives |
| Rewritten soft path in a shipped Blueprint | draws on the named bone |
| Cloned Blueprint | spawns, boards, drives |
| Mesh of our own through the component, with `Transform.Scale3D` | draws at that scale |
| Model variant `none` | no chaingun objects on the clone |
| Cooked material instances on `M_CE_*` masters | load and draw CE's textures and glass |
| CE collision on a driven vehicle, other regions empty | loads; a biped stops at the hull, 132 cm from centre, and pushes it |
| Shrunk physics model, mass 1650 | drives level, 18.7 wu in 2.6 s |
| Mongoose: seat marker, four wheels, forward, reverse, turning | works; 18.4 wu in 2.6 s, 89 degree turn |
| Mongoose off an 8 m ledge, wheel boxes stretched with the hull | all four wheels 19 cm under the ground, boxes 5 cm over it, will not drive |
| The same bike with `wheel_boxes` and lights clear of the body | a player drove it and reported both right; the 8 m drop itself not repeated |

## Riders

A rider's hands and feet are not in its seat animation alone: the mode's idle
carries IK chains to named markers on the vehicle. `ghost_d` wants
`spartan_hand_left/right` and `spartan_foot_left/right`, `warthog_d` wants
`spartan_d_*` and `warthog_p` wants `chief_p_ik_*`. A marker the vehicle lacks
does not fall back to the plain animation: the limb stretches at the map's
origin. A seat offset cannot fix that; it looks like a skew to one side.

The Spartan's `mongoose_d` is a stub and no shipped Spartan graph has a Mongoose
pose, so the driver borrows `ghost_d`, with four unused skeleton marker groups
renamed to what it wants (`tools/level/data/mongoose_rider_ik.sets`), at CE's
wrist and ankle joints from `M-driver idle`, not at its grips and pegs. Markers
sit on the joints, and the rider's position is drawn at the rig's scale, so a
marker move shows at 0.59 of its size. The `driver` marker's rotation pitches the
torso: 20 degrees gives CE's 46 degree lean, and the IK limbs stay put.

| Bone, cm from the actor | CE | In game |
|---|---|---|
| Hips | -41, 0, 118 | -42, -1, 119 |
| Head | 2, 1, 160 | 12, -1, 167 |
| Wrists | 22, +-38, 149 | 30, +-38, 150 |
| Ankles | -27, +-37, 76 | -22, +-38, 79 |

The passenger keeps `warthog_p`, whose three chains (`chief_p_ik_left_arm`,
`left_leg`, `right_leg`) match CE's `M-passenger` IK, so the right arm stays free
to aim. A limb marker is drawn at the rider's origin plus its offset from the
seat, so moving the seat by d moves a limb by 0.41 d the other way: move the seat
first, then the limbs. CE's boots sit inside the rear body; here they stand on
the deck, 39 cm above CE's joint, on purpose.

| Bone, cm from the actor | CE | In game |
|---|---|---|
| Hips | -108, 1, 148 | -107, -2, 148 |
| Head | -69, 5, 200 | -81, -17, 212 |
| Left wrist | -42, -11, 136 (IK marker) | -65, -13, 161 |
| Ankles | -87, -12, 70 / -83, 11, 69 | -86, -12, 109 / -82, 10, 109 |

The marker sets are measured for this vehicle: they do not generate yet.

## Boarding

The prompt and E need the crosshair on the vehicle's collision. A small hull
is easy to miss from a spawn that looks over it: no prompt means aim first, not
a broken seat.

## In a map

A CE map can park vehicles out of reach and teleport them out by script. Here a
vehicle spawns and returns at its placement, so `tools/level/ce_place_vehicles.py`
moves each one to its flag, on the ground, and makes the plan's custom ones `tag`
placements (`tools/level/data/yoy_vehicles.json` for Yoyorast). It also copies the
vehicle's containers with names `map pack` takes, such as
`pakchunk985-MJOLNIRVCOOK-YOY_P`: the contents keep the `VHT` paths, so the tested
bytes ship. `map pack` carries `vehicle_sounds.json` into `map/`. Without
MJOLNIRLevelLoader 0.10.0 and the CE runtime such a map drives silent, with its
lights floating.

## Sounds from a bank

`tools/level/ce_vehicle_audio.py` is the native route, for a Warthog clone. It plays
through the game's own audio, so a vehicle built this way needs no
`vehicle_sounds.json` row and the sliders work:

```
python tools/level/ce_vehicle_audio.py <ce_vehicle_sounds.py's out dir> <out dir> \
    --class BP_VHTMongoose_C --code RWC --name Mongoose \
    --actor <folder>/<actor container> \
    --vehi <folder>/<vehicle tag's container> --vehi-tag <vehicle tag path>
```

- **Engine.** Its pitch ranges become looping sounds in one bank, with Pitch and Volume
  curves on `RTPC_VEH_Speed`. The Blueprint keeps its engine loop, pointed at that
  sound, and its `Audio_EngineTick` sets the RTPC. The Banshee's graph has no
  `SoundVariant_EngineLoop`, so a Banshee clone gets no engine this way.
- **Horn.** With `--vehi`, a clone of the Warthog's horn weapon and its Blueprint. Hold
  fire, as in a Warthog. CE's horn runs on crouch.
- **Containers.** `pakchunk996-MJOLNIRBANK-<CODE>_P` holds the banks in its `.pak`, so a
  map's `map pack` picks it up by name. `pakchunk996-MJOLNIRVWEAP-<CODE>_P` holds the
  weapon.

That `.pak` is for a local install. `map pack` takes the banks out of it, the archive
carries them bare and the launcher builds the `.pak` again
([map_distribution.md](map_distribution.md#a-vehicles-banks), with the release order).

## Not done

- `tools/level/native_mongoose/build_native.py` starts from a built physics model,
  so a native vehicle takes the wheel boxes only once that model has them.
- The vehicle data asset keeps the Warthog's HUD icons. Kill feed text is not traced.
- 22 rifle rounds at the empty hull did no damage. Stock vehicles were not
  compared, so whether it takes damage at all is unknown. Destroying a wheel is
  untested.
- Handlebars and suspension arms do not move; tyres spin about 24% slow.
- The passenger's left hand stops about 34 cm short of CE's fin grip, and its torso has none of CE's 37 degree lean. Firing from the seat is untested.
- The Spartan is bigger than CE's cyborg, and the idle is the Ghost's, so it has no bob or lean into turns of CE's own.
- Top speed and handling are the ratio recipe, not yet felt out by a player.
- Not tested on a second PC. Yoyorast's build (above) is baked and packs, but has
  not been played yet. Its `rhog_1` stands within 1 wu of a ledge and an overhang.
- Reloading a level in the same world silences the old engine loops, and stock
  maps skip the spawn check: `vehicle_sounds.lua` passes its unit tests on both,
  but neither has run in game.
- Yoyorast holds the same packages as `VHT`, so the two sets must not be installed
  together. Roadworks' Mongooses are only on PC 1 and need these containers too.
- The installed vehicle model has 43 imports where build13's has 45, with the same
  tag payload. Yoyorast ships the installed one, since that was played. A rebake of
  the unchanged level differs from the installed bake by 22 bytes, cause unknown.
- The song clip CE sometimes plays at engine start (`lsnd` 1057) is left out, as it
  is likely licensed.
- Weapons: the same route should hold (first-person actors use the same
  component), but no weapon has been tried.
- Tooling: a `tag` placement is not checked against installed containers, so a
  wrong path bakes and fails in game. Duplicate plan regions and `material` or `node`
  indices are not validated. `ce_vehicle_lights.py` assumes four headlights and two
  taillights. `ce_vehicle.py` and `ce_vehicle_name.py` look up the `997` stub and
  raise if no map is installed. The latest fixes to `ce_vehicle.py`,
  `ce_vehicle_sounds.py` and `ce_vehicle_instances_editor.py` compile but have not
  been run.

notes.title: Native support for CE tag data
notes.summary: A CE object's own tags decide what it does and how it looks. Tools translate fields by rule. Nothing is measured, posed or tuned per vehicle.
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-11-05, experiments 1 to 3, the skinned Mongoose, rider limbs, map players and the driver's CE pose passed in game; see Results. Marks: V verified, I inferred,
NF not found, F seen only in secondary research and to be confirmed against
`sapien.exe` before anything depends on it. Addresses are the sim DLL unless marked.

## Principle

A CE object's own tags decide what it does and how it looks. Tools translate
fields by rule. Nothing is measured, posed or tuned per vehicle.

## How CE works

- **Tick** (F): unit and vehicle update, damage, function export, nodes with
  function-driven overlays, children, rider IK.
- **Attachments** (F): built once, each scaled by an object function.
- **Rider** (F): root attaches to the seat marker, no offset field. The seat label
  picks the rider's antr mode; IK targets vehicle markers named in that antr.
- **Jet:** `speed` seeks raw throttle (V, Sapien 0x66415f), so the tag's 4.0 is
  unreachable (limit of 1: F). Zero throttle gives zero lift (F); powered points
  have no antigrav flag (V). Function D peaks at 0.25, so `jet_engine` stays at
  quarter scale (I).
- **Mongoose:** body vitality 0 (V, tag); no body damage (F).

## Design

**Blam side.** One translator per tag group, emitting real fields:

- skel, coll, phmo and jmad carry CE's hierarchy, as one unit. The hlmt load
  (0x180281850) silently blanks any ref whose nodes disagree (V).
- A general N-node jmad writer. `vehicle suspension`, `vehicle:steering` and
  `vehicle:ground_speed` are the homes for moving parts (I).
- Physics: translate first. Wheel mass points become friction points (I). CE's
  thrust and lift have no field (NF). A native port is untested, not excluded.
- A weap and proj route, splitting CE's trigger into `new triggers` plus `barrels`.

**Unreal side.** One generic actor: a drawn SkeletalMesh with bones named as the
sim's nodes, cloning `ABP_B40_Elevator`. `BlamSyncPose` (exe 0x147cf66f0) matches
by FName with no count check (V), so rig scale goes (I). An identity `pedestal`
sits above an off-origin CE root, as node 0 does on the Warthog and shipped
Mongoose (V), so CE's locals stay verbatim.
`tools/level/ce_vehicle_nodes.py` builds the tag side from the mesh's `bones.json`.

## What replaces each shortcut

| Shortcut | Replacement |
|---|---|
| Borrowed rig, 0.589 scale | Own hierarchy |
| Static handlebars, suspension | jmad blocks above |
| Ghost pose, measured IK | CE antr modes, `ik points` (674 maps at most) |
| Lua lights | `ligh` if it draws, else `effe` bound to a BP |
| Lua sounds | A Wwise bank per vehicle, played by its Blueprints (result 13) |
| Donor weapons | Real weap and proj |
| Banshee handling | Clear slide, boost, tricks, cruising throttle |
| Ratio numbers | Tag rules; `wheel circumferance` 1, CE's value (effect untested) |

A CE function evaluator may be partly redundant: the sim names `speed_absolute`
and `driver_seat_power` (V), but their handler is NF.

## Order of work

First lift the importer gates: `fit()` and `rigid_check` turn away 537+ maps.

| # | Unknown | First experiment |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SK, ABP cook | SK with Warthog bone names, ABP clone, cloned BP |
| 2 | Node agreement | Mongoose skel, coll, phmo, jmad; hlmt refs survive load |
| 3 | jmad writer | Rewrite `any:idle` for N nodes, re-decode |
| 4 | Rider | CE mode in a Spartan override; Megalo action 42 |
| 5 | Functions | Which names evaluate on a vehicle |
| 6 | Effects, lights | `antigrav_lift-effect` clone to a BP; find `ligh` schema |
| 7 | Sound | Find what `lsnd` to AkAudioEvent needs |
| 8 | Speed | Unit of `maximum forward speed`: 22.7 or 30 wu/s |

## Results

Measured in game on PC 1, 2026-11-05, one player, on a B40 canvas.

**1. Skeletal rig: passed.** A SkeletalMesh, Skeleton and animation Blueprint of
our own loaded in a cloned actor, with all 119 Warthog bone names. Driving it
spun and steered the wheels, moved the suspension and turned the steering wheel
while a parked stock Warthog stayed still. The test boxes drew, with no crash.
A mesh saved before its skeleton is renamed keeps the old path and cooks with no
Skeleton; the mesh then loads and draws but gets no anim instance, silently.

**2. Node agreement: passed.** Mongoose skel, coll, phmo and jmad on 14 nodes
kept all four hlmt refs and 14 runtime nodes (the shipped control has 119).

| Variant | Node names | Root | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| NAS | registered | origin | boards, drives |
| NAO | CE | origin | boards, drives |
| NAT | CE | CE | refs survive; floats about a metre; not boarded |
| NAR | registered | CE | not run; NAO and NAT isolate the root |

So CE's node names work as they are in tags (V).
The root node looks to need the origin, with CE's root offset moved into the next
node (I: one look at an unboarded vehicle; an offset in phmo is not excluded).

**3. jmad writer: passed.** A rewritten Warthog `any:idle` with `hood_base`
turned 30 degrees put the drawn bone about 30 degrees of pitch from `Body` on the
same actor; without the rewrite the two matched. The game accepts our members and
they reach the mesh.

**4. Skinned Mongoose: passed.** CE's model on its own 15-bone mesh (`pedestal`
above CE's 14 nodes), own skeleton, animation Blueprint and six skinned materials,
beside the shipped Mongoose. All four hlmt refs and 15 runtime nodes survive, it
draws with CE's textures, boards and drives. Parked, every drawn bone matches the
sim's node to the reading's precision: 0.15 cm, 0.001 of axis.

Driven, from the sim's own node matrices:

| Part | Measured |
|---|---|
| Tires | all four spin forward, rate tied to speed: about 31 rad/s near 6 wu/s |
| Suspension | each corner moves on its own: 1 to 13 cm over one run on the deck |
| Steering | front tires 25.6 degrees left on A; `frame steering` turns with them |

The sim turns a node's string id into an Unreal name with spaces as underscores:
`frame hull` reaches `BlamSyncPose` as `frame_hull` (V, read from the node's bone
array). A bone named with the space takes no transform and stays at its bind pose,
with no error. Tags keep CE's name; the mesh takes `frame_hull`.

`bNoSkeletonUpdate` reading true on a driven vehicle is normal: the flag came back
about 120 times a second after being cleared, so the sync looks to wake the mesh
for one refresh at a time (I).

**5. Rider limbs: passed, torso open.** The seat's IK proxies moved to CE's own
limb ends: hands to CE's wrists after its IK, on `frame steering`; feet to CE's
idle ankles on `frame hull`. The mode is still `ghost_d`. Read from the sim's
Spartan nodes, in the vehicle's frame, cm:

| Joint | Driver | CE | Miss |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ankles | -50.5, 38.1, 87.4 and -45.0, -36.7, 86.4 | same | 0.0, 0.1 |
| Wrists | 2.2, 31.4, 158.9 and 1.3, -33.5, 158.3 | 8.8, 32.6, 158.0 and 7.3, -34.1, 157.4 | 6.8, 6.1 |
| Hips | -73.0, -0.2, 116.1 | -61.7, -1.2, 129.0 | 17.2 |
| Head | -42.4, -4.1, 181.8 | -18.7, -1.3, 171.0 | 26.2 |

Limbs land on the marker's position, and CU4 stops an arm at its reach: the wrists
stop short along the arm (I). Hands follow the bars, but at full lock the far hand
falls short (right wrist 0, -42 against about 40, -50 on a left turn). The
passenger's ankles land on target and the left wrist within 3 cm. The arms-up pose
was the IK proxies left at VHT's height when the seat moved to CE's place.

Hips, head and knees are the mode's: only a CE idle on a Spartan mode moves them.
No shipped mode comes closer than 20.9 cm of torso error.

**6. A map's own player: passed.** `blam.player_representations` in a level writes
`override player representations` and sets `override globals`. On NMG the player
spawned as a cloned biped, with first person and HUD intact; hosting Rat Race next
gave the stock Spartan. A cloned model and full graph (111 MB uncompressed) also
loaded: all four hlmt refs hold, 122 runtime nodes, and the seated joints match the
stock graph's. The stock graph stays loaded beside the clone, so a map pays the
memory twice. Give all three rows: the copy replaces the globals' block (I).
Not tested: bots, Elite rows, armour customisation, two PCs.

**7. CE's seat pose on a Spartan: passed for the driver.** `tools/level/ce_vehicle_rider.py`
translates CE's seat idle onto `ghost_d:idle`, `ghost_d:grip` and
`warthog_p:rifle:idle` in the map's cloned graph, by one joint table per rig pair.
`Clip` now carries chain data, so IK survives the edit. Driver in game, against CE, cm:

| Joint | Miss |
|---|---|
| Pelvis | 0.4 |
| Wrists | 0.0, 0.0 |
| Ankles | 0.0, 0.1 |
| Head | 8.6 |
| Knees | 6.7, 7.2 |

These match the offline build, so the overlays leave the pose alone, and it holds
after driving. At full lock the hands stay on the bars. The knees are over the
6 cm goal: the Spartan's hips sit 7 cm off CE's and its shin is longer, so with
ankles pinned the knee has nowhere to go. The head is proportion.

The passenger pose is built (offline: pelvis 0.0, wrists 0.0 and 1.3, knees 9.1),
but it was not read in game: the seat could not be boarded on this run. Its right
arm sits at 98% of reach, with no chain on it. Enter, exit and other weapon classes
stay the donor's. CE's idles do not close their loop, so a small step shows at the seam.

**8. Lights: the Blueprint's own.** The Warthog's light components hang from
names like `VFX_Headlight_L`. `ce_vehicle_skin.py --markers` adds each as an unskinned
bone on CE's `headlight` and `taillight` markers, so the components stay and switch
with the Blueprint: headlight intensity 0 parked, 18 with a driver, brake 12. No Lua
moves them. CE's markers can sit behind the body (outer headlights 10 cm, tail lights
3.5 cm), which buried the glow, so each moves along its facing to 1 cm past the surface.
The sim leaves those bones at their bind pose. Socket fields are read-only to editor
Python, which is why they are bones.

**9. Two PCs: passed for the driver.** On Roadworks, a map with its own world, the
joiner spawned as the map's cloned Spartan and drew the host's native Mongoose. Read
on the joiner while the host drove: engine state, tires spinning and turned 32
degrees, handlebars 18.6, and the rider on CE's pose (pelvis within 0.3 cm of the
host's reading, wrists on the bars through the turn, ankles exact).
A joiner cannot enter a map that borrows a canvas world, with or without a map's own
player: the host puts it in the game, its session leaves, and it returns to the menu.
So test a vehicle on a map with its own world.

**10. A small graph over the stock one: passed.** `mjolnir jmad child` keeps only the
animations a map changes and names the stock Spartan graph as its parent. The sim
rebuilds the rest at load: the child holds 3 animations and 3 resource groups in
526,650 bytes, and reads 50 modes in memory. A map carries 0.5 MB instead of 111 MB,
and the graph no longer costs memory twice. A row a child keeps merges with the
parent's, so `ghost_d` keeps its enter and exit. The driver's pose matches the full
clone's to within 0.3 cm, and it holds through driving, getting out, walking and
firing. A cut Warthog mode also played correctly through a parent. Not read yet: a
child on two PCs, or the passenger's pose.

**11. Seats of their own: passed for the driver.** Result 10's child overwrites
`ghost_d` and `warthog_p`, so a real Ghost or Warthog passenger on the map would take
the Mongoose's pose. `mjolnir jmad child --mode` now carries those modes under
`mongoose_d` and `mongoose_p`, the seats' labels come from `SEATS` in
`ce_vehicle_rider.py`, and the parent keeps the donors' rows. The child grows from
0.5 MB to 9.5 MB, nearly all of it the passenger's other weapon classes. Offline, the
edited frames match the full clone's and every pool entry is reachable. In game, on one
map: a real Ghost's rider matches stock `ghost_d` (head 30.9, 65.7 cm from the pelvis
against 31.2, 65.5), a Warthog passenger matches stock `warthog_p`, and the Mongoose
driver stays on CE's pose (pelvis 0.8 cm, wrists and ankles 0.0 to 0.1). Not read: the
Mongoose passenger on `mongoose_p`, or this build on two PCs. A hub map reads
`vehicle_sounds.json` from its own folder. See `docs/jmad_format.md`.

**12. Vehicle sounds from a bank: passed for the horn and engine pitch.** A `.pak` of
our own carrying a real `.bnk` mounts beside the game's banks, and new `AkAudioEvent`,
`HaloAudioSound` and `snd!` packages play from it, so CE's horn played through a tag. An
`lsnd` attachment only starts and stops its loop. Engine pitch comes from the
Blueprint's `Audio_EngineTick`, which sets `RTPC_veh_speed` from
`GetEngineAngularVelocityFraction`, so the Mongoose's Blueprint keeps that tick. Pitch
moved on an idle-only bank, and the user confirmed it by ear. From Lua,
`AkGameplayStatics:PostEventAtLocation` is silent for every sound, and
`HaloAudioBlueprintFunctionLibrary:PlaySoundAtPosition` works. The game mutes when
unfocused, which looks like a silent bank. The spike's scripts stay in
`tools/level/native_mongoose/sound/`. Result 13 is the build.

**13. Engine and horn from a build: passed by ear.** `tools/level/ce_vehicle_audio.py`
writes a vehicle's banks, events, sounds, Blueprints and tags from
`ce_vehicle_sounds.py`'s table and the game's own files, with nothing extracted by
hand. Ids and package paths carry the map's code. On Roadworks, with no
`vehicle_sounds.json` row for the vehicle, the user heard all four engine samples
through the throttle and the Mongoose's own horn, and called both right. The engine
fraction read 0.60 at 9 m/s and 0.85 at 28 m/s, so the high samples are reached.

The horn is the driver's weapon. Its `lsnd` attachment names events with no bank behind
them, as the Warthog's engine `lsnd` does: `BP_WarthogHornWeaponActor` is what plays it,
from `Audio_Horn_Start` and `Audio_Horn_End`. So a vehicle gets its own clone of that
Blueprint and of the weapon tag. In play, both Mongooses carried `mongoose_horn` and the
three Warthogs the stock horn. Its trigger is fire, where CE's is crouch.

Measure sound by ear. `meter.ps1` read 0.0000 for all of this while the user heard it,
so a silent reading says nothing about a Blueprint's sound. It does read
`PlaySoundAtPosition`, but that call plays whatever position it is given (a sound
"1 km away" read 0.13), and its loop kept playing after `StopTrackedSound`.

An archive carries the banks bare and the launcher builds the `.pak`
([map_distribution.md](map_distribution.md#a-vehicles-banks)). Under the launcher's own
name, `pakchunk901-MJOLNIRHUB-roadworks-circuit-0_P`, its `.pak` mounted in the game:
`BlueprintPathsLibrary:FileExists` read true for both banks, and false with a stub of
that name in its place. The engine's file layer found them. That run wasn't checked by
ear, since the game mutes when unfocused, so nobody has heard a hub-installed bank yet.

Not covered: a joiner in the driver or passenger seat. At top speed wheel rate implies a radius of 0.197 wu against 0.174
for the model, so `wheel circumferance` needs a steady-state check. Whether the
25.6 degrees is CE's limit is unchecked. The prompt needs E held, not tapped.

## Stays approximate

- Handling: CE's solver is not this one.
- Lights are the Warthog's look on CE's places, until a `ligh` tag draws. The sim
  creates a light datum (0x1805a0fc0), but no tags ship (V).
- Sounds stay Lua in published maps until a launcher that takes banks reaches players
  ([release order](map_distribution.md#a-vehicles-banks)).
- The start and stop clips in a vehicle's sound table aren't in its banks yet.

## Open questions

- `allows weapons`: the clone's driver also has `gunner (player only)` and
  `prevents weapon stowing`; interaction unknown.
- Why did the clone, at vitality 500, take no rifle damage? Compare a stock Warthog.
- 177 maps teleport named vehicles; the variant holds no names.
- Stock weapons lose CE numbers too: assault rifle 36 rounds, not 60.

notes.title: Halo CE terrain as Campaign Evolved collision (2026-09-03)
notes.summary: How a classic bloodgulch.map collision BSP becomes something the Meteorite simulation walks on, what was proven offline, and what the single remaining in-game test is. Tooling lives in crates/blam-sbsp (unpack16, pack16, transplant, examples). No claim below needed the game…
notes.body:
**Status:** 2026-10-21. Closed. What every converted map ships is "A BSP of
our own" below: `mjolnir level collision --own-bsp`
(`blam_sbsp::convert::convert_own`), with scenery in the BSP tree or behind
instances of its own (2026-10-03), each such piece one whole-instance key in
`structure_physics` since 2026-10-12.
[ce_map_conversion.md](ce_map_conversion.md) has the pipeline. The sections
before "A BSP of our own" are the investigation, superseded turns included;
the in-game test the next paragraph awaits has long since passed.

How a classic `bloodgulch.map` collision BSP becomes something the Meteorite
simulation walks on, what was proven offline, and what the single remaining
in-game test is. Tooling lives in `crates/blam-sbsp` (`unpack16`, `pack16`,
`transplant`, examples). No claim below needed the game running unless it
says so.

## Where walkable collision lives

The world shell (`raw_items.collision bsp`) is not what the pawn stands on.
Every walkable surface is an **instanced-geometry definition**, referenced by
an **instance** (transform, bounds, a `physics` block with the Havok shape) and
reached through a two-level Havok broadphase:

    cluster to instance group spheres / mopps   ->  instance group to instance spheres / mopps  ->  instance

- A definition's `collision info` carries the same eight 16-bit tables as the
  shell (nodes 8 B, planes 16, leaves 8, 2D refs 4, 2D nodes 16, surfaces 14,
  edges 12, vertices 16) plus `bsp3d supernodes`. Nine shipped definitions have
  no supernode; one ships 3,205 surfaces, so size is not a limit.
- Raising the definitions under the spawn by 3 wu (`examples/shift_defs.rs`)
  changed what the pawn stood on (it fell through), so these tables are the
  source. Confirmed in game, one launch.
- An instance without a `physics` block (the navmesh instance) is never
  collidable. An instance moved away from its group's sphere is culled before
  its shape is tested: relocating instance 105 to the origin gave no collision
  even with valid tables.
- `instance group to instance spheres[g]` has `center`, `radius`, and an
  `instance indices` block; `examples/groups.rs <payload> <instance>` finds the
  group. Instance 763 (a spawn-floor platform) sits in group 58, radius 17.87.

## The encoder is byte-exact

`examples/roundtrip16.rs` decodes a shipped block into the CE structs
(`unpack16`), re-packs it with `pack16`, and compares. Definitions 10, 159
and 178 and the world shell of `BSP_01_1_Start` all come back **identical**,
every table. Our leaf flags, 2D sign bits, plane-negated flag and edge order
match the engine's.

## The 2D projection convention, and the translation bug

Each 2D BSP lives in the projection of its parent 3D plane. Scoring every
candidate against the surfaces the shipped 2D trees actually sort:

| convention | def 10 | def 159 | def 178 | shell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| drop the largest-normal axis; keep the other two in cyclic order when that component is positive, swapped when negative; right child = positive side | 100% | 100% | 100% | 99.5% |
| every other candidate | 0–72% | 28–72% | 39–65% | 19–81% |

`pack16::translate` used to move vertices and 3D planes and leave the 2D split
lines alone. After any sideways move every point-in-leaf lookup then chose
the wrong surface, which is why transplanted shells and definitions let the
pawn through. It now shifts each 2D line by `i·t[u] + j·t[v]` in its parent
plane's projection (`pack16::projection_axes`, `pack16::node_planes`); the
probe stays at 100% after a `(-35.4, 151.17, 50)` move of a shipped
definition. On the Halo data the probe reads 98.3% both before and after
translation, so that residual is the data or the probe, not the move.
`examples/probe_residual.rs` narrows it to 14 of 5,098 surfaces (flat floors
among them), with no 2D subtree shared between references. Scored in each
reference's own frame (below) that is 12 surfaces, and clipped to the 2D cell
above each node it is none: the rest is outlines that reach past their cell,
not bad trees.

**Update 2026-11-06:** a reference with the plane's sign bit reads its tree in
the swapped projection, the same as `projection_axes` of the negated normal
(`pack16::reference_axes`). On shipped `BSP_01_1_Start` definition 5 the
unsigned frame agrees with 230 of 320 vertex checks and the signed frame with
236 of 236. `translate` used the unsigned frame until then; see "2D trees and
the reference's sign" at the end.

## Placing Bloodgulch

`examples/def_transplant.rs --keep-position` puts the CE collision into a
definition behind an instance that stays where it is (so it stays inside its
broadphase group), resets that instance to an identity frame, subtracts the
instance position from the geometry, and sets the instance bounds, bounding
sphere and Havok shape box. `examples/def_clear.rs` empties the competing
floor definitions so what the pawn lands on is unambiguous, and
`examples/widen_group.rs` grows the group sphere to the new extent.

Staged for the next launch (`pakchunk999-MJOLNIR-Windows_P`):

    def_transplant  bsp_01_1_start.bin collision_0.json out 159 763 -35.4 151.17 44.0 --keep-position
    def_clear       out out2 78 97 110 129 32 141 168 71 9
    widen_group     out2 out3 58 33.504 33.532 68.826 99.4
    mjolnir pack --group scenario_structure_bsp --tag Solo/B40/_Generated_/BSP_01_1_Start --payload out3

### The broadphase, as far as it is decoded

`examples/mopp_dump.rs <payload> 58` prints group 58's Havok mopp: 141 bytes
of bytecode, build type 0, scale/offset `v = (16.70, 24.37, 37.86; w
635595.9)`, over ten members `[165, 214, 279, 545, 550, 593, 643, 722, 763,
779]`. It is a bounding-volume tree over the members' boxes, so a query far
from instance 763's original box will not return 763 even after the group
sphere is widened; near the spawn, inside that box, it should. Regenerating
these mopps (both levels) is the price of placing terrain as instances
anywhere in the map — or the price is avoided entirely if the world shell
turns out to be walkable once its 2D splits are right, which is why two
variants are staged:

| variant | where the terrain lives | broadphase | in `Paks` now |
|---|---|---|---|
| shell | `raw_items.collision bsp[0]`, pass-through supernode, Chasm_old kd companions | none (kd supernodes) | **yes** (`scratch/bgshell`) |
| definition | definition 159 behind instance 763, group 58 sphere widened | group mopps, untouched | no (`scratch/bgsbsp`) |

Both clear the spawn-floor definitions (78 97 110 129 32 141 168 71 9; the
definition variant leaves 159) so the pawn has nothing else to stand on.
Every earlier "the shell is not walkable" verdict came from transplants with
the 2D-split bug, so it is unproven either way.

### The one-launch protocol

NEW GAME → Assault on the Control Room (row 5), no screenshots. Then:

```lua
local pawn = FindFirstOf("BP_MeteoritePawn_C")
local z0 = pawn:K2_GetActorLocation().Z / 304.8
local t = os.clock(); while os.clock() - t < 3 do end
local z1 = pawn:K2_GetActorLocation().Z / 304.8
print(string.format("z %.2f -> %.2f : %s", z0, z1,
  (z1 > 43.5 and z1 < 45.5) and "PASS: standing on Halo terrain"
  or (z1 < 30 and "FAIL: fell through" or "inconclusive")))
```

Prediction for the blank B40 map, NEW GAME: the pawn spawns at 48.16 wu with
no tower floor under it and lands on Bloodgulch's canyon floor at about
**44.1 wu** (CE z 0.12 + 44). Falling to the kill plane means the group's
Havok mopp still culls the instance, and the mopp bytecode is the next thing
to decode. Do not test through RESUME: three of three resumes with a modified
structure BSP hung the game thread, while NEW GAME loaded every time.

## The scenario half

`tools/level/gen_bloodgulch_level.py` turns the halo2ue staging export
(`staging/bloodgulch/placement.json`) into `examples/levels/bloodgulch.level.json`:
eight CTF/Slayer starts, the 28 vehicles, 15 weapons and 18 pickups the CE map
places (through `defs/level/palette-map.json`; health packs, the flamethrower
and the plasma cannon have no equivalent and are dropped), and 170 netgame
markers kept for a later game-mode layer. Everything moves by the same
`(-35.4, 151.17, 44.0)` wu offset as the collision, so a start at Halo
`(98.49, -157.64, 1.70)` lands at `(63.09, -6.47, 45.70)` wu, 1.6 wu above the
transplanted floor there.

Assembly for a test, two containers plus the loader's level file:

    mjolnir level bake examples/levels/bloodgulch.level.json --install-test     # scnr: pakchunk998-MJOLNIRLEVEL-bloodgulch_P
    (one of the two collision containers above)                               # sbsp: pakchunk999-MJOLNIR-Windows_P

Remove `pakchunk998-MJOLNIRLEVEL-blank_b40_P.*` first: two `_P` containers
over the same scenario chunk would race. Order of tests: blank map + shell
collision (landing height), then this level on whichever collision variant
held the pawn.

## The visual half

The world under the blank map is already a MapKit cook: the installed
`pakchunk990-MJOLNIRWORLD-Windows_P` holds one file, an empty `B40.umap`, so
the void with one streaming level and no lights was our own canvas, not the
shipped world. Visuals therefore ride the same container as the world:

1. `unreal/MJOLNIRMapKit/Content/Python/mjolnir_import_bloodgulch.py` builds
   the empty canvas with the existing generator, then imports halo2ue's
   `staging/bloodgulch/bsp/bsp_0.gltf` (one mesh, 42 materials, 16 textures)
   under the level's folder, which the chunk label routes into chunk 990. The
   UE 5.6 HaloUE project's 343 assets cannot be reused: cooked formats are
   engine-version locked and the game is 5.5.
2. `scripts/package.ps1 -LevelPackage /Game/Levels/Halo1/Solo/B40/B40` cooks
   world and mesh into the container. Two things had to be true for the mesh
   to come along at all: nothing in the empty world references it, so
   `DefaultGame.ini` lists the folder under `DirectoriesToAlwaysCook`; and a
   label's "assets in my directory" rule does not descend into subfolders, so
   the mesh folder carries its own chunk-990 label.
3. The level file's `decor` names the mesh
   (`/Game/Levels/Halo1/Solo/B40/Halo/Bloodgulch/bsp_0.bsp_0`) at the
   collision offset; the runtime loader spawns it.

Coordinates check out from the glTF alone: its position bounds are
`(18.0, -1.06, 137.33)..(402.04, 79.96, 579.79)` m, which is Halo
`(x, z, -y) x 3.048`, and Unreal's glTF import turns that into
`(x, -y, z) x 304.8` cm — the same mapping every other placement uses — so
the mesh at identity sits at native Halo positions and only the transplant
offset is applied.

Two unknowns the next launch answers, both in
`tools/level/checks/bloodgulch_check.lua`: whether the game deserialises a
stock-cooked `UStaticMesh` (the actor/component wall documented in the MapKit
README is about unversioned *actor* properties; assets are untested), and
whether a package absent from the shipped asset registry can be loaded by
path from Lua at all (`LoadAsset` versus `KismetSystemLibrary.LoadAsset_Blocking`).
If neither loads it, the fallback is to make the empty world import the mesh
so it arrives with the level.

## Installed right now (2026-09-03 evening)

| container | holds |
|---|---|
| `pakchunk990-MJOLNIRWORLD-Windows_P` | empty B40 canvas world + `bsp_0` terrain mesh, 42 materials, 16 textures (79 chunks) |
| `pakchunk998-MJOLNIRLEVEL-bloodgulch_P` | stripped B40 scenario with Bloodgulch starts, vehicles, pickups, startup script |
| `pakchunk999-MJOLNIR-Windows_P` | BSP_01_1_Start with the Bloodgulch collision in the **world shell**, spawn floors cleared |

Plus the loader's `levels/B40.level.json` with the terrain decor entry. One
